Text:
This was not our first time dining here and it won't be our last. We love Peach Valley Cafe but unfortunately, there isn't one near us. We were in the area and we happen to have our four-legged son with us (yes, our dog) so we called to make sure they were open and that dogs were allowed in the outdoor dining area. The phone was quickly answered by a very nice lady that said "Yes, we are open and yes, dogs are gladly welcomed".

When we got there we were quickly shown to our table. My wife and I are 99% sure our server's name was Richard. He was younger gentleman and appeared to be fairly new. We loved him so much. He really did a great job of taking care of use and making sure we had everything we needed. He seemed a little hesitant and unsure of himself a couple of times, but there is no need.

I wanted something a little lighter than normal, so I just ordered a half order of french toast. My wife ordered an egg sandwich and one of her favorite items, a peach cream muffin. We also ordered 2 plain scrambled eggs for our dog.

The food was out to our table in no time and it was hot and fresh. I quickly dove into my french toast and it was gone in just a few minutes. My wife loved her egg sandwich and of course, she loved the muffin. She did comment if you are expecting a noticeable peach flavor, it is not there.  Oh, the muffin is also cut in half and cooked on the griddle for a minute or two. MMM, that makes for a nice finish on the muffin. Our dog didn't complain about his eggs, nor did he pay us for them. I had a bite and they were plain eggs like we requested, they were nice and fluffy.

Our total was $20 for everything. Great value for some really good food, that was served quickly and was very fresh. We will continue to come here and hope to see Richard on our next visit.

So I had plans to take my mother to another restaurant for Mother's Day. But when we pulled up it started raining  's &  'a. So we decided to wait but then parking was hectic so we said let's just find some where else. I googled restaurants in the area and Revival came up. I had never heard of it but the menu and the description looked like something I'd be interested in. We got there at about 4:40. They didn't open until 5. So we waited. When we go in the host says they are fully booked but that we could sit at the bar and have dinner. I was worried because my mom is not a "sit at the bar type"  But she said she wanted to try the place so it was ok. So we sit and we're greeted by Kevin. Who was great by the way. He explained the concept and the menu. We decided to go with the family meal. Which is $42 per person. Now I was born and raised here so at first I was like "do I want to pay $42 for soul food?" Lol Now each person chooses an entree and they pick your 5 shareable sides. It includes an appetizer, desert, and coffee or tea. My mom chose the meatloaf and I had the fried chicken. The appetizer was a smoked salmon pasty bite. I liked it. And a Kale/strawberry  salad. Delicious. Once our meals come out we realize that we have enough food for four or five people!  The meatloaf was excellent! Thick and juicy. The chicken was very good. It wasn't complete though. Had to ask Kevin for hot sauce. Lol  The mac n cheese was creamy & tasty. My mom loved the cabbage. It was tasty but I'm not big on cabbage so I let her have that. Another side was grits with a tomato sauce. Yesssss! It actually complimented the fried chicken. The greens were tender. They were a little bland for my liking but I added salt and pepper and I was good. My mom got the strawberry  fried pie w/ice cream and I got The Lemon ice box pie. Both were delicious. I really didn't want to share my pie after I tasted it though . Overall everything was great. Great Service as well. The most important thing was my Mom absolutely loved the place and was already making plans to come back with her sisters. She so loved the atmosphere and the antiques that decorated the place. She's a classic southern girl so this was right up her alley. We'll back.

Went there for the first time yesterday for brunch.

Nice place.  A little small, but it's cozy.  I'm a boring eater, so I got pancakes with some home fries and bacon.  Tasty!  The portions are actually reasonably sized.  I felt there wasn't quite enough pancake on my plate because they were so yummy, but I left feeling just full enough.  No complaints from anyone at the table... lots of mmmmms and wows going on.

Service was pretty quick.  Not spectacularly friendly, but no complaints.  Food came out super fast.  The bill was less than I expected.

Extra touch- they had a bluegrassy banjo/fiddle band playing.  Cool!

I love the circuit rowing classes at btone. It is a great way to get a cardio workout with strength building built in. The Instructors are great at keeping you motivated and focused during the workouts. They also review technique to ensure that you have the right posture and protect your back as you row. I have also tried the tone classes which are deceptively easy. I was able to keep up and follow the workout but I was sore for several days after (which is how I knew I got a good work out)

I received a phone call yesterday at work from my apartment manager letting me know that my '98 Honda Accord had been broken into and the entire front passenger window was smashed in. Since I was planning to use my car quite a bit this weekend, I wanted to find a shop that could do a day-of replacement to get me on my way.

After calling around to several places, I got in touch with MS Glass. Their quote for the window replacement was the lowest out of everyone I called, and the representative I talked to (Melissa) was super friendly and willing to work with my schedule to find a time. They also came right to my car without my having to move it at all. So convenient!

The gentleman who came to do the replacement was right on time (15 mins early, actually) and worked very efficiently - he was done in 45 minutes, as he predicted at the beginning. Very friendly guy. The quality of work was excellent - very smooth installation, no issues when rolling the window up and down. I wish I'd had cash to tip him!

Overall, I'd highly recommend MS Glass for window/windshield repair and replacement. I had a great customer experience and I'm sure others will too.

A while ago (I don't remember when), Boston Bodyworker eliminated insurance discounts. That much was communicated to me via email, and they'd reduced rates slightly to offset the change. Everything seemed ok.

It wasn't. They also eliminated their no-tipping policy. Perhaps they reached out to me, but I don't recall ever seeing any correspondence to communicate the change. And so, I received 5 or more treatments without ever realizing that tips were "a thing" here. Not only was I humiliated when I realized that I'd been stiffing my therapist... I was extremely disappointed in the change. 

Massage therapy is part of my medical care. It's the most effective form of physical therapy for managing my degenerative disc disease. The environment at the Boston Bodyworker is not that of a spa where I can go to treat myself to some pampering from someone who clearly works in the "service industry." I come here for medical treatment. Tipping changes the whole dynamic of the experience and makes me feel extremely uncomfortable. Please note: I did my time waitressing, and generally have no problem being fair and generous with gratuities. 

Just feels like yet another business passing on costs to the consumer while burdening their employees with an unpredictable source of income. I think the therapists at Boston Bodyworker are well-trained, well-educated professionals and they deserve consistent pay that reflects that.

Not so great. I was a little disappointed. This isn't authentic Italian food. There's nothing special about the food. 
I had lasagna that taste like tangy tomato sauce with meat, ravioli and melted cheese. Not so great but ok. 

Hummus with wheat pita bread: hummus was extremely spicy with hard stale pita bread. 

Salmon and spinach: salmon was grilled nicely and fluffy. But I thought I was going to get a sautéed spinach with a cream sauce on top, like what I saw in the yelp pictures, but I didn't. Oh well. It was edible. 

My husband had spaghetti and meatballs. As soon as he opened the box he knew; this is just some "fake spaghetti " with red tomato sauce on top. No thrills, no love in their food. 

SHUCKS.

So this was my first time ever being at a BWW and i thought it was delicious. I had a Buffalo Zoo/long island and they where great. The service was ok for being a new restaurant. Nice bar area. Perfect area to have a BWW right in front of the mall right off the highway. I will be a returning costumer. 

I had the ribs and boneless wings(wild sauce) they where pretty hot. I'm going to try out the blazin next time around. The Gf had the Asian Zing which i liked alot. We also got a sampler came with onion rings,chicken wings(honey BBQ sauce),nachos, and mozzarella sticks. 

Alot of T.v's! In every direction there is a t.v, so no breaking a neck trying to look at a t.v lol

Overall a Good experience and will be back soon :)

Made a reservation for dinner, everything was amazing, the server was very helpful at explaining what each dish was. They only had one beer on tap, since they are a seafood restaurant it did pair with my dish well. I would have like to have more than one option. They do have bottled beer but that just does not taste the same. My wife had a margarita and that was amazing. No complaints and would recommend to friends or anyone that is looking to have some amazing seafood.

As much as I want to give this place 5 Stars because the thought & concept is THE BEST.. I just cant do it. 

I attended a Birthday Party here a few weeks ago & this review is strictly based on THAT PARTY!  The place was packed when we arrived as we were attending a twins birthday that had LOTS of people.  The girls there hosting were trying to be great but just werent coming across as genuine. Clearly they didnt have children and it was showing all too often. Their patience level wasnt there and they kept expecting things that just were not going to happen from this room of kids (should I preface this with that most of the room was kids under 4 - I know they say the age is 7 and above & maybe that would be a better thing to know ahead of time - but I guess I was invited I showed up, I didnt know the preface) 

But I have a 2 year old who was painting the table, the chairs, anything in his reach in addition to having spilled the water 2-3 times & was just making an all out mess and I am not the parent to just walk away & say Oh Well, so I was sticking around trying to help out & at MANY instances the girls kept asking all the parents (there were soo many of us and maybe that was part of the problem - again I was only invited & knew no one else there as this was a co workers Childrens birthday.) but they kept asking the parents to leave the room and could the parents of the older childen have left the room, ABSOLUTELY - did they?! NO... But I felt I needed to run interference between my child & EVERYTHING In the room... But I was continually given the Ugly Side Eye with the "get out of the way face" Well sorry my son just painted pizza and you allowed him to eat it, Sorry Not Sorry!!!   

So this place seems like the BEST Idea and I would def go back if they had a free paint session and maybe just take my 7 year old, because I like the concept & the place was super stocked with stuff... 

Also my gf who threw the party told me on SEVERAL Occassions she informed the location what style of painting she had specifically requested & that was never taken care of & we ended up painting the theme she DID NOT WANT.  So all in all, concept great, but this location didnt make me a Huge fan!

Conclusion: will stay again. 

The places is dated. Definately needs some renovations. Commons areas especially. The rooms were clean. Beds very comfortable. Simple paint could make rooms a lot nicer in appearance. Bathrooms were not so pleasant. Mildew around shower heads. Wallpaper peeling off in bathrooms. Air conditioner was sporadic. No microwave in room but did have toaster oven. 

Did not partake in any amenities as we were there for disney. 

Continental breakfast was good as well. Enough to keep you filled up for a few hours so saves quite a bit of money having to avoid buying breakfast. 

As I said I will come back. The price is right but some very simple maintenance would make this place a lot nicer.

Tutti Frutti is a great place to go after dinner on Park Ave. My favorite flavor is cookies n cream with oreo cookie toppings. Tutti Frutti is another weigh and pay fro-yo place. They don't have as many flavors and toppings as other self serve places but they have a fair amount.  The staff is friendly. The decor is peppy and hip. The seating is limited but I've never been in when there wasn't a place to sit. Overall, Tutti Frutti is a great addition to Park Ave.

This is one of our favorite places to go because their food is consistently good and they are very reasonably priced. 
The wait staff is attentive and the bar staff is always a hit.
We've never had to wait for a seat but have not always been able to get outside seating.
They have a good selection of beer on tap and their drinks are generously poured.
They always have a homemade daily soup and their daily special is a really good deal.
We have liked everything that we have ordered there. In particular, my boyfriend claims that their burgers rank in the top 5 on his "list" which covers all of Ohio. We've both enjoyed their chicken and regular gyros. He loves the Southwest Chicken sandwich (I think that's what it's called) and I love their Italian Panini.

In the realm of food, there are few things that make me happier than a quality protein over rice. I've been here once before and had their chicken pho and wasn't' a big fan. Not their fault, I can comfortably admit now that I'm not a fan of chicken pho. However, their sliced pork dish over rice dish is awesome. It's also a huge portion, the pork is seasoned perfectly, under $10 bucks and comes with friendly service! A guy can't ask for much more than that. Oh, and there's a fried egg on top which is included, not extra (I'm looking at you nearly every trendy new restaurant!). As Mr. Bourdain exclaims about himself, "I'm a total egg slut." Well, so am I.

With fewer and fewer places in Austin, or so it seems, filling you up with one dish for a single digit price, that makes this place even more appreciated.

Let me start out by saying that I feel a little silly reviewing a Dunkin' Donuts.  I mean, really, c'mon... there's one on every corner in this town.  Hell, there's one on every corner in ALL OF NEW ENGLAND.  But this one's different.  It's special.  And you know why?  Because it's MY Dunkin' Donuts.

No, I don't own it, nor do I work there.  But it IS the one I visit pretty much every morning on the way to work.  And let me tell you, it's actually got some of the friendliest service I've ever encountered at a DD's.

I used to go inside to order all the time, since I had this weird perception that drive-thru lanes were both less efficient and more likely to mess up one's order.  The ladies who work inside are generally, shall we say, "women of a certain age."  Oh, and they all totally incessantly flirt with their male customers, which is kind of awesome.  In fact, one time one of the ladies was hunched down on the ground behind the counter (getting more cups or something, probably?) and this good-looking construction dude who also happens to be a regular customer walks in... and what does she say to him?  "I'm already on my knees for ya, honey!!"  Now I probably don't have to tell you, but that made my morning.  Also, any time I would get a bottle of soda or juice, I'd be offered a cup of ice for my beverage.  I always declined, but it was still a very nice gesture.

Nowadays, I'm a drive-thru guy all the way.  The woman who works at the window when I go there in the morning has gotten to know what I order, and can instantly spot without my needing to point it out when something has gone awry in the "kitchen."  Also, they haven't discontinued poppy seed bagels like some OTHER locations have done, and I always get TWO lemon wedges with my iced tea.

You can probably tell I could go on and on, but I'll spare you.  Just know that this Dunkin' Donuts is awesome.

Stopped by and found a nice new location for refilling my bar.

The space is not big but it had a very nice selection of locally sourced alcohol. They had some special releases that I had not seen before. Don't really want locally produced "Cucumber Vodka" or "Watermelon vodka", but I appreciate being able to view a wide assortment of local products and then choosing the ones that I want. The wine selection was limited but they do not have the square footage to do much more.

Of course went back again a few more times...tried yet again the honey lavender but this time in a cone that was too thin and brittle ..wished it was less sugary.  
On another visit I had the cracked mint and it didn't dissapoint but it didn't give me that feeling I was searching for...'natural speaks to your DNA type' oh well!
The coconut chocolate seems pretty decent just because its like eating the inside of a young coconut...and lastly the olive oil and pine nut was amazingly good!

I had Beau Jo's in Idaho Springs and that was like 12 years ago. I couldn't remember much about it so thought I would give it a try.  I get the whole Colorado Style thing and I like the honey.  I think it is a good concept but here the pizza itself just misses the mark.  We had the Chicken Cordon Bleu Pizza and the Cajun pizza.  Both sounded good on paper but were not very nice in real life.  The dough is just so sweet!  Maybe that is why it is good with honey.  I did like their salad bar which has pretty much everything that you need to make a yummy salad.  But I found the pizza very disappointing.  They do have a gluten free menu and that would be important to some people so that is a plus but not for me.  Oh well, I don't think I will be back.  If I do find myself in another Beau Jo's I will just stick to the salad.

Caramel latte was superb!  First time trying the macchiato and it was strong for me but my husband love it. He also got the pour over and said that was good. We also like the cold brew. 
The almond croissant was pure heaven. I am serious. I could have eaten a hundred of them.  We also got the corn and gruyere  muffin which would have been better warmed up, but honestly I can't complain. 
The atmosphere is very laid back. It is fun to see all of the equipment around while you are drinking your coffee and eating your amazing almond croissant.  The staff was kind.

To be honest the only reason why this place is still in business is because it's right in the middle of a college campus. 

I ordered the tom yum noodle soup with vermicelli, tofu and chicken, which I've had before and is alright. This time I got it togo and when I got back home I found a hair wrapped around a piece of tofu. I was so disgusted and immediately threw it away. I called them immediately and spent a long time trying to explain that I wanted a new order. Twenty minutes later I went to pick up my new soup and not only the cashier, but the manager asked where the original soup was. I told them multiple times that I threw it away. Why would I go through the hassle of bringing it back? I spent 15 minutes fighting them on this and they finally gave me a new soup. Upset and hungry, I stormed out. When I opened my soup, however, it didn't have the tofu that I had asked for (and paid extra for!) it was spicier, and the amount was less. 

This is probably the worst food experience I've had. Definitely don't come here because it's not worth it. If you want Thai food, go to nud pob or giggling rice.

How have I not done a review for DPH?? It's not that I've been here a bazillion times but I've been here enough to know that it's dangerously good. Was in the area at Hillside Hardware (plug) and Tasty Gourmet (plug plug) and thought I would get a little something sweet to go with my dinner. A double sided florentine with butter cream you say? YES PLEASE! I usually get the florentines from Modern Pastry (plug3) so of course I had to try DPH's and compare. Well I will say that they are both very different from each other. Modern is more chocolatey and Danish is more caramely. The butter cream puts it way over the top. I think I found my new favorite florentine spot. 

Modern- 12.99 a pound. 
Danish- 3.25 a piece. 
Not sure which has more bang for your buck??

SIDE NOTE- DPH will be taking over the Ulla's Flowers & Gifts store next door. That means the House is getting bigger! YEAY!!!

We were all too tired to cook.  Decided on take-out.  Peel Pizza.  We have had their pizza a few times already and it has really "hit the spot".  We created our own based on the list of ingredients.  One roasted red pepper, blackened chicken, garlic and corn and the other was bacon, potato, caramelized onion and corn.  I was in the mood for a salad and decided to try some skillet chicken wings.

The word that came to mind when we started eating was "OUTSTANDING"!  The salad was cold and crisp  with fresh greens , caramelized onion, bacon and Gorgonzola.  Delish!  The chicken wings were everything one could hope for.  The fall-off-the bone tender meat was packed with flavor.  I did not use any sauce.  Straight up and totally satisfying.  The pizza was perfection.  We had enough left for lunch the next day.  The quality of product and the care with which the food is prepared shows a true understanding and love of food.  Thank you, thank you!   Keep up the great work.  Peel Pizza is holding steady at the top of our take-out list.

The food here is unbelievably delicious and flavorful. I love the enchilada sauce especially. I come here with a large variation of people. My parents frequent it, my best friend is always up for a trip, even my roommates loved it when i took them here. 
The margaritas are made to perfection each time. Absolutely without a doubt, the best Mexican in Boulder. However, the service is incredibly awful. They take forever to get to you, but when they do their always friendly and it's hard to stay mad.

Let me preface this review about the actual dwelling space we lived in. The office staff was always courteous and friendly. I hope they find a better place to work as they deserve better.

Here is the list of items that were issues throughout our time at the Collonade:

1.  Each and every toilet overflowed at least once. The secondary upstairs toilet overflowed multiple times and even flooded the floor so much that they had to pull up the carpet and bring in an air blower
to dry everything out.

2.  The place where they pulled up the carpet was at the seam between the hallway and a room, which caused carpet fibers to show a gap.

3.  The flooding went through the floor and to the ceiling of the lower living room which caused the drywall to bow and leak onto the carpet below. 

4.  When the toilets flushed, the pipes would bang against the walls. One time it repeatedly banged against the wall so hard and rapidly that we thought the pipes had possibly busted.  We had the maintenance come out to which they found no reason for alarm. The individual informed us that it was normal and that it happens frequently.

5.  The burner on the front right of the stove was constantly going out. All attempts at fixing it by maintenance were met with the burner going out almost immediately after they left. The stove is old and needs to be replaced.

6.  Eventually all of the burners ceased to work at all to which videos were taken showing the burner dials set to "High" and hands resting on the burners. This did nothing to speed up the process to have the stove replaced.

6.  The kitchen faucet would shut off on its own when anything else other than the high setting was used rendering it virtually useless to wash hands or gentle use.

7.  The walls are pretty thin and you will hear your neighbors if they are even within a moderate decibel level. This can cause some awkward moments when you hear them and then get to see them after arguments or "exercising".

8.  Canine excrement is evident after it rains. If you have a nice breeze and you open the windows, the aroma will fill your home.

9. Electrical outlets were used so much that plugs would not stay seated in the sockets. 

10. Washer and dryer are old, loud, and extremely inefficient. The dryer takes several runs to fully dry loads.

11. Main entrance foyer allowed water through the front door because of space in between threshold and bottom of door, which caused swelling of door jamb and flooding of bottom floor.

12. Dumpster divers are frequent visitors. 

13. Fan lights were an upgrade that cost extra.

14 . Rent increased to almost $300/month per each individual month or $125/month if renewing for a year.

15.  Before we moved out, we asked the maintenance person if there was anything additional we could do before handing in the keys to the unit. They informed us that they would get back to us. They never did. Two months later, they charged us over $900 for replacing carpet because they said that both stairwells and the bottom room needed to be replaced due to cat urine smell that was already in the unit before we moved into it. (See number 11 for flooding of bottom floor from rain and number 1 for toilets flooding the carpets.) They never notified us of anything until they sent a bill where they subtracted the deposit and left a significant balance left for us to pay. This is robbery, plain and simple.

16. They were hesitant on giving an itemized listing of what we were paying for after we moved. 

17.  They tried to write in as much as possible for items that were not caused by us, such as a stress fracture of a long window pane above the sliding glass doors which we filed maintenance request for months in advance. 

This place is horrendous and if you happen to come across this place, it's truly not worth your time and definitely not worth the extra cash you will be shelling out.

A very creative way to eat a potato. I love the steak and cheese rosti potato! Recently I have been on a health kick so I get the "veggie lovers" sweet potato and sometime I add chicken to that. The chicken capituary  empanadas (Brazilian cream cheese) are amazing. Sometimes we order just the empanadas. The other day I mistakenly ended up with a beef capituary empanada which had an abundance of flavor. I don't care for beef I really only eat chicken but I was shocked at how delicious it was. Now with that being said there have been a few order mistakes over the time we have come here but they are very helpful and cooperative. One time they came and dropped off the correct item to my house. I had ordered and my roommate picked up the food and when I got it, it was incorrect. When I called they apologized and offered to drop the item off at my house I figured they would just "leave my name at the register" like many other places do. I'm pretty sure this is family owned and they are all very nice and welcoming. Go enjoy.

Great experience for some awesome bar food!  We stopped here after a night out and we all needed some greasy food and a breakfast beverage.  Javelina hit the spot!  You order at a counter and take a number to your seat.  That kitchen cranks some food out!  

I ordered the green chile pork fries.  They were amazing!  The fries were cooked perfectly and doused with queso-like cheese and that delicious pork.  The girls at my table ordered other various entrees from burgers to tacos, and everyone enjoyed their meal!  They even had a few brunch options that looked yummy.

I had a drink called "That Watermelon Drink."  It was made with vodka and watermelon juice, and was the perfect balance of fresh and sweet.  They also had a great selection of local beers on tap.  The restaurant is small, but there is outdoor seating as well.  I definitely recommend for a relaxed atmosphere on Rainey Street!

My husband and I came to Orlando for our honeymoon, because we were tired of paying so much for a small meal at the Disney parks we decided to eat off site. I had eaten at Joes in Maryland and we like seafood, so it seemed like a good idea to go to Joes. 
The experience started off a little uneasy because there was such a small crowd; we were seated immediately. The wait staff was very friendly and our drinks were promptly refilled. The food took forever to get to our table and when we started eating, it was clear they had used old oil to fry our fries and our fish. Everything was greasy and the breading wasn't crunchy. We paid over $60 for 2 fried meals that ended up making both of us sick. We won't be back to Joes.

I went to the Saturday night show with one of my Hospitality Perks and it was cute. A regular price ticket is about $64 and you get a 3-course meal with that. There is onsite parking as well, but that's for an additional $6. They recommend you arrive about 1hr prior to the show in order to get good seats since it is first come first serve.

Due to my friends arriving late we had seating in the back closet to the bar, but it seemed like they forgot about everyone there when it came to the food. I had to stop and ask a manager when we were going to be getting our salad since the area in front of us on the 1st level had not only gotten their salads, but some of them were starting on their meals already. That was aggravating, but the show was distracting us from realizing how long it really took to finally eat. I got the pork loin, shrimp, mashed potatoes and vegetables plate which was delicious and very filling. 

Some of the performers were very impressive and others were just okay. I see why they say you must be at least 13yrs old to go since there are some adult innuendos. Overall it's a different and interesting night out, but I recommend looking for a flash special or something on groupon before going. You may feel disappointed for what you experience with the regular price being paid.

This was a stop on a whim and so glad we did. It is a small location but wait is worth it. It was later in the evening so although busy, did not wait long. They do an extremely constant flow of take out. The staff is great, prices low and portions large. 
As to the food; absolutely mouth watering delicious. We had the Spring rolls, the small serving of the duck and Drunken Noodle dish with chicken. After filling out our tummy we took home doggie bags. 
Do your tastebuds a favor and stop in.

I loved my experience at Jasper's. The dessert alone is worth a trip up to the Domain.

We walked in on a Monday night just before closing during restaurant week. When I found out they were about to close, I offered to go to a neighboring restaurant that stays opens later. The manager checked with the chefs, and invited us to stay. I felt a little guilty, because I hate making people stay late at work, but they seemed more than happy to host us for dinner. Score big points on the customer service.

One of the things I really liked in regards to their Restaurant Week menu was the number of choices they had to offer. Most places will only give you one or two items to choose from, but Jasper's offered all of their top menu items. (another big star from me).

Our waiter was really nice, helpful and knowledgable. I started off with a glass of wine and a Ceasar Salad. In between the salad and entree the chef brought us a small sampling of Swordfish on goat cheese risotto. Heavenly!

Maybe it was because we were in on a slow night, but I get the impression that the chefs really take a lot of pride in their food and have fun playing around with interesting flavor combinations. We were lucky enough to be in there when they were experimenting with some dishes.

For a main course, I tried the Salmon with asparagus and marscopone polenta. I was quite pleased, but very anxious to move on the the main event: dessert!

Rocky Road Ice Cream Sandwich. To die for. Seriously. And I am quite picky about my desserts. If I am going to ingest that many calories, it needs to be well worth it. Warm chocolate cookies sandwiched together with ice cream, caramel and marshmallow creme. Wowzer!

I am an avid foodie from Phoenix, AZ, which happens to also have some of the greatest Mexican food restaurants found anywhere.  I have been spoiled.  I was happily surprised to see Latin cuisine in Vancouver, BC when I came across Polito's Latin Cafe.  It is a tidy, clean, family-owned establishment with a lot of menu options.  My first meal there was fantastic, and they also serve excellent Margaritas!  In fact, the food was so good, I hired Polito's for my recent Fiesta Party.  The catering team did a great job and the food was perfect.  Our guests loved the Menu: savory Green and Red Enchiladas, superb Salsa and spicy Mexican Rice. If you're looking for flavorful Latin cuisine, I highly recommend Polito's Cafe.  You will love it, and bring your appetite because you will not leave hungry!  :-)

This multiple award-winning restaurant is still the most amazing restaurant in the Walt Disney parks. Everything from the appetizers and flatbreads to the mains and the desserts is work-class. 

They no longer have any African chefs in the kitchen, but I understand that some of their international interns bring thoughts and flavors of Africa that keep things fresh.

You start with a cup of sweet iced mint tea that clears the palette. 

Farm-raised ostrich and boar are a no-no in the PC PETA world, so we've moved to elk and Berkshire pork, but they're done spectacularly well. The sides are not stacked mile high, so it's about the tastes of the puréed root vegetables against the wonderful meaty-salty of the elk tenderloin. 

The dessert, see photo, was a tour-de-force of textures, tastes and temperatures. 

Even the appetizer bread was wicked. I tried a South African whisky that was delicious, and their house coffee, specially made by Joffrey's was so smooth. I hear you can get it at the hotel's gift shop. 

I like to sit at the prep bar table, as you might guess if you read me a bunch. All of the staff is very friendly and enjoy putting out such great meals!

If you're a true foodie and Disney fan, and you haven't done Jiko, then this has to be your first major meal on your next visit.

ugh and ugh.  I went to see Coraline 3D and the theater hadn't been cleaned at all.  At first it was kind of funny that it was so dirty.  Then, it was like...oh, no...this is for realz.  ew.  I love my 3D movies and since this is one of the only places showing them I guess I'll be missing the next round.  It's not worth the funk.  I did take the time after the movie to thank the two disgruntled teenagers who were looking around knowing they'd have to clean it all up.  or not clean it up....whatever.
--I don't know if it's appropriate to review clientele, but man...the people next to us I swear were eating a four course meal, with their mouths open and smacking and slurping.  And what kind of parents bring three year olds to see this totally creepy weird-o film (which I find awesome and most excellent).  Some kids screamed in certain parts.  It had to be terrifying.

So, i have been wanting to try this food truck for the longest time and decided to wait on line one Friday a.m. and go for it!  The line was long and slow. However, it's just because there is like one person handling the orders and one person cooking.  It's a food cart/truck but not big.  I eventually received my order which was egg and cheese on toasted sour dough - a standard - i opted out of the meat and I was not overly impressed.  First, my bread was not toasted or warm.  I think it may have been on the grill for seconds and not minutes.  No grill marks at all. The egg was running and cooked well but the cheese not melting or warm.  I was not impressed.  AND I would of returned the whole thing and asked for a refund, but I had to go and started eating at work.  I am a NYorker and we know a good egg sandwich when we have one and this was just okay.  But it wasn't expensive and it didn't' make me sick.  I just won't be going back .

This Japanese restaurant is a HIDDEN GEM. Out of most of the sushi restaurants I have come across in Boston. It may seem as a small place outside but the food that they serve is phenomenal. Sakana approaches their sushi craftsman in a unique way and has found their way to standout as a japanese restaurant. My favourite one is the seared salmon belly. This 2 piece nigiri has a combination of sweet and salty on top of the salmon belly. Definitely the best sushi restaurant in Boston.

I have officially lost faith in the Legal's chain. Despite the 4 star rating, this may be the worst Legals in the Boston area. The service was awful. Our waitress had no idea what she was doing. She took the wrong order, forgot to bring us requested items, and was not attentive. The food was equally as bad. My chowder came out cold twice, and the food was either over cooked or way too salty. The only redeeming item were the oysters, but that's hard to mess up. 

I hate ranting but I'm really disappointed with Legals. They used to produce quality experiences, but my last few visits have been awful. Hope they make some changes here.

Great service, amazing food, I definitely hope to eat here again. I can't believe anyone would leave less than 5 stars! We went in tonight for dinner and sat in a nice big booth. The decor was lovely and our waiter Oliver was very helpful with my parents who have never experienced Thai food before. All of our food was superb. The best tom kha I've ever had, wonderful massaman curry (which isn't on the menu, but I highly suggest it!), my parents also ordered the tom yum, eggrolls, prawns in chili sauce, and pad thai. Everything is made from scratch and the chefs are from Thailand. We spoke with the owner on our way out and he was very friendly.

Had dinner at Friendly Toast last night.  It was my first visit and I will definitely be back.

The food was very good: I got the Mexican Mashed meal which was really unique and was both delicious and filling.  My friend got the burger and it was very good and he wasn't even able to finish it.

The atmosphere is great.  Sure the dolls are a little creepy and may haunt my dreams, but the place had a very cool vibe.  The bar area is the perfect size.

The service is what really set this place apart.  Our bartender was Jordan and she couldn't have been more fun and friendly.  She was extremely attentive to us and really made the night awesome.  I can't remember ever getting better service.

Can't wait for our next night out at Friendly Toast!

I ate there last week. I got the falafel plate, which included two sides. The falafel didn't strike me as especially fresh, but was fine. The humus and babaganoush (not an expert here) were cold but tasted okay. 

In summary the food was entirely edible, but nothing to go out of your way for: fresh falafel and humus (I can get cold humus cheaper from a grocery store). For the same money I could have got more food at Boloco next door.

The first time I walked into the Bowling Palace, it just about blew my mind.  Sixty-four lanes, all lined up side by side?  The small-town alleys I was used to had maybe 20 lanes at the most, so it was an impressive sight to see lanes stretched as far as the eye can see.

I'm sad that bowling has such a redneck/loser reputation, because it's really fun.  You'll run into some characters when you come here, but ignore them and focus on the game.  It can be difficult to find open bowling hours here, but it's open 24 hours, so if you're willing to stay up late, you can do a ton of bowling for a few dollars (they have all-you-can-bowl specials after 9 p.m. that get cheaper the later it gets).  I've never had any issues with the equipment here, and the lanes are kept in great condition, with regular upgrades to the scoring system.

I've also spent a lot of time at the arcade here.  Believe it or not, in 2002 the Palace was the first place in Ohio to get the newest Dance Dance Revolution machine.  I remember going there at around 2 a.m. on a Tuesday night, shortly after the DDR machine was installed, and encountering a crowd of several dozen people waiting to play.  But that was then, and just like any arcade, there are a lot of redemption games here now.  Still, there are enough good games here to keep you busy for a while.

The Palace is pretty much the only bowling alley I consider when I want to bowl, even though there are two closer to my house.

I have been going to Jessi for years.  I am very happy with her services.  My hair has never been in better shape.  I love the product she uses, her color techniques are amazing!  Above all, Jessi is an absolute sweetie!  And I love that she gives me wine and great conversation while I'm in her chair.  In addition, the salon is beautiful and in a great location in the Pearl District.  Parking is very easy!  She is certainly worth my drive!  I highly recommend Jessi!!  Thank you Jessi for pretty hair!

Great resource with wonderful staff and Good selection of animals and supplies. The best thing about the tropical hut is their staff. They are always incredibly helpful and patient in answering all my questions. I've found all the supplies I need there for competitive prices. The fish I've purchased are healthy, as are the bait food. I considered giving them a 4.5 because they are a little smaller and don't have the same selection as a huge store, but upped it to a 5 because they have done so well with their medium sized space and their customer service is outstanding.

Not vegetarian friendly. It was my first time here and I left a bit disappointed. I ordered the vegetable bean curd soup. Turns out this is chicken broth egg drop soup with tofu. It is served with no added meat, which is why they call it vegetable soup. I also ordered the vegetable dumplings. They are served as a huge order, which is nice, but they also have eggs in them, even though the menu said they have Chinese vegetables and noodles. They have veges, noodles, AND EGGS. For most readers this is no big deal, but if you can't or don't want to eat eggs, you may be out of luck at Mu Lan.

As it should be done, I am separating the Grange Audbon Nature Center from the park as they are two distinct entities. 

This is by far the loudest, most un-natural park in the metro park system and I've been to every Columbus Metro Park.  The problem is 71 runs down one side of it, 70 across another, and a train yard across a third side.  So when you're hiking the trails you're greeted by a loud cluster of urban noises which are anti the nature experience.  Plus, being a very urban park you get a lot of homeless camps and homeless people in the area who can be quite threatening.  In fact there is a big camp just north on the Scioto Bike Trail right after the retaining wall but before the train tracks up on the hill to the left.  Be careful if you go over there.

The other big thing I don't like, besides the bike trail, there isn't really any shaded hiking trails.  They are all out in the open so if you're trying to take a quick lunchtime hike without getting too sweaty don't plan on it if it's a sunny day.  It's also not a very pretty park as everything around the park looks run down or industrialized.  

It does have several good things going on for it.  The observation deck by the river has a free telescope and you can almost always spot turtles, birds, and some type of huge fish that likes to swim in the shallow waters playing in the mud.  There is also a boardwalk over a pond where you can see giant green frogs, fish, ducks, and sometimes even a turtle or two.  And of course there is the rock wall and dog park if that is your thing.

The Elbow Room is a good option to come enjoy a drink, watch the game, & eat some wings.  The wings are big & filling.  The only drawback was that they weren't made to order.  They tasted like they'd been sitting in a pan under a lamp so they were dryer than I like.  The lemon pepper & hot mix was delicious tho. The salad I ordered was crisp & filling.  The service was rushed.  The young lady told us she was the only server that day so we understood.  She had to take care of patrons both inside & out but luckily for her it wasn't a busy day.  I'm glad the weather has broken & we can sit on the patio because this establishment allows smoking on the inside.  I'm allergic to cigarette smoke & don't like to walk away smelling like an ashtray.  Still not a bad place to get some food & a beer!

Synchrony is quite good --  at offering bill paying customers exquisite BS.  Not your average poor customer service, the I don't speak understandable English foolishness but ridiculous explanations for their questionable procedures in perfect English.  They will even call you from their corporate offices and tell you the same horrible explanations that the call center provided hours earlier.  Would like to give this company zero stars, so they get only one out of me.  I paid my bill in total.  But my account is on hold for 5 days.  Synchrony explained that they had concerns of bank fraud, concerns my bank might take the money back although the payment was authorized, and my personal favorite -- that a $25.00 payment is a lot of money.

We needed a new mattress, and I wasn't sure where to go. First I looked at Costco--what don't they sell there? But they were too high end and pricey. Next, the Sears outlet, which was ok but nothing special. I thought about Brooklyn Bedding online because I like that they make their own beds. Then I went to Parklane right here in Portland. Very nice mattresses and showroom. Every mattress I liked there was closer to $2k, and that gave me pause. Finally I went to Mattress Lot, based on all the great reviews here. 

I am now sleeping on a fantastic mattress that is a wrapped coil and latex hybrid. The salesperson who helped was just the right combo of helpful and hands off. I got an excellent price. The mattress was made in the northwest. It's organic cotton on top! And it was delivered promptly. They charged $45 for delivery, FYI. God I do love this mattress. Time for a nap!

I love Bartaco! I enjoy their food, service and ambiance and I like that most of their food is gluten-free.  They have both, indoor and outdoor seating.  Well behaved dogs are allowed in the outdoor seating area.  To place an order, you fill out a paper slip (like at sushi restaurants).  To get wait staff attention, you put up a rectangular card on a special cardholder on your table.  Sometimes, after your meal, you will get a card asking you to rate your experience at the restaurant that day. You get a token for a free taco for the next visit if you fill out and turn in the card.

As the name implies, Bartaco serves tacos.  Tacos are priced a la carte and are served family style. You can order them in a soft corn tortilla or on a lettuce leaf.  Baja Fish tacos are my favorite :) I also enjoy portobello, roasted duck and crispy rock shrimp tacos. I am not a big fan of chicken pastor or cauliflower tacos. 

Bartaco serves other food besides tacos.  I am partial to their chicken soup. They have also recently revamped their menu to include duck quesadilla (and a few other things).  I tried duck quesadilla and thought it was heavenly, but it was pricey for its size. It is sized more like a large taco than a quesadilla :(

I really like their corn with cotija cheese. Normally, corn is served on the cob, but I always ask them to take it off the cob. I even ask them to take corn off the cob in my chicken soup. ;)

Chipotle slaw - you're gonna love it or hate it. Personally, I hated it as a side.  However, I have learned that chipotle slaw is put on my favorite taco - baja fish. Go figure!

Plantains - yum! I forget what they are served with, but it is some sauce that complements the sweetness of plantains perfectly. 

Spiced chocolate pudding.  At first, I was hesitant to try this dessert because I was told that it was "spicy." I think it may have a little bit of cayenne pepper in it.  Now, I order this dessert almost every time I go to Bartaco because it is delicious!  If you are not a fan of chocolate, then try their gelato. I have eaten their coconut gelato twice and it was yummy!

As far as beverages are concerned, I have a couple of favorites. Nonalcoholic drink - pomegranate limonada. Alcoholic beverage - sangria. Also, if you order iced tea, they bring you a carafe, so you can technically order one iced tea and split it between 2 people, but only get charged for one iced tea.

Bartaco rocks!!!

Let's start with the food: ordered the California burger medium. Presentation was good. It's a very photo friendly burger. Cooked slightly over medium but still good. And I love shoestring fries. So if there was a separate review for food I'd give it 4 stars.
Service: when we walked in no one was at the hostess stand. It was 2pm and no one was around? After waiting a few minutes someone came to seat us. When asked if inside, bar or outside, we chose inside. The hostess then said it'll be a 10-15 min wait. Looking around I saw the dining room 1/2 empty. Hmmmmm why the wait. So we opted for the bar. Still saw the dining room 1/2 empty when we left.
Bartender was pleasant. Food came out hot and tasty. Menu is a mix of everything from sushi to burgers to salmon. A little confused by that. Haven't decided if I'll go back.

In the beginning of the movie "Fargo," all you see is the white of winter and in the distance are headlights. The car is slowly coming at you and there's this uneasy feeling of sorts, but not necessarily a bad one. You don't know what's going to happen when that car gets to you, but you can't help but watch and wait to find out what's coming. What happens when the car gets there? A really great movie, that's what. Turning onto East 6th, it feels like the street gets narrower. At night, it's pretty dark and I'd never quite gone this far. This is where that slight uneasy feeling entered. I found myself surveying the neighborhood passing by and not knowing what would happen when I got to what looked like a dead end. What happened? I had a really great meal at Mettle. 

We had the escargot to start, which was a wise decision. They come in a savory chipotle-kaffir lime butter sauce and it's plated with grilled baguette slices. They're very tender and the dish is perfect for two people to share. For the entrée, my long neglected need for a really good burger was finally satiated. I have to say, I really appreciated that they didn't need to do anything terribly complex with it. They are working with really great ingredients and didn't have to dress it up to create some fancy gourmet, bells-and-whistles burger. It's simple and really tastes great. Hats off to the kitchen for sending me a perfectly medium rare burger! Too many times have I been burned by something coming out medium to medium well, which I don't find enough of a crime to send back. I ended up deconstructing my burger as I went on so as to experience the patty sans bread/toppings/etc and it really was great meat. Over the course of the evening, I observed several other dishes making their way to other tables and each of them looked just as great as what I was eating, so there is much to try here. 

The service was great from start to finish. The bar area is very open and has this wicker structure in the center that is really striking. In the other dining area, there's a large, modern chandelier over one of the tables that's rather pretty. The interior has this industrial-chic feel that really works for the location. And if that's not enough, they have a really great patio. I seriously cannot wait for warm weather to come back to us. Where I was sitting in the restaurant had a good view of the neighborhood and the area and sitting outside on that patio just seems like it'd be conducive to a really great time. They have happy hour from Tuesday to Saturday from 3pm-7pm and I'll be damned if I don't intend on spending a good number of happy hours on that patio indulging in conversation and the $5 bar snack/appetizer menu. We all have our "we're going back there" places, but this is definitely cutting the line on my personal list.

NOTE: AVOID PACIFIC SOURCE AT ALL COSTS!!! THOSE 5 STAR REVIEWS ARE FAKE!

I was denied coverage for no reason. I have suffered from insomnia and other sleep issues for the better part of a decade. I go through most days with very low energy and struggling to concentrate. I have tried all kinds of alternative treatments but nothing really seemed to work. My girlfriend told me that it sounds like I am holding my breath and choking throughout the night and suggested that I get a sleep study done. 

Though it took Pacific Source forever (over a month) to approve the sleep study I finally completed it. The results found that I have sleep apnea. My doctor, a respected pulmonologist here in Central Oregon, told me that while I was low on the scale due a strong lung capacity from athletic training but that I do indeed have sleep apnea. Finally a tangible problem!

I was relieved. After researching sleep apnea and its symptoms I was so excited to know that I might be on my way to sleeping well again. While I wasn't overjoyed with having to connect to a CPAP machine every night, if it meant I got to feel human for a day, I was all for it. 

After two weeks passed and I heard nothing in regards to when to pick up the CPAP machine I contacted Pacific Source only to find out that my claim had been denied. According to Pacific Source, my sleep apnea was "not severe enough to warrant treatment" (a direct contradiction to what my doctor told me). 

Not only did they deny my valid medical claim but they failed to notify me of this action which means I was much later than I could have been in starting my appeal process which takes upwards of 30 days. But hey what's another month without sleep...right?

I have since talked to my doctor, the manufacturer of the CPAP machine and done some other research both on and offline and it turns out this is a very common practice for Pacific Source THEY DO NOT CARE ABOUT YOUR QUALITY OF CARE!!! They would rather you stay sick so long as it doesn't cost them anything.  

AVOID PACIFIC SOURCE LIKE THE PLAGUE BUT AVOID THE PLAGUE EVEN MORE IF YOU'RE UNFORTUNATE ENOUGH TO HAVE PACIFIC SOURCE AS YOUR INSURER! IT WON'T BE A SEVERE ENOUGH CASE OF THE PLAGUE TO BE TREATED AND GOOD LUCK LASTING THE 30+ DAYS FOR AN APPEAL DECISION! YOU HAVE BEEN WARNED!!!

Today I had my second amazing experience at Market. I had gone for the first time a few months back and was impressed by just about every aspect of my visit. From the minute you step foot inside and glance over at the lobby bar, the creative decor is intriguing and captivating. The restaurant follows suit with its modern, yet inviting atmosphere. 

I had a tomato and basil pizza as my appetizer. The crust was thin and crispy, the mozzarella fresh and thinly sliced, and the tomato and basil were in perfect proportion. For my entree, I had salmon with a mouth-watering warmed German-style potato salad and crisp snap peas. For dessert I chose the cookie platter, which included everything from a very rich double chocolate cookie to caramels to macaroons. All courses were prepared with fine attention to detail and exceeded expectations. 

Anyone looking for a great fine dining experience with interesting, carefully prepared dishes in a hip, exciting environment should definitely be pleased with a meal at Market.

No, this is not the best Thai food in the U.S., but it does get consistent high marks for being delicious.  I eat here regularly.  Seating and service are prompt and friendly.  This is not a 4 or 5 star restaurant, but it certainly worth going too on a frequent basis because the food it hot and delicious.  Most of the meals are not too spicy, but I love the one's that make my eyes water!  I highly recommend you try Sap's!

Horrible customer service, every time I go in am never acknowledged when I walk into the store, nor while I am shopping, the girl working inside past by me, also was rearranging shelves next to me and never said one word to me... I also feel like she was inappropriately dressed. I asked her a question and she simply pointed at the sign that I had a question about. I like this location, but do not enjoy my experience, it's a cold uncomfortable environment every time I visit... When I go next door to Bath Body Works it's a comfortable, friendly experience always! Yall need to take you're team through some serious customer etiquette training....

Firefly provided me great service.  I called them a few days before my wedding (after my initial alcohol plan fell through and I was in a bit of a panic), and they were wonderful and helped me build a well stocked bar.  They even provided delivery, which was amazing because it saved us the bother of lugging around a bunch of alcohol the day of our wedding or having to ask friends to transport alcohol for us. 

They have a great selection of wines, beers and liquor.  They provided some really great recommendations of local products that our guests loved.  Would recommend them to help stock a bar for a party, or to just pick up a few bottles for yourself. 

Thanks Leanne and team!

Fat G. coming in with a review of a place you might have seen in Chinatown but probably not dared to try. Wai Style Restaurant, located across from Apollo and Ding Ho Fast Food, is owned by the same folks who run Wai Wai Restaurant (http://www.yelp.com/biz/wai-wai-restaurant-boston) on Oxford St. Having been to Wai Wai and knowing their quality of food, I tried this place as well.

Enter the inside and there are a couple of small tables in the back and the side. On the right is where you can order cuts of meat to go and pay your bill. From what i understand, the menu selection is the same as Wai Wai restaurant. I ended up ordering a combination rice plate with duck and bbq pork for around $7. The duck portion was mostly bone and the pork was dried out. Also there was this fan that kept blowing back and forth amongst the tables, making it very hard to eat comfortably. 

Service was ok, and so was cleanliness. This place is alright if you need a bite to eat and can't wait, but there are better options in the Chinatown area.

Garlic Parmesan Wings Wet & House fried rice with everything in it & then  large drink no ice ( LEMONADE, PEACH AND FRUIT PUNCH MIXED TOGETHER!!!)  I get the same exact thing every time. It's soooo good I'm trying hard not to curse. Call it in and every time they going to say ready in 10 minutes lol. Don't forget to ask for extra yum yum sauce and blue cheese for the wings! I think I'm about to call right now and have this for dinner. I swear I want to try something different but I'm afraid to pick anything else because I might not get the same taste .... The one time I tried mild wings with lemon pepper sprinkle and it was just okay so I ended up walking back in for my garlic Parmesan wet wings. Since then I just stick to what I know.

The area seems to have some nice views, and it is close to the City.  But that is about all I can say for it.  The trails are very poorly marked, if at all.  Some paths are paved for no reason.  There are work trucks driving around frequently near the reservoir, which seem to disturb and scare away any wildlife.  There are dogs everywhere and all of them are off their leash in clear violation of the park rules.  And the paths seem to be dirty and littered.

There are better hikes in the area.  Try Blue Hills, or take a trip outside the city and check out the Audubon Ipswich  Preserve in Topsfield.

O. M. G.  I have laughed at the whole national affair with cupcakes that has occurred in recent years. Having tasted a few from specialty shops at social functions, I was always left with an "eh...it's a cupcake. Big whoop" thought. Until tonight. Wanting to truly have an Austin experience, I decided to give Hey Cupcake's coco loco cupcake a shot. I was totally unprepared for the sublime coconut explosion in my mouth. This wasn't just a cupcake, it was a CUPCAKE!  The best cupcake I have ever eaten. EVER.  Worth every bit of the $3 I spent (and the $1 tip for the great service and cute to go container). This place (and this cupcake) are not to be missed. Seriously, it is worth going well out of your way for...yes, got a flipping cupcake. You won't be sorry.

Best piercing experience ever! My sister and I both got our noses pierced last week and we do not regret it at all! Kellen and the 2 women working the front desk (who's names escaped me, sorry) were very professional, kind and made us feel super comfortable. They are very clean, and made sure to show me every thing was sterilized and safe to use. I've heard lots of horror stories, so cleanliness was EXTREMELY important for me. He made sure the piercing would be lined up perfectly & made the piercing quick and easy. Piercings are healing just fine. Haven't had any problems at all. I'm so glad a friend told me about them! I will be coming here for all future piercings. 100% recommend!!

I love Kung Fu Tea! If I lived north I would be here ALL THE TIME! Since I don't live nearby when I'm in the area this is a must stop. Today I tried the Mango slushee with bubbles and popping grape bubbles.... it was soooo gooood! I love tapioca. The popping bubbles are so fun too and a nice little surprise as you sip your drink. I love that you can choose your sweetness level and everything is completely customizable. I always get the least amount of sweetness because I never need extra sugar. The staff here is always super nice and helpful too. Don't be afraid to ask them questions or for suggestions. If you are looking for a boba tea drink this the spot for sure! My one request is to open a south Austin location... please!

Stay away. This place is horrible. People in the management office are dumba$$, unprofessional and not helpful at all. Yes, it is dog friendly but you are basically living in a zoo. There are over 50 dogs living in this place and it smells. Yes, they have a donation drop box kinda thing in the building but people treat it like a dumpster - clothes, shoes, furniture etc all over the floor. The maintenance folks are nice but other than that do yourself a favor and STAY AWAY.
Lastly, do you know why there are still so many positive reviews there? They give their residents a "chance" to win $50 amazon gift cards for posting good reviews on social media. Pathetic. smh

With a trip to Paris in the planning stages I was anticipating my first visit to Les Faux Bourgeois with special excitement.  So too were many of my fellow Vancouverites it seems, as there were absolutely no tables available when we first attempted to visit!  We returned a week later, with a quite necessary reservation and I'm happy to report that the wait was well worth it.

Though the packed restaurant felt a little claustrophobic, the service was prompt, polite and appropriately accented.  Our Escargots De Bourgogne starter (surprisingly my first experience with snails) was salty and delicious.  The Filet de Boeuf Grille was nothing short of a revelation, quite possibly the most delicious steak I have ever tasted.  
  
YUM!

Bring on Paris!

I went for a movie screening earlier today and first off, the hallway leading to the movie room was so dirty and there was popcorn everywhere, I even stepped on a chicken nugget on the floor. the movie room was also so dirty and I felt disgusted just sitting there. So I'm thinking I'll forget about it when the movie starts, however for some odd reason, the movie started with all the lights on. In addition, many people were still scrambling looking for seats, it seemed like there were none left - why would the attendants let the people in if there's no seats? the rest of the movie was good but I'm glad this film was free, I'd never pay to go see a movie here. I wish I could give it less than one star.

We love endeavor! It's a great to have in Grandview and in walking distance for neighbors! The space inside is industrial and great for a gathering or a trivia night. The tables are picnic style.
There's a lot of things on the menu here that I like, depends on the season but they're friendly about sampling if you really can't decide! There's usually a food truck outside so I believe that's the only food option at the moment. There's TVs at the bar too, so you can catch a game or Bob Ross whichever suits you!

*Edit* Please read full review after this paragraph! I was contacted by a san marin employee who had helped us while we lived there. she asked that I more clearly state my specific experience with the staff. As I say in the last paragraph, the staff was awesome, and she actually helped us by letting us break our lease without penalty. Again, it's unfortunate that the staff is so awesome at an apartment complex plagued by noise problems. *Edit*

I reviewed this place a month ago with a promise to give a more accurate review after I lived here for a month. Well, I'm reducing my review of this place down to one star because living in San Marin II is a horrible experience. The main problem is the train tracks nearby. 

The train comes mostly at night, and especially on weekend nights, making it impossible to get a good nights rest. There have been Saturday or Sunday nights when the train literally comes 10-15 times between the hours of four am and ten am. I have lived near train tracks before, and actually found the low rumble of the trains to be pleasant. So when we were looking at these apartments, the rental lady casually asked us "do you like the sound of trains?" I fondly remembered my old house in Sacramento, where the distant sound of trains actually HELPED me to sleep.

However, what she failed to tell us, or even imply, is that the "sound" of trains, are air horns blasting so loud that you literally can't hear yourself talk. furthermore, the jerk-off conductors that drive the trains obviously think it's fun to hold the horn down for a good two minutes straight, blasting it over and over and over and over as they slowly cross the street. apparently two short blasts isn't enough to warn drivers that a train is coming. the whole thing is exacerbated by the fact that the horn echoes in the apartment complex and amplifies the noise. it is LITERALLY impossible to sleep.

I've tried blocking the windows in our bedroom with sound padding and thick blankets to reduce the noise, but my wife and I can't sleep, period. My eyelid has been twitching for two weeks now due to lack of sleep. We can't WAIT to move out of here.

My advice is that if you HAVE to move into this place, then move into San Marin 1 where the apartments are much farther from the tracks. However, be warned that there is dog crap literally everywhere and no one cleans this place, ever. The staff is friendly, attentive, and the apartments are actually reasonably priced and look nice inside, so it's unfortunate that I have to give it a one star review. But you come home to sleep and relax, and that is literally impossible at San Marin II.

Meh is all I have to say. I can get cooler stuff and have a way better time doing it at hippo hardware. Not one sales person even bothered to say hello to us, and only did they come out of hiding when the more well to do looking customers approached the order picking counter. The lady that rang us up was very friendly, but all the staring from customers AND employees was a bit uncalled for. There are way weirder looking people in town, and sideways glancing is just rude. All I needed were some hooks and cord. Think I'll go somewhere else next time, where an old rusty metal tin doesn't cost $15.

I love this zoo. The fact that it is not too big and can be seen in under two hours is a plus in my mind. Especially in the summer. Plus they have a lot of what my zoologist friend calls "charismatic megafauna" or something like that. In other words, cute animals. There always seem to be baby animals around -- baby gorillas, baby kangaroos, I saw the baby panda. Lion, tiger, zebras etc. Just about any animal you would expect to see and you can get a good look. They're not on some island far away like the Miami Metrozoo.  The kids I have taken have loved it too. It's a bit pricey but you can often find a deal on groupon or another site. Also, there is one free family pass per library.

So I stopped in thinking the reviews might be wildly bogus... The Yelp reviews are mildly bogus. There is nothing special going on here except this guy having friends and family willing to write great Yelp reviews for him. I ended up not leaving my watch for repairs here with plans to send it to a factory authorized repair station.
I live so close and wanted the ease of using someone nearby but after reading the reviews and stopping in... The reviews are just bogus. I would not trust this shop with a watch of grand value.

I see the negative reviews, but that was absolutely not my experience. I took my daughter's tea length wedding dress and my mother of the bride dress to Parkcrest and was totally pleased with the price and the results. They are a bit old school in their ticketing process and not accepting credit cards, but that didn't bother me at all. I wanted someone I could trust. I am using them again to clean the same wedding dress so we can donate it to a military bride. I recommend Parkcrest.

I made our reservation with Michelle M on July 22 for a pick up on August 7 from Orlando International Airport to Courtyard Hotel in Cocoa Beach and another Pick up the next day on August 8th from Courtyard Hotel to Port Canaveral for $280. 

I keep them updated when we landed and while we were picking up our luggage. They directed us to wait at green sign B26. Their dispatch, Richard, Mike kept telling me that they are 15 minutes away.....that many lies kept us waited for 1:38 minutes outside of the airport. The next day, I was nervous and call them at 9am to confirm the 11:00am pick up for our departure. They told us to wait outside of the hotel at 10:30am. We had waited their for another 1:24 minute.  We were forced to call a taxi to take us to Port Canaveral. We paid in full in advance but we did not receive their full service and had an extremely horrible experience with this company. They are rude and lied. They were recommended to me by The Courtyard Hotel in Cocoa Beach.

We came in a large group and we were very disappointed with the service.  

First of all, our food took a very long time to come, and there were no updates nor apologizes throughout the meal.  We were just left sitting there, wondering where our food was.  Half of our party, seated at the table beside us, received their food much earlier than we did.  Our food actually came after they completely finished their meal, making it extremely awkward for half of us.  The lunch ended up being way too long since it was split up so strangely and we stayed at the restaurant for nearly 2 hours!

Anyways, the food was fairly good but the service was just agonizingly slow.  Our waitress was quite indifferent about her job and she constantly ignored us.  I'm not sure if she was just oblivious to her surroundings, but my colleague tried to get her attention several times and she would just walk right past him, ignoring his very existence.  Perhaps she was having a bad day?

Okay back to the food.  The duck confit was fairly good and I enjoyed the fresh bed of greens underneath with the fingerling potatoes but honestly, it wasn't anything special.  The fries were done pretty well and we enjoyed how they provided both mayonnaise and ketchup.  The majority of the table ordered their "famous" rib-eye steak and the opinions were: o-kay, average, good, and mmmm.  

The bistro was surprisingly full for a Tuesday, considering their pricey menu (I think including appies/desserts we spent approximately $40 a person).  The dessert (melting chocolate cake) was quite good though!

I had the opportunity to eat at East Coast Wings for dinner yesterday. I must say after reading some of the reviews im baffled. I had the fried pickles with lava ranch for an appetizer and it was delicious. Seasoned just right and a side salad.  For dinner I had the cajun garlic wings and they were good. Fried not to hard or not to soft. I had a margarita and a cosmo and the bartender was not skimpy on the alcohol. My server Jenny was very pleasant and checked on our table throughout our time there. I definitely plan on visiting again the next time im in Orlando. Btw: my wings were regular size  not skimpy at all

My mouth is still watering after eating here a week ago. I ordered a frozen pisco punch and the Churrasco. The meat was so tender, cooked perfectly, and tooped with fresh chimichurri. We were sat outside, which was a terrible option for a large party (because they do not have tables to accommodate large parties. They put two circular tables together which seperated us into two tables lol) bit they had plenty of misters to help overcome the heat. I would recommend sitting inside for a better ambiance.

We are on vacation from TN so we don't get fresh seafood very often. Our food was very good, some over seasoning in the sale dressing but not too bad. The crab legs were wonderful. But the best part of the evening was our server Andy. He was amazing. He went out of his way to ensure we had everything we wanted and needed all the while dealing with another table that could be listed as "the most annoying table in the universe" right beside us. They "knew everything" about the menu already, but asked him 20,000 questions about anyway including grilling him about the Jack Daniels on the menu. He was extremely professional the entire time and kept a smile on his face as well. I think we tipped him for our table and that one because we couldn't see them leaving him that good if a tip. But hope we are wrong. Either way, we were extremely impressed by our server and we hope he received the recognition he deserves. Thanks so much for a wonderful dinner Fish Bones and Andy!

Went here on a Saturday night, ready to use a Belly offer for either a free thai taco + egg roll or the free thai iced tea + egg roll. I found the place and when I got to the counter, the man/cook told they wouldn't accept the belly offer because they didn't have internet. 

What? Why are you still offering belly cards at your window then?

I was already here so I still ordered some dinner  (a Pad Thai, Thai Tacos, and 2 Thai Teas). When our order was ready, we found out he hadn't charged us for our teas and had to do another transaction -even though I had said 3 times that, yes, we would like to order drinks too.  

Pad Thai - Not good. I don't like my food too spicy and this wasn't spicy at all -but it didn't even have a good flavor. Tastes like they use a lot of fish sauce.

Thai Tacos - Spicy -don't expect anything crazy filling by ordering these though

Thai Tea - The only thing I can actually compliment this place on. Perfectly sweet and a good size considering the price (2.50 each)

The parking here is also really bad. Park somewhere else (such as Dominican Joes/Free Birds across the street) and take a small stroll to prevent backing out of here. This place is literally less than 5 feet from a 4-way intersection that you have to back out into.

Don't come here -there are better food trucks within a mile of this place for sure.

Awesome location, tasty food, friendly service. This is the closest Chick-fil-A to me, and I'm so glad it is.

I go to the drive-thru and it being 9:20PM on a Saturday night, they ran out of spicy chicken sandwiches. They informed me that it's a 5 minute wait and offered something in the meantime. The young man was apologetic and extremely friendly and did his best to serve me at that short moment despite the 6+ cars behind me. I didn't want anything extra but I parked my car in a reserved spot, and waited.

About five minutes later and a nice young woman comes up to my car and apologizes profusely and comes to me with fresh food and a coupon for a free meal for the next time.

You don't get it any better than that. I had no problem waiting, especially since they were apologetic and attempted to resolve the situation in a quick, efficient matter, and that's something extremely rare in the fast-food world. When something is wrong in a different fast food restaurant, they don't care that you wait and usually don't apologize, but this particular Chick-fil-A does (and likely other branches) and they do it with a genuine smile. Will return.

I went in looking to get a cheap wash and chop for a hair donation and ended up paying $40!

I asked for the $18 wash and cut, then switched to the $28 wash, protein treatment, cut, and dry. Lady charged me an extra $7 for an additional protein treatment I NEVER ASKED FOR. I was trying to have a nice, budgeted honeymoon out of Alaska, and she was stealing money from me. After the extra treatment is over, she finally tells me my new total of  $35, and when she's done with my hair, she's done a complete hack job! Don't go here. They give you extra hair treatments before asking you and then demand you pay for it and then do a terrible job even cutting your hair. Had to go to a local Alaskan hair cut place to finally get my hair done right a month later. 

TL;DR:  They'll steal your money and make it look like a 3 year old with scissors got a hold of your hair. Go to JB Haircutters here in Anchorage and ask for Chong because she's incredible!

Went there for brunch. It was a beautiful day and the patio looked very nice. 

Unfortunately there was no room so we ate inside which was still very pleasant. I liked the menu especially the brunch special, affordable fare for $9 I think (starter, main course).

Bloody Mary was bloody spicy but bloody good.

Service was abysmal though. Didn't asked what kind of water we wanted, didn't bring coffee refills, didn't seem to want to get our order or check on us often. Still the food was great.

We have dined here a handful of times and have yet to find a dish that we haven't loved! You can always expect a high end meal for a very reasonable price a long with a great glass of wine or creative cocktail. I can't say enough good things about this place. Once you enter the restaurant you forget that you are in a business/strip mall in Lewis Center. Totally worth checking out- and if there is a wait when you arrive- it's completely worth waiting for an opportunity to dine here!

I stop by these new food carts to try out this new spot. The lady running the food cart was super friendly. I placed my order, they were out of what I wanted but she was able to make something that sounded  delicious. I waited five minutes then picked up my food. Drove about four minutes home and took my first bite in. The most disgusting food I've ever eaten in my life. The biggest waste of $10 and I regret tipping her. I tossed it all down my garbage disposal. I thought about giving it to my dog but I didn't want to downgrade him from his normal dinner.

Whatever cheese sauce they've tried to create made me want to vomit. The chicken I had added to my meal for three dollars was ice cold. It honestly smelled terrible as well.
