I'd advise anyone to just go by Velveeta and chicken nuggets if they want to replicate what she cooks here. You're way better off doing it on your own. I spent five minutes searching for a phone number. Now I understand why they probably don't have one available online.

I would have had a more enjoyable experience if the table we were seated at in the back wasn't infested with fruit flies of some kind. They might have been coming from one of the vent above our heads that was coated in what I hope was dust, but they were everywhere.

Other than that, the experience was just meh. The food was alright, but nothing special. The half-price food deal was nice, but you needed to buy at least $3 in drinks and none of the non-alcoholic drinks were above $2.75, and I wasn't in the mood for alcohol in the afternoon when we went. They also don't serve you water or refill your glass unless you ask for it, which is smart from a green perspective, but when your waitress doesn't come around too often it is a tad annoying.

I can't say enough good things about this place!! The food was great, drinks were fantastic and the service was top notch! We ordered the Queso Verde appetizer and split the Pasta Del Mar. Now I know you're thinking that this sounds like Italian food but the flavors were so unique but had that Mexican flare. The bartender Steven made us his own special concoction the "Anejo Ball" or as I called it, "The Steve-tini" and it was great! Sweet and spicy! I loved his originality and passion for his craft. This is my go-to place in Round Rock from now on!

I've been here twice now and both times it was around the holidays when there was a Lego exhibit. 

Four years ago when I went, the Lego exhibit was huge. It took up at least 4-5 rooms. This year it was pretty small and was only in one room. The model of Columbus was cool, but I expected more based on the last time I was there. 

The rest of the museum is just ok to me. There are only a couple of rooms that have anything impression/modern. It's a pretty small museum so it's easy to see it all without spending much time there. 

I probably won't be back again unless there's a special exhibit I'm interested in.

Hospitality was great and large portions pushed this out of being a one star rating.    Well that and the free soft cone ice cream.  It seemed more of a soft opening as half the menu was unavailable.

The queso flameado was really just queso with veggies.   My food was very salty, especially the tamale. If it weren't for the saltiness, it would have been pretty bland.  My wife's tacos were also very salty.

I ordered a taco for my son from the kid's menu.  Note to people with a kid's menu: don't put pepper in the food. Their brand new taste buds are just too sensitive. He was a good sport and ate a few bites but just couldn't do it.

It's hard to justify the price with the food being less than mediocre. I can see why it's a little pricey with the portions though. We spent $42 for two adults and a child. I would rather spend that kind of money and get some good wings or bbq.

This place used to be called Badayori, was dying a slow death (I'd have given it 2 stars), so I was pleasantly surprised by the much better food quality and selections this newest incarnation has to offer.  

The nigiris are pretty fresh and taste great for a buffet.  Aside from a few clams that you don't often see (cockle, whelk), the big attraction has to be the presence of uni.  I suppose they do charge enough money to offer all you can eat uni--and it's good quality.  I think the same kind that comes in a whole box that most restaurants use.  I must have had about 12 of these altogether, yum.  

There's a small robata section, from which my favorites items were the ribeye and calamari.   There's a tiny soup section that also serves udon (the noodle is cooked as you order), it was just decent.  From the cold food section I enjoyed  a variety of marinated fish, shellfish.  There's a whole plate of mackerel, great.  I also had about 2 dozens of raw oysters, again pretty fresh.  Unfortunately there's no king crab or lobster, just snow crab and it's not that great quality.

To round out the offering there's a couple of dim sum choices in the hot  food section, tempura, and stuffed shellfish.  Not many dishes worth eating there.  The shrimp shumai wasn't bad though.  Overall this buffet as far as cold food and sushi is concerned is better than all the other buffets in Atlanta I've been to.  I would be willing to pay $10 more to have king crab and/or lobster on offer as well.

Advice...for best selection, go for weekend dinner.  My many buffet eating experiences have taught me that the difference between a weekday lunch and a weekend dinner can be significant.

I love this Bar!, This is my home bar. Not only is the staff great and pay attention to every detail but they treat as if you were old friends.  Its great to people watch on a weekend night as you never know what you're going to get. On weeknights, its the perfect dive bar to meet up with friends and grab some food. I highly reccemnned the Macho Nachos. Be sure to have some one to share with as this is a plate for 2 or even 3 people.

NOT worth the money by far!

Went here with a group of friends for dinner one night, and while the place is pretty nice looking, the food and service were TERRIBLE!  Our server was more interested in gawking at a group of ladies and tending to them, rather than taking our orders.  When we did get our food, the order was wrong, and he basically just blew us off.

I was not impressed by any of it, and neither were our friends.

I had an appointment with Dr. Stulting today and it was the first and last time I'll see him as a patient. I made the appointment based on a referral from my optometrist -- I'll be asking for another. 

Two people walked into the room and neither knew my name. Dr. Stulting quickly said his name and started looking into my eyes. He commented that my pupils hadn't been dilated long enough and asked how long ago had they been. I declined dilation and the lab tech noted it on the chart -- a chart that Dr. Stulting apparently didn't bother to look at. 

I took it upon myself to ask who the other person was in the room. He was an observing student. I admit, I figured as much. I've had interns and students observe me as well. When they do, I make certain to introduce them and ask if anyone objects to their presence. As professionals we're used to things that not everyone experiences regularly. Lawyers are comfortable in courtrooms, certainly more so than the person that has one speeding ticket. Real estate agents buy and sell more houses in 3 months than I will in my lifetime. That shouldn't mean you gloss over the process, it means you take care with people that are probably less knowledgeable than you and don't assume everything is copacetic. Obviously students need to learn and I didn't mind his presence; I did mind the lack of acknowledgment and the presumption there is no choice in the matter. 

After this point, another person entered to give me paperwork, which I sat aside as I had removed my contacts and couldn't read. Apparently, this was uncouth in Dr. Stulting's eyes as "the paperwork would be more useful at home." I told him I'd take it home, but as I couldn't read it I didn't need to hold it. He spent the next several seconds filling out paperwork, reminding me to read the papers, seeming very excited about a experimental treatment, and asking me three times if I had any questions, apparently not satisfied when I said no either of the first two times I answered. 

When it was time to leave, I was walked to the front desk to "check out." I asked to put my contacts back in first, was directed to check out first, to which I responded, "I cannot see," for the second time. To people that have seen my eye chart and should know just how much I cannot see. My contacts are -7.0 in one eye, -8.0 in the other for reference. I go to the public restroom, replace my contacts, and return to the desk to find the woman with my chart has disappeared. I'm told I'm all set and can go. 

The follow up appointment the doctor wanted was never scheduled, but that's quite all right because I'll never see him as a doctor again. I consider my optometrist a quality professional; the only cause I've ever had to question anything he's said or done was making a referral to Dr. Stulting.

Friendly staff: they greet you upon entering the store, they greet you and ask if you need help when passing through the aisles, and they offer to call and find your size at local stores if they scour and see they don't actually have it--before you even ask them to.

Store itself: well stocked, purses/accessories well organized, but the shoes people try on and leave laying about could get restocked a little faster (especially if I am reviewing that after visiting the store on a Monday afternoon, not super busy time)

Bathrooms: spacious and handicap friendly but a little creepy... dimly lit and flickering... please fix the light bulbs in there so we don't feel like we just walked onto the set of scary movie

DSW prices: not sure if each store gets to run different promotions, or if there's a difference between regional stores, and online... there must be. Plenty stocked clearance section, I actually found the perfect shoe my husband was looking for in his size which never happens with clearance stragglers. But, since the online promos are not applicable in stores, I wish the cashiers wouldn't hand you flyers about those discounts because if I just spent money in the store, the chances are unlike I'm going to log onto your webpage and buy more... so now you're just making me feel bad like I wish I could've saved money and shopped online... better left unsaid.

I used to love Khow Thai unequivocally, but they've cut some corners and some dishes are just terrible now.  I still love the Pad Kee Mow and Pad See You, which are consistently excellent and super-hot.  I had the green papaya salad the other day, but they seem to be using some canned lime juice that has a nasty, soft-drink-lime flavor.  I couldn't eat it.  Similarly, I tried the Sticky Rice Jay for dinner, and it was just terrible.  First, it was just overcooked white rice, not sticky rice at all.  Second, it tasted like almond flavoring. 

I think if you stick to the noodles and curries it is good.

They may have changed Disney Springs but the World of Disney will stay unchanged. 

The reason for my 5 yelp stars, the store really has everything in one visit. You can visit other stores throughout your stay, make a mental note and then come to World of Disney for comparison.

There are so many different sections: Kids, Mens, Womans, Star Wars, Games, Cookware, I can't even count all of the sections. Last year it was chilly so I bought a really cool, chunky gray Mickey sweatshirt. My sons are so jelly! haha

This year we had tickets to the Very Merry Christmas Party and I wanted a whole ensemble, I want to be the Christmas fun dad! I picture myself in a Mickey shirt, with Mickey wearing a santa hat!! Bring me there World of Disney! I found the best shirt, I'm so in the zone. I was going to buy a santa hat but then I remembered I bought one a few years ago and that sucka sits on my closet shelf. So pass on the hat. :(

Cookware is my favorite section. There are cookbooks, glasses, plates and platters all with Mickey themes. I bought a breakfast glass set with all of the older Disney rides on the glasses. I love Sunday breakfast with my Disney glasses. Just how I roll in my humble abode. 

It really is a "World of Disney"

I was in the market for a suit for my cousins wedding and a friend recommended Milanos. I'm extremely picky with clothing but they were able to help me find exactly what I was looking for! The staff is very friendly and welcoming and were very helpful with assisting me in putting my outfit together. They had everything I needed including somebody to make the alterations. Don't hesitate to stop here, they will help you find the perfect outfit for your event/outing!

I went to Byblos this afternoon for a work lunch. I was surprised with how much space they have here. The service is a somewhat leisurely pace so keep that in mind if you're on a tight schedule. I got the baba ganoush to start. It was a delicious smokey flavor! Then the lunch falafel combo plate. I couldn't believe how crispy the falafels were! I would love to head back to Byblos again if ever in the area. Absolutely delicious food.

Just visited for the first time.  I don't always go to the smaller boutique pet shops because I find they can sometimes seem overpriced.  In this case, the quality of items they have is better than a big box store (which is why I went there in the first place, since I was looking for a better coat for my dog), but the prices were spot on compared to what you could pay elsewhere or online, and the staff was super helpful.  They even have a rewards program and free delivery in the immediate area for orders over $50. Would absolutely recommend!  I also see that the support some of the local animal shelters which is an added bonus!

I really want to love this place, and the food is pretty great.

BUT THE SERVICE IS AWFUL.

They are so so so so slow, the older woman at the counter constantly has a chip on her shoulder that says "I hate being here".

The younger women show almost zero hustle for a busy breakfast place, although they are at least mostly more friendly.

And try to order takeout....you cannot get through on the phone and then when you get there, it takes them forever to work through the line.

If these people had a real manager or someone who knew how to run a restaurant, this place would be great.  It's really too bad and I hope it improves.

Monday night oysters for $1 are worth it for that alone!

We went as a group of four, and the environment was nice for a cold, rainy Monday.  I can see how it would get very busy on a warm summer evening though.  Between the four of us, we got the scallops, tuna tartare, NY strip steak and parpadalle pasta. All the plates were clean at the end of the meal.  Portions were reasonable but not over the top.  Prices were competitive, since it's seafood that is the star of this restaurant!  We might go back, but only on a Monday - the oysters were delicious!

Quickly and warmly greeted as I walked in the door. The ambiance of the restaurant is definitely that Tex Mex beach vibe. Actually very refreshing from other cookie cutter corporate restaurants in the area. My server was amazing as well. Friendly, efficient and on top of her game. Meal, well it was ok. Not the best TexMex but certainly not the worse. It was fresh and hot when served. But definitely could use some improvements on the flavor combinations. Would I come back ~ certainly the overall experience would make you want too, if not for the food. I could see this as a fun meet up after work for a few drinks and just a fun place to wind down.

If you are looking for a good deal this is not the place.  Average price for average cabinets.  Shop around and you can learn for yourself.  The main problem I encountered was told a 10-14 day turn around when I bought them Columbus day October 2.  Delivered to the store in a mixed shipment Second week in November then the remaining after Christmas.  Are you kidding me.  Excuse after excuse.  I'm thankful they were not going into the kitchen and I had it all torn up waiting on them.  Second issue was install for counter tops was finally quoted $1200-$1800 extra for install.

The food is good, but here is my gripe. Venetian Moon offered a special coupon through Eversave, a $30 gift certificate for $15. The deal was listed to run through December 10th. I purchased 6 of these coupons in the Spring as did my friends and we took turns using them when we went out. I went to dinner tonight at the VM and was informed the deal date (5 months into the deal) was listed wrong and it will end on November 1st....three days from now...Really? For a little more than the price of a cocktail that you make an 85% profit on, wouldnt you rather welcome customers in to your establishment  than push them away by blinsiding them at the door with a recant of a deal? 

We spent almost $100 on dinner and drinks, so the $15 coupon that you threw in, works out to be about $5 or less on your part.. There are plenty of good places to eat VM, so pissing people off that bought into your restaurant isn't good for business, for a lousy month left on a coupon.

A-OK exactly sums up my feelings on Champps.  I went here with my senior citizen parents who are kind of in love with this place.  I thought it was fine.  

We went during the lunch rush, so service was pretty good, although drink refills were a little hard to come by.  It was super busy though, so I'll cut our waiter some slack.  There are some (but not a lot) of options for not burger eaters and the venue (the couple times I've been there) mostly seems to cater to guys and businessmen who want to watch the game and eat a burger at the same time.  Not that there's anything wrong with that.  I'm just saying.  If this isn't you, think about taking your dollars somewhere else.

Overall, I would say if you like burgers, you will like this place!  If you feel just ok about burgers or are not into burgers, this might not be the place for you.

I've been going to Broadway medical clinic for over twenty years, seeing Dr Hirsch. She is a fantastic physician. Always listens to everything I have to say and genuinely try's to do something about my concerns. I can almost always get an appointment the same day if I need it, or at the very least a phone call.   My husband and children also see other physicians at BMC and have received the same high quality care as myself.   I would highly recommend Dr Hirsch and the Broadway medical clinic.

If you do not get yourself an AM Bagel, you are doing yourself an injustice.  Add avocado, add prosciutto if you're feeling frisky, and commence eating bliss.  I have always wanted to find a coffee place where I truly feel comfortable staying and enjoying and this is it.  Some people complain about the mom's and their kids, but it makes it feel like a reunion of friends and family.  Great coffee, PIE (need I say more?), and bagel sandwiches to kill for make this a weekend must. It's located in Montavilla and if the mood strikes you, the Academy Theater is across the street and is playing a $3 movie in a beautifully restored building.

This place is a mystery to me. Every day the line is half a block long for dinner. And yet each time I go I feel almost repulsed by the size of the fish servings. I love sushi but when you are just chomping on massive pieces of cold dead fish, you start to feel like golem in some underground nightmare ripping open live fish while filled with existential angst. At least that's how I felt. Why the lines? The only thing I can imagine is that people love value. And good lord do you get value. One nigiri here has the equivalent amount of fish to four nigiri at Mio. But at least with sushi, this doesn't necessarily mean better. For my money, I'll go to Zenbus lounge down the street and not worry about the lines.

I usually purchase my Toms online due to the limited selection in department stores. The selection here is the largest selection I've ever seen of Toms shoes. I came primarily to try on the Chelsea ankle boots. Luckily, it was available in my size and the color I wanted. The best part was that boots were 25% off too. This was a no brainer for me coming from California since this going to tax free and discounted. The person who was helping me was friendly too. I would definitely shop here again.

Love Cafe Zen!

A friend brought me here about a year or so ago and I returned several times. On Sunday it get's fairly busy as many people come in for brunch and some try to kill their hangover with the really big portions of food. They also offer half orders if you are not that hungry. My personal favorite are the egg's benedict. The hot chocolate is very good as well. Right next to the beach if you want to stroll around and walk the good calories off. :)

Enjoy!
~S

I have been going to Pho Basil for many years.  I think the quality of their food has gone down.  I think they are more concerned with flipping the tables than the quality of the food.  I received my main meal before my appetizers.   Staff was fast to get you in and out.  Service was ok.  Like I said, a few years ago this place was awesome.  Now it's hit or miss..... sad to say,,, if there is another Thai restaurant close by you might want to check that out.

Used them last week.

Pros - connected to airport, so transportation was very quick. Parking was easy to find. A shuttle bus picked us up literally within two minutes of parking. Five minutes later it dropped us off at the airport. Our driver was very friendly and helpful.
The entire process was pretty effortless and smooth. Will def use them again.

The only con - and which dropped it from a 5 to a 4 rating - was the driver on our return trip. It was close to 5 pm (Monday) and this guy either had a bad day or was eager to go home. We couldn't find our blue business card that had the lot number. He was exasperated by this and was pretty rude to our party - in front of several other passengers. We told him that this was our FIRST time using the service and didn't know we had to show him the card. I had my receipt and he snapped at me "that isn't going to work."  It was kind of a humiliating experience, especially with other passengers watching the entire conversation. 

When we got to Park & Zoom I finally located my ticket and gave it to the guy. His response "Oh good, so you did have a reservation." What? Did he think my party of four - with kids included - was lying about having a reservation (even though I had a receipt) and was just using him to get a free ride.....a free ride a hundred yards away from the terminal??? It was a weird comment. 

When we got to my vehicle I was still going to give him a tip. I figured he must have just had a bad day, maybe had some unruly customers, who knows. I was giving him the benefit of the doubt. But at my car he quickly took my bags out and turned away before I could say thank you or give him a tip. I was literally standing at the back of my car with my hand out with a tip - but as soon as my bag touched the back of the car he turned away and walked off. 

I've never understood why people work a customer service type job if they don't like working with the public.

Other than that guy, the entire experience and process was top-notch and I'll certainly use them every time I have to park at the Austin airport.

Mother's reminds me of the San Antonio Spurs - it won't show you any super inventive or flashy dish you haven't seen before, but it does the fundamentals of breakfast food very, very well. I went with my girlfriend and a friend on Saturday and we all left full and happy. As an appetizer, we got breakfast nachos, which was an enormous dish. Don't expect chips though: it's an amazing medley of potatoes with bacon blanketed in cheese with green onions sprinkled on top - on a side note, if you don't seriously love onions, you may want to ask them for light or no onions; they are super liberal with their onion use. Be warned though, it's a gigantic appetizer. For my dish, I ordered their eggs benedict, which are only available on weekends, and they are well deserving of their "world famous" title. They were ridiculously amazing. The drink I ordered was great too. Mother's has a whole menu of alcoholic breakfast drinks that aren't posted on their website, so make sure to peruse that menu.

Yeah, the wait was about 50 minutes when I went on Saturday, but after reading some of the other reviews on Yelp, I was prepared for that wait time. The service was good and I will most definitely be back in the future.

I love sallys but the new employees at this store are horrible I literally walked out with out my items because they were all un accommodating and would not use a coupon I had. Asking for a manager did nothing to help and the snotty attitude of the male employee with bleach blond hair is unprofessional. Definitely drive to the wilsonville store this location is the worst!! Never coming again and making a complaint! Would do negative five for this location if I could!

Shake Shack or P.Terry? P. Terry. In-n-out or P.Terry? P.Terry. Considering price, taste, convenience, and speed of service (It's called fast food for a reason...) P.Terry's wins in all categories for me. And I love how it's a local Austin chain! 

Favorite menu item is their shakes, hands down. Not for the lactose intolerant since they use real ice cream and milk, but that makes for extra richness and goodness. I also like how they always have a shake of the month to keep things interesting. Also have never had bad service at this location. 

What keeps me from giving this awesome local chain 5 stars is that the burger isn't knockout amazing. Then again I'm probably just chasing imaginary fast food hamburger unicorns though.

I had a perfectly fine sandwich here recently while waiting for my flight back home but I guess in reading other reviews, YMMV depending on what you order. 

Located near gate C15 there is a Wendy's, a pizza joint and a Mexican place as well as a coffee bar.  After nosing around, I opted for a sandwich so I could have half before boarding and save the rest for later if necessary.   A sandwich would go over far better with the surrounding passengers than more ummm.... "aromatic" options, plus I try to eat relatively healthy.  

I wasn't expecting much from airport food but I was actually impressed.   I chose tuna salad with no mayo and no cheese, all the vegetables.  The bread was *really* fresh and soft.  Vegetables were crisp.  Tuna tasted fresh and there was plenty of it.  All good in my book.  

Service was fast and easy.  Price was reasonable.  If I find myself in PDX again and in need of  a quick lunch I would go back.  No complaints.

Not a bad place for a burrito. The service was really fast on the food came out extremely good. Obviously is a fast food joint so it's not gonna be the best but it was pretty dang good. This is the type of place that I would go if I don't want to go into a restaurant and I want to quick meal. Seems like this place has a lot of mixed reviews but I had A pretty good experience. My burrito was pretty bag that I had to to go about 25% of it. I'll be definitely coming back here again.

I typically LOVE Dulins; however,  today I went there with my children to feed them and I ordered an ice tea and was told that they had to charge me a "split charge" if I ate anything off my kids' plate.  First, I was not hungry enough to order a full meal and second, we were attending a movie after we ate and it was very hot outside, so we couldn't take leftovers. She asked if that was ok, I asked why they would charge me if I was not eating or finishing what children cannot finish and she stated, "for the use of the silverware and for the water". The kicker is that an older couple without children sitting right nex to us ordered a meal to share and the same waitress never said anything to the couple about a $2 split fee??? Won't go back!

Had an order delivered. Very underwhelmed by the kalbi sliders, it was two small pieces of meat w mayo in a pork bun for $10. Literally 4 pieces of met which I'm actuality is only 1.5 strips of short rib cut. It's very unfair. Also heavy on the Mayo. Also got the jajang noodles. The one redeeming thing about this order which was $25 was the sauce for the jajang but the noodles were all stuck together to essentially be inedible. It does seem like going to the restaurant would be useful for the jajang but not sure. Otherwise it was an exorbitant cost for little in value

I really want to give this place 5 stars, but the service was so slow I just can't do it.  Other than that, they were amazing.

They had an excellent happy hour that lasted till 7 on a Friday night, and we were able to eat so cheap.  I got a $5 grilled chicken sandwich that was incredible, and on some of the best bread I've ever had.  It was flavorful and filling, and easily could have been $12-$15 elsewhere.  Another in our party tried the black bean burger and loved it.  The Shrimp Tacos were good, but they were kind of a train wreck, chef has no idea how to assemble a taco.  As an Arizonan, I wanted to pop back and introduce them to Tortillas 101.  She ended up eating the insides of the taco with a fork.

Two of my friends each got a pot of tea, and just raved about it.  The other two of us tried a beer, and it was the perfect compliment to our sandwiches.

After dinner, we tried out their special cocktail menu, and this is where Tea Zone shines.  I had the hot "Peppermint Patty" which was like the most amazing hot chocolate I've ever had.  We all passed around our drinks, and not one of us was disappointed. 

If you go, bring a truck load of patience and don't need to be out the door in a set amount of time.  Service was slow, and it seemed like the staff wasn't very experienced with the general concept of table waiting.  They were super friendly and nice, they just didn't come around often enough, and took forever just bringing water.  Normally this would really annoy me, but everything else was so good that I just can't be too upset.  I just pretended we were in Europe.

I had heard such great things about this place and was assured that THIS was THE place to go for a great meal.  It did not disappoint.  The only complaint I had was some of the meat that came round was a bit cold. But EVERYTHING was super tasty.  The staff there alone deserved 5 stars.  My husband is gluten free and they took such good care of him.  They went above and beyond to make sure he had everything made special for him. I personally did not care for the bread pudding dessert, but that's just my own personally taste. My favorites were the dumplings, and the chicken. So very yummy! Plus we all love the unique Hawaiian theme.  Would definitely go back.

I was planning on painting my Living Room and Kitchen myself, took the time off of work, and woke up with my shoulder in a lot of pain.  I reached out to APP for a quote on yelp and had a response back from Barb very quickly.  She was very helpful and was able to send Ismael out the next day to paint for me.  Ismael was on time, friendly, worked fast, and most importantly he did a great job! Kudos to Barb and Ismael for making me a happy customer!

As always the Hammered lamb has been one of our new favorite spots, but this time we were treated so sweet by everyone on staff because it was my birthday that I had to give a review and say thank you! I wish I could remember their names but I can tell you one of the girls mad me a delicious watermelon drink that was soooo good! We all sat at the bar rail and they were busy, but she was still attentive and fun! If you haven't been here yet you need to! No if ands or buts!

My family has been a regular at this restaurant for many years. In recent years, we've noticed the quality of service to be declining. That came to a peak last night when I went through possible the worst restaurant dining experience of my life.

To begin, we were seated at our table and only two menus were placed on a table of five adults. We were seated for a good 10-15 minutes and not a single waiter or waitress came to address the fact that we only have two menus that five of us are sharing. In fact, not a single waiter or waitress came to address us at all. Only 15 minutes later as a waitress was flying by our table did she ask "ready?". 

We ordered the chicken corn soup, dai ching prawns, prawn fried rice, and red chilli prawns. As we were ordering, the waitress began complaining that all we were ordering was prawn and began insisting we eat chicken or pork. My family only eats seafood and we had to tell her this three times before she stopped critiquing our order. I just want to know in what world is it alright for the waitress to criticize an order that is being placed by patrons of a restaurant. By her discretion we canceled one of our orders and went for vegetarian dish.

The soup is supposed to arrive as an appetizer, but for some reason our fried rice and dai ching prawns arrived first. When we asked them where our soup was, the waitress ran in and brought a completely different soup to our table. As we were already annoyed, we asked them to take the soup back and politely cancel our order. Immediately the waitress got ticked off and she told her shift lead and they were pointing at us and glaring. 

We began to feel uncomfortable and continued with eating our food, which was good and tasted as we expected. We had asked for water 15 minutes prior to this and were still waiting for some so we asked a second time. The man went into the back and did not come back out for a good five minutes and we asked our original waitress a third time for water and in an extremely sharp and condescending tone she told us "he's bringing it!" As if we were in the wrong for having to ask for water a third time.

Having only ordered three dishes amongst five people, we figured it would be a good idea to go back on our original order and order the chilli prawns again. Another man took our order and went into the back, about 15 minutes the waitress came out with a dish that was nothing like what we ordered. They brought out deep fried prawns with rock salt when we specifically ordered the stir fried chilli prawns with red chilli sauce. At this point we were extremely fed up with the lack of decent or acceptable service and asked them to cancel the order and bring the bill. 

The waitress and her team lead again were glaring at us from the back as I watched them eat our canceled order right in front of us. The waitress did not even bother to come bring the machine to us, she decided to give the machine to another worker to come bill us. We paid and did not tip since this experience was particularly awful and we did not get an apology for a single error on their part. 

As stated before, I have never had a worse restaurant experience in my life. I would honestly give this place 0 stars if I could, the only thing I can say is the food was decent but it's too bad we only got half of the stuff we ordered. With that being said, you can get food that tastes just as good at a restaurant that values its customers and service. So save your money and go to any other Chinese restaurant in Vancouver.

It's clear to me why this place looks emptier and emptier each time I go, you can add us to the list of families this terrible organization has turned away due to their garbage service.

What a disappointment. Sat on the patio which is nice, except...they had LOUD head banging music playing. They finally did turn it down a bit, but  it still was terrible and completely inappropriate for this setting. 

My wife had mussels, which they said came in that day. Three out of twelve were spoiled. Yuck!

I had over cooked cannelloni,  not good. 

A server stood across the narrow isle chatting with one of her friends, blocking the aisle for her colleagues, who we working. Not to mention the fact she kept backing up and hitting my wife with her butt.

I will not be back.

I did the Groupon thing a while back and got $10 worth of food (2 orders) plus a basil-lychee lemonade for $5!

Today, I ordered the chicken karaage and korean short rib tacos.  The guy forgot my lemonade until I reminded him.  Nice start!

I really like the korean short rib tacos (2 of them).  Good flavour.  Would order it again.

I wasn't pleased with the chicken karaage.  It tasted pretty salty - probably too much soy sauce.  Plus, it wasn't crunchy so it was more like a terriyaki.

The basil-lychee lemonade isn't good.  It was lots of club soda and bits of lychee.  I wouldn't pay the $4 they are selling it for.  Thank goodness I got it included.

But, will go back to try the rest of the menu out.  Looking forward to the duck confit salad!

Getting to the point. The service was slow and turtle tailed. I really don't see why they are popular amongst the Yelpers. The oysters were sent back. They were fried hard and cut in half.The BOGO sushi is the only reason, I give them 2 stars.  Asked for 2 menus and got 2 different prices for the same appetizers. Not good at all. I left hungry and unsatisfied.  These sushi places need to STOP skimming on the portion. Until then I will keep searching for the 1.

Our youngest adult daughter has been a resident of the Atrium on Commonwealth Avenue in Boston for approximately the last two years and our oldest daughter resided there about five years ago. We cannot say enough positive things about the Atrium management and other employees at this location. Dennis Hall is professional and skilled and has exceeded expectations (ably supported by Kiki, Oanh, and Adolfo) as have the terrific, courteous and conscientious security at the concierge desk (Dave, Arthur, and Fred). Our relationship with the Atrium is supported by the fact that we read and follow the rules, which are there to protect all the residents and which we support fully. While the vintage of the building is on the older side, management and the employees do a very commendable job of keeping it clean and functioning well. Kudos to a well-run apartment building and the management, security, and other employees there who work hard to make the Atrium a great place to live in Boston and at a great location.

Had a large group party here over the weekend, first time visiting the place. We were given a nacho/taco bar which was really good! The steak that was provided was excellent. Unfortunately the food wasn't out for very long and was packed up while the majority of our group was still standing by.

Our group also had the drink package but we didn't seem to get a server that was assigned to us - this resulted in lengthy waits at the bar.

Game area is nice and there is plenty of room to get around. They have some classics in the game area. I opted out of the laser tag though.

We all still had a great time but I do wish we had our own server as it would have made the experience even better for our group.

Wonderful experience had by all, even the kids! The entry was warm and cozy complete with roaring fireplaces and a sophisticated log cabin decor. The art on the walls was interesting and the kids enjoyed looking around. The server was quick to greet us and take drink orders. The kids were given crayons and an activity sheet. They really enjoyed it! The menu had a wide range of options. My husband ordered the NY strip steak and the portion was huge! I kept eating the yummy mashed potatoes off his plate lol. I ordered the rattlesnake pasta. I really liked the citrus lime taste and all the fresh veggies. Our son had chicken with fries and was very happy. Our daughter wanted dessert instead so they brought her out some ice cream in a dish. The customer service was outstanding. We will be back!

I've been to a ton of Les schwab stores all over the Pacific Northwest, this one was by far the absolute WORST store I've ever been to! This place is a joke. There was only 1 other customer when I went there and it took them 2 hours to put new tires on my truck. Which normally takes other stores 30 mins tops. Then he brought the keys in and I waited for another 20 minutes to get checked out. I'm paying these guys $2,000 for tires and I get treated that shitty. And they charged me for valve stem replacement which they never did and I ended up with a flat tire less than a week later and 2 other tires that were very low. I will never go here again nor will I recommend it. That place is a shit show no organization. Didn't even clean the tires they put on. Whoever the manager of this store is needs to be fired.

We have loved this amazing country style sushi place for over a decade. It's a lovely, small restaurant. Show up early if you have kids--5 to 6 is the family dinner hour. My son learned to love sushi here, starting with sushi rice balls. He graduated to tobiko, then salmon sashimi. We often get looks of admiration and comments from other friendly customers about his love of sashimi, a bit unique for a child his age.

If you love good, simple, freshest-of-fresh fish, come try Toraya. You won't be disappointed.

This is a really good lunch place. I don't remember the name of the bowl I got, only the number because it was B4 (get it? Sounds like before?) Anyway, it had pork with vermicelli noodles, lettuce, bean sprouts, carrots and little cut in half egg rolls stuck in the side of the gigantic bowl. The pork had a really nice flavor to it and the egg rolls were quite tasty. If you weren't starving you could split this because it is a really large portion.

The waiter we had was really nice and on the ball. I would go back for sure.

This cafe has been on my hit list for some time now, and I finally got to stop by the other day. Interior is very homey, and has a variety of seating options available. There are L-shaped tufted couches, plush armchairs, a long communal table, and small round tables for you to choose from. The walls in the back seating area have exposed brick, and outlets along the sides are relatively plentiful. There are low hanging pendant lights, as well a a chandelier in the center of the back  room. Menu features standard expresso drinks and teas, and they have many sandwiches to choose from. From my observation, most of the clientele here look like Berklee students, as the campus is just across the street. Many of the patrons sit here for a while chatting or doing work on their computers. Baristas are very friendly, and even when there's a line, I did not have to wait too long for my Spanish Latte. I paid around $4 for this beverage, which is pretty standard for a specialty latte in small coffee shops. 
The Spanish Latte is one of the specialties of Pavement Coffee (I haven't seen it anywhere else), so I decided to try it. It's basically a regular latte with condensed milk. (Note, they use counter culture coffee beans here, and they do have pourovers, if that matters to you.) I loved the latte art, and I also loved the teal green saucer that it came in, but I was not the biggest fan of the condensed milk actually. This may be a matter of taste, so I'm not going to hold it against Pavement. Otherwise, the latte had good flavor and next time I plan to try the regular latte, or maybe the chai latte. 
I also had the bagel and lox for $7 on the everything bagel. Everything bagel was a little salty, though toasted nicely. The onions and tomatoes tasted fresh, but I think they could have been more generous with the smoked salmon, especially given the price tag on this bagelwich. Disclaimer: I had a bagel sandwich at one of the best bagel shops in NYC recently, so perhaps I sound more critical than I should be. I miss you, Ess-a-bagel!   
WiFi is only free for one hour a day, after that you have to pay. I think it was $5 per day, or you could do $15 for 30 consecutive days.

Well if you look at the little map that's provided by yelp showing the location of this place it's really close to Passion City Church.  I don't know if that's a good or bad thing :-) This location is pretty close to me and while not my favorite package store it's been consistent in having all the staples I'm looking for and some of the harder to find items.  Nothing special in here if you've been to one package store you've been to them all but this is bigger than most.  They've added a new on-line ordering process, and have in-house hostesses. If you buy quite a lot they will help you carry it to your car.  For wine and spirits, Tower is your friend.

Are you interested in elbowing people out of the way, getting dirty looks, battling baby strollers, squeezing through tight aisles, dealing with obnoxious and unfriendly cashiers, and finding the only game in town for an extensive collection of kosher for Passover foods? Then you've come to the right place. The Butcherie.

We headed here today after stopping at a Judaica store across the street and weren't disappointed. This place has every type of Passover food imaginable...but you pay the price. The Butcherie has a monopoly on everything kosher, and if I had the clams (oops. Not allowed to eat clams. I mean moolah.), I'd open a grocery store that could compete directly with this kosher-only establishment. No one seems to mind shelling out (oops. No shell fish allowed.) for the goods. In fact, I spent about $30 on four items. Couldn't believe it. And I skipped the $15.99/lb kosher brisket this trip. That would have tacked on another $64 or so. Yikes.

The meat, frozen food, and prepared food departments are well-stocked, and the wine offerings are extensive. Israeli import items and ethnic foods abound. Whereas Stop and Shop in Lexington (where I usually get my Kosher foods during the Jewish holidays) has one whole aisle dedicated to Passover items (I make the trip to Lexington because my local supermarkets generally have only one box of matzoh, macaroons, and jelly candies, and I obviously need more than that to sustain us for eight days), The Butcherie is ALL Passover during the eight-day holiday. I'm from the Bronx, and this type of store is pretty typical in the five boroughs, but it always surprises me that Brookline has something similar. 

During non-holiday times, this supermarket has delicious deli meats and breads and other wonderful items...all kosher, all the time. 

Hint: Don't go on a Friday morning cuz it's packed, and of course, it's closed on Saturday. Also, parking can be difficult; there's a lot in the back of the store, but it's hard to find spots there, too. Today we lucked out. Found a place 10 steps from the entrance.

I deducted 1 star for high prices and unfriendly cashiers and 1 star for the myriad black and blue marks on my arm. Too many people shoving me, and I try not to shove back. Next time, I should wear full body armor.

great place, friendly barkeeps.  only complaint, my first jameson was served in a small neon pink plastic container that i'd expect to see being carried by a shot girl in a dance club (which i think is upstairs, definitely never made it there).  when i mentioned it to the bartender, she immediately made good with a lowball glass over half full.  that's service.

mostly empty and male, but everyone was cool.  my guess is more blue collar than white, but doesn't think anyone really notices.  

smaller area with the bar on the left.  to the right are some two-seat high tables.  the back of the room has more of the same.  wooden bar stools with back support.  bar top is wooden, as is the larger rail.  lights directly over the bar provide perfect lighting.  bar back is a register, taps, & bottle shelves.  hdtvs are hung above.  didn't eat any of the nights here.

not a huge place, but a great place to grab a drink, with a friendly staff and strong drinks.

I take the train a lot from the Portland area to Seattle but I don't think it is the most efficient way to travel. It is plagued by delays that can span from 10 minutes to 3 hours in my experience. The employees try their best to redirect people to other trains when there is an extreme delay but these trains don't come by often enough. I would avoid coast starlight for shorter trips. This train often takes longer time due to the scenic route and is more prone to delays due to the distance it travels. 

I think the employees are very friendly and understanding. I think the problem lies in the trains themselves. We need better train system.

I honestly prefer the timeliness of bolt bus but I dislike the downtown location of the pick up and cramped seats. . . Also smelly toilets... but if you really need to get to Seattle punctually, bolt bus is the way to go.

This is the ghettoest HEB I've been to.  It's the one closest to our house so we're here a lot, but it's not unusual for us to have to go to other locations to find what we actually need.  

The parking lot is a scene straight out of "The Birds".  If you go in the fall there's a good chance you'll get pooped on.  The parking lot resembles a paintball field of bird droppings. 

It doesn't get much better when you get inside.  You can tell the store is old and there are lots of cracked tiles.  The assortment of produce is ok, but nothing compared to what you'll find at parmer/35 or parmer/mopac or gattis school / 45.  

Within the past months I've had to go to other locations to find several items.  Here's a list of them, maybe you'll see a pattern and be able to gauge when to go here and when not to.

1.)  Blue Foaming Dawn Dishwashing Detergent Refills
2.)  Smoked Parika
3.)  Sea Salt
4.)  Peppercorns
5.)  Broom Handles
6.)  Hash Browns
7.)  Family Size Lasagnas

I live in California and was only in town 1 night. My flight was delayed and when I called the first time they were very nice and accommodating about me and my boyfriend running behind. They said we could be caught up on the tour once we arrived at the office. Sounded great and very nice since there's nothing that we could have done! I called once again as we were leaving the rental car place and the guy on the phone this time was beyond rude. I tried explaining my situation to him and he didn't care. He said he was in charge of the tour for that night and he was wasnt going to wait for anyone! We basically rented a car to drive up to Salem for no reason. Thankfully we made a trip to the cape out of it instead! Extremely rude customer service. If that's how he acted as a customer service rep, I can only imagine how he was as a tour guide. I understand that we were going to be late, but don't tell me it's not a big deal and I can get caught up on the tour when later you basically yell and are rude to me on the phone.

Pros:
Reasonably priced
Lots of space
Enough outlets.

Cons:
Some of the worst music I've heard in a coffee shop. They've clearly chosen the music for the benefit of the baristas and not the customers trying to work. To top it off, they clearly haven't paid for the music service they're using because there are ads which are annoying and distracting.
The baristas are very loud and seem more concerned with socializing than providing the customers with a nice ambiance. The acoustics are horrible so it's hard to enjoy your coffee or concentrate on your work with the obnoxious ads and loud chatter coming from the baristas.

Let me preface this by saying that I've been going to Dr. Roth for over a decade, previously at his Hollywood location.  As a person, the doctor seems nice and does his job well.  However, his business apparently is incapable of creating or delivering glasses.  The service I received was shockingly bad, and I'm not alone -- because I've met many people who have had the same problems with this business.

To make a long story short, I ordered glasses in January.  In fact, I brought a friend and we both ordered them on the same day.  I had already had my eye exam and was told I could expect my glasses within a week; my friend's situation was the same.  Three months later, after a total of twenty-six phone calls and five visits to the store (always with a promise that the glasses would be ready "tomorrow" and bizarre excuses about lenses, frames, factories, weather problems, and shipping), I received my glasses -- my friend never did, and finally gave up.  I was promised a refund, but it was never provided.  The new glasses give me a profound headache, so I don't wear them.

To make things worse, Dr. Roth lied to me.  He claimed that he had only billed my insurance for an eye exam; my EOB clearly showed that hardware (including lenses, frames, coatings, etc.) had all been billed on the original date in January -- but no glasses were actually created or delivered for many months.  When I called him out on this lie, he said:  "I don't know what to tell you."  I know what to tell him:  this is at best a lie to a longtime customer; at worst it's insurance fraud.  Is either an acceptable thing for a doctor or a business to do?

During each of my visits to this clinic, I witnessed others who came in, trying to figure out where their glasses were (all to be turned away, told their glasses would be complete the next day).  As I told Dr. Roth, all I wanted was my glasses -- I was not going to pursue a fraud case against him, although I clearly had grounds to do so.  For this process to take months and literally dozens of phone calls, plus repeated in-person visits -- that's utterly unacceptable.  I told him so, and he repeated, "I don't know what to tell you."

Well, I know what to tell other shoppers:  stay away.  This is the worst customer service experience I have ever had.  It is an abominably bad business.  Please do yourself a favor and read the "filtered" reviews for others who have had similarly bad experiences, and ask yourself who marked those reviews so they'd be hidden.

I will begin by saying THANK YOU for a great experience.  This was my second visit to this great office and I must say that I am yet again impressed with the great service.  The sign-in kiosk was simple to use with easy to follow instructions.  I was greeted by a smiling Jasmine (hope I spell this right) who took me back within five minutes of my signing in and actually about 15 to 20 minutes BEFORE my appointment time!  She was very thorough and compassionate about her role in my visit. Dr. Weiss was an active listener and answered each and every one of my questions in simple to understand language.  All in all I must say that I am very grateful to have found this practice as it is convenient to where I live AND has a GREAT staff!  You will NOT be disappointed!

Came to Boston for the weekend and was craving soup dumplings, as I always am! Trekked it here and I had such high hopes! I was a bit put off when entering, since there were 3 employees tending to a group of 4 ordering takeout and my friend and I weren't seated until 5-10 minutes in. The place was pretty empty at 4pm on a Saturday.

I ordered the soup dumplings with pork, and also a chicken pan fried noodle to share. The service was good, the waiter and busboy were both attentive and noticeably solemn... I guess they were trying to be formal? I don't know but neither of them cracked a smile at any point. 

I was sad to find out that this place's idea of a soup dumpling turned out to be entirely different from what I am used to. I was expecting a dumpling with thin skin, an abundance of piping hot flavorful broth, and tender pork filling. The dumpling skin here was on the thicker side, and the meat inside was similar to that of a roast pork, very salty. The broth was almost none existent and to me, seemed like soy sauce and that was it. They were warm but not piping hot.

The pan fried noodle was pretty good, with a lot of toppings (carrots, celery, etc) and an average amount of noodle, and there was a ton of sauce (thumbs up). 

Overall, I wouldn't recommend the soup dumplings but if you're here for other Chinese food, I'd say it's worth a try! The place started to fill up about the time I left so maybe other dishes are better. My friend and I paid $20 after tax+tips.

I love love love this place. I have been two times now and each time was a blast. I love going to the second entry into the water on a tub and floating down the spring. It feels just like a lazy river. The day we went there was even a manatee who swam down to the swimming area and everyone had to get out. It was Truly a sight to see. I also love the fact they have food on site. I got the jolly rancher popsicle and loved it ! If your looking for something fun to do I highly recommend this place!

Great service! We were flying out of the country for more than a week and did not want to park at the airport so I searched around for a car service. I chose Austin Black Car Service because the pricing was fair and included taxes and fees, others didn't. 

The car was fantastic, showed up on time and got us to the airport in plenty of time. When we got back, we came down the escalator and there they were waiting for us. It was perfect! I'll never drive to the airport again!

I've been to this place once. The local is nice (clean, well illuminated, parking available on the street) and the service is friendly. 

The pizza is tasty - beats any chain pizza. The cheese and tomato sauce are excellent; this is all I care about since I don't pay much attention to the dough. In regards to size, a large pizza is enough to feed three very hungry people.

The combination of toppings provided as specialties look good, but you can try your hand at choosing your favorite ingredients. I have to say that my mix wasn't as good as I expected, so next time I'll stick to the menu.

This location is right next to the Fresh Market on Mills. You can easily make appointments online which I did. I went in to get a gel manicure, and pedicure.

They do have an interesting seating area where both can be done in the same chair. I had two ladies work on me at the same time which is pretty nice. 

I do feel the quality of work in the gel manicure could of been better. She always had to switch sides in order to work on the other hand and the polish could been applied a lot better if it was more of a controlled environment. There were some areas missing polish in the corners when all said and done.

The pedicure I had was excellent at least. Don't have any complaints on that. 

The color choices they had was a great variety as well. At the end of service they do give you the materials that they used on you. Like the buffer and filer to ensure they don't reuse it on other guests which I liked.

We take the Grands to see whatever show Do Jump is offering for Christmas and it is a huge hit with all of us, from 8-80. There's wonderful music, lots of fun and laughs, beautiful segments, it's a fantastic time.

My 8 y/o daughter has taken classes at Do Jump for 4 years, and she's learned enough to make it worth every penny, but her strength, confidence, and positive body image, and the supportive teachers are more than I knew we were getting, and so, so, so valuable. She loves these classes more than any other she's taken (and she's liked a lot of classes).

My fiancé and I each got an order of the Double Double, I also got an iced Dong Ding oolong tea and he got an iced ruby black tea. Everything was absolutely delicious! I loved the complementary soup, it reminded me of my mom's. The iced teas were also good but a bit on the sweet side so next time I'd ask for less sweet. I thought the chicken was moist and the sauces were delicious. I also hardly ever comment on rice, but I thought the rice was the most perfectly cooked rice I've ever had. I will absolutely come back again.

For sixty dollars, a haircut better blow my damn mind. 

Now, don't get my wrong: historically I have always paid about 60 dollars AT LEAST for a haircut and I haven't always been thrilled with it, either. But that is extremely disappointing. I mean, you fork over more money with the presumption that the stylist and the salon is charging more because they are bringing more skill and experience to your head than a a different stylist who charges less might have. That may not be the case, but that's the implication in a higher price tag: a better product. So, yeah: I am not thrilled about paying 60 dollars for a haircut for the same reason I'm not thrilled about paying someone to yank my wisdom teeth, but since it's something that can go wrong, I'm happy to pay a lot more in the hopes that it would mean a reduced likelihood of things going poorly. Sixty dollars is definitely a fair price for a cut that doesn't go poorly; i.e., is going to rock me. And so it had better rock me.

Jamie cut my hair today, and new in town; I was nervous. I didn't know what I could expect here. Is 60 dollars a lot here? Maybe that's not a lot here. I don't know.  Jamie is absolutely adorable, sweet, with enviable red hair and endearing green converse. I came with pictures off the internet that I could point to instead of trying to tell her what I wanted, because, really: I don't speak stylist (although I would like to). I also had my old stylist write down what she was doing when she cut my hair (I have no idea what it says, because I don't speak stylist). She definitely delivered; I am very very happy with my hair: chin length, layers, wispy, disconnected parts, broken up around the face, took a lot of the weight out. not too mainstream, but not too hipster. 

That's what I was hoping to drop around 60 dollars on, which hurt to do, because IN THIS ECONOMY!!! letting any dollar go ain't fun, but neither is having suck hair, or impacted wisdom teeth, etc. Anyway. JAMIE ROCKS. SHE DELIVERS. 

My favorite part? It was 35 dollars.

Probably some of the best Indian food I've ever had and I'm pretty picky about heavy spices in my food. I've been to this restaurant countless times and I will keep going back.  For an appetizer I would recommend the vegetable samosas, for an entree the palak paneer and for dessert the rice pudding. I'm not a big fan of buffets, but for the lunch hour I would actually recommend their buffet to try an array of their food choices. Great food. Good service. Pleasant atmosphere. Decent price. Enjoy!

I had been craving Indian food all week, and decided to check Scout Mob to see what I could get into.  I have never heard of this place, but I am always game for new spots.  I didn't expect this place to be like an Indian version of Chipotle, and didn't get my hopes up.  It was great!  I like the layout, and the food is very reasonably priced.  I looked forward to going back.  They are open until 8pm on the weekdays and that is a plus for the area that they are in because no one else is open.  

Oh, and I love the raita!

Nice, new (2006) apartments not far from Boston. Medford isn't quite all that but the shops (Starbucks, Kinko's/Fedex, Walgreen's, Cold Stone, Evergreen Cleaners, T-Mobile) and restaurants (Average Joe's, Yoki, Regina Pizza, Qdoba) downstairs go a long way toward making life easier. Stop & Shop, Shaws, Best Buy, Target, Costco, Home Depot, Bed Bath & Beyond are a short drive away.

Advantages: underground parking, friendly staff, new building, good construction, decent neighbors, convenient location (Wellington T-stop is an easy & safe 5-10 minute walk away), high ceilings, in-apartment washer/dryer, modern appliances, marble countertops, Zipcars nearby, clean grounds, several gyms nearby (Boston Sports Club is opening a big one across the street December 2007, Gold's is jogging distance away), decent jogging areas directly accessible.

Disadvantages: price, traffic, traffic noise, delivery trucks parked & idling under your window, only 2 elevators for whole building, many neighbors have dogs, weak heating/cooling system.

Came here for a second mediocre experience at Uncle Julio's. We arrived at 8pm for a birthday with a party of 10. I understand larger parties are harder to deal with and manage but we waited over an hour for our food to arrive. The food was decent, nothing to write home about. Tradition Tex Mex with decent flavor profiles. We all waited for our food for so long we didn't even care about the food quality at that point. I had a Paloma which was delicious. What really stood out as far as service went was that it took over and hour and 15 minutes for the server to separate and give us the checks back. Again, I completely understand that a large party and multiple checks makes it harder on the server but there's absolutely no reasoning as to why it was taking so long. The manager did absolutely nothing to irradiate the situation and just kept telling us it would be a minute. Pretty disappointed since it was for a birthday celebration and we left at 11:15pm for an 8pm reservation. This is more of a place for a quick drink and appetizer rather than a 3.5 hour long dining experience.

My dryer continued to cycle but wouldn't heat or dry the clothing  so I called these guys.  I told them that it took sometimes more than 3 cycles to dry effectively.  They told me that it was likely the vent being clogged and sure enough it was.  They said to do it on my own and to call them if the problem persisted.  Well, they were right and saved me a good chunk of money.  I never actually used their service but I did take their free advice.  

I would definitely use them in the future.

Grooming services particularly by Nate are fantastic! My Shizu-Llapso looks and feels great every time and we've been a client for years! I've moved away and drive-in for appts bc I trust Nate and he does teeth, ears and nails, as well as the best rounded cut my dog has ever gotten & Nate's consistent. 

My only concern and reason for 4 instead of 5 stars is that they use cage dryers and I do not like this form of drying. It's convenient for the business and less than desirable, I'd say even uncomfortable for my dog. I think about this each time and ask him to keep an eye on my dog. When my dog comes home he's very thirsty and this is not the case when he comes home from other groomers (no cage dryers) or mobile groomers.

We ordered BIBA! on caviar and loved it. We got the bbq plate, kelaguen, titiyas, and empanada. Everything was so good! The only thing that I was sad to see was only one titiyas (flatbread) for $4. I hoped for 2 in an order. 
We look forward to visiting the restaurant once businesses open back up. 

We ate the delicious food while watching a documentary about Guam- we learned so much and have so much respect for that country and people and are glad to support in a small way through supporting BIBA!

DO NOT go there!! The same "Dr. I" does the same scam at this new location: worst experience I've had all 15+ years of going to optical stores annually! Waited for 50 minutes until seen and during that whole 50 minutes no one once checked on me. When finally seen I was given the b.s. how it takes longer for new patients--I got there 10 minutes earlier to get paperwork and pre-exam done. When I asked how much longer for the wait and mentioned my appointment was at 2pm, all I got was a snide reply "I know!". And, the rest of visit got progressively worse from there:
1. I never had a "doctor" meddling with insurance and charges where the staff have no slightest idea how my charges came about. I later then learned from my primary physician she file false insurance claim to get more money (fabricated my complaint of experiencing headaches and dizziness to get a retro-referral. Why would I go to an optical store for that!!!) 
2. During the exam, I mentioned I want to stay with the same contacts, she told me what I have been wearing is "discontinued". And of course that was a lie, but I didn't know then, so let her fit me with whatever she thought were "the best!" When I asked isn't the daily ones more expensive, she shrugged! And sure enough the bill came to double of what I have been paying the past years. I was not happy and asked them to readjust the charge and refund me the difference, all they could tell me is "you were charged correctly!" When I asked my insurance company to step in, she told my insurance company I was charged at a higher rate because they "don't do standard contacts fitting." Em, shouldn't I be told of that when making the appointment or during the exam?
3. She also told me my insurance company is terrible at making glasses, and I should go with their type of glasses lenses. AND, she told me I can't use frame insurance allowance if I am using contact lenses allowance!!!! Duh, frame and lens, do they sound the same to you? It's either frame and contacts, or frame and eyeglasses lens. Of course they refused to listen to me and quoted me $900 for a pair of eyeglasses, while it would be under $100 with my insurance.
4. The contacts that "Dr. I" had me tried made my vision blurry and everything is out of focus. When I finally got the prescription, they were of course way high! And she still claimed those were the right fit when I explained more than twice that they don't help my seeing better!
5. She is not a doctor but an aggressive, dishonest salesman. And that's exactly how I felt the entire time. She dismissed my preference of contacts and my insurance to get money out of me. When confronted, she responded "misunderstanding..." but continued to pushing for sales. 

...Read other reviews of their Medford location as this Dr. I also works at that location and you will see a pattern (same shit she has been doing for 2-3 years!) One even mentioned the Dr. I refused to confirm the prescription for online purchases so we will have no choice but buy from them, which of course is doubled the cost.  This place should not be in business! Very unethical!! Stay away!!!!

I stayed at the embassy suites during our last nor'easter when it got pretty bad outside. My job booked the room for me however they must have done something wrong in the booking procedure because when I went to check in a wonderful man at the front desk told me there was no reservation for me. His name was Calvin. It was extremely busy the phones were ringing off the hook and there were so many people waiting behind me to check in. Calvin really went above and beyond to find my reservation and fix my problem, all while answering the phones and acknowledging all the other people that were waiting. His customer service skills were impeccable , I've never gotten such kind and amazing service like the one he provided to me when I stayed there. The room was so comfortable and I slept like a baby. Thank you Calvin

Spa Sydell's Dr. Herbert Kollinger is still as awesome as ever! As someone who's been to the most highly-regarded cosmetic surgeons in LA, NYC, Paris, etc. (just for a *little something* here and there ~ *smiles*), I can assure you that Dr. K is amongst the VERY BEST! He'll not only take care of you so that you look your 'natural best,' he'll ensure you don't end up with fish lips, a heavy brow, that dreaded 'deer in the headlights' look, et al. Major PROPS and 10 fins up! :)

This restaurant made me feel like I was back home in NYC. The venue was trendy-modern, and the place felt alive. The patrons ranged in age and all seemed to be enjoying the atmosphere. There is a good balance of food options on the menu for both meat and seafood lovers. The vegetarian options were very slim, and I don't recall seeing any vegan options on the menu (would love to see one or two options added to the menu). The food that our group ordered was delicious - flatbread, roasted chicken, Caesar salad and the lobster hole. We had a new waitress that seemed very uncomfortable in performing her job duties, but we didn't let that deter us from enjoying the venue and food.

Went on a Friday night. Food was good, came out really quick. Music was good. Would have given a 5 star besides the fact they made us get up from our table after 1 hour and 50 minutes despite the fact that we were still ordering drinks and we ordered an appetizer after we ate our dinner meal because we were still a little hungry. 10 times we were asked to take our appetizer plate that we ordered after dinner even while we were eating out of it because they wanted us up and out.

We have been utilizing this office for several years now in different capacities. All of their doctors are friendly, but Dr. Joe Feste is the absolute BEST!! He is wonderful!! He listens to your concerns, no matter how small, and takes the time to answer your questions. He is considerate and flexible and really does a fantastic job of putting patient care at the forefront of everything he does. The office staff is also really helpful and kind. But if you need to go here, whether it's for hormones, weight loss, Botox, or whatever, try to see Dr. Feste because he's just amazing!

They failed to honor the reservation on Open Table, waited 25 minutes as others were seated.  Then waited 47 minutes for the meal to be served.  

Management made a serious mistake: large family group was seated, 15 4-person tables set up as two long runs (2 persons each) on a Saturday night, many small children running around, family taking many flash photographs indiscriminately. Then the birthday celebration started.  We could not  hear one another at our table of 4.  Of course the large family occupied the main dining room for an overly long time and dominated the kitchen and the wait staff.

One of our party got cold chicken!

I like exotic food and a good environment to eat in and this place understands that but it falls a little short in the food department. 

The Nan was thick like a tortilla, filling and okay, but it's not what I am use to. Most Nan I have had has been pretty thin. I would have liked more garlic on it but you have to understand that I consider garlic its own food group.

My wife and I ordered the grilled chicken breast skewers with the peanut dipping sauce for an appetizer. The chicken was very bland and the peanut dipping sauce was on the sweet side. 

Next we ordered the Korma with chicken. You could taste the spices in this dish but they were still over powered by the sweetness of it. Also, the spices didn't seem balanced. You would get over powering taste of clove then garlic there wasn't a good marriage of the spices.
 
Our service was good and I did like the environment.

Although, I would consider this place average I have to say serving this type of food in Colorado has to be really hard work. This style of food is extremely exotic to most Americans and probably other worldly to Coloradoans and the poor college students that live near by. To have a successful business you have to walk a delicate type rope of pleasing everyone and not making dishes that would offend a "meat & potato" pallet. I am sure the owner is an extremely excellent cook but unfortunately he is probably restrained by his demographic.

I think this place could go to the next level. I personally would have liked more spice and flavor in my dish like I have had at Indian restaurants in Birmingham and Seattle. It may have to be set up more like a Thai restaurant where you give your order a rating. 

Example: a 1-5 with 1 being the lowest and 5 being the hottest.

The owner could even use this to his advantage by coming out and greeting tables that have dared to order hotter and spicier dishes who seek what he probably wishes to unleash upon Boulder. This type of networking as well would create a loyal following by creating a memorable experience for the people he really wishes to attract.

In fact when my wife and I ordered our food our waitress asked us if we had been in before to which we replied, "no". Our waitress then rambled something about having never tried Indian food herself but now was instantly hooked; implying this was our situation as well. Perhaps my blue jeans and black hooded sweat shirt suggested a lack of sophistication that I otherwise do poses. However, this is not our case and I do wonder how the waitress will feel when she finally has real Indian food also.

Bottom line is I will keep an eye on this place. It has tremendous potential but you cannot serve average food so as to please everyone or you'll just end up with an average clientle at an average restaurant.

I was really nervous booking this place after reading all of the bad reviews. But, hands down, Mystic Dunes is awesome!

We're a family of five, so having a lot of space was great for us. We went to Disney every day, and it only took 10-15 minutes to drive there from the condo.

The kids loved the pools and big TVs in all the rooms. It was clean and the staff was attentive.

The rec room offered a great place to "play" and do crafts on a rainy day. My preschooler loved the huge collection of Mr. Potato heads and Thomas trains. 

The only drawback is the internet connection. We had to pay for internet at all, and then it was plug in only, so I had to use my husband's computer all week. It was kind of bizarre that there was no wi-fi in this day and age. We've come to rely on wifi to do everything from planning our day at disney to making dinner reservation.

Fix the internet situation and we'll come back every year! We loved it. But, like I said, we need wifi.

I came here after desperately needing my hair fixed from a haircut I had done at a trendy, hip salon that I won't name. I thought the reviews looked good, so I was willing to take my chances and have my blunt, choppy, undone layers fixed! 

I pretty much walked in, and got Hugh, who did an amazing job in fixing my layers. I also got ombre highlights and they look gorgeous! Hugh made the the colors blend seamlessly and really paid attention to detail. I think I just found my regular stylist in the Atlanta area, which is very exciting!

The other customers who had other stylists seemed to be as easily pleased with their hair as well. This is a great salon, with really nice professional stylists. And they don't overcharge! Haircuts are about $35 for a woman, and my highlights were $65! I'd easily make the trek up to Buford Highway to get a hair done here.

Came on a hot Saturday in August!  Fortunately, we used the app to get on the waiting list, requested 5:30, seated at 5:40...good deal.  Our waitress, Jasmine was wonderful, friendly and efficient. She made our experience a pleasure.  Food was good.  While waiting to be seated I listened to the manager tell people 15- 75 minutes for a table.  It was hot to wait outside. After we were seated in a side room, I noticed 4 four tops and a 6 top empty.  Why people had to stand in hot sun should be looked at,  manager should walk around a little more often and be aware. Again, Jasmine was outstanding.  Ask to sit in her section.  Overall I would give a 4 out of 5.

Went Restaurant Week, with a limited menu.  The food was quite tasty!  
I wasn't excited about the starters when they arrived.  The gazapcho was the right flavor, but wrong texture for me. The melon, very nice, had crisp prosciutto, that didn't add anything. 
The sauce on the hanger steak was a bit salty, but easy to skip.  The best part was dessert! Sour cream panna cotta with fresh berries compote.  I wanted chocolate, but it wasn't an option (I'm glad cause this was amazing, and I am not wild about sour cream).

The dishes (steak medium rare, and steak rare) did get mixed up. No one checked.  
We were greeted by a very friendly hostess, and we chose to sit outside.  It was gorgeous, and you can forget you're in the middle of Boston.  The restaurant is very convenient to Back Bay Station.  
Tables are pleasantly spaced apart. You can see what others are eating, but you can't hear their conversations.
Worth repeating!

I tried picadillo empanadas and plato cubano, and they were just perfect! Price is super reasonable, too. Empanadas were crispy on the outside and moist/ juicy on the inside- with their banana salsa and chili sauce, it was such a great experience. Plato cubano had juicy pork - i first thought it was chicken because it shredded so easily when i forked at it. Very flavorful in a subtle way (what i love).
I really wanted to try their desserts but i was too full and i had to go to bed a couple hours after. 
Im thinking of visiting on friday again.

Hadn't been here in years.  A good local chain, with a loyal following.
