Sweetie and I went for a pizza on a (hopefully) quiet Sunday evening.  Service was good, and friendly.  The pizza (pepperoni) was burned on one edge, but not too badly to eat.  We also got a large salad to split (eating healthy, you know...)

Our enjoyment of the evening and meal was diminished by a loud family in the next room with unruly kids.  Not the kids' fault- the parents let them run wild, throwing toys, trying to get into the kitchen, etc.  Parents were almost as bad.  We could barely hear ourselves talk at points, and almost said something to them- but I don't think either of us could have left it at a polite "please keep it down."  They clearly did not care.  

Not letting that affect the review- food and service, definitely three stars.  Just wish the parents would have controlled themselves and the kids.  Those folks- half star (at least they didn't seem to be drunk.)

It may be kind of premature to give 4 stars to a place I've only been to once and ordered just an appetizer at that. However, I think that the fact that I've given it 4 stars is proof enough that I'll be back.

Went here on Saturday with the man friend en route to a birthday party at The Tam. After scratching my head for a bit, trying to think of a cheap but yummy destination that was close to the bar, Chloe D provided the answer. Apollo it was, since I'm fairly unfamiliar with Korean food ("Like Chinese food, but spicier" was her description). 

I wanted something "light" in anticipation of Meat Week starting the next day, so I ordered the Beef Tataki off the appetizer menu. He had the Bi Bim Bop, which came out in a huge sizzling bowl and turned out to be a multicolored cornucopia of AWESOME. He expressed similar approval. 

As for my Beef Tataki? It came out looking much like pan seared tuna with a little bowl of (ponzu?) sauce, which tasted like a more vinegar-y variation of soy sauce. The beef itself was extremely tender and just the right texture. Normally I don't chow down on rare meat (due to the texture) and often get ridiculed for my tendency to order beef medium well. In this case, rare=AWESOME. The beef was served on a bed of matchstick-sized cucumber slices, which provided minutes of fun trying to dip them in the ponzu sauce. 

The staff is pretty hands-off but timely, and our food came out super-fast, so I have no issues there. The decor is offset by the giant flat screen TVs that play movies like Wanted while you eat. The bathrooms--well, not bad, but I hope that I go in warmer weather, when there's less likely to be a draft.

The prices are right, which is one of many reasons why I like eating in Chinatown. Perfect for this economy, in my opinion.

I'll definitely be back to try an entree in the near future, though. Also on the list: grilling meat over an open flame like the carnivore I am.

I've used Diem for quite a while now and overall, it's a pretty great service. The variety of products is pretty varied and competitively priced. One thing I've noticed, since I order pretty frequently, I don't think they update their stock too often. I've found products that I really like from them that the next time I would go to order, are no longer offered. Maybe it's just timing? But if you know what sort of cannabis products you like and don't have to consult with someone who knows more about the product, I think Diem is a great option. Their site is easy to use, delivery may take a while but they text you when they're on their way and it's extremely convenient.

We stopped during a long road trip.  Columbus, OH was lunch and I'm so glad that I found this place on Yelp.

My requirements were pretty simple:
- food doesn't suck
- stop doesn't take too long
- not a national fast food chain
- something for both PITA (about meals) teenager daughters who can never agree on a meal

This place met each of those requirements.

Kid 1 went with a chicken basil pasta.  I snagged a bite and it was really good.  Very big on the basil taste and the pasta was cooked perfectly.  I also liked that they used olive oil instead of butter.  She didn't want the garlic bread thing that came with her meal so I inherited that bit of yumminess even though it didn't pair well with my lobster bisque.

Kid 2 had something called a steak piada.  It was a similar to a quesadilla but different enough that the comparison ends with thin, griddled and filled.  I managed a bite and it was quite flavorful.  Good steak flavor, fresh vegetables and a little spice from the sauce.  All I managed was a single bite - she snarfed up the rest of it.

We split an order of calamari also.  Instead of rings, they cut the squid into strips and hand-breaded it before frying.  Not sure that I have ever had fresh calamari in a place that resembled a Chipotle but it was damn good.

I also ordered a parmesean piada as a side because I didn't think the soup would be enough for me.  That sucker was delicious!  Think about how much you enjoy those crispy pieces of melted and browned parmesean cheese that result from accidentally (or deliberately in our house) putting a little too much paresean on something before baking or broiling.  Now take that rare bite and turn it into a side dish.  Soooooo good!  Didn't really pair well with the lobster bisque but oh well - both were delicious in their own rights and the kids ate most of my soup anyway.

Hey there Piada people - if you read this review please add St. Louis to your list of coming locations!

Beautiful selection. Great sales as  and design staff. Unfortunately , everything goes downhill from there. Delivery times are long...not unusual for quality furniture. but very unreliable. Ship dates are not met and the customer is not advised. Complaints and issues do not seem to be taken seriously by the management. Love the product. We have furnished three homes with them. Just cannot take the lackluster, non responsive follow up service any longer. Premium prices should also include premium service. That is not the case with this store.

I love the food and most of the people here.  I go out of my way to recommend them to others and I have given them a good review before. However, today I had a horrible experience with the coffee roaster at the store.  

I was walking along Hastings and stopped by at Pallet Coffee for a coffee.  It occurred to me that I could also have lunch at Basho.  So I go in with my almost empty Pallet coffee and ordered a tuna tataki lunch set.  I tipped generously.  It was delicious.  

Then, as I was enjoying my meal, the barista with the sweet mustache comes to my table to tell me, "just so you know we also serve coffee."  That caught me completely off guard.  I was embarrassed and put off that he felt the need to school me.  So I went to order a coffee from Basho.  When he comes to bring me my coffee I asked him to please not make someone feel bad for deciding to stop by their shop for lunch.  He replied that it was "common sense" not to go to a cafe with another coffee. I told him that they had no sign telling people not to bring in outside food.  To me, I was just enjoying my day supporting two local businesses I love (one I love less now).  I just happened to be at pallet coffee first, and I wanted a basho lunch.  Not to mention my cup was almost empty by the time I got to basho (picture attached). If they had put a sign asking people not to bring in outside food I would've respected that and found a garbage can outside to throw it away. 

While this experience by no means put me off Basho, I have to leave a review that is reflective of the service I received.  

Food=good, service=could see improvement, lesson=don't bring in your coffee.

Visited Urban Farmer on a Saturday night to celebrate a friend's birthday.  Our group was looking for a nice place to go for some cocktails.  I had mixed feelings over our experience here.  

Urban Farmer is located inside of the Nines, literally.  It's kind of smack dab in the middle of everything, so you have hotel rooms that look out over Urban Farmer.  It did provide some entertainment because where we were seated we could see a dance party going on in one of the hotel rooms.  

Urban Farmer is kind of split into a few different spaces.  It made it a little confusing at first because there's not really a sign to let you know that you for sure found the restaurant.  You first get off the elevators and walk into a big open space that has more casual seating and tables.  Really it's more like a lobby.  You don't actually find the hostess desk until you walk through the lobby-esque space, where there is then a partial wall that creates a separate where there is more traditional restaurant seating and the bar.  There was also a billiard room, but it stayed pretty busy the whole time we were there. 

I started off with one of their signature cocktails, the Matador.  It was a very tasty drink, consisting of El Jimador, Triple Sec, Brandy, Hot Monkey, orange, lime and mole bitters. After that I went with the First Course, which has Smirnoff Pear, St Germain, Prosecco, and a meat wrapped fig.  I decided I needed a snack with my drink.  

If you can make the timing work out, it sounds like they have a happy hour menu worth checking out.  I would especially recommend that since drinks and food there is on the more pricey side.  

As for service, we sat out in the open lobby type space.  The first waitress that helped us was very friendly and took great care of us.  Part way through the evening she was replaced by another waitress.  She was a bit cold towards us and then it took quite a while to have her bring us our bill.

Absolutely wow! Ambience is PERFECT for a date night, even a first date! The interior design is upscale and modern, with dim lighting. Best part of the night was the service, we had the best server who was able to answer all our questions and make the perfect recommendations. 
You will find a very unique selection of cocktails that is suitable for any palate. We had the purple rain, which was just the right amount of sweetness and the aroma of honey was a great taste in the mouth. We also ordered the green seed, tequila and fresh kiwi, very yummy! Both cocktails came with a rose petal on top! 
Appetizers: the baked mussels were phenomenal, they are served warm and the topping mixture of Japanese Mayo, eel sauce, massif, and scallion perfectly complemented the mussel. The fresh yellow tail was thinly sliced with a hint of wasabi and lemon zest and cilantro that left a great finish in the mouth. Our favorite appetizer was the truffle aioli fresh salmon. No need to dip in soy sauce as it came plated with the right amount of nikiri sauce. The salmon WILL MELT in your mouth. If you want to try a fish in the fatty side, I would also recommend the sea trout. 

Entrees:
If you are not picky about the fish type and want to try a variety, I recommend the signature dish which came with sake salmon, hamachi, Masai, kampachi, chutoro, and A5 wagyu beef. ALL SO DELICIOUS and no need to dip in soy sauce. You will be more than satisfied with the freshness of the fish and it is worth every penny. As for rolls, we ordered the spicy tuna crispy rice. If you are willing to try something less traditional this is the perfect roll. You still get the classic spicy tuna taste with a twist of crispy texture. The shrimp tempura and eel roll is filled with a very big shrimp tempura in the middle. The Negi salmon roll had salmon in the inside with tuna and yellow tail on top of the roll to give you that extra flavor. 

We will definitely be back and highly recommend anyone who wants an excellent sushi dining experience!

The only reason this didn't get 5 stars was for the service.  Although I understand they are superrrrrrrrr busy and the place is veryyyyyyyyy small. But they should have more staff to serve tables.  There was only one person outside for 10 tables.  Other than that the food was AWESOME!!!!! This was the second time we tried going here because the first time the wait was soooooo long.  The manager kept coming outside to let us know they are waiting for a table and being we were the only people waiting alone for quite sometime I would have thought he would have at least offered an app or something on the house.  We did wait very patiently.  So onto the important stuff...the food! 

We ordered curry cakes, paradise beef, spicy BBQ, thai roll and pad thai.  The only push back on the food we had was with the spicy BBQ because it was served with a cucumber salad which was HEAVYYYY o the red onion.  The pad thai was incredible.  Everything was really great too. DEFFFFF GOING BACK.

For as long as I can remember, I have fought the natural curl in my hair. If it made pretty little ringlets, perhaps I wouldn't have tried so hard to make it smooth and straight, but with the random curl-frizz-wave fiesta on top of my head, letting it do its own thing was just  not an option. But following some trips where my styling tools were not readily available, I began to appreciate the benefits of having a curl-friendly 'do. Which is where Vain Salon, and the incomparable Teddy Baker, come in. Thanks to Yelp reviews, I made an appointment with Teddy while visiting town from Reno. She immediately recognized the problems (and a few it wouldn't have even occurred to me could be solved) and proceeded to give me a cut that was the answer to my prayers. That cut lasted for the several months it took me to make another trip to Austin, and a trip to Vain is now part of my regular list of must-do's when I'm in town. The last time I was in there, Teddy was being observed by a young stylist, and explained everything she did to my hair and the reason behind it. It had to be one of the most fascinating experiences I've ever had in a salon. So go to Vain, and see Teddy if you can. You won't regret it!

I'd been looking forward to trying Chick-a-Biddy for some time, having read about it in the press and hearing good things from others. Some dear friends f mine, who I'd not seen in many months drove quite a distance to meet me in Atlantic Station (a fun destination) and met me at Chick-a-Biddy. 

The hostess was friendly and courteous; we were seated right away. Our server arrived promptly, but then... It was downhill (from a service perspective) from there on out.

The ladies ordered first and then I ordered the house-made pimento cheese appetizer for us to share, and then ordered my entree. 

30 minutes later....

The appetizer arrived and three minutes after that our entrees arrived. What an insult to a customer's intelligence. Did you forget to put in the order or did the chef not look to see that an appetizer was ordered? 

I was entertaining friends and was so incredibly embarrassed. I had to apologize for the wait AND it made me late getting back to work. The only thing that's keeping me from being boiling hot mad is that I had such a delightful time with my old friends.

The server didn't acknowledge the delay, didn't apologize for the delay, never told us his name, I don't remember ever seeing a smile...I know it's just a cafe, but really?!

The food was good. I had the Fried Chicken Sandwich--an obvious attempt to reproduce the Chick-fil-A sandwich, but tasty. My friend had the fish tacos (which she said were amazing!) and my other friend had the Fried Chicken Tenders Platter (which she also said was very good). 

The pimento cheese was good, too (But, from where I was sitting, the components were pre-sliced veggies, store-bought crackers, and factory-shredded cheese...not exactly what I would call "house-made", but it was good.).

No time for dessert...I had to get back to the office (and had to call to say I would be later than I'd indicated earlier). 

The restaurant was busy, but not packed and there was no line. And in fact, the couple that was seated before us left by time our appetizer arrived at our table. I don't know if they were served or just got tired of waiting. It was bad enough that I was entertaining friends and had to wait so long...I can't imagine if I was entertaining a client or on a business lunch! 

I do NOT like to write negative reviews, but I'm making an exception in this case. Not cool, Chick-a-Biddy! You embarrassed me in front of my friends AND made me late. Not cool at all. I tipped my usual 20%, but not because it was deserved, but because I wouldn't embarrass my friends the way the restaurant embarrassed me.

I won't be back to Chick-a-Biddy, but I do want to visit their sister restaurant Bantam + Biddy at Ansley Mall. Fingers crossed!

We have employed GW Construction on a number of different occasions, and have been more than satisfied with the work they provide.  Owner Orvill Garren is  a licensed contractor, an excellent craftsman, an extremely hard worker, and does a job right, paying great attention to detail.   

We've had his company do all kinds of work for us, including roofing, drywall work, electric fan installation, and all kinds of home repairs.  We were provided with reasonable estimates, and the work was done on time.   We have always been pleased with the quality of work.

I can't say enough good things about Orvill and his company.  I don't think there are many things that he can't do, and I highly recommend this company.

Located in the Hotel Vancouver, right next door to the Omega store.  I've worked in the CBD all these years and have not walked into here in all this time.

Lots of stuff for women, and some of it was quite nice I must admit.  Not that I looked very closely at it.

There is next to nothing here for men.  They only carry accessories such as shoes, ties, wallets, cologne, etc.  Nothing for you to put onto your upper body.  I scratch my head as to why they would do this???  There is a Leone in town, and they do carry crazy expensive stuff for men, so why wouldn't this store???

There were a couple of very nice ties tho.

So my review will have to be for the merchandise selection available to men.  Not a whole heck of a lot.

The staff was friendly enough to me.

These guys are by far the BEST auto mechanic in Vancouver. As long as I live in this city, I won't go anywhere else.

After working late on a Wednesday night, I found that my alternator had died. I managed to make it to Fowlers by 7:50pm, just before they were closing. They made a rush trip over to Lordco to pick up a replacement alternator for my CRV just before Lordco closed at 8pm! And after that they worked late to get my new alternator installed so I'd have a car to drive for work the next day. To top it off they even gave me a labor discount, incredible.
 
These guys provide great service, are friendly/excellent to deal with, have the best rates in the city and will go out of their way to help their customers out. I have had nothing but great experiences with Fowler.

Growing up in Buda...and living just a few miles down the road from the Salt Lick...I probably took it for granted in my earlier years.  I can honestly say up until the last 5 years of so I could leave it or take it...and didn't necessarily get all the fuss...

Maybe it's nostalgia...maybe it's that they took care of us when we had a small party reservation post our nuptials...but they've definitely won me over.

Scanning the reviews - I see there's a bit of a love hate relationship with Salt Lick.  Being the Libra I am, I can see both sides.  There's a lot of accolades and notoriety (travel and food network celebs!) for this place.  Can it live up to all the hype and expectations??  Probably not for everyone...  However, I do think they indeed do have some real winners...and hence all the fuss.  As for myself, I'm a fan of the pork ribs, the sausage, the unique sauces, the pickles, the cobblers, and the unique hill country locale.  Their brisket is honestly not my favorite (I echo the Rudy's extra moist sentiment).

Good to know cash only and BYOB.  (Oh yeah, I like the occasional bring your own event...it's like going to a friend's BBQ.)

These guys are the TRUTH!!

Very Honest and good people!! 

i come here for my routine oil change and tune up. or if anything is wrong with my car. these are the guys to see!! A small shop and a little hard to see from no 5 road but a great place none-the-less.

They'll never tell you any bullshit u don't wanna hear. They will tell you exactly what you need to fix your car. and they will sell it to you for a very good price including labor! Ive saved more money here in 1 year then i did in Canadian Tire and the GM dealership put together. (appx $8.600 i saved!! or more! )

so then next time your car is being a DIva?? pls consider All Tune! you'll be glad you did! 

We need more people like you!

After picking up hubby from the airport, we wandered and found this place for a late dinner. It was actually more upscale than we realized and feared we may not be seated with Mark A. in a t-shirt. Luckily, they gave us seats at the bar. 

Omg, amazing food! The duck breast crust was delicious! I couldn't get over it. It came with a side of brussel sprouts, done wonderfully. 

It's fun sitting at the bar, watching the bartenders do their thing. It's like an added show to your dinner experience that you didn't have to pay for. Mark surely enjoyed it since he wasn't planning on ordering a drink, but the bartenders' magic lured him in. I don't think he was disappointed either. Great drink, according to the bourban fan that he is.

I opened up a Yelp account a couple of years ago, but I never reviewed any of the establishments that I frequent.  Today, I specifically re-activated my account to write a negative review of Leon's Full Service.  

I moved to Decatur about 6 months ago, and I have been to Leon's on 5-6 occasions.  Of these trips, I have eaten about half the time, the other times were reserved for a quick drink or two.  The times I have eaten there, the food was very good.  I have had the lamb burger and the scallops.

The decor and ambiance at Leon's is very nice as well.  The bar area is beautiful.  They have a wide selection of drinks whether you are looking for spirits, beer, or wine.  

My complaint is in the snooty service.  Every time I have been here, the server or bartender has been rude and condescending.  I understand that I may not have the palate of Anthony Bourdain,, but I have eaten in some nice restaurants in my day and every time I have been to Leon's I've been made to feel like a second-class citizen who doesn't deserve to eat or drink in their presence.  Without going into details, I'll say that today was the proverbial "straw that broke the camel's back" and I will not be coming back to Leon's anytime soon.  

Peace out Leon's.  You've lost my business.

Do not use this company. Scheduled a window cleaning, received a call late the night before cancelling. Rescheduled for a week later, NO SHOW, no answer when I called. Received phone call from the manager who offered a discount and I agreed to try one more time. The "crew" of 2 showed up but looked at my windows and determined they could not do the high windows and suggested I reschedule when they could bring a taller ladder. They should have all the needed equipment to clean upper windows on a two story home; I wasted three Saturday mornings and got nothing to show for it. Terrible, unreliable and unprepared. Would never recommend them to anyone.

As we all know, the Oasis and Billy's are sub par. Let's just put that out there up front. My boyfriend and I have been incredibly hesitant to try Soleil, and that is unfortunate because we had a superb experience there tonight. 

It is true, they have hired a new chef and rolled out a new menu - and this was an excellent choice, because everything we had tonight was simply divine! 

I had the Hippie Hollow Punch, which was an wonderful cocktail that tasted like bananas, midori, and pineapple all at the same time..very good. We were served bread, as well as an appetizer which was crab meat with fingerling potatoes in a small ice cream cone shell with a tasty Asian inspired sauce as a compliment of the chef that was very, very good. 

For our entrees, we had the Marinated Chicken Papardelle - a pasta dish with chicken, olives, wide noodles, and an array of other tasty things that was a very nice combination and an excellent dish. My cohorts had a mushroom inspired pasta dish, that unfortunately I don't know by name because it is not listed on the online menu - but was very well done and the Pan Roasted Duck Breast. The duck was incredibly succulent, seared to a medium well and placed atop a squash mash that was a perfect pairing to the duck. My Dad ordered this, and asked me to use the words "truly content" in my review. For dessert, we ordered the blueberry tartlet and the brownie with red velvet cake ice cream - both were superb. 

As long as I've been in Austin, I've wanted so badly to have the exact experience at the lake that I received tonight - a beautiful view with the great Austin cuisine experiences that I have grown to love. The service was spot on and the atmosphere was luminescent. I am so surprised by my experience, it shouldn't blow me away that *someone* finally got a restaurant in the Oasis "cove" correct but it does. I really and truly hope that Chef David Burton Sanchez is around to stay! I'd also like to mention... now I will not be hesitant to take guests up to the lake for dinner..yay!!!!

The food here was really tasty! I especially liked the bruschetta because they wood fired the bread, roasted the tomatoes and used goat cheese instead of mozzarella. So creamy! 

My husband had the broccoli, chicken and Alfredo and I had the veal and beef tortellini. Both were really good and exactly what we were looking for. 

The service was just OK. We had a reservation and there seemed to be a lot of confusion from some of the people that were walk-ins as to why others were being seated first. Also, people were just standing in the doorway crowding the entry and forcing people checking in to crowd the diners. But I didn't really blame the restaurant for that. It was the patrons' fault for not waiting outside like everyone else. 

Our waitress was nice, but did the bare minimum as far as service. 

All in all, I'd definitely go back for the tasty food but I wouldn't go expecting stunning service (even with a reservation).

Qoola gets 3 stars and here is why:

- The yogurt and the toppings are awesome. I'd recommend this low calorie snack to anyone. 5 stars here.

3 stars:
- It always appears to be a DISASTER in Qoola. You have to wait in a short line for like 15 minutes to place your order... what the hell is up with that anyway? A 3 minute endeavour always turns into 15 minutes of waiting for no good reason. Honestly, Qoola, you need to redesign your layout and train your staff because both sort of suck. 

- The people. My god the people that are in there. Not Qoola's fault, it's the West End's fault, but seriously, stop bumping in to me, breathing into my ear and bringing your dog in a bag to a food establishment.

My completely made up list of what a junk removal service needs to be cool includes:

   Friendly and actually useful website
   Ability to book within a reasonable amount of time
   Friendly staff
   Great communication
   Fast, but not rushed service
   Clean, hygienic and educated guys
   Accurate -ish estimate
   Arrival within the provided time window
   Guys who know what they're doing
   Option to pay with CC

General niceness is awesome too. And they check all the marks above.

I needed to get rid of a bunch of old or otherwise hard-to-move stuff. An old crib frame. An oddly-shaped piece of furniture. Terrible sofa bed. Breaking apart bookshelf. Among others.

So I visited their website, booked about a week in advance (mostly to give me time to clean up stuff, but they had appointments available pretty much the next day). The guys called me 20 minutes before my estimated time window, said they'd arrive in 40 or so. They actually arrived in 30, nice!

  - So, is there anything in addition to what you told us on the website?
  - Actually yeah. If possible I'd also like to get rid of this, and this, and that...
  - Sure, no prob. We charge you by volume, and I estimate it's going to be this much $$$, probably a little bit less. Shall we?
  - OK!

Note: they're not on the cheap side. But considering what they took, how they did it (promptly, carefully, etc) and that they ticked all the above marks, it was not expensive either. Very fair, if I may.

They were *lots* of things. But these guys managed to do it in just 2 elevator trips. Wife and I joked that "Tetris Champions" was probably one of the requirements when hiring  . "Hey, what if you take this from the balcony as well?" "Yeah, sure!". Nice.

Came back. "Hey, it's actually going to be a little bit less $$. Credit card? OK! You absolutely don't have to tip if you don't want to, but if you want, it can also be with your CC... Email receipt? There we go, thanks, see you!"

Will 100%, without a doubt, call them again if I need to. Thank you so much!!

We came to Elder Tree on a Saturday night at about 10:30. We had stopped at a few places in EAV and popped in for a drink and an appetizer. This had the feel of an old pub or bar and it seemed like it was full of regulars. This place is no frills and compared to some of the other places in the neighborhood was pretty basic in its beer and liquor selection. 

The menu was irish-inspired and since we didn't order a lot of food, I can't really give an adequate review

I had a Guinness and we ordered the loaded chips (which I stupidly thought would be chips and instead were fries). It was late and the kitchen was about to close, which was obvious in the food. It honestly wasn't very good. 

The service was wonderful, which is why I am giving it 3 stars. 

All in all, it was just okay.

Not being someone that knows much about cocktails, this place had me intrigued as we walked in and I definitely want to return. Wether it be on a date or to meet some friends here before heading to dinner downtown, I liked it!
Prices were reasonable, the staff were friendly and I kind of wish it were closer so I didn't have to drive downtown to get to it! I think it's in a fine location though. The outdoor seating is nice, I wish they had a few more tables for the summer- but maybe they do and haven't put them out yet? Not a negative though, because there are plenty of seats inside as well. It's a long, rectangular room...well...bar. So there are tables you can sit at by the window or hop right up to the bar instead. 
I love that they do have a menu for food as well. I'm not someone that can sit around sipping on booze without munching on something, so they have charcuterie plates and such that looked nice and I'd be interested in trying out next time.

The heb is my grocery store of choice, mostly b/c it's affordable and has 95% of the daily stuff I need.

But when I'm looking for something slightly out of the ordinary and have an hour to spare, I happily zoom over to CM.  On a recent occasion, I needed watercress and none were to be found at the heb so wala! an excuse for a CM excursion.  It's a carnival in there with little mazes.  Maybe not so great if you come here on a time crunch.  Especially since you might use up those minutes looking for parking.  However, when I'm here, it feels like I'm in the travel channel of the food world.

Enough, I'm sure you get the picture.  So overall, I did find some watercress and my foodie curiosity was quenched until my next excuse for a CM trip.  
 
CM -an open library of foods/drinks of all kinds and just down the road from me, how great!!

Very good Mexican food! love the place, will def make this a regular joint!
Went on a Friday eve, was very crowded, had to wait for 20 min for a table. We were started off with some nachos and salsa for the table. We ordered the black bean soup cup just for appetizer, Veggie Fajitas and Poblano Chiles for the mains. The soup was very mediocre but the 2 mains were fabulous. The quantity was humongous & we ended up packing half of it. The staff is very polite and courteous. For 2 people the tab was $28 and it was enough for 2 meals.

I really enjoyed going to this location. My cohort in the school psychology program all decided to go out and have drinks after our last final on Monday. We arrived at about 7 PM. And it was about 10 of us at a table. The waitress was nice and as attentive as she could be. They appear to be pretty busy so she had other things to do. However our drinks came on time and our food came equally as on time. 

I really enjoyed the free chips and salsa! Always a plus! The chips were very, what I call, durable. Lol. They were warm and they were thick enough that they could dip and cheese and salsa and not break into 1 million pieces. The waitress came with multiple bowls of chips over time and was very conscious of what we needed.

We ordered margaritas and beers and the waitress was able to offer my friend a really good ale that she never had before. My phone was very impressed with the selection enjoyed it. We sat outside it was a little chilly but still nice. It was clean and it wasn't too loud even though it was facing a busy street.

I ended up only having a regular margarita because I had to dip out early. But it was very tasty though I felt like I could've had a little bit more tequila. That may just be the exams talking! Overall, I would definitely return. They have half-price appetizers during happy hour in a really good drink specials. The crowd was younger two older grad students which I really enjoyed and big ups to this place love it!

This zoo is located in the hills in Northwest Portland close to the Japanese Garden and Rose Garden.  Parking is paid at meters like most of the parking in Portland; plan to pay $6.40 which is the daily maximum.  Adult tickets (12 and up) are $14.95 and kids tickets (3 to 11) are $9.95.

This is a smallish zoo that that has most of everything.  I did not see African Elephants, Gorillas or Pandas here.  Most animals were in view but were not able to see the Cheetahs or Painted Wild Dogs.  It was raining about half the time I was here so some animals retreated into their dens.

It took me about 4.5 hours to see the zoo but you should plan to be there for 6 hours or so.  The food and snacks were expensive as expected so come after breakfast.  The animals I liked the best here were the Polar Bears and Sea Otters.  Four stars!

Been able to come back from time to time since August but not as often due to the COVID19. Over time since my last update, things has gotten a little better. 

Despite the COVID19, there's still the same amount of people still coming and going.

The one thing I noticed is that prices are still kinda ridiculous. One of the things about this store is that they had always been sort of like Value Village in terms of prices and sadly, the prices still isn't great. Not the worst but still could use some improvements.  


This place is still a relatively okay place if all you wanna do is poke around.

I would review this facility based on level of care, however I'm finding it impossible to even get an appointment. They emailed me a consent form to fill out and return, and I returned three copies with each filled out for a different hospital or doctor. According to the email correspondence, all three requests for medical records have yet to be replied to, and it has been 30 days at this writing. The person I am in contact with does not seem to think it's unusual that all three requests have gone unanswered, and she gives no indication that WP&S plans on exerting any effort to find out what happened. It's the oddest admission policy I've ever encountered - first of all for assessing people sight unseen, and secondly I seem to be getting stone walled by a less than competent office drone who has a condescending email style. It's infuriating. I have real, chronic pain going on, and these people want to play games. Very unprofessional.

On the one hand, I really love fast food, though I don't have it very often anymore. If I had to choose, though, it'd be Jack in the Box, or McDonald's.

It was about 2 am.

Lucky, 24 Diner was closed for their weekly deep cleaning, and lucky, Jack in the Box is one of those 24-hr places! I had a craving for curly fries.

Some guy with a gruff voice took my order via the drive-thru, and when I rambled out my order, I swear I sat their for a coula minutes wondering where he went! I wasn't sure if he was still there, cuz I didn't get a confirmation response.

I ordered a coffee. I opened the lid and tasted it, and it had almost cooled down to room temperatutre; the curly fries weren't hot, but they weren't cold, either. Same with the sandwich. 

I didn't bother complaining about the coffee since there was a huge line of (assumably plastered!) people behind me who prob had the munchies, and the worker would prob have had to brew the coffee and make me wait for it! I figured - what the heck - this is Jack-in-the-Crack after all!

I took everything back to the hotel room, and devoured everything as if I hadn't eaten in days...

....sooooo the food did it's job even if it wasn't perfect, and I ran the coffee through the coffee pot, so I was a lot happier.

I love Jack-in-the-Crack cuz of their Sourdough Jack, Curly Fries, and the fact that they're open 24-hours.

They could have gotten 3-stars, though, cuz I have also been to ones that were actually better.

We were very excited to try this place. We had four in our party and we all ordered burgers, and we split a basket of fries and a basket of onion rings. The fries came out well before the burgers and they were okay at best. The fries on top were fresh but the bottom were "bits" and well stale. We finished the fries before the burgers arrived. ALL our burgers were not cooked fresh as they were all medium but dry and lukewarm. We were almost done with our burgers when we were asked if everything was okay and we mentioned we hadn't seen our onion rings and they delivered what they stated was only half a basket and that they were working on the other half. The onion rings were hot and tasty saving this place from a one star review. Disappointing.

I'm going to give it a 3 for now, but it may be more of a 3.5.  We went for the buffet lunch.  Everything I tried was pretty good flavorwise, although if you like spicy it was pretty limited in that department. I don't, so I was okay with the spice level.  Some of the chicken on the buffet was a little dried out, but it is a buffet after all so I'm not expecting perfection in food that is sitting out.  The wait staff was very attentive while we were there, so previous reviews noting problems in this area may have been there on an off day or while they were still working out kinks.  I'd definately be interested in going back to try out some of their menu items and seeing how those compare.

Good scenery, good food and does not cost an arm & a leg (easy to do in Coal Harbour) Great if you are in the hood, don't need to park anything and are OK with mediocrity. 

Patio faces North so gets cold as soon as the sun disappears, and if you need the Loo, you have to go to the Public park washrooms next door.

If you are in the area and can't make it any farther it will do good, as long as you don't set your expectations too high.

To put it simply this place is just not my cup of tea. 

I was served in a decent time frame by friendly enough staff. I found a seat...my tab was respectable. They did not have $1 PBR as other yelp reviews would lead you to believe, did I need to use a secret knock? 

Somewhere in-between the neon decor and random old men in cowboy hats this place just lost me. Which is strange because normally both of those things sit really well with me. Not to mention that I'm a dive bar enthusiast. 

I came to see a show, which is conveniently located in another room. When you walk into the room it's like stepping into a whole new establishment. You leave the busy decorations at the door and step into a really nice venue area. That part of Kellys I enjoyed, and i would go back to see a show. 

Sorry, that I'm not sorry Kellys I just wasn't feeln' ya.

Tasty authentic home made Greek food served up in a super friendly casual atmosphere. I started out taking pictures of our apples but got totally engulfed in our delicious meal that I completely forgot to take pictures of our 3 entrees (roast lamb, kebab & chicken souvlaki). All that was left were empty dishes to show for it. Bob was pleased with our stacks of empty plates. Then it was time for dessert. Wow!! Huge servings...good to share. This place is definitely worth coming back to try their other dishes!

Love this new Japanese restaurant with an American modern flair. Came here with my wife and son and we felt like we were treated with royalty.

Located inside the Terminus, where MF Buckhead used to be.  The decor was top notch, the vibe was excellent, and ambiance was delightful.  We had their Osaka style tiered sushi which was amazing!  Also tried a sampling of several other of their dishes.  Had a chance to meet their manager Eric and also the owners who were very upstanding individuals.  Amura knows what they are doing, having several years experience and success in Orlando, Florida and I believe their attention to quality and detail as well as service and delicious food shows and make a winning combination.

All in all, I'm happy to announce they are an awesome restaurant and I wish them the best of luck in Buckhead and hope they are here to stay!

Note : they had a very kid friendly atmosphere and had a kid menu.  So makes the restaurant very family friendly yet upscale enough to feel like a very high quality restaurant and great for dates or to impress clients.  Price points were reasonable.  Look to spend roughly $40 a person.  
Park with the valet or park in the deck and they validate parking.

Will be back again.  2 thumbs up, way up and 5 solid yelp stars for me.

best wishes to them.

Lunch pre-covid 

Udon not pictured. Flavor of the broth was good and the noodles were tasty! Coming from someone who doesn't usually like udon or fish based broths it was surprisingly good and not at all fishy! 

I really liked the skewers, they tasted fresh and were very flavorful! The jambi has a good marinade and the sausage was very juicy. The dumplings had a great crispy fried skin and the filling was juicy! The meat looked cute on the skewers but it was much easier to eat after taking them off the stick. 

Service was also great and they gave us enough time to look over the menu as we waited for the rest of our party. Food all came at around the same time despite ordering different foods and it was all hot and fresh.

I loveddddd Verts. The snack sized kabops were one of my favorite lunch items in town. When Verts took on an investment, everything went downhill. New name, totally new menu, and no more kabops (WTH?!). Sadly Noon's changes were all for the worse and now I don't even go there to eat anymore. So thankful that Cava just opened three locations across Austin. It's 10x better. PS I still miss Verts, please change back to your old concept otherwise Cava is going to take all the Mediterranean bowl business in town.

Last nite my girlfriend, 2 of my best friends and  4 others (  all tourists )ventured  down to  Dinner at P F Changs.. we  arrived at 7:15 and the place was  quite busy.   I realized I left my phone in the car,  told the valet and shortly there after  he retrieved the phone and brought it to my table.  Excellent valet ,,,,

  I started with chicken lettuce wraps,,  they were very good,  we did have to ask for extra lettuce.  The waitress was quite good, and the attention to detail is what make most chains like   P F  Changs a success.  They are detail oriented.  What  is difficult for most  mom and pop restaurants are the little things,,  customer service is so so important in todays fast pace  society.  P F  Chang  does a quality job I must say.

 I ordered  the Sea Bass on a bed of Spinach.  My dish was outstanding.  Even my girlfriend tried a bite,,  just so you know, Kimberly eats no  seafood outside of  shrimp,,  but asked for a bite and I recommended the crusted edges to give her the least fishy taste and she actually enjoyed  the flavor. Of course I avoided giving her a center cut  bite which was  moist and delicious. As for her  spicy chicken dish,,  I had a taste,  it was good, not real spicy  though but tasty as well.  My friends all enjoyed there meal as well.  
 
 There were a couple issues with dropped  / broken plates next to the table, the waitress was quick to make sure  the table was  OK, and quick to apologize.  Things happen,,, and the staff was quick to respond both times.  

 We left and went  to Pete's Piano bar for  a couple hours,, came back and pick up the  car  from the valet at midnight,  the car was out front  waiting.. 

  Although  PF  Changs  wouldn't be  my first choice for Chinese in Austin,,  for friends visiting and wanting to visit the entertain district I highly recommend  it.  It definitely  American  Chinese,  but,, heck,, they do it  very well,, and from a service standard it was a  5 star evening.

In town visiting my son and needed a quick bite and a beer on a Saturday night.  Found myself in CitySide.  Mostly college crowd and I'm a bit north of my college years but I did not at all feel out of place here.  In fact the bar tenders were friendly and welcoming.  Good atmosphere, good food (I had the Rattlers which is basically a baked buffalo chicken wrap and man it hit the spot and I'm looking forward to ordering it again), decent draft beer selection but I'm easy to please on that account, juke box music was fine and not so loud that we couldn't talk....what more do you want?  Will make this a regular stop when I'm in town.

I stayed here late one night just to be safe from driving in snow and ice. I found the place through my maps gps. My maps said it would be $50, their website says $65, when I got to the counter they told me it was $80.
When I told them their website said $65 the person behind the desk argued with me saying they wouldn't ever post that on their website... well clearly they don't look into it as I screen shot it. They still didn't uphold what their advertising said.

I mean it was a quiet decent stay... I knew this wasn't the Ritz... but the pricing thing and the way it was handled I found it to be misleading and unprofessional-
As a paying customer, I really value honesty and integrity and I left feeling as if I had been ripped off and I was very disappointed at the level of integrity in which this business conducts itself.

I was feeling sluggish after eating pizza, burgers and French fries the previous nights while visiting in Boulder. Don't get me wrong, it was amazing while I was eating it, but the after-effects are not so great. So I was craving some good, wholesome healthy food for our last night. I popped into Zeal and was immediately impressed with the overall atmosphere, which was on-trend without being unwelcoming. It was around 8:59 PM and to my dismay, the hostess informed me the kitchen closed at 9PM! I was confused because according to Yelp, it claimed it was open until 10 PM. However, the hostess could tell she about broke my heart and sweetly begged the chefs to make an exception for me, and to my surprise, they politely obliged! Hip-hip, hooray! I'm back in the game! Not wanting to be too much trouble, I asked for the hostess' suggestion and she steered me toward the Mighty Bowl! I opted to add some protein and fat, with chicken and avocados, and topped it with half Zeal Vinaigrette, half Tahini Dressing, also per her suggestion! Boy was she on the money! It was not only beautiful to look at, but deliciously tasty and completely filling to boot! I also ordered their Lavender Lemonade which was sprinkled with lavender buds and refreshingly cleansed the palette, making it a perfect paring to my bowl. And because I just can't help myself, I also snuck in the Mother Earth organic smoothie to go, and I'm pretty sure my hair grew 2 inches after sucking that thing dry in a minute flat. The total was a little over $31, which may seem a bit steep for one person, but given the farm-to-table provisions and organic, locally-grown fare, I'd consider it quite reasonably priced. And there's truly no comparison to how nourished and incredible I felt after consuming such fresh ingredients! Thank you for squeezing me in, I'm so happy I ended my weekend here in Boulder with such a savory spread!

went here on a weekday night, no wait. parking is TERRIBLE. food was good for the all you can order. keep in mind it's not their whole menu, it's just select items. for their special rolls you need to add $1/each. no complaints about their service, though they did get slower as it became more packed. i also noticed how no one really came to check up on us and i regularly had to call someone or get their attention to get new menus etc etc but it didn't bother me. food quality/rolls are a lot better than minado and it's cheaper too!!

BUT - worth every penny if you want to get stuffed by sushi

This is not regarding the car device but a gas station attendant who worked on Sunday, February 28, 2016.

I'm so disappointed. We live down the street from your station and have used your services for years. We even get our car worked on there. Today one of your employees treated my mom like a criminal because the color of her skin. She was pumping gas and he came out and yelled at her because she didn't pre pay. Meanwhile, I've seen the same attendant not say a thing when a white customer didn't prepay. Horrified and shocked that in this day and time racism is alive and well

Just wanted to point out that someone from Angora wrote me a very nice email, offering to make things right.  First off, after seeing so many businesses freak out at negative reviews (er, not mine), this was pretty cool.  

I gave them a second chance, and the sandwich I had was pretty damn tasty, and my tummy was perfectly happy with it.  It seems the previous problems are no more.

I went a step further and ordered from Angora for a work event, and everyone seemed to enjoy their lunch (and I looked good!).  

So - end result?  Angora not only reached out to an unhappy customer, but that alone made me try them again, and I think we can have a happy relationship from here on.  Bad days happen to everyone, yes?  I know I have 'em...

Thanks, Angora.

I've been to this place a few times and it's probably one of the most unique food joints ever. It has your typical seating and you can order what they have on their menus with the typical bar. But what makes this place so different is the fact you can go up to this "food bar" and put together your own meal.

Of course it's limited to the size of the bowl but you can keep going up for more. And you can season it and put whatever you want with it. When you've completed your selection you bring the bowl to a circular doughnut like grill with about 3-4 cooks putting other orders together. Then they grab your bowl and throw it on the grill and keep everything in a neat wedge shape pile. They'll continue cooking it all the while throwing on the selection of flavors and seasonings you've brought up. The whole process takes about 5-15 minutes. (depending on what you're eating)

It's a pretty hot spot in my honest opinion. The only thing I don't care for is that the food selection IS out in the open, sort of like a salad bar, and there's always that possibility someone has to sneeze. Another complaint I have with the place is the floors, tables, and even handrails are sticky. Sort of like walking into a flytrap. It could be just this location though. 

Other than the sticky parts in this place, everything else is just flat out awesome. I enjoy the idea of this improv restaurant.

This place is a total diamond in the rough.  It's off the beaten path on Southwest Parkway..which is fine by me, very close to home :) I love the atmosphere, and the owners are so inviting they make you feel like you're in their home.  The food is good, desserts are amazing, and the coffee is soooo good.  It's a great place to take kids for lunch or have a nice dinner with your someone special.  They have live music and the best part? You can bring your own beer or wine.

I would like to start by saying that Adam does an excellent job, I have been extremely happy with every haircut. Unfortunately the owner's customer service practices are very poor which is why I don't plan on going back. My appointment was cancelled 2 hours and 30 minutes prior to the scheduled time - unfortunately Adam had an emergency. I was given the option to have my haircut done by Debbie (the owner, who was available at my appointment time) as long as I was ok with paying what she charges, which, for a haircut, is $100 (I am not kidding). Since I don't live in College Park and I had planned my entire day around my hair appointment I kindly asked if she would consider doing the haircut at Adam's price ($65) considering my appointment had been cancelled with only a few hours in advance. Her answer was NO. They have a 48 HOURS cancellation policy, so if you have an emergency and have to cancel your appointment "a full fee will be charged to your credit card" (see their website). However, if something comes up and THEY have to cancel on you, they don't even try to meet you half way. Again, Adam is great, but what happened left me quite disappointed and I am never going back.

I was looking for an Italian restaurant that wasn't part of a chain and my GPS led me to this gem.  It's nestled in a small shopping center, but what a treat it was.  Lola's is tastefully decorated and has an extremely homey feel.  It was very clean and has an intimate setting.  I was greeted promptly by Shannon who was also my server.  She was very attentive and was sure to point out everything is made from scratch using the owners recipe's.

I started off with a great Chianti ($9/glass) and opted not to have an appetizer.  A nice basket of fresh, warm garlic bread was brought to my table and I  decided on the Veal Parmigiana ($28).  Speaking of magic, the veal parmigiana was amazing!  It is described as "triple-breaded", but you would have never guessed it.  It was a nice sized portion and it came with a light breading and was topped with  and was topped with mozzarella & provolone cheeses.  It was also topped with with a delicious homemade red sauce.  It came with a side of spaghetti and fresh vegetable of the day.  I didn't want this meal to end and I savored every bite.

What's unique about this restaurant, is that you must go through the kitchen to use the rest room and the kitchen was spotless.  You can also chat with the owner as she is there every day and she is very personable.  Where i sat, you can actually see partially into the kitchen and watch the chef work his magic.

I highly recommend this restaurant, not only for the food, but for the atmosphere and the whole overall experience.

I haven't been to Boston Market in a long time, and after tonight's experience, I remember why. The customer service at this location is deplorable.  My friend & I ordered the 2 for $20 Deal they're promoting. My friend ordered Meatloaf, Stuffing, & Squash Casserole.  I ordered the Chicken Pot Pie.  The woman taking our order wasn't sure if the Pot Pie was included.  She asked someone on her headset and was told that it was... I told her what sides I wanted and she emphatically said it didn't come with sides. (This is from the person that didn't even know  the pot pie was included in the deal) I reminded her that the sign on the counter said "each Meal comes with a main course option, two classic sides and cornbread..." she said the pot pie never came with sides.  So, I ordered turkey instead with Squash Casserole & Sweet Potato Casserole.  She said it would take 10 minutes for the turkey.  I got my drink, unsweetened tea. I had to go back to the counter to get Sweet n' Low because there was none next to the fountain.  Another woman handed me Equal when I asked for Sweet n' Low.  She said that was the only sweetener they had (I stopped using Equal years ago when it was deemed the number 1 worst sweetener on the market) I drank Lemonade instead. I ate my sides while I waited for the turkey.  The sides were delicious.  My friend said the meatloaf was good.  As I was finishing the sides, a woman brought the turkey & gravy.  The turkey looked funny; nothing like "Roasted Turkey Breast" normally looks.  It was wet, it looked and tasted like it was boiled (see the picture).  It tasted awful even after soaking each piece with gravy.  I couldn't finish my meal.

Scammed me of my money. Today I went to see Dr. Lai, to see if he can get me new dentures. He did a series of imaging, just to tell me that he couldn't do anything about my implants. The tech literally jammed the mouth piece into my gums, and didn't seem to care even after I told her I was pain. Was told that it would cost me $3,500 to replace everything and got charged almost $300 just for him to tell me that there was nothing he could do. I was in and out in a total of 30 minutes. Sorry, but never again!

Service review only - The gist is, stay away!  I had my 09 M35X in three times for a groan in the steering column.  Knowing that I was about to move to the south shore, I gave up that battle and made an appointment with their main competitor, but it wasn't before my steering had started cutting out on me.  The competitor had it diagnosed in a matter of hours.  Who knows how bad things would have gooten before Herb Chambers would've solved it?  I shudder to think...

I've used Promed several times-for my son's sports physicals- which were very thorough, and for acute, non-emergent illnesses (which always seem to occur after hours or on weekends). We have always received friendly, thorough and professional care at a very reasonable cost. The clinic isn't fancy (like one urgent care I went to on HWY 620-sure, they had FLAT SCREEN tv's in the rooms but who goes to an urgent care to watch TV?) I have always been very satisfied with their care, and I am an RN myself. And no appointment required.

New hair, new life!

I swear this place has changed my hair for the better!  I get my hair done by Anna and I will never go anywhere else.  I love how honest and realistic she is.  I was told I would never be able to get my hair blonde without damaging it from previous stylists.  I am happy to say I have blonde in my hair and have been having more fun.  Anna was able to safely and healthily (if that is a word) take my hair to blonde.  My hair is healthier than it has ever been, soft and has been growing very quickly.  I cannot wait to see what other fun things we can do to my hair next. I love that they have a ring light here for awesome pictures :)  The ambiance of the salon is great too.  I love escaping reality for a few hours and being pampered.

Portland roasting coffee, 2012 coffee of the year. I'm listening! Well it is true. No copious amounts of sugar and cream for me! I would come back just for the coffee. We ordered the carrot cake pancakes with cream cheese butter (included apples and rasins) and the corn beef hash (has peppers and real corn beef) with multigrain toast. Large portions and food the iron chef would be proud of. One thing I will say is...you can really go wrong with breakfast potatoes and this place won top ten, well top 1 of 1 because I can't think of any other place that has done such an amazing potato! One of the best corn beef hashes I have ever had said the boyfriend who usually turns his nose up in the air to the thought of this being any meal of his. Wow, someone did it right and won his heart. It grew three sizes today. We sat at the large table in the middle of the establishment (montage restaurant style) and had the best breakfastiers next to us. This place officially won my potato and coffee heart. Thank you screen door for having 30 people in line and yelp for the breakfast suggestion.

This place was okay. Nothing compared to in-N-out!! the burgers are more expensive, the sauce isn't as great, and there were no onions in my burger. 

I also tried their crispy chicken burger, which is nothing compared to the ones at KFC in CHINA (like if you know what I'm talking about). 

Both the meats on the burger and chicken burger were tender, so I'll give them that. Oh yea and the fries were pretty delish. 

I got a burger, chicken burger, fries, fries and their 16oz draft beer for $21

I had read that Voodoo Donuts was overhyped and that it wasn't that good.  In the words of Jesus in the Big Labowski "Let me tell you something pendejo"  They live up to the hype and they were some of the best donuts I have ever had.  Marys Donuts in Santee is my benchmark and these things could easily hang with theirs, some of them are even better.  My wife and I ordered 2 maple bacon bars, one chocolate raised long john, an old dirty bastard and a powdered sugar cake donut.  Total for 5 donuts was $8.50.  Here is how they tasted.

Chocolate Long John-  My wife said it was good.  I did not have any of this one but she seemed to enjoy it.

Powdered Sugar-  This was your basic powdered sugar donut.  The donut had a bit of a crunch to it signifying that it was fried properly.  It was tasty.  A tad small but still really good.

Old Dirty Bastard-  This is a raised donut coated with chocolate icing, then dipped in Oreo cookie pieces, then drizzled with peanut butter.  A better name may be the "old diabetes"?  This thing was rich!  It was really good though.  You think something like this might be too gimmicky, but it wasn't. The raised donut could stand on its own, the chocolate icing was just the right amount, the Oreo pieces were plentiful and the peanut butter icing drizzled over the top to give it that extra flavor twist.  I would definitely get this again and it may have been my favorite donut of the night.

Maple Bacon Bar-  I'm usually not the biggest maple bar fan but this thing was great!  It was a great raised long john donut totally covered in maple icing.  The best part of this thing though was that it was topped with 2 thick slices of sweet/salty/crunchy bacon.  I would get this one again too.

This was their 2nd branch I guess.  I liked this one.  It was funky.  It had pinball machines in it, chairs and wrap around couches etc.  The workers were friendly and parking was right outside.  This was around 6:15pm Thursday night.  These were some great donuts!

We were looking for a place to have lunch and drinks after visiting the Aquarium. We passed by the outside menu on our way to Faneuil Hall. The sandwich menu boasted a spiced sausage and ricotta focaccia sandwich. It reeled me in and did not disappoint. The roasted red peppers and mustard aioli combined with the carmelized onions and FRESH ingredients were a nice complement to the soft, rich focaccia. Absolutely heavenly! The apple/cranberry chicken salad was creamy and bursting with fresh aromatic herbs grown from their own farm. *All produce and herbs are grown from their farm in Essex. Try the grilled flatbread pizza as an appetizer. Each bite was as flavorful as the next.
Top the experience with a cozy corner table with a view and a great bartender/waiter (Brian) and you have a great date place. Our bartender, Brian was also very knowledgable of the quality and origin of the ingredients used. He recommended a nice Reisling that was a perfect pairing to my meal. He also sent over a complimentary dessert.
Great experience. Can't wait to return.

I had heard good things about the brunch at Takoba but dined at dinner time because it was in the neighborhood, I wanted to try something new, and friends were in town for Memorial Day Weekend.  

The server sort of took a long time to bring us water and get our drink orders.  This is always my biggest pet peeve!  But if there are two tables sitting inside the restaurant it really shouldn't take THAT long.  She was really not the greatest server.

The guacamole was good, not the best, it was spicey.  I like spice but my friend couldn't handle it.  They serve the thick cut tortilla chips. Not necessarily a bad thing, but I do prefer the thinner ones. The beef tacos I had were OK.  Tacodeli makes a better beef taco, go there!  Nothing about the food here was really that impressive.  The mexican martini was good, but are those really that hard to screw up?

It was not by any means the greatest restaurant experience I have ever had but I do want to try their brunch so I will probably be back at some point in time.   Had the food been overly impressive I would have been OK with the subpar service but I have had better tacos at many many other places in Austin.

Saw previous yelp reviews and decided to give this place a try! Had no idea it was in a strip mall or that it was super divey haha. Just focused on the food pics! So I was clearly overdressed when I arrived. Regardless, staff was welcoming! We were allowed to sit anywhere. Tables were covered in white paper. We found a four top in the middle. 
Our server brought menus and was patient with our drink order and questions. I started with a cocktail and ordered appetizers for the table- gator bites, a dozen raw oysters and the boudin balls. The gator was so tender! The boudin balls were standard. The oysters were freshly shucked, served with all the fixings, and delicious. They were meaty in size. 
They serve their seafood at market price. A dozen was 13.99. But you can order a half. They also have a bucket, which has 24-28 oysters in it, not sure how much it cost. 
The dinner menu had a lot on it. We decided to go with the crab and shrimp special. Three of us shared it. It was the perfect amount of food. But I'd recommend ordering more if you don't stuff yourself with appetizers first. It was market price, $52.99. They have a bucket for the shells and little wipes for your hands. 
I had another cocktail, and ordered dessert. We tried the beignets and the cheesecake. The beignets were so good. I saw a box from cafe du monde behind the bar. So they're legit beignets. The cheesecake was standard. The praline flavor is in the crust, that's about all I could detect. It was a large slice and for only $4.99, it was a good deal. 
We paid our bill and finished our drinks. And as I was leaving, the waitress brought me a free shot of Jameson!!! How nice! And that was before she even picked up our check. I can say that's never happened before. I was thrilled. 
Restrooms are clean. Parking is the lot for the strip mall. This place isn't much to look at, that's for sure. Not a fancy date spot either. But it's right next to the mall and the cirque du soleil show (luzia). So if you're in the area and you're craving some good Louisiana style seafood, stop by! The food is fresh and the service is stellar. We will be back!

Decent seafood restaurant at a modest price point; it's not over-priced Keep it real; to get it cheaper, it would have to be frozen, breaded and fried. 

There are better restaurants, but they are super-expensive. There are cheaper but pass the Pepto.

We've had oysters, clams, shrimp, calamari, ribs, pasta and salads. All were competent and fairly priced. Every time I've had fish, it's been properly cooked (which seems to be a difficult feat for some places) and every once in awhile, they come up with a really professional twist in flavors...

This most recent trip featured a marlin with hazelnut and blackberry. 

On the downside, the salads were at least few hours old when served which is shocking. One occasion served up reheated veggies from the previous service mixed in with a freshly made... as though we wouldn't notice.

In summary, reasonably priced, most of the items are decent, but can be spotty at times.

Love this place!  Everyone that works there is really friendly and the food is yummy.  I particularly like the fact that even though it's a small cafe, they make things to order.  And they do it graciously!  I know I'm a picky cry-baby about my food, but they never even bat an eyelash when I order.

They are quick too.  I don't always have a lot of time between clients to get something to eat, but I know I can always get something nutritious and yummy PDQ when I run up there from my spa.

Def check out the super fluffy pancakes!  YUM!

I'm only speaking to the downstairs restaurant portion and my rating is based on the food only. Mediocre is too high of a rating for the dinner. Service, setting and ambience is four stars. I could never say you get what you pay for here because the food was so... well, blah. At an average of $50 a person (without drinks!) expectations were not met. They need a complete kitchen leadership overhaul. Maybe then I would go back because the place was charming and service really good.

This is my absolute favorite breakfast spot in Boston. It's a little out of the way otherwise I would go there more. The food is fantastic. It looses a few points for the extremely tight seating, you can at times be right on top of the next table. My husband and I got a pitcher of a sangria type drink and it was waaaay too much. It would have been nice to have a heads up about that before it arrived, we couldn't even make a dent.

So I have an update on this store.

Over the Thanksgiving holiday I took my 6 and 1/2-month old to my mother's house for an overnight stay. Unfortunately, my boyfriend (although he swears it was my fault) forgot to load the Pack-N-Play into the trunk of the car. My parents live out in Johnson City so we didn't have many options to just run out to the store and buy something for the baby to sleep in. (And I have just never felt comfortable having her sleeping in bed with me...all those horror stories about smothering I guess).

My two younger sisters were driving in from Austin and my mom asked them to pick something up on their way out of town. She suggested going by Wal-Mart and picking up a play pen for her to keep at her house.

But looking to save a buck my sisters stopped in to Once Upon A Child to see about buying a used play pen. The store didn't have anything but the clerk helped my sisters pick something out that would be "PERFECT for my 6 1/2 month old to sleep in."

So my sisters show up with a BASSINET. Yes, a BASSINET for my rolling, crawling, flipping 6 month old. I was appalled. My sisters don't have children so they were very clear to the clerk that they needed something safe and big enough for the baby. They even gave her my daughter's age and weight.

And they come home with a Bassinet. The clerk assured her that it would be perefect for our situation. You can not put a 6-month old in something so small and unsturdy. A newborn won't be able to roll out of the 8 inch sides but my 6-month old can just about sit up and would have thrown herself right out of it while tossing and rolling at night. I was trying to explain that to my sisters while they were trying to give the clerk the benefit of the doubt.

Until we looking inside at the warning sticker. In ALL CAPS the very first warning out of the 10 listed...DO NOT USE for children over 3 months of age or children that can roll around as bassinets will tip over.

So either the clerk was clueless about selling age-appropriate products or she knew and just thought she could make a sale to two equally clueless customers. Either way is equally disturbing. That night we put a mattress on the floor for my daughter to sleep on. I slept on the floor next to her so she didn't roll/slide herself somewhere in the room she wasn't supposed to. It was a long night for both of us.

The only plus side is that they did give us a refund on the bassinet but did not apoplogize for the mistake.

What a disgrace.

I absolutely adore this place   I have been to Olympia oyster house.  4 or 5 Times on my business trips to Portland.   My first thoughts of the decor is of Ballard's whale and walrus.   Love the look. The open kitchen area and the oyster bar is awesome. The staff is kind and sitting at the bar brings some extra treats of special details of the oysters.  Being fro the San Juan area of the pnw the Briny salty smell brought child hood memory's    

This is more than an oyster bar.  There is something there for the non oyster Eater and marlin chevez is a gifted well rounded chef.  Traveling internationally to share her gift.   

The highlights.   
The wine selection is top notch.  They are pros in pitching wines that match up with the oysters 

The smoked goat butter.  Yes it is amazing 

The phyllo ribbon wrapped oysters 

One nights special.  The salmon collar 

The house pickled jalapeños 

O o b. Is a gem.   Truly a special place.

This is some of the best BBQ in Portland. The whole "toasted yet softly chewy bun piled high with proper pulled pork NOT smothered in sauce becaues it's BBQ done the correct way" thing really blows my skirt up. Yannow?

Their biscuit are fluffy and buttery. The owner competes nearly every weekend in BBQ stints all over the West Coast and greater U.S. There's lots of really, really tasty food coming out of this place. However, I prefer to eat on the bar side of the restaurant, which is technically a Mexican bar seperate from Slabtown but owned by the same guy. (see also: Acapulco's Gold) No kids on this side, and that suits me juuuuuuuuuuuust fine.

This place is very spacious and extremely classy. The prices are great and the service is even better. I was greeted as soon as i walked in and was able to get my nails done right away. Im very picky but they have a large option of colors and were super patient and catering. The employees seem to be very skilled, friendly and make you feel really welcomed. I read their menu and they do all sorts of services including different types of pedicures, manicures and a private room for waxing (which is extremely important for me because i hate going to places to get my eyebrows done and they have you sitting in a regular chair in front of everybody.) Great options, great service, I give my two thumbs up!

Holy freaking moly. This place is ridiculously fantastic. I am vegan and there was only one vegan option in terms of sandwiches and their hummus sandwich is so delicious. The pickled vegetables that went in the sandwich made me feel like I was eating some kind of a vegan Banh mi. It was super crowded when we went and there isn't much seating on the weekends but we would just take our food back to our hotel lobby which wasn't a problem. Their coffee is also wonderful not gross at all. I found it interesting how their biggest size was not a 16 ounce but instead a 20 ounce. That was really awesome for me because I like huge coldbrews.

Comes highly recommended on all travel websites but falls a little flat in real life. Some of the exhibits like the monet and Renoir stand out but others like the Islamic art fall flat. The cafes are less than satisfactory. Be sure to eat before you come. A bit steep but good way to kill a few hours. I recommend joining a tour or, better, getting an audio tour to supplement your visit. But the placards are very informative on their own.

It's funny how there are 2 unfiltered reviews, and 27 FILTERED reviews. That means that Yelp finds those reviews suspicious. Haha!

Anyway, as you can see from my previous reviews, I tend to only review places that I really like. But in this case I'm making an exception. 

I lived there for 3 years and each year we had new management. I can't really judge the newest management other than the fact that I pulled into my usual parking spot to pay my rent and my car got towed. Apparently they were painting the lines in the parking lot. SO NOW I HAVE TO PAY $50 BC THEY TOWED MY CAR, WHEN I PARKED IN FRONT OF MY OWN APARTMENT BUILDING TO PAY MY RENT. That, to me, is bs. Oh, and the same thing happened to my roommate as well.

As far as price goes, it's cheap but you definitely get what you pay for (and apparently they aren't afraid to come up with other ways to get your $). I DEFINITELY wouldn't recommend any girls staying there for safety reasons. 

I've seen some pretty crazy stuff while I was there. I've had a drunk person randomly mistake my place for his and walk in, and I lived with a guy who shot a hole in our kitchen floor. I also know of people who have been robbed there (at least 3--one got his car stolen), and I've heard of one guy who was stabbed and killed just outside of our apartment the year before. 

If you do decide to live there, make sure you know your roommates first. 

Anyway, like I said, they're making me pay for them towing my car and that's the straw that broke this camel's back, so I'm taking the time to write this review. I'm giving them 2 stars instead of 1 bc anybody who's willing to pay rent that cheap can't be expecting much--and bc I'm a nice guy who understands how much reviews effect business so I don't want to be too damaging. But if you can afford it, I highly recommend you look elsewhere for housing.

I used to love this place, but I feel that the quality of their food has declined recently. Maybe it's just been the nights we've visited. My date reported that his dinner was just okay, and my veggie tacos were pretty boring. Our top-shelf margaritas tasted like orange juice (odd!) and they weren't strong at all. I used to be a big fan of their mushroom enchiladas, but I didn't notice them on the menu the last time we visited. Maybe I just missed them. I'm willing to give Las Palomas another try, but I won't be rushing back.

I always love going to this place. If you have been to Thailand you will know that this restaurant is very authentic. Eating here always teleports me back to my experience in Thailand. Especially Northern Thai food. The decor is very similar to the decor in Thai restaurants and the vibe is the same as well. One difference is that is you accidentally drop your fork on the table top that you don't need to throw it away. Thailand is fairly unsanitary.  I had the Papaya salad, very spicy if you haven't had it. The spice builds as well. If you like spicy, the. This is a good dish. I love the Da Chom's Laap Meuang. Very authentic and spot on. The chicken Khoa Soi is great too. This dish is a curry dish and if you don't like Some of the Thai flavors, you will probably like this dish.  This dish is also very similar to the authentic Thai dish. There are a lot of other options as well. This place, and any other Pok Pok restaurant is a staple in Portland and a must visit if you come to Portland.

I visited this location today to buy the cheapest pair of glasses at the fastest speed I could and Amy helped me accomplish this without even trying. The minute I walked in she was able to give me the best deal, without wasting any time. She is very knowledgeable and helpful if you know what you want. I've bought glasses here many times before and this has been the best experience so far that I've had. Not to mention, the staff that makes the glasses are twice as fast as they tell you they will be which is a plus plus in my book! Thanks for the glasses and having such great, friendly employees.

I've been going to Kat for lash extensions for about a year now and I honestly wouldn't want to go anywhere else. She is REALLY good at what she does and really listens to what I want for the desired outcome. Not to mention, Kat is just cool. She's super fun to talk to, knows a great deal about esthetics, and is an all-around lovely human! I highly suggest you book an appointment for any of her services. You won't regret it!
