A cute, casual place to grab some sushi!

This is a fast food style sushi and completely customizable! It is leaps and bounds better than your average publix sushi that you may think can satiate your sushi needs.

My recommendations are the bowls. For the price of 6.99 with UNLIMITED toppings?? I think that is definitely a hefty lunch right there. Some people on here say that the rolls are small or may not be filling, but if you only put in tuna and cucumber... I'm terribly sorry, but I don't know how big you're expecting your rolls to be.. 

Anyways, I personally create a salmon bowl with masago, avocado, EXTRA cucumber (completely free), scallions, sesame seeds. Sauce? I asked for Ponzu, Sriracha, and a dab of spicy mayo on the side with an extra of seaweed salad, which is a great value for only 1.00 extra. This is all my creation I can't get this anywhere else without some extra charges left and right for extra avocado or sauce.

The staff is very friendly, convivial, and ALWAYS willing to cater to your needs and they crank out sushi at ninja fast speeds! How many times have you been at a slow sushi bar and just stare at the chef wondering if that's your meal he's making? With that being said, please understand if it may not as fast as the pink slime being pressed into nuggets you're used to eating at McDonald's. 

If you ever need a fast place to get sushi and no hassles, this is your place!

Happy hour at Clarklewis is our "go to" after a long day.  The prices are incredibly good, the food is great, and the menu changes seasonally to keep things interesting.  All of the staff there is super-friendly, and we enjoy the environment.  I moved here from LA, and a lot of Portland restaurants just seem pretty half-assed to me.  Clarklewis is clean, cool, and well-designed, and has exciting food and a great waitstaff.  Even though we couldn't afford to eat a regular meal there, the happy hour is more than satisfying, especially compared to others that only offer fried food or dinky servings.

Buyer Beware!!! If you knew that your food was cooked in a microwave would you still order this food from them? Do not believe their review stars, they have to review themselves because once you figure out the food sucks they don't get repeat business. Which totally sucks because they could make fresh burgers and food & really kill it for this area with no competition. Sad, I ordered an Engineer Cheeseburger, chilli cheese dog, a taco. I couldn't eat any of it. The cheese on the dog was stuck to the styrofoam. Disgusting.

The CNN studio tour was just okay. I went on the regular tour, not the VIP one. The tour is around an hour long. They have a couple of cool things like seeing how the controller room video set up is like, seeing the large open office space, and looking into a studio from the outside. But those things are short and far between. You don't get to see things up close and personal. No in studio tours, no backstage walkthroughs. You'll spend a lot of time walking through hallways and looking at things from afar through a window. I went because I had the citypass, but it could be good if you're a die-hard fan.

Been a member since this Y branch opened, and it really is a great value.  The gym portion is large, with lots of treadmills and ellipiticals.  They also have alot of the bikes with the TVs that you do theracing games- not my cup of tea, but people seem to be very addicted to them.  

The pools great, and this place is fantastic for families.  My favorite part is definitely the classes, there are some fantastic Tae bo and strength training classes that have wonderful instructors.  And yes zumba.  ALways crowded, I personally don't get it, but seems to be a hit.  

Love the comment about the muscle heads.  There probably are only about 2 crazy diehard muscleheads, but never fail anytime I go, no matter what the time, they are there.  Personally find them very amusing.

Great way to make a little extra spending money (e.g., gas money) for a small amount of time. I can usually donate in 45 min or less. 

They have really streamlined things since I first started donating back in 2006.  You get a debit card issued to you and the payment is loaded on your debit card after a successful donation is made. 

They seem to have had some employee tuen over and some of the non talkative / rude ones are now gone. 

All in all it's a quick way to make $50 a week plus they offer bonus / incentives to keep coming in.

I would definitely recommend you stay away from this place. I lived there for almost three years but there are much better options for the price range in the area. Front office and management staff are horrible, rude and incompetent. Packages that you order routinely go missing from the front office. There is a small but effective group of teens that vandalize and break into cars (I had mine broken into three times in three years) Maintenance is sub par with a low level of professionalism and attention to detail, meaning you'll have to have them back a few times to fix the same issue. The main entrance gates are almost always open and there is a false sense of security throughout the whole place. You are forced to pay monthly for valet waste disposal and half the time they never come get it. I reached out to corporate a few times and never heard a word back. All in all, I would not recommend and I'm glad I moved out.

The worst! I was so excited to go to the Radio Room for Saturday night happy hour.
We arrived at 5 pm and loved the sunny weather and the look of the patio. We went to the top level and shared a table  with a nice gal. We were never even acknowledged after 30 minutes!!! We watched as  everyone around us was served. I have never in my life been ignored like this. We left because there are so many other awesome places on Alberta. Don't bother with this place!

As an art major, I've been dragged to a fair share of museums that I have absolutely no interest in. This however did not make the list. The ICA is a clean cut museum with several floors to visit. It's very tiny, and there is a limited amount of artwork on display at a given time. However, the exhibits they do have on show will make you stop dead in your tracks. It's relatively affordable admission, and there is a student discount available as well. There is also a breathtaking view of the harbor from a glassed wall located near the back of the building; make sure you take a trip out there before you leave! You won't regret it.

We saw this place while we were picking up food next door and decided to get some mac and cheese, honey muffins, and a piece of cake to check it out. If the rest of the food is anything like what we tried, this is gonna be one of our new faves. The staff was so nice too! We're heading back now to pick up dinner! :)

Update: This food is so good! Adding to the list of favorite Atlanta restaurants! I accidentally left my pineapple lemonade, but I will be back to try that too! Ha! :D

What an experience. My boyfriend is in town from Colorado, so I decided to take him to some good Texas BBQ. I had heard great things about The Salt Lick, but it was both of our first time here. Two things important to note: CASH ONLY and BYOB. We saw a long line but were seated immediately upon arrival. Trey was our waiter and was more than happy to answer any questions we had. Trey was a great server. We went up to the barbecue pit and James was there, excited to take our photo. All around, a really great experience at The Salt Lick today. Would definitely recommend on a nice day or if you have visitors in town. 

One thing I wish they had more of a choice of would be sides. I wish they had Mac and cheese, but beans, coleslaw and potato salad were the only option. The pulled pork sandwich and sausage was delicious and the spicy sauce is to die for!

Beautiful venue....we had our work party here and were very well taken care of. The staff was excellent. 

Passed apps - the crab cakes were excellent. Perfectly crispy outsite and the seasoning/overall taste was on par. 
As for the goat cheese tarts - these were OK. Nothing to write home about. 

The dinner is the main reasoning for the 3 stars. We had passed salads to begin with. These were simple....good. The buffet was a bit disappointing. Both the beef and chicken were not great. The chicken was overly cooked and the beef lacked seasoning. The mashed potatoes were fine. The mushroom risoto lacked seasoning as well. The meal as a whole was OK, but was a bit surprised for the type of venue it is. 

Once desert came around the chocolate mini cakes were dry and tasteless as well. I did enjoy the mini pecan pie. 

I would possibly come back to give it another try but certainly is not high on my list right now.

I would never order takeout from here judging from the three arguments I heard just sitting here and waiting for my own order. They can't seem to agree on any detail.

+one star for leaving animal planet on because it amuses my drunken sense of humor.

The chicken fingers came out fast. Yummy and crispy.

Cheesecake had the texture of american cheese with slight cheesecake flavoring. 

Tables are messy. Was not wiped down the entire time I was there.

Good for drunk hunger pangs

Finally, finally, finally, a good tex-mex place in North Austin.  This is just down the street from my house, and I can see that I will be going there many, many more times. This is the old location of Curra's - an awesome restaurant that was terribly managed and eventually closed.  The decor is similar.  There is a large bar with lots of TVs and a good number of tables.  Also nice outdoor seating, tho there isn't much to look at besides the parking lot.  But the FOOD, the FOOD, the FOOD....was fantastic. Incredibly spicy salsa, homemade corn and flour tortillas, fresh guacamole.  They had me before they even brought my entree.  I got the grilled chicken tacos.  Light, flavorful, perfect.  My folks got the combination plate.  My husband got the barbacoa.  It was all delightful.  I will be back to try everything on the menu.  They even have New Mexican red and green chile sauce.  Be still my heart.  Thank you Margarita's.  Please don't close!  Please everyone, go eat here so they don't have to close!

Ok Chinese bakery located right at the Aberdeen train stop. 

The pastries were ok. Pineapple bun was decent. We had some purple yam rolls that I thought were going to be filled but they weren't and didn't taste like much. Also got a condensed milk and cream bun. Looks yummy on the outside tasted butter filled. A little too rich for me 

They have a buy two get one free special at 730. We got there around 720 and the nice lady there was letting a customer leave without paying the full amount - looked like her boyfriend was being some extra cash. She was friendly and was recommending things to us. Then we tried to buy our stuff on special before 730 and the got stone faced and said no way. Put the pastries back and didn't speak to us. 

Store was empty and when we went back to the register at 730 she said we needed to wait one more minute. Awkward...

Been driving by here for years, never stopped in before. They were open at 10:30pm, and I realized "hey, I'm out of whiskey and beer. I should get some before getting home." We had just gotten out of Boston after seeing John Mulaney at Boston Symphony Hall. Instead of having a drink in Boston like classy people, my wife was tired. I can't argue because she's in school and works part time, and like my schedule when I was in college, hers is garbage.

What does this all have to do with Donovans? Nothing. I'd figure I'd let you know, because after seeing the collection available at this Packey I forgot my frustration about not getting drinks in Boston. 

There were two ladies that came in, they talked about a mamosa recipe using hard cider with some champagne and a splash of orange juice. I was intrigued. The clerk was pleasant, transaction was quick. Jameson Cask Mate in hand with some beer and hard cider, I was on my merry way.

Second trip to a Seasons 52 (other location Ft Lauderdale) and it is consistently high quality food, great service, and a great option for people eating veggie/vegan or just healthy. The concept is seasonally changing menus. For veggie people on the winter menu, that might include their winter veg sampler, with wood roasted tofu, a quinoa salad, and roasted veg. I enjoyed that plus a roasted yellow beet dish. My family also enjoyed a pork tenderloin and a roasted shrimp over pasta.

I received a Groupon here as a gift, and tried to book an appointment, but the phone number was wrong, so no one ever called me back. When I finally yelped the phone number here, they were completely booked for the days left in my groupon and would not honor it after (just the original purchase value, unlike any other company I've had any issue with- usually they will book it and honor the groupon). Very poor customer service. The girl on the phone was completely clueless and did nothing to try to help.

This is a sore subject for me. I might get emotional here.

When I moved to Austin from Philadelphia, I knew that I was leaving behind several of my favorite delicacies on earth. Cheesesteaks (which I've since given up, anyway) and water ice were a thing of the past. Out with the NY-style bagels and in with the breakfast tacos. I never, EVER, imagined that I would be giving up decent pizza. Pizza has always been one of my top five foods. When people ask me where I used to get pizza from up north, the answer was that it didn't really matter which one. That's because authentic and family-owned Italian restaurants are ABUNDANT. I guess I took that for granted when I was growing up.

I can tell the way a pizza is going to taste with one look. All of the local chains here are on par with Pizza Hut and Domino's (I don't want to talk about it). I struggled with other local shops until I saw you. 

Homeslice!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!  (Sound the trumpets! Rejoice!)

I love you. 
Your perfect, precious, paradisaic pizza is exactly the way pizza should be. You are a diamond in the rough. You have managed to perfect pizza in a place where no one seems to know or care about real pizza and the way it should taste. 

Thank you for existing and for being so friendly all the time. No matter how busy you are (I call my order in way ahead of time), you still deliver my food to me in and efficient and pleasant manner.

On a different note, props to you for hosting an action-packed carnival every year. It never disappoints!

Not a secret, LanZhou Ramen is one of the more packed eating spots on Buford Highway, though it has a lot of tables stuffed into the space and wait times are short. Despite the name, this is a Chinese restaurant specializing in hand-pulled noodles, which takes up most of the menu. The open kitchen features a fellow doing the hand-pulling for kids to be temporarily distracted by. The noodles are exceptional and can be ordered either dry or in soup. We always order the Vegetable & Egg Stir-Fried Hand-Pulled Noodles medium-spicy, which is as spicy as Szechuan-style noodles. Our other constant order is the Garlic Shanghai Vegetable, which is stirred with black mushrooms and cooked perfectly with a garlicky sauce. The cold dishes are displayed in an open fridge on the counter and among them I would recommend the Cold Bean Curd Sheet ($4.95), which doesn't sound like much, but is a charmer with a winning brown sauce. Among the many places in the general area to obsess over noodles, this noisy spot is among the best.

I had a breast augmentation done years ago by a doctor who took liberties and did what he wanted and fully disregarding my wants. I was unhappy for years. This past summer, one of my implants popped. Knowing I wanted to stay far away from the guy who did my first surgery I called several doctors and Dr. Swail's office was the only office to return my call in a timely manner. I had a consult scheduled for the next day with surgery a couple days after.  Not only did Dr. Swail  remove/replace the old implants, but he also listened to my wishes and did what I wanted and fixed what I did not like from my first surgery. After three months I noticed one was larger than the other and voiced my concern to Dr. Swail (I also told him that I actually wanted bigger implants as well) . He completely understood and wanted me to be nothing but happy. He did another procedure to make sure I got what I wanted and I was happy. He was super accommodating and was eager to do what I wanted (for an absolutely fair price) so I felt good about myself. I couldn't be happier and would highly recommend Dr. Swail's staff is absolutely amazing as well!! Super happy I found BVPS!! Highly recommend!

-CHEAP CHEAP CHEAP materials used for the apartments. The carpet started tearing/coming up when vacuumed a year in
-Faucets, cabinets, floors, everything is the cheapest building material, so expect many things to break in your apartment. In the two years we've been here our blinds broke, sink busted, toilet leaked, BR fan broke, heater broke, carpet ripped/tore, cabinet door fell off.. A lot more that you would expect to break in such a short amount of time. 
-Floors are very squeaky and paper thin. You will think a pack of elephants lives upstairs, regardless of who it is. I can also hear my upstairs neighbors urinate, its that bad. We even have holes in our floor where you can tell boards are missing, as you sink down when stepped on. 
-Maintenance staff is great. They are very friendly, and usually pretty speedy
-The grounds look spectacular. They keep the landscaping looking top notch
-Plenty of parking 

Management staff is often misinformed, gives different answers, or overall not very helpful. 

Also, know that your "security deposit" is not actually a security deposit. They charge a mandatory cleaning fee between $170-200 regardless of how the apartment is left!!!! So if you pay a $250 security deposit, just know that its NOT a deposit, thats pre-paying your mandatory cleaning fee for wear and tear. Scammers.

Do not go here! 4 of us went in for a fun dinner before our friends returned to Switzerland (where they don't have hibachi). 1st dish was fried rice and they cooked it and served it on my plate....with a hair in it. Besides offering me more fried rice, they didn't do anything to compensate for the hair. After we paid full price, I spoke to the manager as a matter of customer service and said he should comp someone in the future who finds a hair. He then basically said it looked like my hair. Just for customer service issues, I was blown away that they didn't offer anything and then made it sound like it was my fault!!!!! I am so pissed. I was happy to pay full price (which I did) so all they needed to do was apologize. I can't believe the rudeness. I live close by and won't go back again.

Stumbled upon this place with 3 other friends and decided to give it a try. Overall, a solid place, but with disappointing paella and definitely overpriced dishes. 

It's a cute spot with good, chill vibes and ample outdoor seating. 

We ordered a pitcher of rose sangria, which was quite good. Had a hint of grapefruit, which we LOVED. 

For appetizers we got the brussel sprouts, potatoes, pork ribs, and mixo ceviche. We ordered a paella to share as our main dish.

The tapas were great - extremely overpriced (i.e. potato squares with sauce for $10) - but nonetheless delicious. I felt this is where the restaurant SHINES. Brussel sprouts also flavored amazingly and the pork ribs were NEXT LEVEL. Melted in your mouth and fell right off the bone, absolutely delicious! I'm not a big meat eater, but these were genuinely delicious. 

The ceviche was definitely different than the ceviche I've had in the past. And while initially, we were a bit hesitant, the dish turned out to be okay! I didn't hate it, but it also wasn't the best ceviche I've ever had. For a place that advertises on its ceviche, I was a bit disappointed. But in the long scheme of things, I don't think it was a terrible dish or anything. 

DO NOT ORDER THE PAELLA !! I am unsure if they had an off day, but the paella was, for lack of better words, not good. The rice was flavorless and definitely not even cooked thoroughly (half of the pan of rice was still hard). I was shocked at the lack of flavor considering the seafood inside, but it almost felt as if they cooked the rice completely separately. 

Similarly, the mussels in the paella tasted SO FISHY - really low quality and definitely anticipated a stomachache afterwards. I was so looking forward to the paella but it overall felt like an extremely rushed dish with little care or quality.

I enjoyed this place overall and would definitely recommend the sangria and tapas. Beyond that, maybe look elsewhere.

We had to rework the entire drainage under one bathroom in our new home. We were having a lot of difficulty in getting any other plumber to respond to phone calls or show up to even look at the problem. We ended up calling Reliant Plumbing and someone came out the very next day to take a look. They scheduled the work for the day after and gave me an estimate. Next day, they showed up on time and finished the job in a very professinal manner. The new pipes etc. were neatly laid out and they took the time to explain me everything they did. They cleaned up after themselves and wore shoe covers when inside the house. They also gave me a few tips on maintaining my water heater!

updating my review for this place because wowie i've been in portland for almost a year and SAF is still my #1 go-to pot shop!!!! whenever someone asks me where do i get the best green on the westside, i tell them *go to stone age on canyon!* duh! the staff is STILL cute and friendly, the prices are STILL affordable and they still have great deals via txt alerts, and i love that they're close to home. in the year i've lived here, other dispensaries have opened out here but i still stay true to my stone age! also, THEY TAKE CARDS!!!!!

I was driving down to Portland from Tacoma and 1/2 way there my check engine light came on.  After some initial freaking out I identified this dealership was on my way to the event and would be open on Saturday.  I stopped in and spoke to Zack and explained my circumstance and asked if the service department could check the code to identify the problem.  He did so, confirmed that it was not something wrong with the engine and cleared the code.  This saved my day!  On top of it, I was in and out in less than 10 minutes and they did not charge me for the work.  I am seriously impressed at the willingness to help me, do it quickly and not charge me the hefty fee I would have expected at some of the dealerships I have dealt with here locally.  Thank you very much.

My never-ending pursuit of the perfect haircut landed me at Rooks this morning. I didn't have an appointment but barber Brian indicated that he would fit me in as soon as he finished up with the fellow who was currently in his chair. Nice guy. 

While he was working on me with the clippers, Brian asked me where I was from. That scared me. I sometimes get negative reactions from native Portlandios when I mention my SoCal pedigree (imagine that). The last thing I wanted was a reverse Mohawk from a hater. I started out with a disclaimer that my wife is originally from Eugene and that I...gulp...grew up near Santa Barbara...

Brian told me he's from Orange Co. (BTW, nobody who lives there calls it "The O.C.", or ever has.) I exhaled. Phew!

It doesn't take long to give me my short, semi-buzz cut, but Brian took his time and even put me back in the chair when he noticed the right side was a tad longer than the left. I left looking much less shabby than when I walked in.

I like that the place looks like a barbershop. The neck trim with a straight razor is always appreciated. I don't mind spending $25 for a haircut if it lasts for awhile. I'll definitely go back.

Trying on wedding dresses is a stressful but also an exciting event. Sales people and shop owners are supposed to be there to help you every step of the way, and guide you through the whole process so that you can find a dress that matches your personality and style, not to mention, one that fits you. 

I made an appointment to try on a dress and arrived at the shop on time. There was one other bride in the small shop trying on dresses along with her family. No one greeted my mom or I when we entered, and as I was just about ready to leave (approx. 10 minutes later) someone finally came over to the counter to ask what they could do to help (actually, they talked over my head to the girl that arrived after us to check on her first, and she graciously told the woman that we were ahead of her).

The woman took us to a back room, asked what kind of a dress I was looking for, pointed us to a small section of the room, and told us to look through those dresses. She said she would be right back.

After about 15 minutes of looking at these dresses by ourselves, not seeing anything that really stood out or that was reasonably priced, we decided to head back to the front of the store. The woman who said that she would be back to help us was lounging by the counter, not doing anything at all. I don't think she ever intended to come back. 

There was better service and selection at David's Bridal - where I ended up purchasing my dress the very same day.

The ambiance makes me feel like I am in a SE Portland bar! Which I love! Great place to chill and talk to neighbors. The owners are pretty nice. Lots of wood and DIY feel but very tasteful. Great beers on tap. Wish there was a unique juke box or something. A great jukebox with lots of unique stuff can totally take it to the next level. If they had one with old school punk and blues I would be there plenty. Check it out! Plus you can have food delivered there from the hood!

I stopped in for a late lunch today with my husband. The majority of my dissatisfaction stemmed from the inconsiderate AHOLES who were also dining there: a man with a very thick European accent screaming on his cell phone the entire time we were there, the lady behind me with two screaming toddlers, then she gets up to take one to the bathroom and leaves the other one alone at the booth...

Aside from that, not a bad lunch.  I ordered the Bistro Vegetable sandwich with no peppers. They actually accommodated me! Normally when I order no peppers they always seem to sneak some in.  The sandwich was very delicious and tasty, very fresh. My only complaint was that the bread was a little too crispy and cut the roof of my mouth a little. 

I like their mango and peach flavored teas, but they are not sweetened so by the time you add all your sweetener in you can't taste the fruit flavors anymore.

I HATE that they charge over $2 for fountain drinks. Between my husband and I, our entrees ran around $8 each, plus $2 each for a fountain drink = over $20 for a couple of sandwiches - a little more pricey than I normally like to pay.

I went there for HH with my boyfriend a few weeks back, after a rough day at work.  Quiet, not too crowded (until a softball team came in, but we were leaving, so NBD) which is just what I needed.

Bonus points for happy hour until 7!  Us 9-to-5ers appreciate that.

Service:  friendly but slow.

Drinks:  Deep pours, definitely the attitude adjuster I required at the time.  I do agree with other reviewers about drink mix-ups though;  seems like there's a communication gap during the round trip between my table and the bar next door (where the drinks are actually made.)

Food:
Sliders (beef): A+
House sausage (Hungarian): tasty but dry; a minute (or more) less on the grill would improve it.
warm spinach salad:  too sweet
kale chips:  best I've had outside my own house
house-made ice cream:  delicious

I think if they trimmed a few dishes from the menu in order to focus on the items that they do really well, this place would really fly.  I'd love to see them succeed.  I will definitely be back to try the Kaiserschmarrn.  My grandma and mom used to make it for me when I was young, and I haven't had it in ages.

A go to for anyone looking for a delicious, satisfying Italian dish. This is a place that you go to for the food and pretty much only the food. The service is just okay and the atmosphere is nothing to write home about, definitely not the place for a quiet romantic dinner followed by hours of gazing into each others' eyes. They get you in, serve your food, and shuffle you out. The food, however, is consistently delicious. Usually, I go for the butternut squash ravioli served with a brown butter sage sauce, however during my last visit I decided to change it up and ordered the Eggplant Fusili which was also another great dish. 

The Special dish of the night was fettuccine with a smoked mushroom cream sauce, served  with rock shrimp and scallops. I have never tasted something quite like this - I was surprised at just how powerful the smoky flavor was. It took me a couple of bites to realize how exceptional this actually was. I'm so glad my boyfriend didn't finish his. I got to eat the rest the next day! 

The original location is in the North End, however they don't accept reservations. I highly recommend making reservations if you are planning to head to the South End location. If not, you can expect to wait at least an hour or more on the weekends. Make sure to pack the cash, this place doesn't accept Credit Cards.

Dan's is exactly as it should be.  The burgers are quintessentially american, delicious, and come in three sizes!  

Everything's dirt cheap.  It seems like the last time they changed any menu prices must have been 15 years ago.  One heavenly Saturday I got a jalapeno cheeseburger, curly fries, a coke, and a chocolate milkshake for about $7.  Really. Really.  You just can't top that.

Dan's is definitely a South Austin favorite. 

(And, anyone know why you'd go to the A&W across the street? really?? When Dan's is right there, why??)

We came in for their happy hour.  Oysters were a buck a shuck and all appetizers were half off.  There was a small selection of $5 drinks (cocktails, wine and beer).

I wasn't totally wowed by this place.  It's in a central location and has all the right bells and whistles.  We sat on the patio which was alright.  The outdoor fireplace was nice.

The oysters were meh.  I'm pretty sure I'm an east coast oyster person.  I did enjoy the calamari, that was pretty good.  I think we had some other food item but it wasn't that memorable.  The cocktails tasted totally watered down.  I'm sure they were pre-made and just sat there.  You can't really screw up beer, so that was OK.

I'm not sure if I would recommend this place nor would I be in any hurry to return.

Always fun to go to Michael's. So many things to get creative, they have great selection for anything from arts and crafts to frames, flowers,, baking and so much more! They have really good specials too, always a plus! Great location, I can visit during lunch time and serves as therapy, lol 
I took a star off as been as busy as it gets they only had one cashier, it took a while and I mean a while for customers to be on the line for one more employee to come and assist and this is not the first time I experience this at this specific location. Other than that, I say it is a great store and I do recommend it.

Out of all the breweries that I bookmarked prior to our trip to Denver, Avery was the one I was looking forward to the most. They had just been on Thrillist's list of best breweries as ranked by state. Yes, they topped notable craft beer powerhouses such as Oskar Blues and Lefthand. 

The fact that they're located about 45 mins away from downtown Denver didn't deter me. I was determined to at least sample a few of their legendary stouts and other amped up dark beer offerings, and maybe bring a few of their hard to find releases back to California with me. 

When my honey said she would drive back, it was as if I had been given the keys to the kingdom. The entire portfolio of all their nearly 30 beers that they had on tap became available to me. I opened up their beer menu to glowing bright lights and a chorus of "hallelujah" in my head. "Holy shit is it my birthday" crossed my mind several times over the next few hours.

What I really came for we're the massive ABV behemoths such as Uncle Jacobs's Stout, Mephistopheles, and Tweak. However since the taproom was at my disposal that day, I decided to sample a few of their more traditional and reasonably priced offerings before moving onto the big boys.

Out of Mind was a coffee beer that blew my mind. One of the best beers that Avery brews. Even my honey stole a few sips and she doesn't even like beer. But she does LOVE coffee and this baby was loaded with so much freshly roasted goodness she probably thought she was at sitting at Caribou. Probably my favorite beer here if you are talking overall value as it was only $6 per pint. It's listed as a taproom rarity, so unfortunately I wasn't able to snag any to take home with me.

I tried the new Raja and their classic Maharajah double IPAs. While they were both solid beers, I preferred the lighter galaxy hops that were in the Raja. See, Avery does things well other than just make high ABV beer.

Normally something called "Czar Imperial Coffee Stout" would be high on my list of favorites. Here it was overshadowed by the more value priced Out of Mind and the much more bolder beers in the lineup. Still a quality brew that I felt needed to come home with me. 

Now onto the huge ABV beasts that Avery is known for. They had something called the Ratman 10,000 to commemorate a dude with his beeradvocate 10'000th review. How cool would that be? "Yes may I order the John B. 1,000 please?" It was an outstanding barrel aged beer of mixed identity. It's similar to what Speakeasy does with its Syndicate series. 

I enjoy a good pumpkin brew as much as the next guy so I needed to try the PumpKYn. I've never had a pumpkin beer over 11% so this one was a treat. 17.22% ABV of whiskey barrel aged wonder and spices. It could've easily been the dessert to end our meal. 

Tweak was the finally beer in my coffin. Coming in at 17.81% ABV, it is the heaviest beer I've ever tasted. A turbo charged boost of a coffee stout aged in Bourbon barrels for only 4 months. You wouldn't know think this beer would be as smooth as it is from the description, not aroma. Sure it packs a punch but it delivers on all the flavors as well.

Are these high ABV beers a gimmick? It doesn't feel like it. Every single one was as smooth as something with half the kick. Avery just seems to know how to coax every drop of booze out of the beer making process. Sure they may add a ton of sugary substances to do so, but in the end, the finished product is flawless. 

Yes, there was even Vegan food to be had. A seitan sloppy joe to be exact. There was also a salad for my honey but I can't get down with salad while drinking beer. The Seitan Joe was outstanding. It's something I would order anywhere. Think of it as a less greasy, yet still sloppy version of the regular Joe. 

Service here was phenomenal. There wasn't a waitress here that wasn't friendly and perky. Our main girl Jocelyn, was incredibly sweet and always there to bring us more beer and a smile.

We took an unguided tour of the canning area. It wasn't too much to look at but it's always fun to watch the production process in action. I would recommend the guided tour if you have the opportunity to do so.

The only thing I have negative to say about our entire experience is that their beer is a "you get what you pay for" experience. While it may indeed be some of the best beer that I've ever had, it's also some of the priciest. My wallet is just glad that Avery is located several states away and their beers aren't too easy to get ahold of out in Cali. 

Even my non-beer drinking babygirl is a fan: http://www.yelp.com/biz/avery-brewing-boulder-2?hrid=jSw2M1Wvzq24Xw1KdM3ORA&utm_campaign=www_review_share_popup&utm_medium=copy_link&utm_source=(direct)

This place is new and it shows.

While the store itself is nice and big and clean, the staff... well everyone seems pretty clueless. I stopped in here on evening on the way home to grab one thing and once I got to the only checkout that appeared to be open I stood there for about 5 minutes while several cashiers debated over who was running that cash register. Once they figured it out, I paid for my one bottle of pop with a $20 bill and received $18 in change back because apparently none of the registers contained any bills? Irritating.

It's a good food market with historical African American backing to it.
If you need any kind of meat to cook up for dinner or cheap fruit, this is the place.
It's also a nice place to go to for small lunches, a drink, or snacks.
Just make sure you check ahead of time when all of the shops inside are open because a lot aren't open the entire week or close early. 

The surrounding area is really interesting & the parking lot is right in the back, so make sure out don't miss the turn into the lot.

Very cool bar / lounge / restaurant (what combo, I'm still not sure) in the Fairmont Hotel YVR.

I pulled up to the bar one night for a night cap. The gentleman that night was a cool dude, friendly and smooth. He mentioned a pretty good recommendation on I believe their bacon burger (casual spelling) with sweet puh-tay-toe or regular fries. It was a solid choice, kind sir, thank ye, thank ye.

The vibe all up in here is pleasantly swish, modern and sleek. It's also kind of neat how the bar rear peeks into the elevator corridor.
I do admit those drab gray bar seats are so0Ooo Saved By The Bell, je regrette.

Good staff, food--OH, and the Fairmont Honey Lager was also delightful!

Bottom footer: My beer palette is steering in the lagers, lighter ales and light-medium pilsner directions. Sweet!

I really wanted to give Dantanna's a better review, but their food was just OK. I came here with a conference buddy. Looking for a non chain restaurant away from the mall. We sat outside for dinner and it was not too busy. Service staff was amazing very courteous and knowledgeable. For starter we had the oysters, mainly a selection of east coast oysters, not that great almost seemed like they were water logged, no real flavor to them. Next we had soups I had the gumbo it was good, but a little too spicy for my liking. We shared the seared tuna plate. Tuna was prepared well, but again nothing to write home about. 
This place is great for atmosphere, lots of people hanging out and enjoying themselves in the outdoor section!

I want to give this place 3.5 stars, but I think 3 is too low so I'll be generous. 

You have to go into this place knowing this is a dive bar, sooooo... it wreaks of smoke and the food is typical bar food. I thought the wings and onion rings were good, but artichoke hearts and fried mushrooms were eh. The waitress was very nice and service was prompt, but we also went when it was slow (mind you, some bars have service that sucks even when its slow!). Plenty of tv screens to watch the game and they have specials M-F. We went on Monday so they had $1.50 drafts which is the ish! I live right down the road so I would go back again if I wanted a quick bite or a bar to watch the game aka they guys watch the game and I down some beers :)

This place is an absolute gem in the heart of downtown, I'm kicking myself for all the years I wandered around the city and walked right by it. My girlfriend and I went here for their half price oyster special (it's a must if you're into raw bar). The restaurant is nicely set back from the busy street, which is a nice change of pace from the restaurants where you're constantly looking passersby in the face awkwardly for your whole meal. We were on the second floor to eat (with a good view of the city at night) and when we got there at 5 it was totally empty except for a few folks at the bar, which was surprising even for a Monday. The decor is just awesome, sort of 1920s French art-deco, definitely a collared shirt type place, nice enough to be a good date spot but not stuffy. We did half a dozen of each of the four types of oysters, and the Wellfleet and Duxbury oysters were our favorites. All of them were fresh and ice cold and delicious, though the cocktail sauce was a bit mild for my liking, definitely take them up on the extra Tabasco sauce offer if you like hot cocktail sauce. We then had a sampling from the cheese menu, 1 oz. each of Camembert, Cravero and some kind of Pecorino the name of which escapes me. The Camembert was the best in our opinion. The cheese plate included four slices of toasted brioche each, some (AMAZING) fig jam, lavender honey and some candied walnuts. The cheese is expensive though, $6.50 per ounce. The service was fantastic as well, our water glasses were never less than 1/4 full, our waitress (Carolina) was very nice, always offered us extra bread, Tabasco sauce, and recommended us her favorite cheeses as well. Overall, an awesome place for happy hour oysters, good cheese if that's your thing, and some of the best service we've ever had in the city, along with a very comfortable and attractive interior. Not one to be missed, 5 stars all the way!

Food is pretty good quality but the customer service is pretty bad. The wait times for food are awful for the little traffic they get in on a weekday night. Also, they advertise 24 hour dining, but employees actively guard the door and kick you out past 10:30PM. Staff are inattentive and rude as well.

Everything else is fine. The self order kiosks are high-tech and cool; it was my first time ever using them and the novelty quickly wore off when I realized how atrocious the UI/UX is for it. Excessive amount of menus and confirmation screens, I could design a way better UI in a day.

I would've ordered at the register but no employees were even nearby the cash register. They were all chatting and loitering in the back as orders began piling up. It was pretty apparent that because of the addition of self order kiosks, employees grew lazy and stopped attending the registers. Seems like robots are already replacing our jobs. Scary.

I've always really appreciated Idle Hand's dedication to producing fine Belgian Ales. It's great to see them grow into their new space in Malden! My friend and I got to talk with Dan the bartender and I was impressed by his customer service skills and knowledge of beer and the industry. I have been coming to Idle Hands since the Charlton St. days and they have always been an amazing brewery with an amazing ethos about the beer they make and how they want to continue producing it. Being so close to the Malden Center T station, this is a brewery that any Bostonian will easily be able to enjoy!

So I was driving home last night, listening to a self-made CD, and up came "Naked Eye" by Luscious Jackson...and it always makes me think of Audubon Circle.

Many moons ago, I was dating a GREAT guy.  Good looking, in awesome shape, very intelligent, and knew all the right things to say and do.  The night I met him, he was wearing a turtleneck sweater, which is kind of a turn on for me.  Of all my conquests when I lived in Boston, he was one of the better ones...but he was Jewish and I am not, so it kind of died.

Our first real "alone" date, he took me to Audubon.  I couldn't get over what a good vibe it had.  I noticed that  Boston can be a town of pretentious eateries, all of them cockier than the next, trying to outdo each other in exotic food/decor/patrons.

Audubon is definitely tries, but not offensively so.  I adored their burgers with brie, and found that any date would look good with the lighting and decor.  The staff was usually friendly...taking the time to help me remember the song playing that I couldn't remember by Luscious Jackson.

Back in 1997, when I was but a fledgling lawyer, I was sent to Tulsa for just over a week to help try a medical malpractice case.  We stayed in these horrible apartments that were right near a Jason's Deli...so we ate there Every.  Single.  Day.

I have never quite gotten over that experience.  Jason's is fine, but it's not great, and eating there every day for over a week was basically tantamount to torture for a foodie like me...especially when paired with the stress of the situation and the fact that I was on a low-carb diet at the time, which grossly limited my choices.  I have these vivid memories of getting their salad bar and basically filling up on pickled okra at practically every meal.

But wait...this review is supposed to be about Jason's Deli...not the story of my life.

So, for some reason, my office often wants to pick up from Jason's, so I still venture to order from there pretty often - maybe 2-3 times a month.  When I do, my favorite thing is their turkey wrap.  I've also tried their chicken salad, which is good but very pineapple-y, so you only want to get it if you like pineapple; their muffalettas, which don't quite work for me (not enough olive salad and the bread seems kind of dry); and their reuben, which is admittedly piled high but just not the real thing.  Probably a few other things, too, but I can't remember what they are right now.

So yeah...it's fresh...it's decent...and that freaking sauce they serve with their fruit, which I suspect is a concoction of brown sugar and sour cream, is to DIE for (seriously - I got busted once by somebody in my office who caught me licking the dregs out of a container of this!)...but I just wouldn't choose to go here if it were up to me.  Too many stressful memories...too many Lexus SUV's in the parking lot here to deal with...not enough goodness to balance it all out.

I've had a lot of terrible haircuts, but this one might take the cake. I have short hair and just wanted the sides and back trimmed and some length taken off top to get it out of my eyes. Pretty simple. But it looked like someone took a weed whacker to my hair when the girl was done! It was way too short and hair was completely uneven and choppy and stuck straight out from one side of my head for weeks. Most stylists will trim a little at a time, then ask if I want it shorter. This woman just chopped it all right off in one go! She seemed like she didn't know what she was doing at ALL, and it also somehow took longer than any cut I've had before. She cut my ear too.
I hate how it costs extra for a blow dry. My hair takes less than 2 minutes to dry, and I wanted to see what it looked like before I left the salon, but it was pouring rain outside and I'd be walking home so I wasn't willing to pay so much extra for that. My fault I guess, but I wasn't going to let her touch it anymore at that point anyway. 
Anyway, it has been a couple months now and my hair is overdue for another cut, but you can still see how uneven the previous one was. I'm scared to go back, but I've heard good things about Justin so I might try an appointment with him because this place is so convenient and affordable. He was in the salon with another customer while I got my last cut, and seemed professional and knowledgeable, unlike the stylist I had. Will update if I have a better experience.

Loved this resto for several reasons. We ordered different dosas...lamb, regular chicken, and butter chicken...they were all good. I particularly like the butter chicken as it was so flavorful. The sweet corn soup was very yummy too, and there was a lot of chicken in it. Also, the servers were very attentive. My friend was not very sure about the menu, and he asked many questions. The server patiently answered them all and gave him a few advice as well. As for myself, I didn't know which dessert was good and I usually don't eat anything too sweet. The server recommended me the Kulfi pistachio which was not too sweet and very delicious. The resto is located right next to the Independent grocery store on Davie and parking is very easy. There are lots of street parkings as well as parking lots. I'd recommend Davie Dosa Company to anyone who's looking for good dosas. Give it a try, I promise it won't disappoint you.

My gf and I moved to this neighborhood a year ago... we decided to give this place a try and it was horrible. The ambience felt old and sad right away but we wanted to eat either way. She got some salad and I got a chicken parmesan. Half of the salad felt like it was mostly onions so my gf didn't have them all (obviously). When the waitresses came to pick the plates she sassed at my gf for not finishing the salad. For me however, it was even worse. The chicken tasted like it was a frozen meal from superstore  and everything was basically flavorless. I don't know why people say this place has great food... maybe we should've eaten something else.

Very overpriced for the mediocre food and unprofessional service. Sad.

I was amazed at the speed of service. The two people who helped me at different times were cordial and efficient.

Great service! Very helpful and attentive. I was surprised how easy they made each step. Both women were very nice and helpful. They were patient with each customer. I couldn't have been more pleased.

P.S. Call in your order and they will have it ready and waiting for you at customer service! Grab your order from customer service and proceed to the checkout line.

I had high expectations of the Hainese chicken from all the reviews and hype I've heard about this place but it was everything that I expected and more! 
  We visited Nong's as soon as they opened in the morning as we were heading to Blue Star Donuts down the street. I grabbed some donuts and my boyfriend picked up some hainese chicken for breakfast (since he is not into sweets). I had a couple of bites of his chicken and as much as I loved the blue star donuts, I have to admit Nong's chicken is exceptional! Would definitely revisit if we're ever back in Portland.

Paid for the 15,000 mile service to be done, was told i had a screw in my rear tire. The young woman handling my paper work informed me that my tires were being rotated and that the tire with screw on it was now in the front if my car. I got the tire replaced at another service center and they informed me that my front tire was fine and that the one with the screw in it was still on the rear. So i paid to have a totally good tire replaced while still driving with the faulty one.  So Pride Hyundai never performed the tire rotation and when i called about this issue the receptionist in the service department admitted to the fact that my tires were never rotated and told me "at the very least we will refund you for the tire rotation". It's been 2 weeks and Mr Luiciano the service manager has never been available when ive called and has never gotten back to me even though i was told that my name and number were left on his desk multiple times. It's very poor customer service to not even speak with me regardless on weather you'll refund my money, atleast be somewhat professional and tell me yourself instead of dodging your customers. They got my money so screw me right? Don't be fooled by the name PRIDE because they take no Pride in their jobs or addressing any issues their customers might have with their service.

I've experienced better. I really wanted to like this place. The girls are all sweet, beautiful and friendly, they gave me a Lonestar, and had a decent parking situation.

It's been almost a year and I'm still disappointed with my experience. My ends are ridiculously brassy  for those couple of weeks between touch-ups (at another salon). My hair looks so tacky if I don't have it toned. I came in with dark brown hair, hoping to begin the process of going blonde through highlights. My stylist suggested ombre, which I was excited about, because I had been interested in that look for some time. She asked how dramatic I would like for it to be, and I said very, which I thought meant blonde on the ends and brown on top. I definitely felt rushed, because my hair didn't sit long enough to process. I ended up with only slightly lighter ends, which she must have noticed because after (only partially) drying my hair, she kind of moved it around with her hand and said "yeah....if you decide you're not happy with the shade, you can come back and we can try to lift it some more." A month later, I decided to give this place another try and get more highlights, although my ends were still basically orange. I asked for partial highlights, and got maybe about 10 foils, and no offer to break the base and lighten the hair in between the foils. After a couple of weeks I couldn't stand it and I had to find a new stylist, where my hair (ends included) have been significantly lightened. I know my ends are capable of being blonde because they ARE blonde right now. 

It's a cheap place, so that's a plus, but I wouldn't immediately recommend this place for quality, dramatic color changes because my stylist didn''t seem capable of providing that kind of service. I've had a hard time posting this review because I don't want to discredit the entire salon.

I can't speak for their products as I've barely started using them, but my experience at this location was wonderful! The store is organized in a streamlined and straightforward fashion that makes choosing what you want easy -- it feels exactly as one would expect, given the minimalistic design of their products. The staff are friendly and  approachable and give the impression of caring about more than just selling their products. As someone who is far from well learned in the science of skincare, their help was critical in deciding what to get. They are incredibly well informed and have lots of personal experience with the products.
On a side note, there weren't many people when I was there, and and I'm curious as to how only two salespeople would manage the store on a busy day.

I was a bit let down because everything I had specifically gone for was out of stock. I'm not sure how often new product comes in but I definitely caught the end of the cycle (I was told the shipment would be coming in that night). I'm not too bothered because they opened recently and I'm hoping this will soon be dealt with, but it was disappointing nonetheless.

Worst dining experience ever. Bought a groupon for my mom part of my mom's Christmas gift. Arrived and waited for over 20 minutes for someone to acknowledge us to put my name in. We waited for about 45 minutes on a Tuesday. Our waiter was annoyed we had the groupon and didn't even bother to take our drink order. He took a food order and then ran off. Had to flag him down after several attempts to get a drink. My chicken Marsala came without pasta. The waiter vanished and by the time he came back I was done with the chicken... one piece I couldn't cut with my knife because it must have been old. I told him that my pasta never came and he said "yes, you're right. Our kitchen is very busy tonight... we only have two waiters so..." Then because the restaurant was so crowded my drink was spilled. I asked for a napkin and no one returned for over 5 minutes. He handed it to me, leaving a giant puddle on the floor and my belongings soaked. After the mediocre meal we were given only 1 dessert option because he said they had run out of everything else. When it came time for the check, I didn't add a tip to my credit card because I was going to leave some cash... not 20%. The waiter, not realizing I was holding cash to leave, said sarcastically "thanks for the tip.. it's included anyway," which is NOT true with a groupon. I just checked my CC statement and they added 20% gratuity without my authorization. I've been trying to call the restaurant and no one answers... mailbox is full. I'm livid. I would give this place zero stars if I could.

I am a fan of The good Ole Cheesesteak been torn about leaving a review. This place is just a rip off honestly. You can go to Aldi purchase the shaved meat/peppers/cheese/bread for about $10 and feed 3-4 people. 

I don't mind paying for food if it's worth the price and it's delicious. This sandwich was not delicious it was OK. It was a bit on the greasy side, lacked cheese, and lacked taste. I give it a 2.5 out of 10 on taste. Yes, Chef Gordon Ramsey would be disappointed. 

I only come here if I am hungry and been drinking at  brewery and need some food.

Located in the quiet neighborhood of central square, I stumbled onto this body shop on my way home. Needing repairs for my car, I stopped by to inquire. Their rates seemed reasonable as did their turn around time. After bringing my car in for repairs and asking for quick diagnostic, they stressed that I needed to have multiple items replaced and that they would not be willing to repair the issues that I initially brought the car in for. They were not the first mechanic to look at my car...and somehow the others didn't find all of these issues. This shop is either really good at forcing you to take preventative measures with your car, or they look for ways to repair things that don't need immediate attention. Good shop, employees were ok, but I would not recommend a shop like this to any of my friends..

After hearing sounds from my car I took it to another mechanic. Looks like the work that was done there was horrible. How does a mechanic improperly install brakes?!?

Update based on Hermes' recent comment: 

Thanks for the comment. If you cannot handle basic automotive repairs (because you're an autoshop) you should NOT agree to perform the work. If an auto 'repair' shop states that they can perform the work, an unsuspecting client would most likely agree to have the work done there. If the work isn't done properly, causing more damage to the car, ANY car owner would rather take their vehicle to a shop that can get it right the first time especially if they claim that they can perform the work and provide customers with quotes.

The rating:
Three point five stars is the consensus rating from Ms. Sarah-pants, my sis and myself.

Why we chose to eat here:
My mom had mentioned it as being a pretty good pizza pie after having it for a work function, and well, she's my mom, so I figured why not.

The food:
Round one we chose to start with the mozzarella stick app, as it is usually a pretty safe bet and being Italian I have a tough time turning down cheese and red sauce. They were certainly mozzarella sticks, perfectly adequate mozzarella sticks with perfectly adequate marinara sauce. Cooked nice and brown without any sticks being devoid of cheese from over frying. All in all not a bad start.

Round two, the pizza round. We got two large pies, one with hamburger and sausage, the other, half cheese, half pepperoni. The cheese was the most underwhelming, which is usually a bad sign. Ms. Sarah-pants thought the cheese seemed plasticky, and I resorted to dipping the crust into the marinara from our app. Next up, pepperoni. Definitely getting better, they use a very wide diameter pepperoni to achieve full meat coverage of each slice, and with the spicy meat adding to the flavor I could put he marinara away. This was also Sarah's favorite of the three. Finally, the hamburger and sausage combo, which my sis and I deemed the "slice of the night". The hamburger and sausage were both ground up, so no slices of sausage, which is actually how I prefer it. Once again the toppings really elevated the pizza and the mediocre cheese pizza became something I can really get behind. While not quite as loaded as the pepperoni there was more than enough meat to go around.

Round three, the main course. My sis and I each got a steak tip dinner, both ordered medium well. I opted for double fries while my sis went with broccoli and mashed potatoes. The steak on both of our meals was over cooked, into the super well done range, but we agreed that they still tasted pretty darn good with the sweet BBQ sauce slathered over them. My fries came unsalted but were fine all the same. My sisters broccoli was simply steamed, which was as expected, and fine by her. The mashed potatoes though, wow, amazing! Really, I would have never guessed this, but for all three of us this was the number one aspect of the meal (my sis was so impressed she HAD to have us try them). Buttery, creamy, just chunky enough so you know they are real. So very very good. She may have said they were better than our Dad's but I will neither confirm nor deny that statement.

Also, a little side note, they go the extra mile with condiments with little containers of parm cheese, red pepper flakes, fresh scali bread, butter and ketchup.  Very thoughtful.

The service:
Very good overall. We called the order in for pickup and the woman on the other end was very professional even though she seemed to have a tough time hearing me. She was thorough and repeated the entire order back to me, as well as giving me a time without being prompted, also letting me know to just ask for her upon arrival. Just be aware while you can pickup food, it is more of a sit down, bar/restaurant with no hostess stand. Sarah and the sis picked it up and had to feel around a bit to locate our food. Obviously this is a non issue after the first time, but I feel it should at least be mentioned in case it is your first time.

The final rundown:
The food ran the gamut from meh to wow, and the service left little to be desired. Portions were also pretty great for the price. I don't consider it a destination meal, but I will probably be back at some point, if for nothing else than for my own order of those crazy good mashed potatoes.

We recently used Heavenly Care Moving to relocate across Texas, and we were very impressed with our experience. Scheduling the move was easy, and they were flexible with adjusting dates/number of trucks required. Chase, Anthony, and Ben showed up on time, were friendly and professional, and loaded everything in less than the quoted time. They communicated with us during the long drive the next day, arrived for delivery on time, and again unloaded in less than the quoted time. All three men handled our belongings carefully and were so easy to work with.

Came for a large birthday party. I ordered the crunchee roll and the B52. They were both drenched in sauce, but they were still tasty. My biggest disappointment came from the sweet and sour chicken. It surprised me that they used Lychee so I gave it a try. I wish I hadn't.

The chicken was not seasoned and the breading wasn't either. The breading on the chicken was also pointless as it would not stay on the chicken. The vegetables had grill marks but tasted cold as if they had just came out of the refrigerator. That was really weird. Overall that was the worst, cold food. I don't think this dish was meant to be served cold, and yet this is how it came to me. 

I definitely understand why this restaurant is only 3/5 stars. Very disappointing!

This is my favorite bookstore in the Boston area. They always have interesting author events, a great selection of books, journals, Boston-themed gifts and more. If they don't have an item in stock, they can order it for you and often it comes in just 2 days...same amount of time as Amazon Prime, but you are supporting your local economy and an amazing small business. They also will gift wrap your purchase for you for no additional cost. You have no idea how helpful this is for people like me who wrap presents that look like a two year old did it. Join their frequent buyer program to get discounts and early bird opportunities for events. Their warehouse sale is amazing. You can get so many wonderful bargains. The staff is always friendly and helpful. The Harvard Book Store never disappoints.

This is a bar I don't go to nearly enough. It's got a great atmosphere and is a great way to start your night. I generally come here before going to a concert downtown, and recommend it to anyone as a nice "pre-game" spot or when you want a more upscale night. While I say "upscale", it's definitely not pretentious. It's been a while since I've gone on a Wednesday, but they used to have free bacon with every drink! I'm not sure if they still offer this, but if you find yourself out on a Wednesday, it's worth checking out! 

As another reviewer said, stick to the basics. The only bad drinks I've had were when I ordered something creative from their menu. If you like old fashions or Moscow mules, stick with those and you won't be disappointed!

Drinks, good. Food, good. Atmosphere when not busy, good. Atmosphere when busy, really bad. Too loud, too crowded, long wait in line to get a drink unless you are an opportunist or cut people (happened to me twice).  Then when you want to leave? Go wait in line to get your card and cash out. I would have ordered 2 more drinks and twice as much food if there was table service but left just generally unhappy and feeling like I spent more time in line than socializing with my friends. I seriously wonder.... If the average person would order more food and booze if they had table service, wouldn't this pay for 1-2 more servers to help take orders/get checks/refill drinks, etc?

Jeffrey and Thien have been walking my dog since he was a puppy  and I cannot imagine my life without them- I get weepy at the thought that someday I might move out of their walking zone. I look forward to each day's photos or video, to see what a cool life my dog is having while I'm sitting in my cubicle. If I wasn't so lazy about printing pictures, my walls would be plastered with the photos they send every day because they are incredible, I can barely get my dog to sit still and Thien has him lined up between other dogs on a bench overlooking the harbor (do not know how he does this!!!) My dog has boarded with them several times and he always comes back happy and exhausted, which is great since he has no energy to eat the walls like he once did.

Some of the best pizza I've ever had.

The indoor space is quite tiny, but it was cozy and intimate. The outdoor patio is bigger and also beautiful. Our waitress was very knowledgeable and prompt, and gave us great recommendations.

We loved getting to watch the chefs toss the pizza dough and it was fun watching the comraderie between the staff. There were 4 of us that shared the 1/2 size of the Caprese salad and 3 pizzas. We ended up eating everything...it was just the right amount of food!

The Caprese salad was seriously amazing. The heirloom tomatoes were incredibly flavorful and paired well with the chosen cheese (similar taste to mozzarella but different texture). The balsamic was very high quality.

The 3 pizzas we ordered were: the mushroom, the veggie, and the summer special. I didn't too much care for the veggie; the combination of black olives and peppery sprouts was a little weird for me. But I loved loved loved the mushroom! The special was also delicious...never would I have guessed that squash would be good on a pizza!

Definitely one of my favorite Columbus restaurants.

I went here unaccompanied, sat at the bar, and ordered a glass o' water, a small order of Loaded Cottage Fries, and a Press Burger. The "small order" of cottage fries was *not* in any way small, haha, and neither was the generous helping of sour cream in the center of the dish. X-) Also, it took me a while to remember that the Press Burger contains a fried egg, but what I was able to taste of it, I liked. :-) I'd recommend this place for lunch, especially because its prices are AMAZING ... although considering the restaurant's small size, I would expect this place to be crazy-congested during dinner time. :-D

If you are convinced you don't like tamales, you have to try Tamale Boy's tamales.  You'll be singing a new song.  At least that's what happened to me.  If all tamales were as good and inventive as theirs, I would've been eating these things years ago.  Better late than never, I suppose.  

The crew is energetic and you can tell they love what they're doing.  Maybe that's the secret ingredient in their tamales that puts them on a tier to their own.  Thanks Tamale Boys for showing me what a good tamale tastes like!

I keep joining Costco year after year. There are some things you just can't beat them for on price. I buy my eye glasses and contacts there. I spent a full 50% less than what I had spent at Lenscrafters. Of course, you don't have the convenience of a one hour wait, but if you aren't in a hurry, it's worth it to save so much. Soda is definitely a bargin as well as many of the staples you need in your house. Sometimes things are so much cheaper that buying the bigger size even when you are pretty sure you wont use it, is still cheaper! You are limited by large sizes for a lot of the things you might need, however. Their rotisserie chickens are excellent, as well as their prepared foods. There are great prices on alcohol, too. At the holidays, they carry lots of gift items and I have scored some really interesting things that you can't find anywhere else. I actually even bought my son his most recent cell phone at the cell phone outlet at Costco. They threw in the accessories for free and the price was competitive with the Verizon store, (minus the accessories). I will continue to shop at Costco as long as I am able. It's not super convenient for a household of two, but there are still bargains to be had!

I usually come here for brunch, and I think their brunch is great, and they are not as crazy busy as other Winter Park establishments. Btw, the mimosas are only $3. They have a good beer selection, and it features some rare finds like Belhaven. 

I finally visited them for lunch. I ordered the shepherd's pie, which was excellent.  I thought the lunch portion was big; I can't imagine how huge the dinner portion is.  It is a fun spot, they have live music and trivia nights.

Overall, 4 stars.

Do yourself a favor and go here.

Originally, I came here with friends a few months after Zuma first opened, and the experience was sub-par. However, Josh, the manager, made it right by listening to my feedback and encouraging us to come by and give it one more try. A year later, we came back, and let me tell you...Zuma is now my top restaurant in Boston. Needless to say, beyond glad we came back!

First of all, the service here is now spectacular. Tony, our server, was the highlight of the evening. He took great care of us-- we told him what we like and he said I got you. We ended up trying many different dishes-- the fish was FRESH and the specials were amazing as was the dessert and drinks.

You already know that the space is beautiful. It's located on the 2nd floor of the four seasons. Great vibes inside and friendly staff.

For drinks, honestly, the cocktails here are so so good. If you enjoy a nice craft cocktail, you will enjoy how aromatic the drinks are here and how much care goes into making each. Between myself and my friends, I was able to try 6 different cocktails and I thought each was so good. The bartenders clearly know what they are doing.

What we ate and what you should order:
1. Sashimi/Nigiri - Like I said, the fish here is FRESH. Salmon belly nigiri was my favorite.
2. Chu-toro tartare with miso bun - This was a special, to die for...if you can, PLEASE get it.
3. Edamame with sea salt - A well-executed classic. Damn, their sea salt is good...
4. gin-dara no saikyo yaki aka Black Cod BABYYYYY - I love this dish, my friends thought it was ok but I just really appreciate a good black cod. Yum.
5. Truffle Rice Hot Pot - I'm not sure if this is on the menu but ask for it (!!!). The flavor is 10/10 and they add fresh truffles on top. So comforting, basically the best risotto you'll ever have.
6. Grilled Asparagus - Good staple veggie.
7. Birthday surprise (I think this is the special dessert platter): Whatever you do, do not leave zuma without trying their chocolate lava cake. I've had lava cake 10000 times thinking "oh this is just another" but NO it's Zuma lava cake and to die for.

Ok I think I am done with my rant about how much I loved Zuma. Go and you'll understand.

For more foodie recommendations check out my insta: @internationalfoodieclub

Terrible terrible terrible.  I bought my tires from this location because they told me that my they would service my tires for life.  This is my second purchase from Kauffman but first time using this location.  The thing they fail to mention to me is that you will be waiting at least 3-6 hours (on a good day) to get your tires rotated.  So I left my car overnight and then returned the next day to see that they only did half of the job I requested, they rotated my tires but didnt patch my leaking tire.  Next purchase will be from NTB or a someone else.  This is just a good example of a company selling too many tires and not having enough service people to keep up with their end of the deal of lifetime tire rotations.

I discovered Sarah Seven shortly after becoming engaged last Autumn. IT WAS LOVE AT FIRST SIGHT! Unfortunately dealing with Sarah Seven is a little like having a crush on a boy who doesn't even know you're alive. I have sent 7 similarly worded emails over the last few months. The 2 responses I've receive have been short and led nowhere. Why do you have to play so hard to get, Sarah Seven? I would love nothing more then to be able to come back next year and write a 5 star review about my beautiful custom made dress but I'm not holding my breath.

Service was soooo slowwww, the food unremarkable, and not a good place for two people to go, unless you want to eat the same entree.  I like the idea of family style dining, and have seen it done really well at an italian restaurant in upstate New York, but here, it just doesn't seem worth the cost.  We ordered Chicken Marsala, expecting it to come on a bed of pasta, which it didn't- just chicken breast and mushrooms. The server forgot flatware, drinks, and then billed us for an entree at another table.  I will say, the cheesecake rocked.  Other than that, skip this place.  I have a Buca di Beppo cookbook that I love- next time I'll just cook something fabulous at home!

I was visiting a friend in Portland and the first place she took me was this wonderful book shop. It's a really great space filled with all things inspirational and spiritual located right in the heart of the most amazing area of Portland, 23rd Ave. Its very reminiscent of the Bodhi Tree Bookstore in LA - now closed :-(  The staff are friendly, too. My favorite sign in the place was back in a less-traveled nook that said "Shoplifting is Poverty Consciousness" Well done. I will be back!

Skullys used to be one of my favorite places to go for Thursday Ladies 80's. I decided to go last night to see a great Show and it was ruined by a security girl with blue hair. Somebody needs to put that ego maniac in check, coming at someone like a pit bull is not professional and a bad representation of Skullys. This girl wouldn't let you even talk or explain the situation instead starts yelling at us and swearing and acting completely irrational. She needed to be thrown out not my friends. My friends didn't do anything , they weren't drunk we had just walked in the door. My opinion is this girl was bullied as a child and now has anger issues and takes it out on patrons of this club. I definitely will not be coming back and won't recommend this club to anyone. I used to work at the Hyatt and would always tell people to go to this club. It's sad that they would allow someone to talk and treat there customers like this. Nobody deserves to be treated like this or disrespected yelled at with profanity. She needs fired before you loose valuable loyal patrons of this long standing club.

Our first visit, so I didn't quite know what to expect. Nice atmosphere and the food was exceptionally good and quite the surprise considering we just ordered a burger and their fried chicken burger there's a couple of beers. Very generous portions and the fries were too good to resist! Our server, Olivia, was a breath of fresh air in being very friendly and attentive without hovering. She seemed genuinely happy in her work. We live in Tualatin so we will be back and I look forward to enjoying the outside patio when the warm weather returns.

Excellent, inexpensive and unique. Go for mild flavors or make it crazy hot and interesting, it's all done to your liking.

Ramen is Japan's soul food and the ramen that most Americans eat is a plastic representation of  just how rich and delicious ramen can be. RTY uses fresh ingredients and the results are an explosion of surprisingly rich flavor.

The atmosphere is cool but not pretentious with big murals of dragons and awesome ceiling art. A bit noisy but it's all good noise and fits well with the beards and tattoo's that many of the diners don.

I can't recommend this place enough, except that if you go you're making it harder for me to get in.

Took my aunt and grandmother to Petrillo's yesterday for lunch.  Gram and I had the cheese lasagna with a meatball special, while Auntie had spaghetti and meatballs.  Auntie said the spaghetti was cooked perfectly al dente and the marinara sauce was smooth and delicious.  My lasagna was excellent, too.  The meatball was tasty as well.  My only complaints are these: It was very dark inside the restaurant, which is nicely decorated, but the pendant lights do not hang over each table, so it was hard to see.  Also, my meal was not piping hot when it arrived.  It was certainly warm enough, but by the time I'd made my way through about half the lasagna, it was starting to get cold.  Reasonable prices, good food, and there is a room upstairs for group parties.

Just had dinner and our food was wonderful as usual! Perfectly seasoned and SO much better than the one on Bethel Rd. I don't think they're sister restaurants, but I do believe they are relatives. 

Their Turkish wines are amazing! 

We enjoy getting several appetizers, entrees and desserts so we can sample different menu items and have leftovers for a few meals. 

Our server, Rose, was so nice. She gave us great and honest recommendations, almost all of which we went with! Her timing of our courses was impeccable! We didn't feel rushed, nor did we have to sit and wait overlong between courses.

The rest of the staff is so friendly you almost feel like a face recognized because of the warm greetings and farewells!

How could this place not get 5 stars!! We went there for happy hour where I discovered we were far from the only people to know about this place. The line moved quickly and before we knew it we were holding our empty glass waiting in line for a beer. What I was impressed about was how quickly the beer line moved. Many times when you go to a place like this the lines take forever and it takes away from the fun and atmosphere- not this place. The other thing I was waiting for was piss poor beer. I mean, $8 for 6 tickets and a free glass with the only caveat being that you have a max of 2 hours to finish it.

The beer was very good! I kept hearing about Blue and it lived up to all the expectations and all. It was really light yet had a good flavor to it. Since beer is subjective, it's tough to agree on what's good or not but I'll keep going. I really like the light wheat but didn't care for the regular wheat. The 420 was too bland for me. I really loved the Dank Tank. In fact, I got two glasses. Happy Ending was decent and I didn't get a shot at Brown b/c they ran out. The IPA was quite impressive as well.
