Without a question the next time I'm in ATL you will see me there in line right as happy hour is about to start! I'm maximizing my experience here! ;)

We have been very fortunate to have numerous occasions to indulge in Spoon & Co catering (from office catering to cocktail and engagement parties and more). Their food genre covers the gambit and it is always delicious. 

In addition, Meg and her team catered our night before wedding party at TFWC mansion. She handled absolutely everything and all we had to do was show up and spend time with our family and friends. Of course, she spent time with us beforehand planning the menu, alcohol and drinks and decor set up details. If you don't know what you want, she can help you figure it out and if you do, she fine tunes it for you. Our night turned out beautifully just as expected. She also has a great team (bartenders, etc) 

We got tons and tons of compliments on the food.  It was unique combined with Austin flair for our out of town guests and very special. Plus the presentation was also spot on. Spoon & Co is very versatile too and really makes you feel valued even with the existing strength of their repeat client list. Meg is super professional, talented, creative and has a heart of gold. She loves what she does and it shows! 

One last thing...they plan perfectly for the number of guests...I have been to too many events and parties where the food runs out which then overshadows the rest no matter how beautiful everything else is. Our family and friends are eaters! This is not even a worry with Spoon & co.

I've had a massage before, and I've paid out the a$$ for it, and it's been okay. Then I tried a massage at Breathe...and my world was flipped around, upside down, inside out. SHE IS AWWWWWESOME!!! I have never had a better massage and I don't think a better one actually exists. Now I go back every other week for an hour and my husband takes a half hour on my off weeks. 

Rachel's massage technique helped reduce the frequency of migraines. She's also been able to offer informed advice on diet, and lifestyle changes I can make to further reduce the headaches. I'm also encouraged that she constantly seeks to educate herself on massage technique, anatomy, and health and fitness. I am confident that she will continue to get better and better. Not to mention, she's very careful to make sure she hits the spots you need her to, and she takes time to make sure she understands your specific needs. She'll also be quiet and let you relax during the whole massage or she'll talk to you as much as you want her to. We've had some amazing conversations over the last few years! (I'm a talker)

Do yourself a BIG favor and check her out! Just be aware your hair will look crazy afterwards so don't plan any big important meetings.

Having become accustomed to  Grand Central Market in LA I was happy to hear Portland had something similar. Located downtown this place is a pleasant surprise. The streets surrounding this market feel a little gritty. Homeless people and smells and a few empty baggies lying around on the sidewalk. However once your inside the market is very open and inviting. A good array of some iconic Portland food establishments to choose from. I ate lunch from Common Law but there were lots of good looking options. The guys from Olympia Provisions have a hot dog stand that looks amazing! I'll have to try that one next time I'm back up there. 

I arrived a little before the lunch crowd rush so I had no problem ordering and finding a place to sit but once lunchtime came the place got packed! 

I'm excited and curious to see how over time this market adapts and improves with additional vendors. For me part of what makes a market like this great is that it continues to grow and offer more variety.

This place is a ball of fun!  Went with the family and from the moment you walk in it's fun, friendly, and unique. The service was fantastic and the food was so good. I had the spaghetti and meatballs and sampled and heard nothing but good reviews on the lobster tail entree and chicken Alfredo.  At 8:30pm the hats come out and it turned into an upbeat party, never seen this at a restaurant before. Make sure you check this place out - top notch Italian with an environment to help make it a memorable night. We all left with smiles!

We prepaid for a car that they didn't have on the lot when we arrived. When we asked what could be done the Manager laughed as if quality service and the car being prepared that we scheduled and paid for when we got there was a ridiculous thing for us to expect. She whispered to her colleagues while clearly and loudly making derogatory comments towards us while we waited. It took us over 2 hours to get our car. Nobody notified us that our car was ready when it came even though we were waiting in the main lobby. This was without a doubt the worst experience I have ever had with a car rental service. Will never use or recommend Hertz to anyone again. The manager working today at Wednesday 5/16 at 9am could clearly not care less about the situation or how to rectify it.

I'm only giving Chow Baby 2 stars because the veggies are actually very fresh. The service was absolutely horrible though.

I was immediately turned off by the fact that they valet even for lunch, so I'm immediately out a buck before I walk in the door. 

This was my first time in, so I was unsure of how things worked. I was shown to the bar, where I was handed a little wooden paddle. That's where the service stopped. The process is strange, so they definitely need to offer explanation to first-timers. You place the ingredients you want in separate bowls - one for veggies and rice, one for meat. You're supposed to choose your sauce like you would a salad dressing. This is tricky because there's no option to taste them and there are no descriptions aside from basic names (Teriyaki, Red Curry, etc). So if you choose wrong, your $8.99 meal is ruined. 

I passed my bowls to the "chef" for him to prepare and proceeded to wait at the bar for 15 minutes. I suppose it normally wouldn't take so long, since the meal was already prepared and only needed to be stir-fried, but the bartender allowed my food to sit directly behind him without checking to see if it was mine. And there was no apology - he actually laughed at his mistake. So I paid $14 for a stir-fry with a by then soggy spring roll and a cup of tea, with $1.30 gratuity included. 

I'll order in Chinese next time and avoid the hassle.

I visited during dinner time and was immediately impressed with the ambiance and decor. It wasn't extremely crowded since it was a week night. We were seated right away and our waitress came over to take our drink orders. I ordered a glass of wine and for my entree, I ordered salmon with mixed veggies. 

My salmon was moist and flavorful, one of the best that I've had. The mixed veggies were basic. It was okay because the star was the fish. My coworker ordered steak with grilled shrimp on the side. His steak looked moist and delicious. Our food was delicious. We would definitely visit this restaurant again if we're working in the area.

My family and I made a 3pm reservation for a late lunch today (Father's Day) and upon getting there, there was a bit of a wait - totally normal (especially due to the holiday). The hostess apologized and I joked with her that my family grew up in food service so we totally get it! I was a server for 10 years - so I am always completely understanding of kitchen & front of house struggles. 

However, this was the worst service I've ever experienced in a restaurant. We sat down a bit after 3pm, and it took 10 minutes for a server to come over and take our drink orders. It then took another 15 minutes for us to get those drinks. 

At that time, we put our lunch and starting course orders in. All of my family ordered chowder and I ordered a Caesar salad. Food runners brought the chowders and not my salad - I figured that since it came from a different kitchen line, it'd be coming separately. Well, it never came. It wasn't until our server came over to the table to clear the soups, that I had my first opportunity to tell him I never got my salad. No apology - just, "Oh," then he went to get it. 

Five minutes later he comes out with something other than my salad and walks right by my table into another room. At that point I'm so sure he forgot again. Five minutes after that, I get my Caesar Salad in a hot dish that just came out of the dishwasher. It's whatever, that's life. Not the end of the world! 

Meals finally come out (yum!!) and everything looks and tastes great!! I got the scallops with green beans and mashed potato. Don't get me wrong - the food was wonderful. My meal came with 9 scallops! Very impressive, however, filling. I ate about 5, so I wanted to take it home for lunch tomorrow. When we finished, we were waiting for a good 20 minutes before being cleared - to which we were by the manager and food runner. 

Before I give him my plate, I tell him that I'd like to box it up. My food was literally MIA for 15 minutes. I was so sure it had disappeared into the trash (since I saw the gentleman who took it to box out and about in the dining room), but then the food runner comes out with it boxed up and apologizes for the wait. I take a look in and there it is - my green beans, mashed potato, and a HALF SCALLOP. Literally. There was one half of a scallop. My family thought I had miscounted before but I would not have taken it home had it been that little amount of protein. 

Food was great - however very disappointed in service. I feel for the server because I know how busy it gets, but what ticked me off was he had no sense of urgency and didn't apologize once for the poor service. Sometimes just acknowledging it and saying "I'm sorry for the wait," makes all the difference.

Hidden jewel. One of the few authentic Japanese restaurants in Orlando. I'm half Japanese (from my mother's side) and I'm extremely particular about Japanese cuisine - I'm not a fan of Americanized  chains like Kobe's *gag*. If you're looking for REAL Japanese cuisine made by REAL Japanese chefs and owned by REAL Japanese people...this is the spot.

It's tucked away within a plaza, it's a pretty small and cozy restaurant with limited seating (and also has an additional room for private groups with a karaoke machine set up). Their Katsu Kare is my ultimate favorite (just like my mom makes them).

If you're ever in the Universal/I-Drive area, definitely check them out.

xx MJ

Wanting to try a new Indian restaurant on Diwali, we ended up at Bhojanic per Yelp's recommendation. 

Since every other Indian in Atlanta also decided to eat out that night, the wait was long, but there was live music and a nice waiting area by the bar, so that was fine. We got a table outside, which was probably a good thing, because the weather was great and the music inside was too loud for table conversation.

I ordered a veg thali with three items. The dal makhani was absolutely great, but the paneer dish and aloo gobi were bland and nothing special.

I don't know if this was an average experience, but I'd say that Cafe Bombay's thali is consistently better than what I got that night, and gets you a similar style of food and classy ambiance.

I have to say, we really enjoyed the quality of this Indian restaurant. (I docked them 1 star because there were two pieces of chicken bone in my Chicken Mahkani that I found in my left overs and they were big...like size of a nickel to quarter big. And a piece of cartilage that was the same size. The kitchen staff needs to be more careful when chopping up their chicken!) Okay, soooo again, the quality of the chicken was good AND the flavor of the chicken mahkani was delicious AND our Tandoori Salmon was fabulous. Tandoori Salmon? I have never seen that on a menu here in the US...so of course we had to try it. We definitely suggest it. Lastly we tried Cheese Naan. Also, never seen this on a menu AND it was yummo. Overall we had a very good experience and will go back. Sorry no pics, we dove right in.

I've been a loyal customer for 5+ years.  For the first 4 it was OK.  Then I assume they got new management.  I will not be going back again.

Ok... so a few years ago they changed their alignment machine... my car wouldn't fit on the new one.  Whatever... I paid for their 3 year package, I got to use it once... total rip off, and the refused to refund my money, just told me to go to another shop.  I should have listened.

Then I went in for an oil change, asked them to test my battery, and found out about 3 days later that they put my Battery Cover on crooked and it fell down between the engine and heat shield... plastic melted all over my engine.  A year later my car still smells like burning plastic.  No reimbursement was offered, they just said, "Oh, sorry... it'll burn off."

Recently they destroyed the Engine Splash Shield during an oil change and literally wired it on with like really crappy wire (like a coat hanger maybe or bailing wire) and duct tape.  It didn't even make it home and I heard plastic dragging.  I asked them why they didn't tell me they broke it, and they totally denied that they had done it.  Really?  Who put the duct tape on it?!

No clue why I kept going back, except they'd been good guys in the past.

SHADY.  Do not trust these guys now.

After what has been a week of uncertainty, we went to try this place that has been on my bucket list ever since it was rated by Air Canada as the 2nd best restaurant in Canada. We managed to make it in time for happy hour and recommend standing at the bar as they hand out on the house tapas. They gave us what was similar to an arancini ball with black squid ink inside and it was delicious, paired with their HH red wine, it was much needed given what's going on lately. Then they gave us sautéed mushrooms on toast given my dietary restrictions of no beef or pork. Then I ordered mushroom croquetas (3 to an order) which were so flavorful. Then we went to sit at a table and shared the charred octopus (which is their most popular item) and it was one of best I have had. Smaller portion given the price but it is a tapas after all. Also since we enjoyed the first on the house tapas, and it could not be ordered as they make those fresh daily I believe only for happy hour on the house tapas, the bartender suggested the arroz negro, black squid ink paella rice which was excellent. It was a very satisfying meal to what has been an emotional week. So glad finally got to try this place and would definitely go back.  They know what they're doing! Only negative was one of the restrooms had a broken plate on the floor which was not safe for their guests but they had other restrooms so figured they would take care of it once I informed the staff.

Must order: 
Chicken and Waffles!!!! I ordered only one piece of chicken and it was such an enormous portion!!! The fried chicken was delicate, yet crispy and boy was it ever so juicy!

The Praline Bacon was out of this world! The dish comes with three strips of bacon. I nearly devoured the entire thing by myself.

The Carolina Pulled Pork Sandwich inside a toasted bun was dripping with tangy BBQ sauce, and the Mac N Cheese rich. 

Service was pleasant and we completely enjoyed this lunch! Parking sucks though.

I love love love this cute little bakery and cafe!  I stopped at Pistachia Vera during a trip to Columbus because I'm a huge macaron fan and had heard that they had the best. I was delighted by the variety they had. They varied from traditional to some more creative flavors. I took home a dozen and tried a good selection and everyone was delicious. What made the experience even better though was the staff. They were friendly and took time to have a conversation while they served every customer. My only caution is that they're very busy and the establishment is small so there may be a wait. Rest assured though, Pistachia Vera is worth every minute you wait.

I rarely give bad reviews, however, I want this location to hear the feedback.  This used to be one of my favorite go to spots for a quick bite but sadly the quality has been declining.  My most recent experience was really the final straw.  We received guacamole (large with chips) that was brown all the way through.  It was gross looking.  We had two burritos that were ruined with the old guacamole.  My burrito bowl was ice cold and inedible. Four calls to the store went unanswered.  If this location is to survive, based on this and other reviews, something needs to change here fast.

I went through the drive thru and placed an order.  Upon arriving at the pay window the employee told me I should have came inside for an order like that. After receiving the order, I checked it and determined every item was wrong except the coffee. Instead of croissants they gave me English muffins, instead of 10 munchkins I received 2 and the sweet tea was unsweetened.  I also realized there was no receipt for my purchase. 

I went inside and had to wait for 5 people to order before I could speak with an employee. After telling him the issue he told me to wait for the manager. Five minutes later she asked what the issue was and corrected the issues. We left and forgot to taste the tea until we were down the road; much to my dismay it was unsweetened again.  

Returned to the store and they corrected it again and gave us a few donuts as compensation.  The moral of the story is poor service all around, they were polite but apparently incompetent. I'll not be returning to this particular location again.

Simply OMG!  In Vancouver for 5 days on business and ate here for lunch three times....that's how good the sandwiches are here.  Am I sad that I didn't venture out for lunch elsewhere?....nah!  They do one thing (sandwiches) and their selection is focused (changes daily), but what they do they do well!  Ate the porchetta (their 'house' go to order) which I had to constrain myself from ordering a second of because it was so good.  Only regret is that I didn't have the lamb sandwich the first day I went as it wasn't on the menu when I returned.

I've been here a few times, and I've consistently had a satisfactory experience. They have a decent selection of draft beers (including Sam Brick Red!), and decent food as well. Not amazing, but it's a pub. When I'm craving fish & chips and I'm in the Back Bay, I know I can count on Lir to come through for me. The bartenders are overall pretty friendly, the crowd is tame - which basically means the guys will leave you alone and you never have to worry about getting spilled on, or having to scream to have a conversation. The bar is quite big, and they have a cool table service area toward the back. Lir is clean, relaxed, and unpretentious - tried and true.

The host told us that it would be about a 20-25 minute wait and it was packed for a Friday night. I only felt like we waited about 10-15 minutes though. So at least the wait wasn't too long. Came in tonight for the never ending classics special. You can mix and match entrees as long as it's equal or lesser value. You still get unlimited soup or salad and breadsticks with this deal too. I got the Zuppa toscana soup and I also got the chicken gnocchi. Last time I got the zuppa it was not very good. Tonight it was a lot better, so I was happy. 

The entrees I got:

Chicken Parmesan - I liked the chicken on this, but one of my chicken pieces was more tougher than the other and just tasted like fake chicken. I wasn't really a fan of the red sauce for it. The sauce was a little too acidic and tangy for my taste. 

Lasagna - The lasagna had sort of a weird taste to it. It tasted like lamb in a way and I do not like lamb. It had that weird taste more towards like the burnt. Some parts of it tasted fine, but overall wasn't a fan of it. 

Five cheese rigatoni - This one was my favorite one. I love the five cheese sauce at Olive Garden. Although, since this was my third entree I only could take a couple bites and had to take it togo lol. 

Overall I wasn't really impressed with the food tonight. Our server was Marilynn and she was awesome! She always filled our water and asked if we were ok. She was also very prompt when it came to asking us about our refills for soups and entrees. I give an extra star for her because she made it a great dining experience.

This place is awesome. I am a runner for various venues around Boston at times. One thing that always comes up is dry cleaning being done the same day. Has to be done the same day because these people are leaving the night of or early in the morning. It's impossible to find same day dry cleaning last min in Boston. 

I brought my client's clothes here 4 days in a row and no problem at all. It was pleasant to go in and see them everyday. The woman is very helpful and her daughter is super sweet.

Yum! Fresh fish and nice atmosphere! Came with family for lunch during the week, all three of us got the sushi lunch specials which were a great bite at a great price. 

Parking is easy in the free parking structure by the shopping center. The restaurant is within an outdoor mall area and was easy to find.

Their menu is extensive with many roll options that include vegetarian options and options without raw fish. Since living in Boston, I've learned it is tough to find a good sushi restaurant near Boston that focuses on just sushi/Japanese cuisine rather than offering a wide variety of pan-Asian cuisine. This restaurant just has Japanese cuisine and you can bet it's good!

0 stars............. 
I don't believe yelp reviews much anymore as Vancouverites tend to over-rate mediocre joints but it's nice to see some sanity here.

Here are since reasons to stay away ( btw there's so much wrong you can write a book):

1. Horrible dining experience - seafood is served in shitty plastic bags that leak.
Servers just pile the food in their plastic bags on front of you like you're eating in a dump and they do not care that you have no room on the table to eat.For reference, I've been in the US stores and have never had this problem.

2. Server/manager is brain-dead and disorganized - waited 20 minutes to have the order placed despite constantly nagging and finally had to force him to write down what we want. Soup its served in 1 small bowl with 4 spoons for a table of four. Did he think we'd all eat from the same bowl??? Manager was a dumbass. Asked if we'd like to order garlic bread as it goes well with the sauces in the plastic bags that served the food. I replied the sauces were not exactly easily accessible as they were in the bags, maybe some empty saucers may help. She then seemed confused and walked off. 

3. Food and overpricing
I didnt expect anything great as the food is just broiled, nonetheless I've not had such tasteless seafood ever. The crawfish was way too tiny and tasteless, 3lbs dungeness crab felt like 1.5lbs, everything else tasted like shit despite overpriced "seasonal" prices.

Just don't go. Get real seafood from the Global joints or likes of Blue Water et al...

This is a cute little Vietnamese restaurant located in a shady strip mall on Wells branch. It's a little hidden but you can't miss the huge sign once you drive up. 

When we walked in for dinner, we were the only people there aside from the staff. The music was blaring and it was awesome, let me tell you. Very traditional Asian karaoke-ish music. 

I ordered the Pho Ga and it is probably the best i've had in Austin. 

I will definitely be returning here if not for the food, for the stage.... Karaoke?!?!

You're going to love dining here at Tupelo Honey Cafe. It's located in Sandy Springs, Georgia.

Upon my arrival into the restaurant I immediately noted that all staff were wearing face mask, and it's required that all dining guest must also wear a face mask when moving about throughout the restaurant. The hostess who greeted me quickly found my reservation I had made through Open Table.

I then chose outdoor dining on the lovely covered patio, and it has over head umbrellas which protected me from the hot Georgia heat.

I ordered their bourbon peppercorn meatloaf. It's slow-roasted beef & chorizo. My sides were fried okra and Yukon mashed potatoes. Ladies and gents the meat loaf was about 3 inches deep, and it tasted magnificent! The hot fried okra was seasoned perfectly, and I'm telling you it's good enough to write home about it! My mashed potatoes arrived cold upon first serving, but upon telling Kelly, my server the issue I had hot mashed potatoes in under a New York minute, and they too were very good. 

The restaurant is in a really nice plaza filled with lots of places to walk short distances, and do some shopping before, or after you dine. You know where to dine next time your in Georgia and that's at Tupelo Honey Cafe. It's good southern eating!

To read the full blog go to www.diarytalkandmore.com and click the link Dining Today!

#DiaryTalkWithTamela

I really enjoy various healthy options they serve.  There are multiple locations of Clover and this one is as good as any other. 

They have a few tables where you can sit and enjoy your lunch in case you want to be away from your office.

As much as I enjoy their sandwiches they could be hard to eat without a fork sometimes ... because a sandwich dressing would start leaking as you are getting closer to finish your sandwich.  If they could prepare their dressings of a thicker consistency it will be perfect.

Nevertheless, if you are a vegetarian and want "tasty" "exotic" options, give this place a try - you will truly love it.

We came here on a Monday night and were pleased to find only four groups ahead of us in line. The wait was relatively short- maybe about 15 minutes and there's plenty of people watching to entertain yourself while you wait. We were seated at a table for two that very closely abutted another table for two- so much that it almost felt like we dining with two others. It's pretty cramped in here. However, it was not overly loud, which was nice and we could easily converse. We ordered a bottle of wine and we each got the linguine with half a lobster, mussels and clams in the Giacomo's lobster sauce. So delicious and very reasonably priced at around $20 per plate. Note that they are cash only, so make sure to have cash on hand. The food was absolutely amazing- so fresh and delicious and served piping hot. 

My only complaint was that our server was kind of abrupt. He basically told me that no he wasn't giving me any more parmesan cheese on top of the pasta when I indicated I wanted more. He also threw down our water, wine and meals- nothing delicate about the placement of the glasses or dishes here. Moreover, when my companion got up to use the bathroom, both our server and another server tried to clear the plate away. Our server even argued with me about it. The food came out really quick though, so no complaints about the speed of the service. You do feel kind of rushed to eat and leave because there's a line of people waiting, but the food is really good quality and a great price. Very cool North End experience. Highly recommend.

Solid 4 - 4.5 stars. Price and size of sandwich are the detractors. 

I went for the trio, taste each sandwich roll offered. Lobster roll was the best, Shrimp roll, then Crab. Overall, the roll is what made the roll over the top tasty. You can expect whichever roll you order to be brimming over the top with meat, a big plus. The roll itself, buttery, lightly toasted and with a thin slapping of mayo...really, the roll was the bomb! 

Also, tried the clam chowder, was a bit too watery for my taste, and no Tabasco sauce available...3 stars for the Chowder.

I'd recommend the lobster roll, skip the other two, especially if lobster is what you are craving. 

To drink, the craft root beer was really good. They offer chilled tap water in the drink cooler for those traditionalist like myself...

I'll be back for more lobster roll, oh, and it's Maine style...the meat isn't heated or warmed in any way for the rolls. Just FYI. Yummy. That roll! 

Price - a bit high for what ya get, but I'm not a Bawstonian, so maybe my expectations were off for prices in the big city.

I popped in to grab chocolates for my girlfriend on Valentine's Day. The idea of having a local neighborhood chocolate shop is wonderful. They did not disappoint with the chocolate or the service. The pastries definitely do need some work, however. I doubt I'd go back for anything but chocolate. I also noticed they were not playing any type of background music like another reviewer commented on - may want to try something to liven the place a bit. Hope they stick around, the South End needs these types of local businesses.

I want to love this place.  The pizza is very close to "northern" pizza.  It is by far surperior to Mellow Mushoom's doughy drug fueled hit or miss.  The pizza is always hot, and 2 out of 2 times it has been perfect.  The issue I have is usually about 12am, when it feels like I just ate undercooked Indian food.   It is not like I order sausage, or peppers, just plain cheese pizzas. I have a hearty stomach, but wtf is going on here? I will keep eating here despite the "risks" because it taste so good.  Their beer selection is also amazing.

U Me is Yummy!  We checked it out last night after hearing about them on Fox 25 news.  I love Korean food (since my fiance is Korean!) and we were very excited to hear about a new place in the suburbs.  They offer a nice mix of Korean, Thai, and Japanese food.  

We started with miso soup and the veggie spring rolls.  Both were delicious!  The miso soup was fresh with lots of seaweed and the spring rolls were fresh and crispy, but not too oily.  Perfect!  

We ordered Bulgogi and a veggie stir fry with tofu.  The Bulgogi was the best we've ever had!!!  It was very sweet (yum!) and very tender.  Delicious!  The stir fry was also very good and the veggies were perfectly cooked.

The service was fantastic as well!  Our server, Boyd, was very attentive and welcoming.  He even turned down the AC for me when I was freezing!

Our other favorite place for bulgogi is Koreana in Cambridge which has Korean BBQ, but U Me is awesome for when we don't feel like making the drive.  Overall, we're very excited to have U Me close by!

Moved here from Seattle and was looking for a good pizza place, Bellagio's was suggested by a friend. Not a good choice....sauce tasted like extra salty tomato paste, hardly any chicken on it, the chicken was dry and tasteless, the crust was way overcooked.
While we were ordering,  a very large man was behind the counter screaming in to his cell phone at what sounded like an employee. We were told his name was "Joel" and that he owned "most of the Bellagio's locations." He seemed pretty unaware of his behavior....won't go back, especially if it puts money in Joel's pocket. Will try Hot Lips next time.

I was looking forward to a varied sampling via the usual buffet, but Namaste only does Buffet on Fridays. (Strike one.) Starving, and determined to know the quality of this place, I perused the menu. I decided the best place to start was with my standard staples for this kind of meal: Samosas and Lentil Soup. To my surprise, the waiter asked how spicy I wanted my soup, so I responded "spicy is fine, thanks."

Thus began one of the most memorable and uncomfortable dining experiences of my life.

Before I continue, know that I love spicy food; several bottles of habañero sauce perpetually inhabit my kitchen cupboard, and these are not mild; some of my favorites are Melinda's XXXX (yes, 4x) Reserve Habañero sauce and Melinda's Red Savina (the Red Savina was the hottest pepper in the world until 2006). These bottles of sauce are used so frequently that they are replaced several times a year. I know spicy, & I don't shy-away from spicy food. I can always handle the heat as long as there is an accompanying depth of flavor; heat for the sake of heat ruins food & flavor.

My lentil soup arrived with the samosas; the latter was a very pleasant surprise from the onset because I had expected to receive one per order, but received three. The samosas lasted only a few minutes, and I have no complaints about those except for the wasted, wilted, 3 tiny pieces of lettuce which served as a garnish; the accompanying mint sauce was divine. The lentil soup was simply too hot (temperature) to eat, so I stirred while I waited for my rose lassi. When the lassi arrived I was underwhelmed; I expected a subtle rose flavor to accompany the cooling effect of the sweet yogurt, but instead it had an artificial, cloying sweetness. Shortly after that, my vegetable korma arrived (also "spicy") so I decided to finally give my hunger it's last hurrah and made a bed of rice to receive the korma.

That rose lassi quickly vanished after a few bites of what was the most inedibly-spicy food I have ever "tasted" (as if there was any taste involved). Being a self-assessed champion of spicy food, I accepted the challenge, as those of us who know truly spicy food realize that sometimes true enjoyment involves just going for it until you hit that plateau where you can handle the heat and it enhances your experience; this never happened with the vegetable korma, which just seemed to be so angry with me that it wanted me dead. I sweated, my eyes watered, I gasped for air, I soaked my napkin with the perpetual effluence of fluids from my face between every single bite. I quickly ordered another lassi, this time a plain (screw flavor at this point, or so I thought) sweet lassi. I took a break before my new friend arrived, and that lassi proved to be the highlight of the meal; gently flavored with cardamom and slightly sweet,  it was an oasis the endless desert of despair that was my meal.

I went back for the korma, determined to not be defeated by a dish I've had (and enjoyed) hundreds of times, but I couldn't do it; my throat started to close, and my stomach ached. I decided that maybe this was a good time for the soup, which had surely cooled enough to eat by this point. Talk about out of the pan and into the flames; the soup, supposedly the same "heat" level as the korma, assaulted me on a new level of spicy.

I guzzled my lassi, asked for the check, and requested a package for my leftovers.

One reviewer here said that the wait-staff seemed to not know what was happening, and this was also my experience; two separate waiters seemed to haunt my table, both often asking me the same question and offering me the same things. One waiter would offer me rice, would leave to go fetch it, then another would come immediately after and say he would get me more rice; no rice would arrive until I pointed it out myself. This was also the case with my beverages, and some food I did not order also arrived at my table. 
(Strike two.)

I think that the food was also slightly overpriced for what it was. If I had driven 10 minutes to Westminster for Yak & Yeti I could have had more food for $10 less than I paid at Namaste; I could have driven 5 minutes down Baseline to The Taj and had more food for the same price; I could have had the same amount of food, for the same price, at (what used to be) The Royal Peacock. Namaste just didn't measure-up financially. The exception was the samosa order, but still: if I had gone to the Yak & Yeti buffet I would have had all the samosas I wanted for a smaller bill overall.

The final straw was when my food was brought to me in a carry-out container. The waiter had thoughtfully piled rice inside before bringing it to my table, but I was disappointed that the container was styrofoam. In a town like Boulder this is really not acceptable. (Strike three.)

I will not be visiting Namaste again. Heat-seekers: a new challenge awaits you; Nepali Spicy.

I took my 12 year old Dutch Shepherd to Dr. Valentine looking for help with a few different old-dog health issues, incontinence, arthritis, and some eye inflammation among them. My dog received a thorough examination, and I answered questions about her habits, life, and personality. 
Dr. Valentine then explained my dog's strengths and weaknesses as Chinese Medicine would see them, gave my dog a lovely acupuncture treatment, and sent me home with herbal formulas and dietary suggestions.
My husband and I both noticed a difference in the first 36 hours of her being on her formulas. She was more energetic, moving more freely, and her eyes were less red. Now it's been 8 days, and she continues to improve. She has increased energy and joy for life, and is wagging her tail and smiling more often.
I highly recommend Balanced Pets NW!

This Wawa's is near Disney.

They didn't have a full pretzel only a Half pretzel.

I ordered a whole wheat chicken sub and a quesadilla added a super good warm soft baked cookie.

The coffee had to be picked up from the coffee section my order wasn't put all together and I forgot my coffee. I got to the car and my husband asked about his Cappucino I forgot about it. That's when the girl who made the food order told me you pick up coffees in a different section.

I've been to my share of dueling piano places, but this place was probably the least entertaining, and it wasn't for a lack of effort.  The way that the chairs and tables were placed, everyone had their own conversations going on, and the singing was mostly background noise.

If you come early enough, they have a 'buffet' with some carrots/celery, meatballs, and pasta.  Their fishbowl type drinks have 8 ounces of 'liquor' but it was mostly just really sweet and we had to order four (yes, four) additional shots to pour in for it to be even remotely worth drinking that much liquid.

They don't serve food here.  The bartenders aren't really friendly.  The people who seemed to be having the most fun were those who came with the 'happy hour package' crowd with a wristband.

I have been a Consumer Cellular customer for more than 10 years and was happy with the service except for a few glitches like messaging not working every so often or calls dropping occasionally. But I decided to add my wife to my plan and on every contact with Consumer Cellular I stressed that she could not be without a cell phone & they promised repeatedly that the transfer would be instant. Now my wife's old phone is not functional  & we are being told her new Consumer Cellular phone won't be active for at least 36 hours later.  There is no nice way to say it, they lied to me. It appears that customer service tells you what ever they think you want to hear without any concern whether it is true or not.

Wow, what can I say. Pros: food is phenomenal, drinks are sensational, you gotta try these spiked milkshakes, very good, 11/10.
Cons: we asked about the burger of the day, made sure it was vegetarian friendly, made it known that we don't eat meat, and subbed for beyond patties. Pretty sure the burger still had bacon on it, yolo I guess. Also ordered HH fries, never got them. Like we drank our shakes, ate our other app, ate our entire meal, no HH fries. So we just cancelled the order. Pretty sure we then saw them come out of the kitchen and then they gave them to the table next to us on the house...Then they were gracious enough to tell us they "took it off the bill for us". Thank you for removing an item from our bill that we never received, how nice, love it. They also took my HH app off the bill that I did receive, just because, which was nice I guess lol

I second everything Colleen said. Bee's Knees is also one of my local favs. In addition to having awesome treats: like mini cupcakes, truffles, chocolate-covered marshmallows, and mini cheesecakes, Erica and Emily are two of the nicest ladies. Every time I see them, they are eager to say hello. They always take the time to get to know their customers and talk to each and every person that approaches them at a market or at Redlight Redlight.

I highly recommend you find out where they are right now and go get some treats.

PS: The new orange mini cupcake (made with local honey) and the cookies & cream mini cheesecake are to die for. Just sayin'.

Headed to Picco for dinner and totally enjoyed it. Ragtime music, an ice cream bar befitting a bow tie wearing soda jerk (*hint* anyone from Picco reading this please consider), pizza, and craft beer. It's like an adult's Chuck-E-Cheese except without the ball pit. 

The appetizers were delicious - we had the stuffed jalapenos and the caprese bruschetta. From an entree perspective, I'll admit that we didn't have the pizza. (I might give it a try next time, more on that later...) The mac and cheese is good - a mix of stinky cheeses that's oh so gooey . The fish tacos, which seem to have been written up a bunch of times by the Globe, are good, but I wouldn't say great. If you like fish, these are for you as Picco makes sure you get your money's worth of fish. But, I prefer my fish tacos to feature battered and deep fried fish. And, let's be honest. You don't eat fish tacos because you want great fish. It's the cabbage slaw and delicious condiments that really makes a fish taco pop and Picco's rendition just isn't quite the flavor bomb I look for with fish tacos. 

Overall, I'd love to give Picco four stars and I probably will once I try the pizza because it looked great. But, while we were sitting eating dinner and watching the cooks making pizza, we noticed that one of the cooks regularly scrapes the oven with some sort of brush/broom. This seems like good practice to keep the oven clear and brush out any burned bits, but the cook took promptly placed the broom back on the floor! Normally, I don't care about stuff touching the floor and I'm sure most kitchens have worse infractions, but Picco's open kitchen and the fact that the pizza oven is directly across from the restroom is quite disconcerting especially since it looks like the pizzas go straight down onto the cooking surface. Yes, most of you are thinking, "So, what? The oven is almost 600 degrees! You can't get sick from that." In my head, I believe it, but with the possibility of poo particles (cooked or uncooked) touching my food, i have to take a star away for that...

Run by a professional sales staff, unless you are buying don't ask for anything. Own eight family crypts in a memorial we paid $8K for. Went to ask where my aunt and uncle are interred and was given a hard sell. After some discussion they gave me a map but couldn't provide me with any idea where the section was or provide a cemetery map. Stumbled upon the plots marked on the map, no relatives there? If I knew they were unmarked graves I would have gotten my cousins together on a monument. Either they missed a sale or gave me wrong information. Currently checking into moving my family monument else where.

I love that I can finally get some onigiri in town without having to drive over to Hanamizuki off I-drive. The restaurant is located inside a renovated fast food restaurant, and the decor is reminiscent of a quaint Japanese family run establishment. The service is excellent and the food authentic. There is sushi here, but I would also give the other foods a try. It reminded me of the late nights we would go in Japan to get snacks. I would recommend the salmon katsu -- breaded and deep-friend salmon with a thick, salty-sweet vegetable sauce and an accompaniment of rice. Onigiri with umeboshi satisfied my cravings, and the kaki-age (chopped vegetables deep-fried bundles of joy) was crispy goodness. Everything freshly prepared means thumbs up squared!

Important to note is that they are open 7 days a week from 5 pm to around 11:30 pm. If you plan on coming late like 11:25 pm, the hostess said you can call ahead and they'll stay open for you. I love it!

Summary: The arrival of authentic Japanese bar foods have finally made Orlando just a tiny bit cooler.

We went to this place last sunday, I had a lot a lot of good dish here, and while i enjoying i was chewing some piece of tiny unidentify in my month. So split it out and. Ohhhhhh my goddd it was a piece of steel, that was ruining  my dinner and my feeling. My girl friend was so disappoint about this too. so we decide to take off and pay.... 
I love this place through, It is cheap and has so many variety of foods to eat here, the food here was okey to eat with some good and bad, but it is kind of hard for my feeling to accept the piece of steel in the food... That is why we gave this place 3 stars.

I've been to Lolita two times before my most recent visit last weekend and those two previous times were uniquely wonderful dining experiences. However, I brought a friend from out of town here this past weekend and sadly cannot say the same of this visit. We enjoyed our food and it was well made and flavorful, but we both had a bad case of food poisoning the next day which lasted the entire day. It took us the whole day to recover. Unfortunately, I don't think I'll be returning to Lolita soon.

I had a really great experience here. I came in to get a new stud for my nose piercing on a Saturday night around 7 pm. Everyone who helped me was incredibly knowledgable and helpful. They explained all the different types of jewelry they had and  changed the stud when I picked one. 

Some piercing places can feel a little judgy if you aren't super knowledgable about piercings, but I didn't find that to be true here. Everyone was friendly and nice. 


I will definitely be back!!

We are sold!  This pizza was the best pizza that we have ever had delivered!!  The person that took our order on the phone was very polite and paid attention to what I was ordering, and our order arrived perfect and in a very timely manner. The best part was that  the pizza was loaded, and there was no skimping!!! Also, we did not have to stick it in the oven when it arrived like we do with other pizza company's due to the soggy wet center! Nothing worse than a wet soggy first bite of pizza!!! Give the little man some love and place your order!!! So yummy!!!!

A Plus movers did a fantastic job! When scheduling they offered multiple days for the cheapest option and reminded me to buy the yelp coupon and save extra money. They also offer 5% off for paying with cash.

They arrived at ~8:15 (for an 8-9 scheduled arrival) and they worked their fannies off! We had a moving permit but still had a rude person park in our spot. They worked around it and even apologized for it taking so long. They had a problem with the truck but did not charge us for the wait time to get jumped. They moved very swiftly and very professional. They tried multiple times to get my sofa up to a 3rd floor walk up and would have kept trying if we didn't tell them no worries. 

Overall, very professional, fair pricing, and no damage to my stuff!

Back again on a cold, rainy autumn day for their Friday special, Hu Tieu Nam Vang pho (Pnom Phenh Noodle Soup).   Sublime, subtle, filling, absolutely stunningly delicious.   

This is your mother's pho, not the "standard" pho, that otherwise good stuff with tendons, bones, fat, tripe and varying hints of anise.  This HA & VL Friday special sits in an incredibly tasty, clean pork broth, like the BEST non-fatty broth you ever had.  Added in are delicious bits of sweet, garlicky ground pork at the bottom of the bowl and the rest of the bowl filled with large, fresh shrimp, a fishball, roasted pork slices, squid, pork liver, chinese celery, onion and herbs.  

Orgasmic goodness, served with a smile (and a query on whether you want the squid and pork liver in there---but you know you do!)    Service, as always, is attentive, polite and timely.  As I said before, this is your Mom's pho, a different region and style represented every day.  

I get  tired of the same ol "this is the best (fill in the blank) whatever in Portland," riff, but........This IS the best Pho in the city, state and maybe beyond.  It has no match for care in preparation, variety and lovin' put into every bowl.    I literally could eat here every day.  And you could too after you have ventured into the tidy strip mall off of SE 82nd for this heavenly fare.

Don't take my word for it, or the other fine Yelp reviews, or glowing food critic reviews.  See and taste for yourself.  It's crazy good.  Flawless.

Went to Nomad last night (6/29) for dinner for my wife's birthday.  It's always interesting to go back and look at past reviews after we've dined.  I'm frankly a bit surprised at the inconsistencies in what people had to say.  Our experience was nothing short of fabulous.  Our party does a *lot* of tasting menus together, and this was certainly amongst the tops, right on par with Michelin-starred offerings we've experienced in the past.  

The food was delicious.  There was a good amount experimentation, but everything was very balanced.  Ever been to places where it seems like the chef just figured out how to smoke stuff, so it shows up in every dish? Not so here at Nomad. There was one dish with smoke.  Creative desserts.  Sweet peas with charcoal oil. (Me, to the chef: 'Charcoal oil?' Chef: 'Yes, we get this great Japanese charcoal, flame it so it's super hot, then take the ash and infuse it into grapeseed oil, then strain through a coffee filter.  Charcoal Oil!') (I'm sure there is more to it than that - don't try this at home, folks.) Seasonal ingredients and wines from local purveyors, and also very approachable.  We've been to some places where the food is just down right intimidating, and weird. The offerings here were delicious and unique, and we left full, but not uncomfortably so.

As for the service, it was delightful.  Each member of staff from the chef on down would engage easily in conversation, all willing to delve into their craft to whatever detail we wanted to hear (see: Charcoal Oil). We are always impressed when staff are truly excited and passionate about the work they do, and it was a joy for us to share with them. We conversed with Chef Fox about his vision for the site, how he was looking for a great dining experience, but not wrapped up in an intimidating, all-too-fancy-formal space. Mission accomplished as far as we're concerned.

Thank you to Chef Fox, Cheyenne, and the whole team for contributing to a special birthday evening.

Bad experience busy Saturday night in the bar area... I ordered a Guinness draft and the prime rib salad after the bartender assured me that it was good. Little did I know that the pint of Guinness was going to set me back seven dollars. Then the so-called prime rib salad came and had little bits of shredded beef like you'd find in a Philly cheesesteak. Total with tax $19 and change three dollar tip 22 bucks - the worst money I've spent in a restaurant for poor food in recent memory.

All I needed was an oil change.  Came in first at 1pm on a Friday (off peak time). A "service manager" said that it was a 2hr wait, and I could either stick around or call back to check on progress. Called later on, yet another 2hr wait time quoted. Around 5pm called the 3rd time and they said I would be next in line. When I returned, I was the only person there.  You might expect great service then, right? It took over an hour for the oil change, no bueno. How could it take so long? The other manager didn't offer us anything to help pass the time, a drink perhaps? "There's a water fountain out on the shop floor." Yeah, no thanks. And then came the paperwork. I checked to see if I could help speed things up while the car was being finished,  you know, to save some time. I was again told, "It'll be just another 10-15 minutes."

Sorry Firestone, you blew it!

I am new to the area and want to find some really great sushi. I found this place via the ever so helpful Yelp app. Upon hearing that the seafood on the east coast is so much better than the seafood any where else, I was a little disappointed when the sushi here did not blow me away. With that being said, this place does have great sushi. I had many different rolls and, i must say, they were all delicious. The staff is courteous and the place is clean.  Conveniently located near a theater so you can grab some sushi before or after a movie. The only reason this place is not getting a five star rating is because the expectations I had for it were not realized.

My first time at Allora and probably my last. Their $20 cheese plate had giant chunks of cheese that hadn't even been cut and cold pepperoni pizza topping. When we asked the bartender for the missing olive tapenade as listed on the menu, she pulled out two tooth picks of martinis olives and threw them on the plate. VERY underwhelming for the price point. The only reason I'm giving two stars instead of one is because of the Wine Wednesday deal. Half off bottles of wine on Wednesday evenings. I work on Atlantic Station property and will not enter this place again.

There are too many restaurants in Atlanta to tolerate the poor customer service in this restaurant. Upon arrival (with 4 employees standing there ) no one acknowledged our existence. I moved over to allow people to check out and looked straight at the employee stacking the menus. Our waiter walked us to a booth and asked about drinks. Coffee was not even warm. Pancakes and bacon was excellent. Subsequent coffee refills were hot. Sorry but I would not be willing to wait to be treated thusly again. Sunday morning 8:00am with no wait. Perhaps the manager is unaware of his employees' lacksidaisical attitudes. Imagine the atmosphere when things really got busy?!

Came in at 9pm. They were taking the chairs in from outside and said they always take the chairs in at 9 pm  bc the bar Jack Knives next door has people that sit in "their" chairs and throw up on them.  So I said, so "we can't sit outside before you close?" They said  "no bc we take them in an hour before we close so the people at the bar next door won't sit in the chairs".  So basically this Starbucks closes at 9pm. Also  we tried to order a mac and cheese and they were "out"when clearly one was still in the case. Guess the Starbucks employees run this place vs the owners.

Fool me once, shame on you.  Fool me twice, shame on me.  My wife & I consider ourselves Thai connoisseurs, particularly with 3 specific dishes: Pad Thai, Drunken Noodle, and Panang Curry.  The first time we came here, I was heavily disappointed by the pad thai...it just didn't taste very good.  My wife's drunken noodle was good, but it was SPIIIIIIIIIIICY, as in too hot to eat even though it was a medium.  And we can handle our spice - we don't like it crazy but we certainly enjoy some kick.

We've since returned and been let down again!  My wife got the drunken noodle again but ordered it mild.  Yet again, it was SPIIIIIICY and just not enjoyable because of the spice level.  Meanwhile, I ordered a mild panang curry.  It, too, was SPIIIIIICY and just couldn't really be enjoyed.  I also thought the tofu was gross - way more spongy and lower quality than other tofus I typically have.

We gave y'all two chances but were seriously let down both times.  The staff were friendly, but the food just couldn't cut it.  We won't be returning.

I have only had positive experiences with the National Rental car at the ATX airport. The cars are always clean, smoke free and easy to ride. Check out is easy and the staff is friendly and helpful regardless if your question is about the local area or directions. Located across the street from the airport, this rental company is just a short walk from the terminal making it a super convenient option. Car drop off is a piece of cake and is usually complete before I've removed my luggage from the car. This is the only rental car company I use when I am in the ATX.

I was meeting some people for brunch on Sunday morning and was running a little late so when I got to he host stand my party had already been seated. I asked the hostess Jahnay where she sat them as we had a reservation and she proceeded to tell me in a very rude manner that she doesn't know but I can look around the restaurant if I want to. I finally found my party but I needed another chair pulled up at the end of the table. We asked the Jahnay if she could get me a chair for the end of the table to which she proceeded to say I'm sorry I don't have any. We all looked at each other baffled as the restaurant was not very busy. She told us that we should have let her know that and extra person was coming and she would have sat us at a bigger table but because my friends had already put in their drink orders, we couldn't be moved as it would mess with the servers table. Because we just wanted to have a good brunch, we squeezed four people on one side of a booth table. We then asked her for a menu and she she said she would get us one. 15 minutes later we still didn't get one. One of us had to walk up to the host stand and grab a menu. Our server Shantasia was great but she seemed overwhelmed as she had many tables she was managing. When the food runner brought our food she spilled a glass of water on the table. They also don't split checks which made paying a pain as well.  The food was okay but totally overpriced for what you get. The only reason I'm giving this place a star is because I have to. I'll never go back.

Totally not impressed by the mani/pedi combo I got there.  I only went because I got a deal for both with a "massage".  Like the other reviewers mentioned this salon didn't have a mani/pedi stations which tells me it's not part of their primary business, so can't be good at it.  I didn't realize how bad it was going to be.

The technician (if you can really call her that) first did the pedicure.  She barely trimmed my cuticles and I had to tell her several times to trim certain parts a bit more.  As for the massage component of the pedicure, she barely touched my entire leg.  Hardly any lotion got to my feet.  I couldn't believe she just proceeded to use the same equipment to work on my hands.  Not very professional at all!  At least she was consistently bad with the manicure.

With such poor quality of service and lack of experience I wouldn't go back.  I can't imagine paying full price for such service.  There won't be a next time.

We can't say enough good things about Jeff! 

We moved into a house that had a rodent problem in the crawl space - the problem was probably there for years as the smell was very bad. Jeff came to us like a knight in shinning armor. He sealed up all of the access points, set traps to catch the buggers and then replaced the vapor barrier all for a very reasonable price. He's honest, hard working, friendly and very much so an expert in his field.

If you have a pest problem, don't hesitate to call Ohana Pest Control - you won't be sorry!

Stepped in because I needed a (very) quick lunch and happened to be waiting for the 99 right outside of this place. I wish I could have better things to say, because I really was hoping (good) poke would finally be a thing in Vancouver. Maybe my standards are unfairly high, but what I got was just unacceptable compared to what I've had in southern California. The proportion of salad leaves was way too high; the teeny portions of sashimi made $13 a through-the-roof price (+$1 for getting "fancy" sashimi like ahi tuna......); there's no mixing-in of sauce done for you; toppings were also added in minuscule amounts... To top it all off, the lid of the bowl didn't fit properly, so the entire thing spilled out into my paper bag, making my on-the-bus meal not exactly dignified. 
The only positive comment I'll make is that the brown rice had just the right texture. 
Overall, HUGE disappointment. Will have to try the other recently opened poke places to see if they're just as bad...

I quit eating here after the last price increase.  I can't justify paying more than $10 for a lunch of mediocre noodles or rice.  I actually walked out without placing my order when she rang in a curry chicken dish, that was $9 before I added a drink.  

I would rather get real food on Buford Highway for a lot less money.  I can go to Nam Phuong and get a bowl of Pho or a Noodle dish for $7.50 that is big enough for 2 people, fresh and authentic.

Sorry, but used to eat here a few times a month.

I eat here too much, but that's ok. I normally forget to check in. I am too busy getting out my Plucker's Member card, getting the member special, ordering a beer, and deciding what deliciously unhealthy item I want after that.

I go here for lunch, for happy hour, for dinner. If they had breakfast, then I'd go then too. Yummy sauces, big salads, tasty sandwiches, huge beers, interesting mixed drinks. The staff is generally pretty good, but when they get busy, it can get crazy for awhile.

There is an attached parking garage, and they will validate at the host stand, so def do that. If you're on campus, it's not a terrible walk, even when it's hot. Walk down 22nd, and there's plenty of shade.

Go forth and do crazy wings.

I've tried a few different yoga studios over the last few months, but Highland Yoga is the best I've found so far! I've always been a little afraid to try yoga classes (for fear of being really terrible at it or looking ridiculous), but the instructors at Highland Yoga do a great job of making everyone feel comfortable, welcome, and free to go at their own pace. I was a little worried at first because this studio does not offer any beginners classes(they're almost all listed as all levels classes), but it turns out there was absolutely nothing to worry about! They also offer towels, mats, and blocks for you to use during the classes. 

There are a few instructors whose classes I haven't attended, but all of the ones I've taken classes from offer modifications (both easier and more challenging) on poses throughout the class. Try a few different instructors across both locations; although they're all listed the same way on their schedule, I think some instructors teach a more challenging course than others (they really are all great, though) 

One thing I would like to see is 1 or 2 more Yin classes each week, instead of just Sunday nights, but this class is great at both locations. 

I'm now two months in to regular visits to Highland Yoga---I'm glad I stuck with it and I plan to continue!

I've been to Canvas a few times with family and friends, and I'm always impressed.  I love the exterior and interior decor, and the lakeside setting.  The service is excellent and prompt, but more importantly, the food is remarkable.  What a joy too that it's a relatively short drive from my house.  My only demerit here (something I hope they will improve upon) is for their craft beer and cocktail menu, which could use some tweaking.  Both times that we've had The French Quarter it was a tad underwhelming... and, frankly, I would replace Orlando Brewing as many of their beers are quite bland (this is probably due to their organic nature).  These are of course subjective observations and minor suggestions to an otherwise flawless restaurant.  

We came in last week for my Father's 70th birthday celebration and had a total blast.  The kitchen rotates the menu every so often, so I was excited to try a few of their newer items.  As usual, their spicy oyster crackers and Smoked Fish Dip were perfect (love that cream cheese!)  The Grilled Teres Major (new item) was incredibly juicy and well seasoned.  But by far the best of the night was the Oak-Grilled Cobia (also new).  This was THE best fish I've tasted in a very long time.  It was so warm and tender, and when coupled with the squash purée, every bite was heavenly.  A surprisingly complex dish.  As a birthday treat from our server, we ended the night with the Spiced Chocolate Cream, which was so rich it hit everyone's sweet spot. 

This was yet another unforgettable experience in Lake Nona.  Already looking forward to our next visit.

Just ok.  If I am being honest, it was dry and a bit disappointing.  Small portions, with good flavors, but didn't wow me.  

The chicken schwarma was not the best I've had and the gyros were very similar.  I'd rather go to Antoni's in Beaverton for a much better Gyro. 

Maybe the 2 times we went it was after a show at the Joy and we got the dried out meat?  I probably won't go back a 3rd time to get mediocre food when there are many other options around.

I visit that clinic a few years ago when first moved in Vancouver. They were ok in general, polite. My teeth were always ok up to then. I was doing a cleaning ones a year or so and didn't get stains ever near the gums. Since I visit that place to do a cleaning, every few months my teeth getting stains and tartar near the gums.  As I knew even back then that Asian dentist that they had was "scratching" my teeth to hard instead of using ultrasonic pulses to remove any plaque even at areas that where fine. I even remember asking him if what he does going to make rougher my enamel surface and his reply was that those tools where softer than the enamel, that may be the case but the force he used was excessive. Since then I have issues with the areas that he "scratched".  I believe that what he did either consciously or by accident was to make rough my enamel at certain areas that caused this issue. I wouldn't recommend that dentist office to anyone and would be very careful and aware of what they are doing at my teeth while being there cause those "mistakes" create lots of extra work and issues in the future especially when you area a young adult like I was/ Am.

Subpar service overall. 20 minute wait for a table on Monday night with plenty of tables open. We had a party of 5. A huge section of 4 tops open, but rather than joining 2 tables, we had to wait over 20 minutes for a bigger booth to open. Slow service with food and drinks. You can watch and see that many servers are in slow motion, not a good quality if you want to be a server. Mashed potatoes were cold by the time entrees arrived. Server was cordial but not what I would consider friendly and polite. I had to hunt down condiments myself after asking and then waiting awhile. I was given a complimentary appetizer card because of this. It's not enough to make me want to return. We generally like Longhorns, but this one isn't one I would revisit. I've waited tables. This is an issue management should handle. Management and hiring of servers needs to be worked on.

Where to start! This place is awesome! Extremely clean, not over priced, decorated adorable, large selection of polishes they do a fantastic job as well! I got a gel mani and pedicure & it was so relaxing and looked awesome! The owner Paige went above and beyond in accommodating me and my girlfriends needs!!! If you have a group or want a great reliable place to get your nails done and not over pay this is without a doubt the place to go! I can't wait to go back!!!

A little too pretentious already? 

I don't even know what the food is like, I never even had a chance to get past the snobbery policing the front door. 

I made a reservation on Opentable for 3 people. I realize that the odd number is difficult with it being a small space. The only opening they had was 9:15 pm. I jumped on it and planned to go. I wanted to have a night out with a couple of girlfriends and had been dying to go for dinner. It's just a 4 minute walk away from my house, even more a reason to try it. I called to make sure 3 people was going to work with it being a late reservation. When I looked at Opentable a couple of hours before, I guess I fat fingered it and freaked out. It only said two. 

That phone call just set the tone for the entire evening. Never got her name, but boy did she make it a point to sound so inconvenienced. If it wasn't going to work out, I got it. I would have tried for some other time. She checked the books and came back and said that she could only do 3 at 9:45. She said they had a full bar when I mentioned coming up there prior to see if MAYBE a table would clear up. It was a breezy 102 degrees outside and she was insistent on seating us outside. I stayed strong. I wanted the dining room. 

We got up there. Now there were two hostesses, the bitchy resting face had doubled. The only place to wait was outside. Again, the persistence with wanting us to be seated outside. We said we'd have a couple of drinks and wait. Guess what? There was no full bar. Just beer and wine. Not only that, they only had counter space for those dining. 

So. You can't go to the bar and buy a drink, wait inside for a table or evidently have a smile on your face to be taken seriously. 

They sat us pretty quickly, after mentioning that we were here for a "pretty late dinner". The table was right in front of the door. That's not the problem though. It was right in clear view of the prying eyes of the big balls of sunshine who had been so "gracious" since the beginning. 

How uncomfortable. I was just in utter shock and wasn't about to drop any money here. So my friends and I just looked at each other with our deflated faces and just got up and left. Walked right out the door. 

I won't go here again. This is Austin. We eat, live and breathe community. Good luck.

Staying in Columbus for only a few days during a conference, my son (vegan) and I (vegetarian) ate here twice.  We had a large group which they accommodated with no problem and very quickly.  They even let me get a table for the whole group and didn't give me any trouble when it was a good half-hour before the rest of the group arrived.  We were all able to find something we liked, and the build-a-burger makes it easy to have it your way.  Food took a while to arrive, but it's made to order, after all, and we had plenty of entertainment watching the Halloween block party outside.  The service was fantastic, friendly, and they were happy to do separate checks.

I tried both the black bean patty and the quinoa patty and really liked the latter.  It held it's shape and was crispy on the outside, holding it's own with a handful of toppings, sauces, and a sprouted bun.  The kale caesar side salad was the bomb!!  I would go just for that if this were available in my town.  There were lots of choices of beer, and my companions who had tea (both hot and cold) enjoyed the high quality options offered.  The second time we went I took the flourless chocolate cake to go, and ate it later.  WOW.  It was so decadent I had to eat half of it the next day.  I loved this place and I'm just sad it's so far away.

Went here after some partying. We stood in line for a long time, and all the people around us eating their food was so hard. I almost grabbed some guy's pancakes but didn't want to get beaten.

After ordering, we got a table right away and waited.

And waited.

I mean, it was 1 AM and the place was packed, and the grill isn't very large.

When the food finally came 30 minutes later, it wasn't that great. I wasn't expecting amazing food or anything; besides, the only other place open nearby was freakin' Jack in the Box. But still, big pancakes and eggs were good enough to soak up the mess that was our alcohol-filled bodies. I doubt I'd go here sober.

Best of Inman Park!! 

I started going to AfterGlo last Spring to prepare for my September wedding and I am thrilled I found this neighborhood gem. Janelle is absolutely fantastic at assessing my skincare needs and customizing a facial "just for me!"

My face is brighter, softer, and more even toned. I no longer feel dry or tight spots in the winter despite my frequent flying and often failed intentions of drinking lots of water. Her products are all high quality and not only feel amazing on my face but smell absolutely fabulous! She is truly gifted at creating a relaxing space and putting you at ease with her neck and shoulder massage. 

Whether you're planning for a special event or hoping to achieve your best look I highly recommend AfterGlo! After all we all deserve to look and feel our best! :)

Traveled to Vancouver in Nov 2011 and have delayed writing this review because my mind goes blank every time I try to describe their dishes. It says something for their dishes since it is an upscale restaurant, yet their food is unmemorable.  I guess should start off by writing what I do remember....

*Service: EXCELLENT. I definitely remember being VERY impressed with their service . My BFF and I popped in after hours of shopping on Robson. Although we had no reservation and wasn't dressed for fine dining, they were very friendly and welcoming. The hostess offered  to check in our coats, bags, and umbrellas. We were seated immediately. The waiter was knowledgeable, patient and always provided his full attention.  My water glass never went empty.  

*Food: I remember there was a mushroom festival. The items we ordered from the special mushroom menu, had no mushrooms?! ? I also ordered pasta, but again cant remember what type. The food wasn't bad...just nothing I could rave about. 

*Price: $30 and up pp

*Ambiance: Dimmed lights and comfortable seats. Suitable for romantic dinners or large groups.

Overall the service was the best part of our dining experience. For the prices paid, I expect to have food to be the best part, but unfortunately it wasn't.

Well if your looking for a good gym but don't want to spend a mortgage payment every month for a membership and don't want to be constantly worried that your getting ripped off then here's your place . This place has a great combination of things I like new equipment , clean locker rooms and with almost all the gyms I've been to most staff won't even talk to you and barely say hi but everyone here is awesome and if you try to sign up for a class Brandon will try to work with you instead of trying to scam you theirs no contract when you sign up all you have to do is give a 30 day notice to cancel .
And theirs a ton of different classes and they even have cross fit if you want to get a little crazy .So if your complaining that theirs not a good gym out there well here you go now you don't have an excuse for not working out .  

Oh and They changed vendors at the juice / protein shake bar with a way better company  and any complaints on here I've read of no ac is gone i asked one of the trainers and they said its been fixed and they added more to one of the rooms .

Not a restaurant that values customers. We thought we would give Barrio's a try. We are rating happy hours and arrived in time for half off margaritas, (kind of small). The waitress checked on us once and then returned right at six and informed us that happy hour was over. She said they are very strict about that. She needs to set customer expectations and let us know. It wasn't real busy, it would of been nice if she checked back before happy hour was over. Diner beware!

Wife wasted -a lot- of time & money going there. Hoping to get me a great treat hearing how good and fancy this place is and how hard it is to get good food in GA. Had a scone that was horribly nasty, stale, and tasted like it had been sitting in an old moldy boot for a few months in the back of a closet. More like a stale cake from a store that went out of business five years ago than a scone that was supposed to be hand made fresh.??!!??.
  Spit the bite out and threw away the other three she bought.. (4) FOUR SCONES IN THE TRASH!! $20.00+ sum odd bucks, time, fuel, all wasted. Plus the wife is ****** not only because you wasted her time & money with a horrible product but also because she WENT WAY OUT OF HER WAY TO DO SOMETHING NICE AND Y'ALL ***** IT UP!!
  Called to complain to the management and they laughed at how disgusting it was. Why would you find it amusing? You should be ashamed. Apologetic Even. I don't understand y'all.

DO NOT WASTE YOUR TIME..
DO NOT WASTE YOUR MONEY..
YOU WILL RISK GETTING SICK..


.

Faulk is my favorite Austin Public Library.  The main reason is because the 3rd floor is quiet, making it a great place to get away from all distractions and enter the "flow" state of mind while reading/studying.  The only things that distract me on the 3rd floor are the occasional pigeon sounds/movement/fights :) on the window ledge and the nice view out the tall, continuous windows that wrap around the floor.

If you wish to use the computer, there are lots of computers on the second floor available for use or reservation.  The first floor has a wide variety of magazines.  Their CD/software/DVD/video selection at any time seems just acceptable--it doesn't amaze me.  The APL system does have a lot of new DVDs that are often checked out; you may need to place a hold/request on the item to borrow it.  If you get hungry or thirsty, there are vending machines on the first floor and drinking fountains on all of them.  (You aren't allowed to drink on the 2nd or 3rd floor, though.)  There are self-checkout stations to keep the checkout line short.  The staff has always been friendly.  

Parking's been no problem for me--I only go during weekends and weekday evenings, however.  I almost always find a spot in their parking lot on the north side of the building, but if it's full, I just parallel park along Guadalupe or West.  There is also at least one bicycle rack outside.  Many people hang out at the tables on the south side of the building and play cards or relax.  This library feels very laidback and hanging out there makes me feel like a real Austinite.

I sent my dog there for part of the week, and despite the fact that he was accepted, I will not return. When I was picking up my dog I saw an employee grab a dog by muzzle and scold it for barking. I understand they want to be a bark free doggie daycare, but do not feel confident that they treat the animals with care and respect to achieve this. I know personally that's not how I control my dogs barking and would not want them to treat him the way I saw him treat the other dog.

I'm no longer surprised that the dogs there lay around all day without much energy, they have likely been punished.

Yesterday, our house was really, really hot.  At first we thought we'd mis-set the thermostat, but it became clear very quickly that our air conditioning was not doing its job.

Eric came out the next day.  He showed up exactly on time.  He handled my obnoxious barking dog with grace.  He inspected both the inside and outside unit, pointing out 2 possible points of trouble, and one long-term possible source of trouble.  He fixed everything in about 30 minutes, which included replacing a capacitor.  Eric left me with some long-term maintenance tips and showed me how to make sure my issues wouldn't come up again.  

The best part was, it only cost $150 for parts and labor.  House is cool again, and we were very satisfied.  Obviously if, in 4 months, it craps out again, I will revise this post, but for now we are cool and happy :-)

The tape cassette drawer of my 14 year old Sony DCR-PC10 camcorder had jammed and the camera was unusable. I have switched to my cell phone for taking videos, but desperately wanted to digitize & put dozens of hours of old home & travel videos on the computer for editing and safekeeping.

Sony repair was not available, but I figured there must be some independent technician who remembered how to work on such old technology. Pages into my google search, I found Sanford Camera Repair.

Sanford took the camcorder in, called in a week or so with the estimate, did the repair I requested, and a couple weeks later shipped it back to me. The cost was very fair, the camcorder has worked great to extract all those precious video memories off the little DV tapes & onto my laptop.
