I've eaten here twice and got take out once. The beef brisket is pretty awesome; combine it with a side of coleslaw and baked beans. Probably my favorite meal in central Florida; price considered. For the beef brisket sandwich and two sides it's only $8.59; Great deal. My wife gets the pulled pork and thats pretty darn good too. It's only $7.99 with two sides. They serve crinkle cut fries; which are good. The wife and kids have gotten cup cakes from the bakery; yes 4R has it's own cup cakes/cake bakery. They liked the cup cakes; I thought they were so so; definitely not Sprinkles. That's a different review. I'm talking about the barbecue here... The lines can get pretty long; so come prepared and relax. Because if your waiting for the brisket; it's worth the wait. Highly recommended!!

Blue Genie is a fantastic place where you can shop locally, support artists, and purchase some unique gifts. Or in my case, gifts for myself. It is WAY better than the Armadillo Bazaar and has no admission fee!

The artists are not present, which I think is both a good and bad thing. Bad because you don't have the opportunity to ask questions or find out more about their work. Good because there are no high-pressure buying situations. Now, most of what you'll find at Blue Genie will be pricier than your average jewelry/clothes/home goods, etc. But I don't mind paying a little bit more when I know my money is going to someone local and not a huge conglomerate. 

Also, get the egg nog. It's crazy strong. But it could also be the reason I spent a ridiculous amount of money, so proceed with caution. Blue Genie = all-around win.

I was having trouble finding the prescription eyedrops that I needed before my cataract surgery. My regular pharmacy, Walgreens, said it was on back order and I wouldn't have it until the week after my surgery. I asked the doctor to call it in to Lake Hills Pharmacy and went by to pick it up. Unfortunately it was extremely expensive. The young ladies worked tirelessly trying to find an alternative And gave me suggestions of what to ask my doctor for. So even though I didn't get my prescription filled there I wouldn't have known what to do next without their help. It's the perfect neighborhood pharmacy with that personal one on one help and friendliness.

First of all, I wish that I could tell you better directions on how to find this place but I don't even remember. I just know that we spent half an hour and made a couple pit stops in the Daiso store, chinese plaza and even the dragon art piece between the two centers which connects indoors. 

But once we got there, I.ce Queen was well worth it!!  The two guys that were working were so friendly and amazing that we quickly forgot about our search. The kids loved watching them make the rolled ice cream. They went above and beyond with providing us extra seats for our group. Since we were the last customers for the day, they even offered us waters to go with our ice cream. The ice cream itself was flavorful and delicious. We tried the "I love mango", "Cookie Monster" and the green matcha red bean concoctions -yum!

I love this restaurant for the location and the food.

Specifically, I like the zucca chips and bruschetta from the appetizer menu and you really can't go wrong with any of their pasta. I've also been impressed with the fresh fish nearly every time I've ordered it. One the one occasion where the fish was obviously overcooked, the Manager took the criticism well and brought me a new dish.

Honestly, what prompted me to write this review though, was reading the last review left. I've been to NoRTH more times than I can count and the service has always been exemplary. Until last week...

I think I must have been served by the same bartender as Rachel S, fully equipped with the same bad attitude and seriously lacking interpersonal skills. It was 7pm on a Monday and I was meeting a group of friends for a birthday dinner. Several of us arrived early and hunkered down at the bar to catch up before the stragglers showed up.

The bartender seemed rushed, despite the fact that other than my group, there were only 2 other patrons at the bar. I ordered a gin & tonic, he didn't ask me what kind of gin I wanted. He spilled a drink on my friend trying to pour his beer for him, and also threw the checks at us when it was time to get seated.

I couldn't bring myself to punish the rest of the staff by giving the entire restaurant a poor rating, but be warned... the bartender should be avoided at all costs.

Saw a girl get physically pushed around by a bouncer. She was not doing a single thing just trying to grab her coat and leave. When I went over to stop it he threatened to physically harm me. I walked the girl out so they would stop touching her. While walking away him and several other staff member were yelling absurdities at us. This place is run buy men who were bullied or just completely disliked when growing up because they have extreme anger issues and no respect for women. The guys who work here are about 27-33 years old and I can now see why they work there because they can't get a job anywhere else. They act as if the world owes them something.

My review is for the salon. I also like the store. They have a large selection of cosmetics, perfumes and hair accessories. but I actually only go there for the salon. 

I have been going to Ulta for about 5 years now and absolutely love it. I can an appointment within 4 days of calling, which is great at salons. It's affordable and awesome quality when it comes to products and treatments. My color stays bright (and practically new) for a good 12 or so weeks. 

I'm sure all of stylists are fabulous, but I would ask for Heather. She's my favorite. :)

I felt compelled to say something after reading that others are having the same issues with Vicky. 
Don't waste your time going here. It will just be a matter of time before she flys off the handle at you too. She has no concept of how to treat customers. She is very disrespectful, rude, unprofessional and makes people feel uneasy. I was humiliated and embarrassed beyond belief when she told me not to bother coming back again - all because I couldn't find parking making me 5 minutes late for my appointment. All I was having done was a repair to one nail that would have taken her 5 minutes to do. Its been a year and just as well as found a great place closer to home.

This place is unreal. Amazing craft cocktails with great ingredients. It felt like every sip was a punch of flavor. The food is fantastic as well. We got fried rice, lo mein, and tangerine chicken. No complaints on anything. Great appetizers as well. We were gifted free crab rangoons! The service was amazing  and the covid response is superb. They are incredibly proactive and I love it. I felt comfortable. It feels like a home inside. You need to see this .

I purchased their groupon and I was super pumped about getting shellac! But my experience was not amazing. 

Customer service was not great at all. Other customers were asked if they would like something to drink (e.g., water) but i was never asked. The women at the reception (and later worked on others nail) were not professional at all. When the woman told me that this place is owned by the same person who owns Portland Boutique & Spa I was shocked. Portland Boutique has excellent customer service, so im not sure what went wrong here. 

The pedicure did not feel like a pedicure. I am used to having the bottom of my feet really scrubbed, but that didn't happen. Its likely closer to I would have gotten if I just had my toes painted else where except my feet were soaked.

The shellac came off in 5 days. It literally peeled off.

Although difficult to find and get to by public transit, it is a hidden cozy gem that is great for groups big or small. Prices are reasonable and no complaints about service. The food was good except for the chicken wings appetizer. Although the different sauces/glazes were tasty, the chicken wings were fried a little too long and the batter was just a little too heavy and thick. Other than that, food was great. I went once for dinner and they had a music act that set a chilled ambiance for the restaurant. I also went for lunch on a bright but chilly sunday. We sat outside and were offered cozy blankets because of the light breeze. Great feel, great food, for great company.

Yesterday wasn't my first time at Velvet Taco, in fact I frequent Velvet Taco cause the food is SO good and there are so many vegetarian friendly options. However yesterday's service at the register was surprisingly bad, which was disheartening. I brought my family members in for their first time and they were treated horribly. If you're going to have someone work the register, please ensure it's someone friendly and someone who won't belittle you if you ask "between these two, which would you recommend?"  

Food gets 5 stars! But service yesterday gets 1 star.

I read such great reviews about this place, I thought I'd swap out the place I usually go to.....
First, I took a pair of beloved red mary jane's in, because one strap was chewed by a tiny foster dog. When I got them back, the color that had been used to patch the chew was a totally different color...closer to burgundy. No relation to the red of the shoe. No one would wear these shoes looking like this...I was told by the sales person "they must have told you it would be hard to match the red". NO, they did not. Otherwise, why would I have had the work done? 

At the time of that pick up, I turned in another pair of shoes. I wasn't getting the picture yet, or was kind of in shock or denial over the terrible job done on the red shoes. Or just tired at the end of a day. On the second shoes, I asked that an area be sewn  together so I could slip them on. The person clarified what I was asking, and said fine, that would be no problem. When I got them back, the sewing ripped out the first time I put them on. Boo. Hiss.

Cost of the two worthless jobs: over $30. 

So, now I'm zero for two and thinking that these folks at least deserve a chance to make it right. I take both shoes in and explain, asking for a refund No dice. 

 I'm told, essentially "you asked for a patch" about the mismatched red leather. 

And about the other shoes? I'm told: "you chose to do something experimental, so you get to pay for the result." Huh?? I take my shoes to a shoe repair place so that they can tell me how my shoes can be repaired, or if they can't. Not to experiment with paying for repairs that don't work. 

If I am asking for something so "experimental" that they don't know if it will work, please tell me; I wont' waste money I don't have to waste. If the red patch is going to be so hard to match that the shoes will be unwearable, please tell me. 

I'm going back to the old place. The guy may have charged for his work, but at least at the end of it, I always had shoes I could wear.

EWC is amazing.  I worked with Josh on acquiring an Omega Plant Ocean.  He was fantastic to work with, from my first email inquiring about the watch all the way through to leaving the store with my new watch.  Josh was great to communicate with, replying to my emails quickly and with great detail. I am thrilled to have worked with josh and he was able to help me get the watch I wanted at a great deal that was helpful to me at the same time.  I highly recommend working with Josh and all of the representatives of European Watch Company.

I have been with Fidelity for over 40 years and enjoyed plenty of gains during their Peter Lynch years.  The other yelp reviews are correct, as presenty Fidelity doesn't give a damn about its clients, including those with substantial assets there.  Over the years I have sent several messages to CEO Abigail Johnson over and she never responded or had any of her drones respond.  Who is this terrible person Abigail??  
One would think that customer retention would be a priority, but not with Fidelity, sadly.  Active Trader Pro, Fidelity's trading tool, crashes frequently and is a disaster.  I've had much better luck with Charles Schwab and its associates, though their Streetsmart tool also has its issues.  At least Schwab's reps don't lie to me.

First visit today and I really loved it! There is a simple yet refined elegance about this place. The cozy space is actually quite versatile as well.  They have some great, healthy food options. The salmon with poached eggs and avocado was a delight (for the taste buds and visually).  Service was straightforward, quick and friendly.  Last but not least my mocha was well-balanced in that it was more chocolaty than sweet (dark chocolate is a plus) and the caffeine achieved the subtle but steady uplift effect rather than the pick me up and drop me off short thereafter effect.

Kind of too-hip for me. It was fun, though. We came to bowl for an hour, had an app (duck fat fries) and we each had a drink. Our bowling lane had a reset issue; someone responded pretty quickly. 

Apparently, we bowl kinda fast (2 people) bc we got two games in 40 minutes. Then our arms were sore so we hung up the towel. 

Cool space. Cool idea. Weird location (3rd floor of a mall?). I probably won't go back bc it's downtown and I live in SE. But it was worth checking out.

This place does have old world charm with the Roman statues throughout the cafe.  However, when it comes to customer service, it is absolutely one of the worst I have ever had.

I had gone there this morning with my cousin.  I had asked for a soy latte (due to mild milk allergies).  The older gentleman behind the counter told me they do not have soy, like it would taint his product with poison.  I understand that soy is not exactly the Italian way to make a drink, but for people like me, it is pretty much the option that we have if milk is not some thing we can have.

Also, my cousin did not order anything, but was pointed out very loudly by another barista that she must buy something or leave.  There were only two other tables that were occupied at that moment, and the rest of the seating area was empty.  We understand that cafes are to be in business to make money, but rudeness is pretty much the point that prompted the both of us to leave.

If you are into good food but rude service, then this is the place to go.  Otherwise, I do not recommend this place to anyone.

Apenberry's has it figured out! If you are embarking on a new or refresh landscaping project, I highly recommend paying this cute College Park nursery a visit. The staff is so friendly, knowledgeable, helpful and the nursery is a lot bigger than I imagined with an expansive selection of annuals, perennials, ground covers, bushes, trees, indoor plants...you name it.

The project: redoing the front yard landscaping. I was looking for an ornamental grass (had zero experience in landscaping) had done some research and narrowed down a few types that I liked. I visited 2 other nursery's around Central Florida, to which neither of them had a great selection nor were helpful...one popular nursery in particular, felt like I was inconveniencing them when asking where the ornamental grass was, I got pointed in the direction and that's about it, turned around and the employee was gone. Cool.

As soon as I left the above nursery, I called Apenberry's see what they had in stock and right away, it was such a better experience. The lady with whom I spoke with told me what they had in stock by ACTUALLY walking the grounds and telling me the quantity of items and price! She also gave me info on other options of grasses after asking questions about the area where I planned to put them. I asked about a certain grass and if they planned to have it in stock in the next few weeks (it was not in season and not as common in our area), she was not sure but took down my name and number and was going to call their supplier and get back to me in a few days! Now that's customer service!! And I did get a call back!! While the grass I originally wanted was not going to be in stock until maybe the fall, with the helpful info from the staff at Apenberry's, we decided on another grass option that was even better suited for the area! 

Our experience with Apenberry's, A+. The employees were beyond helpful and took the time to show us where things were located on site and gave helpful tips on how to properly plant. Real good people there! Oh, and their prices...super reasonable and beat out the other local nurseries we went to!

After reading the reviews here on Yelp I knew that I had to try this place and I'm so happy that I did. I ordered the pepper shrimp banh mi and the only complaint I have is I wish I had bought two! The sandwich was delicious and flavorful. The bread was chewy and the vegetables were super fresh! It was chocked full of shrimp as well. I can't wait to go back and try one of their other sandwiches and next time Ill buy two because once it was gone I wanted another one a few hours later but they were already closed for the evening. At 5-6 dollars a sandwich it is definitely affordable and the lady's running the stand were super nice! Ill be back!

This four season hotel was amazing! We stayed there the night before our Disney Cruise and then came back for another 3 days after the cruise just to enjoy the amenities! We were supposed to go to the Disney parks every day after our cruise, but once we saw this hotel and all the activities for the children (and the amazing spa for us!) we decided to stay at the hotel and relax instead of fight the crowds at the parks. We were so happy we made that decision! With the slides, kids club, lazy river and great food, we had the most amazing/relaxing part of our trip right there at the four seasons! My husband and I both had massages during our stay and we enjoyed our dinner at the fabulous restaurants on site. Then after a great day of swimming, spa treatments and great food (and delicious gelato) we relaxed in our room and watched the Disney fireworks from our balcony! 5 stars all the way! We are planning our next trip again, hopefully soon! Love this Four Seasons!!!

Don't waste your time here.  All you come out with is an empty pocketbook.  Two crowns replaced only to find out that my bite was not done correctly and now all my teeth are shifting.  The still refuse to address the issue and I am now reporting them to the Attorney General to get this settled.  Tried to work it out, but they are too busy with their patients to help out one that paid a lot of money only to be totally unsatisfied.  They just don't care.

Now that's a tasty meatball!!
I'm always letting everyone know what the new restaurants are that open up in Orlando. Well I got a treat for you!! Today The Meatball Shoppe has opened. 
I've been watching the progress on Facebook and calling up every other day to see what day they where opening. So I stopped today and got me some meatballs to go! Come to my surprise I know the delightful owner Isabella, we used to work together many moons ago. I must tell you the meatballs were fantastic! I choose three different meatballs; I got "Nonna's" Traditional Meatballs, Chicken Marsala Meatballs, Mediterranean grass grass-fed Lamb Meatballs, White Bean Ragout and Tuscan Farro Salad. There is so many to choose from and so many meatballs styles, you're just going to have to come in and eat some for yourself.

First time here and we come to this area often. This fabulous little cafe is tucked away just off Orange in the Ivanhoe Village area. We found the recommendation on an Orlando day date website and found the perfect table outside on the patio to dine. We ordered the baked Feta appetizer, which was served hot, with lemon and fresh pita bread. It was divine. My husband ordered the Greek salad, which was large enough to share, and I had the lemons chicken and rice soup. Everything we ordered exceeds our expectations. The service was amazing as well. We will be back!

The best thing we ordered here, by far, is the fried avocado taco. I'm not sure how they made a simple avocado on a flour tortilla so good but it was delicious! 
We stopped in on a Friday night and just missed the crowd. As soon as we sat down, after ordering, there was suddenly a line all the way out the door. 
The girl at the counter was very friendly and patient as we figured out what we wanted. Prices are reasonable and they have a lot of choices. 
Our food was served quickly! Less than 10 minutes! 
We ordered a shredded chicken taco, a chicken bowl, (2) fried avocado tacos and chips and cheese nachos. 
The chicken bowl and chicken taco were very bland. The hot sauces we added gave it more flavor. The shredded chicken taco was very soggy and the corn tortilla fell apart as I was eating it. As I said the fried avocado tacos were delicious!  They made the meal worth the drive! 
They serve crunchy tacos on Sundays only so we may be back to give those a try. Crunchy is my favorite! 
It's a cute diner that's kept neat and clean. The staff is fast and friendly. It's worth a stop in to give them a try.

Believe the HYPE. It's LEGIT.

Thank you Andy Ricker for gracing Portland with the dishes you deliver. 

Famous For:
- IKE'S VIETNAMESE STYLE FISH SAUCE WINGS (***Get it spicy***)

What have I tried (from my several visits)?
- IKE'S VIETNAMESE STYLE FISH SAUCE WINGS: Ahh yes, the infamous chicken wings! I've had them spicy and regular and I prefer the spicy version better! Comes with pickled carrots, radish and cucumber to cool your palette from the zing of heat! Great with sticky rice or just by itself! This is a popular dish and is available all day long! I like that they give you some wipes to clean your fingers from getting down and dirty!

- PAPAYA POK POK Over the years I have built up a spice tolerance, but this one takes the cake! Eaters beware! This thing is really delicious but can leave your tongue tingling from all chili seeds surprising you in every corner! The spicy green papaya is quite authentic and you might want some sticky rice with this one! [**spice alert**]

- YAM MAKHEUA YAO (eggplant dish) is a little spicy but not so much. It's do-able and I love that the eggplant is cooked oh-so perfectly! Served with some fish sauce, shallots, diced up boiled egg and cilantro - which are all incorporated into this lovely dish! Great for a side and wonderful for your average heat palette! 

- PHAT KHANAENG (brussle sprout dish) is a milder spice than the eggplant. If you're looking for something for veggies to your meal, this might be a go-to! My cousin doesn't even like eating his brussle sprouts and the way they grilled and cooked this baby had him going for seconds! Seriously! 

- MUU SATEH (pork satay dish) I preferred this dish over the ribs! I loved the peanut sauce and this TOTALLY complimented the satay! There about 4-5 pieces of satay available. If you're unsure what to order, this one is a safe bet if you're not going for something totally outrageous!

- KAI YAANG (chicken dish) You can order 1/2 bird or full. We opted for the 1/2 since we were going to endure a bunch of other goodies. The chicken was cooked moist and great with white rice if you're not into sticky rice. Comes with two sauces: One is savory soy-sauce based and the other is a sweet/spicy sauce which is a good surprise to the dish! If you're unsure what to order, this is a safe alternative if you're not going for something totally outrageous as well!

- KUNG OP WUN SEN (prawns cooked in a clay pot dish) This is a simple dish and the noodles cooked in the clay pot reminded me of Filipino pancit bihon. It was a simple dish for me. Was quite decent in my book.

- SII KHRONG MUU YANG (ribs dish) I probably wasn't a big fan of the ribs. On paper it sounded the best thing to order and we had to have it. But when we got the dish it was kinda dry and more bone and barely meat. Came with two dipping sauces: 1 savory and 1 sweet but wasn't a big fan of the whole thing overall. I thought the sauces had more oomph to the dish than the meat itself. 

- MUU PAA KHAM WAAN (boar dish) If you can't really handle spicy food, but would definitely like to try out some boar, this is highly recommended. Not because it's going to make you want to eat more rice or pickled veggies to counter-balance the heat, but because the dish is so gosh darn yummy you don't care how spicy the heat level is because you're getting a good dose of flavor and kick you probably won't regret having your tongue so scorched! [**spice alert**]

Drinks: I've never really had the alcohol here because I REALLY LIKE their DRINKING VINEGARS! I know the sound of drinking vinegar sounds like blasphemy, but let your guard down because it's just a simple flavored syrup that they mix with club soda or something along those lines to make a refreshing drink! I really like the LYCHEE, PINEAPPLE and TAMARIND ones!

Awards and such:
- Andy Ricker: James Beard Award - Best Chef of NW (2011)
- Featured on Food Network's Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives [3D's] (and another place I would agree with Guy Fieri!)
- Featured on Food Network's Best Thing I Ever Ate
- Noted on Yahoo article's for "Best 20 Restaurants in America"
- Noted by the Daily Meal in "Top 101 Restaurants in the U.S." (Ranked 12th)
- And many more awards throughout the years!

FYI:
- Expect to wait for dinner approx. 1 hour or more.
- Depending on the time you go, depends on the menu (they don't offer everything all day) There's a menu for lunch 11:30 - 2:30 pm, mid-afternoon 2:30 - 5pm and dinner from 5 - close.
- Parking is on the street/nearby neighborhood streets.
- Yes this place used to be Andy Ricker's House! 
- If you live on the East Coast, he just opened up a chicken wing place in NYC!
- If you don't want your nice $$$$ coat smelling like SE Asian food, I recommend not wearing it here. Just spending a meal here will cause your clothes (and hair) to smell like what you ate!

Overall thought? If you're in the area, don't pass this place up! HIGHLY RECOMMENDED

B1 is a newly formed dragon boat team filled with super fun outgoing people from all walks of life in their 20's to early 30's.

No experience necessary, so don't be shy! You can also join at any time in the season. All equipment is provided (paddles life jackets) and there's locker space.

It's a really great deal: one year's membership at 100 bucks gets you 12 months work of workouts 3x a week (summer) or 1-2x a week (winter). If you calculate that out it's something like 100 workouts for the entire year....it's $1 per workout, people! The first 2 training sessions are free, too!

Summer paddling is on Monday/Wednesday nights 6-8pm and Saturdays 11am-1pm (none of the 5am stuff that rowers do!). 

Winter training: The team works out together in a gym where the coaches will design a weight workout and supervise you like a personal trainer. There's also cardio workouts and sometimes yoga sessions. The team also has winter pool training: The pool at JFK Elementary school at Porter Square is booked out for 2h in the afternoon for many Saturdays during the winter. You sit by the side of the pool and paddle working mostly on technique with the coaches working with you.

The team races about 4 times during the summer in the North east (about once a month) - racing is optional but is a great way to get to know the people on the team better. It feels like a road trip and a race day is often combined with a touristy day. 

The team isn't just about paddling and fitness, but also social - there's regular post-training lunch/dinner and also social events that are a nice mix between outdoorsy things (hiking, bike rides, skiing) and bar hopping (dinner & drinks).

The other thing I really like about the team is that everyone is invested in each other outside of the workouts and the paddling. Dragon boaters from this team have become my Boston family. 

www.boston1.org

I hate giving bad reviews to Disney restaurants, I really do.  But I have little choice on this one.  It admittedly was a great ambience, for the first 30 minutes or so, and I was excited when I first stepped in and got seated.  But after that, it was a mediocre experience at best.  We got there at the start of lunch opening at 11 (with a reservation for that time!) and it was about 15 minutes before a waitress finally got to us to take our drink orders.  I decided to stick to basics when I ate here and ordered appetizer wings, burger and fries as an entrée, and a blue raspberry shake as my dessert.  Wings were cooked well and OK tasting but a bit too sweet and over-sauced, plus the skin was pretty soggy.  They tasted boiled instead of deep-fried as they should have been.  Burger was cooked well, and that's about the only good thing I could say about it.  Chef was considerate about my allergy and replaced the brioche bun (which could have been baked in onion vicinity) with another "non-onion" bun...and the bun tasted stale and fell apart into nearly inedible crumbled bits in my mouth as soon as I took a bite.  And while the whole sad experience was, at first, tempered by the great old sci-fi flick shorts and ads in front of me, the film reel set recycled after just 30 or 40 minutes.  By the time I'd finished with the entrée, the set was already halfway through the second repeat.  And by the time I got my dessert shake (nothing to write home about, by the way...a little too sweet), the film reels had recycled AGAIN, so it was about 1/4 of the way through the third run by the time I finally signed the check.  My recommendation?  Come here to rest from the heat and to just grab a single course, one appetizer, or just a dessert and experience the feel of an old drive-in for a half hour.  But don't come here if you have three courses on the deluxe plan.  You'll be bored by the movies before you finish your entrée, and the food simply is not worth it.  I give the place two stars instead of one because of the kindness of the waitress who expressed her concern and offered me replacements, but I did not have time to wait for them even longer due to our fast pass schedule, and by then the film repeats were becoming tiresome and I wanted to get out.  I'm sticking to the 50s Prime Time for my next trip to Hollywood Studios.

Anyone that really knows me knows I have a complete aversion to pretentious restaurants.  When the names of foods are suppose to be pronounced using a lot of nasal tones and the dishes have more fancy "stuff" smeared on the plate than the actual food which is costing you a small fortune, I can't get out of the place fast enough.  When the waiter calls himself Jacques, talks with a fake accent, and takes the bus 30 miles to work because he can't afford to live any closer, I can't get out of there fast enough.

I picked Dixie Crossroads because it seemed anything but pretentious.  I didn't want some chef spending hours playing with my fish.  I wanted to drink beer and dip grilled shrimp into garlic butter and eat them.  I came, I drank beer, and I ate lots of delicious grilled shrimp dipped in garlic butter.  End of story.

It's been over a month since the course was completed and still no certificate. Tried reaching out to customer support and was promise to resend certificate but still have not arrived. No response to multiple emails.  Now my appointment with DMV has passed and have to reschedule. 

CUSTOMER SUPPORT PLEASE RESPOND

Update:  changed my rating from 1 star to 3. Customer support did end up responding and sent certificate through Fedex next day. It just took so long for a response. Once contacted they did respond quickly.

The espresso is pretty good- the line tends to be long but thats because it's a good shop with not many other places around. I also like that they have lots of tacodeli tacos with self serve salsa and good choose of pastries.

My main criticism and reason for 4 stars is that I wish they would put regular creamer out for the coffee. I find the moonmilk too sweet so I don't order those drinks, but I find it weird that they don't put out regular creamers as most cafes do, many people like to control the amount they put in their coffee. And It's really awkward to have to ask them to pull it up from behind the counter- they are clearly pretty busy.

We were on a mission for Cuban food while visiting Orlando, so we looked up reviews on Yelp and found this place. It's away from touristy things in a shopping center off main roads. 

I'm used to Cuban restaurants being casual with styrofoam boxes and cheap plastic chairs. This place is actually more upscale than that, with nice booths and decor on the walls. I ordered the ropa vieja, and it was perfect. The juiciness of the meat, the flavor in the beans and rice, and of course plantains were flawless. My husband had a cuban sandwich, and we each had some of that beautiful cuban coffee.

They asked if we wanted some hot sauce, and brought us a green sauce in a small mason jar. It looked like their own batch in house. You only needed a dab from the tip of a spoon to get the flavor; it was HOT, but it burned so good. The flavor was there, then the heat crept up on you. I'm not usually a spicy person, but I appreciate the flavor and slow creep of heat.

We ended the meal by splitting a slice of tres leches. The slice was more of a block soaked in wonderful milky goodness.

If you're visiting the tourist attractions, take a trip off the beaten path and come here. It's so worth it.

For an Orlando burger Joint, this place was pretty alright. We had met up with some old friends and had a group this past Sunday. We walked in shortly after noon and sat down with 9 at full service with no wait. Everyone was so nice when they greeted us, and everyone seemed to be having fun working. 

I must admit that I have a bias against burgers, just because I have never been a huge fan. Several places (Five Guys, Shula, Burger Lounge) have won me over...it is hard. Everyone at the table had a little bit of everything. I opted for the Thanksgiving burger, which was a turkey burger and all the fixins pretty much. I had to get a side of mac and cheese because I had a two year old on my lap. My wife got one of the regular burgers and some tots, which were pretty damn tasty with the sauce. My turkey burger was pretty good, reminiscing of the wawa gobbler, or Publix sub. The patty itself was dry. Without the fixins, it was one of those things you awkardly chew until you wash it with water (dry cube steak feel). This does not mean it was bad...all together the burger was pretty good. We ended up dissecting it and eating it sans the bun. Well, my son took the top of the bun and ate it...so I worked with what I had. 

I had two Bloody mary's (Amsterdam) for $4.50 each, which was dandy and made my day that much better. Overall, the place was pretty cool. I would definitely return and recommend others check it out.

I order from here all the time. It used to be great, but the last three times I've had a problem. The first time was a spoiled milkshake. The second was a missing sandwich. Today, I ordered and was given a delivery time of 10:30am when I ordered at 9:30am. It is currently 12pm and I haven't gotten my meal yet. When I called to try to cancel it, they told me that the quoted time was wrong and that I couldn't cancel the food because "it's almost there". He said that over an hour ago now. This place obviously doesn't care about customers, even loyal ones. I will not be ordering from here again.

Border grill was outstanding! We had a group of 5 and were able to eat for under $40. 

I'm from the west coast where we have tons of options for good Mexican, and I wasn't sure about this place going in. Small, dimly lit, not the cleanest looking...but I was very impressed with the food.

Lots of great traditional options, and very good rice and beans on the side. I had grilled chicken with beans and veggies and the flavor was excellent. I also had a side of guacamole - highly recommend.

My wife had a carnitas chimichanga - looked great and very good portion. She couldn't finish, but finished it up at home before bed! 

The service was also excellent

If ever a place was appropriately named, it is The Dump.

I wandered around this disorganized warehouse for a while before I found someone that might be able to help me. My conversation went something like this.

Me: Hey I'm looking for some barstools. Do you know where I could find them?

Dump Guy: Not really. Maybe over...there? Maybe you could find them scattered around with the tables.

What kind of answer is that? Also, almost everything in this store is brown and I didn't see any really compelling deals. So in summary, if you are looking for crappy brown furniture this is your spot. Just don't expect a lot of help finding it.

Keep this in mind - the quality of the food trucks increases as the distance from Main street increases.

Momogoose is the worst. Avoid the noodles, the sandwiches are passable. Don't let the line scare you off (the food does that enough), the service is actually quite fast. Almost too fast...

Jerusalem is decent. I get the falafel and hummus sandwich. It's greatly improved if you can pop it in the microwave, but I'd recommend Aceituna a few megablocks north of here instead.

Clover is great food and a great business. They're very transparent and experimental. It's slightly more expensive and significantly slower than the other trucks. As far as I can tell everything on the menu is vegetarian. There are a few staples such as the BBQ Seitan and they're usually rotating various other items in and out. Expect to spend $6 on sandwiches, $3 on sides and $3 on drinks. They're also open the latest in case you ever need a quick snack or drink before heading out of Kendall. 

The food at Jose's isn't as good as Clover's, but it's a great deal and still very tasty. $4 gets you a veggie burrito with sour cream and guac, chips, salsa, rice and beans. Service is very friendly and seems to be much quicker than it has been in the past. It's the farthest truck from my office, but definitely the best overall.

My biggest disappointment with the Kendall food trucks is there is no reason they need to be trucks. It's the same four restaurants since I started working here in summer 2011. The whole point of food trucks is that they can move around to various places. The City of Boston does it properly, with a fleet of licensed food trucks that move around the city to several different locations.

Still new to Hingham, we visited most restaurants in area, but never happened by The Square Cafe... Not sure why, I guess the "Cafe" part of their name suggested other than dinner for us. That said while shopping at nice French store next door, I peeked in and saw a very cosy restaurant, warm lighting, well laid out.
Anyway to the food.
Well it was 2:45pm and we felt hungry, so we went in for lunch (stops serving lunch at 3) and ordered a Stags Cab, and shared a Caesar salad. The Salad was a 4.6... Excellent. Nice start. We both decided on the grilled chicken sandwich. I got mine with spicy sauce and my partner without it. Both Primo. I'm a tough scorer , yet it was a solid 4.2 ... Nice filling - thin cucumbers , pickles , real thin onions, refreshed the sandwich just right. The french fries were excellent, but like everyone, to many for us to eat. Service was excellent from Jane and manager Chelsea both came over for extended chat. 
3 glasses of vino, 2 sandwiches, Caesar salad, all came to $89.88 good value from our lens. Well, we are going back to try the table cloth dinner in future.

This place is good but not great when it comes to BBQ. We were looking for an alternative to Franklin's with top notch BBQ, but without the wait. Micklethwait left us feeling disappointing and thinking that the wait at Franklin's might have been worth our time. The brisket was great; strong rub, and the meat cut had a proportionate fat content. The pork shoulder, on the other hand, was bland and dry. We tried to use the sauce to give it more flavor, but the sauce was too vinegary and thin for our taste. It seemed more like a salad dressing and less like a BBQ sauce.

Woke up this morning looking forward to heat up the pizza I ordered the night before. I heat up my pepperoni pizza rolls, and get to the last one. I take a bite and mid chew I noticed an extremely long hair inside my actual roll, so it was baked WITHOUT proper hair net and was sitting inside my pizza roll. I have spent my morning now gagging and cursing this dump, and want to warn all of you to NEVER go there. So disgusted rn!!!!!

For my wife's birthday I booked a night @hipcooks. Our class was booked for her birthday night. When she awoke the day of the class she was very sick. She was shaking with fever, head cold and couldn't swallow. She had a bug, a very bad bug. 
We are new to area and hoping to use class to met new people, get out and school looked fun.

I called and emailed and finally got the manager three hours before class. I knew cancel policy (penalty 48hrs in advance, forfeit 48 or less). Manager was polite but cold. She said she understood but and this is where I have a problem. I said I knew I couldn't get a full refund (food had been bought) but could we get some of it back or move us to another date with a penalty. The manager said, " I'm the manager, I'll talk to owner and if she (owner) is feeling generous." She then giggled, realized mistake, stopped herself and corrected," My official answer is you understand the policy." I told her I don't have any friends here to go in our place. She said I'll open up your seats and talk to owner. 

They never got back to us, and took our money. Stupid too because they could have had customers for a long time. Lesson learned. Go to bigger schools that you book same day and ditch the hipster, we don't care about people fly by nights.

I almost gave this three stars but decided to bump it up one star based on the freshness of the food. I wanted to come here after I saw it on DDD. The four of us were seated in a booth by the door. Three of us ordered savory crepe dishes and one ordered a salmon special. Everyone seemed pleased with the food. I had the Chicken Duxelle crepe, which was pretty good but somewhat bland. Just a little bit of salt when it was being cooked could have fixed that. It came with some very fresh steamed broccoli and flavorful yet gluey mashed potatoes. The portion was very large. I saved half of it and had the rest for lunch the next day. We ordered two portions of crepe cake to share - butter rum and tiramisu. Both were outstanding and covered in fresh strawberries and blueberries. The crepe cakes were the best part of the meal, and I don't usually get dessert. I would come back but I'm not beating down the door.

This place is a hidden gem and I'm a little hesitant about writing this review because I want to keep it all to myself. I have dined-in about 6 times and I have no complaints.   The place is small but the food is too good to even notice. I have tried a few things in the menu. My favorite by far is the fried chicken, it's seasoned deliciously and cooked perfect. The rice and beans are always a hit which comes with most of the dinner plates. The pupusas are very big and stuffed as much as possible which is great!! If you like them well done just ask them, they will take personal request within reason. Chicken tacos are awesome and their chicken fingers are great too. They also bring along homemade coleslaw with the fries 
  As for the staff, it's normally 2/4 women working and they're just great. They get the job done nice and fast, and are very professional. The kitchen is the main view when you eat and I must say, one of the cleanest kitchens I've ever seen in a restaurant. Sadly I have only one picture of my experience but I will definitely post more next time I go. 
Thank you for your awesome food and service!!

I wish I could give this place zero stars.  Hotel is under construction, no onsite restaurant or bar means you will have to hunt around town for breakfast or to meet up with others from your group.  Rooms are small.  Hotel coffee is bad. Only 1 working elevator (freight elevator) means extremely long waits when the hotel is full.  I ended up hauling all my family's luggage down 9 floors in the stairwell.  Valet brought my car back covered in construction dirt and debris.  Even when construction is done, this should be a $60/night hotel, not $130+ as they are charging.  The Westin is just up the street and MUCH nicer.  My suggestion is to keep looking - there are much better places to stay in Atlanta. The best part of my stay was checking out of that place.

Cool, sexy little lounge - indoors next to the windows, or outside on the patio, it's  a fantastic place to people watch in a very Euro setting around the cobblestone streets that are Gassy Jack's home.  No, not that kind of gassy - it basically means "plastered".  Perfect place to see and be seen, or just relax on a sunny summer day in Vancouver.  This was definitely one of the highlights of our trip - having worked our butts off the day before on the Grouse Grind, we wanted an easy day of just relaxing in the city.

Gastown is quite the artsy little strip, with galleries and expensive clothiers and little modern design shops and Ducatis going to and fro from cafe' to cafe', and Chill Winston is the perfect place to take it all in.

I had the Hop Goblin 20 oz. and the Newcastle Brown 20 oz.  A little pricey at $8 each, but they were 20s after all.  And hey, cool don't come cheap. ;-)  And I'm not talking yuppie-cool here, just cool cool.  dig?

When I read the reviews at the Bankrate website I thought I had chosen the right lender to refinance my mortgage. My error was not to research beyond this website before contacting them and discovered similar complaints that I can now compare with my own experience. First off, I never had the opportunity to talk to the credit person in charge of my loan estimate, only with her assistant, even though I sent her an email about when would be a good time to talk, her response was "you can call me anytime, if I'm on the phone my assistant can answer all your questions". To me this sounds like "I  have other priorities to attend to than talking to you". 
Second, after sending all the requested info, I received the wrong estimate which they blamed on me saying that I entered the wrong info. I saw another review very similar to my situation with the following comments: "they get you to sign and then put you into a processing void, expecting you to do all their work for them, without any instructions. And then they blame you for anything they forget, saying it was your responsibility"
Third, their priority #1 is to make sure you pay $500 "deposit" NON-REFUNDABLE before they can proceed any further. In other words if for any reason you don't agree with the terms of your loan or the APR comes back higher and not what you expected, say goodbye to your 500 "deposit". 
Fourth, they attempted to pressure me into signing an agreement by saying that the interest rate will change if I do not "lock" it by midnight that same day by submitting the $500 deposit. The email that informed me of this lacked any attachments to do so. The next morning, I received another email saying they forgot to send the loan package and gave me until midnight to submit it.
I'm very glad I didn't move forward and I hope my review will help others before they decide to make business with this lender.

Thanks

I'm not new to music but I am new to guitars, needless to say I bought a cheaper used guitar because I've always wanted to learn. I've been playing for at least 2-3 hours a day on a setup that had a pretty bad float on the string action which made it difficult to do bends as well as other technical approaches. I ended up breaking a string not too long after getting new strings and became frustrated. I took my guitar into Five-Star and was helped by Matt, not only did he give me information as to what was wrong with my guitar but he shaved down the saddle to give me better "action" on the guitar as well as replaced the string I broke, and all for no charge! Even though I bought new strings (just for future purposes), I was surprised that he wasn't going to charge me for the small tweaks he made to my guitar. When I expressed my gratitude for the work he did on the fly for me he shared with me a story about when he was young and started playing the guitar that he had issues with it but didn't have a lot of money to fix it and a guy did the same thing for him, and that he always appreciates when he can do the same for others. I'm definitely impressed with the classy approach of Matt and his generosity. This establishment is about the player and whats in their best interest, Matt showed me that today. Cheers Matt/ Five-Star Guitars! I will be back!

I loved my friend's hair cut so her style brought me here. Affordable price and courteous service. First I signed agreement that Q&A isn't responsible for lost/stolen items and questionnaire on hair care and allergy. Then Sarah, my stylist, took sketch of my hair style and asked length of hair cut. And also asked if I wanted straight, U or V shape cut on backside. I got my bangs cut as well.

Got my hair washes before the cut.($16.50 for my hair cut)I had to sit there for about hour and 20 minutes. Patience is the key. Stylist cut my hair onto desired length and instructor came to check and cut little bit more. I really liked the quality of service. As other Yelpers mentioned the price is unbeatable. I found out it's 56 for (medium length) hair colour and $59 for a perm(medium length) after asking stylist.

According to staff, tip is optional and it's cash only. I didn't know about $11 wednesday deal 'till I read reviews and will go back on wednesday for a cheaper deal on my next visit. I really liked my hair cut and my experience at Q&A was amazing.

Business trip to Atlanta, airport hotel. Nothing decent to eat around there and no time to go out to the city. Mellow mushroom is a name I remember from home (ft. Lauderdale) so decided to check it out. 

Nice selection of draft beers, local recommendations were excellent. 
Our pizzas took time so we got a free table starter without much fuss about it. 

Pizzas are terrific! My friends took the small and I decided it's probably not enough for me and went with the medium. Big (medium) mistake. 

We recommend the veggie & the barbecue chicken pizza. Thin crust better than the regular.

I ate here last week, and enjoyed it so much, came back with my family a few days later.  The outside is a lot more understated than the inside.  Whoever own this business spent an unbelievable amount of money reproducing the inside of an Irish pub.  I'm sure there are some hipsters who will criticize the Epcot aspect of the simulated pub, but to those I say there is a 6 pack of Pabst and a roller dog, awaiting your wallet connected to a chain, at the Quick Trip.  

It's a lot of fun.  They have a great menu with some of the best "pub food" I've ever eaten.  The average entree is around $16.  The fish and chips, cheddar ale dip and french onion soup are all outstanding.  It's also kid friendly with a children's menu.

The owner/barista behind the counter is a really cool guy and does a great job of roasting his own beans. He explained to us how he acquired this business from the Angry Baker right after memorial day, so they are both separate businesses... although his pastries come from the Angry Baker Bakery on 5th and High. We had the Guatemalan blend that he was making that day and the Turmeric Ginger Chai. The Guatemalan was extremely balanced. We're glad he suggested that we order that because he explained that the Mexican chiapa was not the best roast. He also suggested making me a Turmeric Ginger Chaider (like a cider) which wasn't on the menu. I wasn't feeling too adventurous when I ordered today, but I will be going back to order it another day.

The reason I give this place 4 stars is that they don't always have the most pastry options available. The cookies from the Angry Baker (and also sold here) aren't my favorite, however, they offer a lot of vegan and gluten-free options so this is a place to fill your dietary needs! Overall, it's a great stop and go place with great coffee and a great owner.

I like the size and the various activities at this place.  The staff is attentive but like any other child-activity in Austin there can be times when it feels like it is too crowded or overrun like on Saturdays or around holidays.  Overall I have had good experiences.  It is inexpensive and convenient for us.  We make a day of it by going there for an hour with my 3-year old so she can get some exercise and then go to Mandolas for lunch.  I would say that the age range of 4-6 year old whose parents have done a drop-off service can overwhelm the younger kids.  I stay with my daughter each time and participate in her activities.  It is a great place to help kids get exercise, participate in challenging activities, and have fun.

My review applies to their Sunday special since that is what we went for.  We wanted some good ole pizza and beer on Sunday so we searched for somewhere to go.  Luckily the bf found this place and said we should try it out.  When we get there, we know they have a pizza buffet on Sunday but were pleasantly surprised to find out they have a special:  Two full pizza buffets and a pitcher of beer for $20.  Are you kidding me?  That is a super good deal!  The buffet includes all kinds of pizza, thin and thicker crusts, cheez rolls, pepperoni rolls, stromboli and a full salad bar.  Plus, we had a whole pitcher of Fat Tire beer.  I dont know of anywhere else in town I can have all I can eat plus alcohol for two for only $20.  This will probably become our new Sunday afternoon hang out spot!  Great deal and the pizza was actually very good.

Team Tastic came here and we ordered a beautiful red box of 6 ($18) with the following:

Classic
Earl Grey
Maple Walnut
Salted Caramel
Cinnamon
Apple Crumble

My favourite 3 donuts started with the Apple Crumble. There was a decent amount of apple pieces on top of these that on first glance looked like nuts but I was fooled. The donut hole was also filled in this one we you get a bit more donut.

I also really liked the Earl Grey flavour. Red is not a colour you often see on donuts but here we got a few chunks of rose petals sprinkled on top of an earl grey glaze. This is how you would have your tea and one donut using only one hand.

Rounding out the favourites is the Classic donut. With a simple sugar glaze and a bonus cookie with the Cartems logo, this was the traditional donut that delivered on donut flavour.

Salted Caramel is usually one of my favourites by default. I'm a big fan of sea salt crystals in my dessert but I didn't taste much caramel in the glaze. This would be better for those who are okay without caramel.

The Maple Walnut was a massive and filling donut. Spinkled with house-smoked walnuts, this thing might be enough for a big snack with how filling nuts are and they were a-plenty. I regret having so many donuts and having the Maple Walnut last so I recommend eating fewer donuts if you're going to try this one.

Last but not least, the Cinnamon flavour was a little bare for me and made me miss the glaze on top of all the other donuts. This flavour would have been good for those who don't like a sugary glaze and preferred a syrupy infusion of flavour in their donut.

You can stop searching for a fireplace service company. You've found the company you should use. As others have written, I wish I could give Phil's company more than five stars! 

I'm originally from Hawaii so I know as much about gas fireplaces as I do about neurosurgery. Phil patiently gave me a tutorial on my fireplace and even suggested what product I could use to keep the glass shiny. 

From the look of the thick layer of dust that was at the bottom of the fireplace, it was evident that previous owners hadn't serviced it in years. Phil took care to spread a tarp on the floor, painted the inside of the fireplace, vacuumed all the dust, rearranged the logs and embers, checked for leaks and checked the integrity of the valves and pilot light. It took an hour and the service is well worth spending money on. My fireplace looks brand new! 

What's more, Phil is the nicest man and you want his company to be successful! Kind, friendly, professional and did I already say patient? If you call for an appointment and you don't hear back immediately, it's because he's popular. He will call you back within a day or two. It's worth waiting for his call. His work is guaranteed for a year. I'll be calling him next year for my annual service!

You can't beat their drum. My friends and I are on a mission to hit every fish spot in town and we decided on this place for dinner on Saturday. I decided on the special of the day, the Texas Gulf Black Drum, and the diablo shrimp for an appetizer. The shrimp was wrapped in bacon, fried, and was delicious. My Drum was outstanding, it was juicy, flavorful, and super fresh. I housed that thing with some really good green beans and broccoli(summer cut season). I even went next door to the market to get some drum to cook later on in the week, it was that good.

"I want a waffle; smothered hash browns and cheese grits." I said, purring.

"You sure you don't want some eggs with that?"

Satisfied that I didn't actually want any protein, the waitress ambled over to the counter to holler out my order.

They forgot the waffle.

It arrived a little bit late, but still tasty.

You get what you pay for. It's cheap, filling and the usual.

But all that's what I like most about Waffle House. Some days, you don't want any surprises (or protein!) with your meal. You just want a good ole dose of carbs to send you on your way.

I've been searching for great ice cream in my area and finally tried Tipping Cow. I had the vanilla and blueberry ginger. It seems like the local ice cream places try too hard and either make the ice cream like a mouthful of tasteless fat with absurd flavors (Gracie's) or exaggerate on the sugar. Tipping Cow is good on the creaminess but way too heavy handed on the sugar. Diabetics beware!

Even the vanilla was too sweet. The blueberry ginger was a mouthful of candied ginger and no discernible blueberry. It's more accurate to just call it ginger with blue streaks. 

If they just dial back on the sugar, they've got a winner! We were 4 people and 3 out of 4 agreed it was far too sweet. The 4th would eat anything so he doesn't count :-)

This review is specifically for Associate Broker Joel Madden at Rick Hale and Associates / Keller William Realty Atlanta Midtown: 

My husband and I had been looking at houses on Trulia for more than two years and could never seem to agree on one that met both wishlists. When we finally found the house for us in East Atlanta, Joel was right there to help. 

I was not familiar with the process, and Joel was very helpful on what the next steps would be and when. He sent us lists of deadlines and reminders as they approached. He helped with the lender, recommended inspectors, set up surveys; he was always quick to reply to emails (and texts) or answer calls - even during the holidays! I always felt in the loop and informed. 

Joel is extremely professional and offered honest advice whenever we asked. When we had some hiccups before closing with seller repairs, he stepped right in to work with the listing agent, seller and inspector to make it right. I always trusted he had our best interests in mind. 

We love our new house and location, and I feel very lucky that we Joel to help us through it. I will definitely recommend him to anyone looking for a new home.

Emory Point is a little shopping center/food court area across the street from the CDC and Emory campuses. It's a mixed residential/commercial complex and would be an awesome place to live at if you work/go to school at any of the local places.

If you're like me and are just visiting, then it's super convenient. They have a CVS on the corner with a full pharmacy if you need to pick anything up. They have an American Chinese restaurant, Papis (Cuban/Caribbean food), Desta (Ethiopian) and one of my favorite places around, General Muirs. GM is great for coffee and their food is surprisingly delicious as well (although I might advise skipping their Sunday fare as it's underwhelming).

Unfortunately for the businesses it gets pretty quiet here in the evenings and on weekends but during the day, the complex is bustling. There's a lot of temporary paid parking but you can also park longer if you go to the garage. I don't know how many businesses validate but you can get your ticket stamped at GM after you purchase something.

I used to come to this place all the time before they changed owners. I decided to go one day because I was in the mood for wings, upon arriving I noticed things looked much differently and so did the menu. I ordered wings and noticed the price for them had gone up as well but I was fine with that but what I wasn't fine with was the fact that the wing size had changed as well. They were the size of my pinky finger and I didn't want to pay so much for some very little wings. In addition, they messed up my order. I always get mine cooked soft, extra wet and they were cooked crispy without the extra sauce which I was charged for. I was very disappointed and haven't returned since.

Masa is in the neighbourhood of my workplace so therefore have been here quite a few times. Lately the quality of service and food have gone up. They've added more comfort food items such as ramen and Japanese curry. I've had the combo lunches and they were tasty and affordable. Just recently I had the miso ramen. It was delicious but not outstanding like a ramen-only place obviously. The servers are nice there and I usually can have a nice conversation with the sushi chefs at the counter.

Great massage, and I get a ton! 
Tony, ? owner, was so skilled . I had one prior with his ? mother, whom did not speak any English, so it was hard to tell her what to do, where to go, hard vs soft, etc. so not great. Then, I tried Tony. OMG. Some people on this planet are gifted, and he, god bless him, is one. I have gotten massages in 22 countries, and he is one of the best. I will definitely go back. And they do feet massage, so important with meridian centers, and chakras. I was so sore going in and felt great going out.

I love Rag-o-Rama for the most part and have had excellent selling and buying experiences here. However, a recent experience has prompted me to write this.
I dropped 2 dresses off a few days before New Years Eve.. Let me tell you how epic these dresses were :a blush colored Vintage lace dress that had been lovingly restored by my dead grandmother who survived WW2 and a horrible bout of Leprosy (she lived in exile on a remote island for many years...I never met her...but I got that damn dress...she couldn't wear it because the lace bothered her delicate ,rotting flesh) .The other dress was a white, tight fitting sexy as fu*k 80's Diane Von Furstenburg  that was said to be worn by lady Di a few days before she was killed in that tragic crash (luckily she wasn't wearing it in the crash...it probably would have had to be repaired just a smidge) when I took them in I was told there was a 30 minute wait for selling.I had an appt and asked if I could come back later. I was told I could come back before 9 pm. I wasn't told if I didn't come back my shit would be gone forever.( I guess I signed something that said if clothes are left they will be donated)#mehughwhoreadsthatsh*tanyway?) Me from now on, that's who.
I go back in the next day and after a few minutes of bumbling and um, er, well,hold I'll check stupidity by the uber stylish, tragically hip staff, I was told that they weren't selected for resale and that they were picked up by the Salvation Army. OK, fine I didn't read the fine print...my bad. 
But...not for one minute do I or anyone I'll ever know or have known my entire life would believe they were donated to SA.
The history of these dresses aside...they were in excellent shape and were a perfect size 6/8 ( which is why I was selling them) but I will spare you the story of why I can't wear them anymore...believe me it's a doozy. So whichever staff member got those dresses...please know that they are also cursed with the souls of several very important but deeply evil former owners and  extra dark forces. Enjoy!

It's been sometime since I have visited Austin. A fun vibrant city with a small town feel.  The JW has been great. Right in the middle of everything.  You can walk a few blocks to the Capital or a couple to the convention center. We got in eat and they moved a couple of rooms around and got us in without a wait.  Rooms are very nicely appointed and the bathroom is almost spa like.  The staff is all smiles and friendly.  The executive lounge is super nice. Only issue is nothing is opened at 6 when I was looking for coffee. I wish I could try one of the nice looking on premises restaurants but in a town that is so foodie friendly it's out and about. They are doing it right at the JW Marriott Austin.

I've been coming to NEMC since I was a baby. I switched clinics for  a while, and decided to come back to Tufts a year ago because my dentist is at Tufts and wanted to keep all appointments/PCPs in the same location for convenience. My doctor in General Medicine was nice, and couldn't have asked for a better doctor. 

It was the nurses and office assistants' attitudes in General Medicine that made me rate this place 3 stars. If I had to ask a question, I was sometimes barked at. When I was being weighed/BP was taken, e.t.c. the nurse didn't engage me - she was busy yelling and having loud conversations with the office assistant at the front desk. I didn't think that this was professional or worth my time/co-pay. I've gone to other departments within Tufts, and had positive experiences, but General Medicine wasn't that positive.

Came here for dinner last night with some friends and found the patio hidden away out back an amazing spot to spend a warm summer evening. The gentle breeze which came and went periodically kept us cool and comfortable. Now on to the food. We tried the antipasto - fresh and a great start to a meal with conversation between friends; the feature vegetarian pasta of the day - girella; a seafood linguine with large plump prawns and scallops and smoked salmon; and lastly tagliatelle agilio e olio - great flavour but I found the pasta a bit overlooked, I enjoyed the linguine however which was much more al dente. Comparable to Ask for Luigi and decently priced; will be back. Perhaps on a date ;).

Vegan gastropub. Some hits and some misses; but overall it is good! 

First, I'd like to state that I am not vegan and can't have soy.... so that limits my options here; but our waitress was super friendly and made sure to offer options/alternatives for me. 

We ventured here with one of our vegan friends and were not disappointed... as expected, they have a great beer list! To start, I had the buffalo cauliflower with garlic aoili sauce (as a replacement for the blue "cheese" sauce made with tofu), and this was amazing!!! I need to figure out how to recreate for home. For entree, I had the veggie burger and it was just meh. . I'd recommend trying something else. My friend's "Caesar" looked great, but according to her needed a bit more tang... 

There is some outdoor seating.. but we sat inside because the ambiance in there was nicer.

Huge fan of this location.  I'm from out of town(2 hours away) and I feel like I shop here more than locals, ha.  The store is always clean and neat when I drop by and the associates are always pleasant and willing to help if you need anything.  I've had many friends come with me during my travels, and they always rave about how incredible the layout and quality of the store is.  I've been coming here for years, and Jonathan and Taylor in RRL have been a major help in getting me everything and anything I want that's offered from the brand.  Will definitely continue to come here as much as I can.

Quick and casual eatery serving up quality, healthy, and locally-sourced food.

Eager to branch out from our usual casual eateries, we stopped by B Good on the way to the airport and then another day for a quick dinner. I had their power bowl the first time, and loved all the vegetables and vegetarian protein, and especially that it was fresh and flavorful. The second time I had the spicy avocado and lime bowl, which was delightfully hot and creamy thanks to the chipotle puree and queso fresco. 

The service is usually pretty quick - considering they're making everything fresh. It is a bit more expensive than other casual eateries, but if you want something healthier and tastier than normal, than it's worth it. I consider the options pretty filling, but if you're starving you may want a side item. 

Overall, a great option if your short on time but want something that tastes good and does you good.

The decor looks like it was new in 1964, last cleaned in 1977 and the waitress last smiled in 1982.

Ambiance consists of the sound of cleaver on chopping block.

On the other hand they probably haven't increased their prices since the last time the AC worked. 

The food is the star here, it is absolutely divine. A very simple menu consisting of roast meats available atop rice or noodles with a spooning of a ginger, scallion soy sauce over the lot. I like the 2-meat rice plate, and for $5.75 you can't go wrong. The soy sauce chicken is juicy and tender, the roast pork is delightful and the duck is exquisite. (Note to all - you might find bones in the meat. Until scientists develop a boneless duck, chicken or pig, this is going to happen - live with it and spit, we won't judge you)

Each meal starts with a bowl of chicken broth, with chicken meat and bones. One time I even got a slice of carrot in the soup.

Order a side of vegetables if you feel like splashing out.

Cash only

My fiancee and I went to Atlanta to visit his kids.  It was still a little cool out, but that's ok because the pool at the Hilton Garden Inn is indoors and heated!  The room was huge and very clean.  And the greatest part of or trip was Miss Bridgette at the front desk.  She is like your mother, she makes you feel at home and comfortable.  The neighborhood is a bit sketchy, but sitting in the middle of the airport outskirts, this beautiful hotel has private parking and excellent security.  And the rates are great for everything that you get.  Only downside:  no in-room movies for the kids, but at least they had cartoon network and nickelodeon.  Thank you Miss Bridgette for a wonderful stay!

Mercado is not the best Tex Mex food around but I think they are the third best Mexican martini in Austin after Baby Acapulco and the Cedar Door. They have a pretty decent tequila list. I am a fan of the sour cream chicken enchiladas but have found deviating away from enchiladas will leave me disappointed. I asked our waiter if the bbq chicken enchiladas were any good and he honestly said "They're not my favorite." with a smile. However, he made a misake not asking us if we wanted another drink.

Fantastic nail salon! I live out of town and every time I come home I make sure to book an appointment. This is the only nail salon that I've been to that is absolutely invested in making sure you're happy. They will bring out multiple colors, compare the shades, talk through different options and scroll through pics with you for the perfect fit. My nails always look fantastic at the end and the gel manicure lasts sooo much longer than other gel manis I've gotten. Definitely the standard for all other nail salons to try and meet!

Stopped here while in terminal C at the airport. Cute little sandwich shop in the airport. Reasonable prices for an airport. Paid $10.75 for a turkey hoagie. A bag of chips a soda and a bottled water. They roast the hoagie roll and the bread was really good. Standard turkey lunch meat. You pick toppings. They also had salads and soup. Place was clean. Only negative thing was service was slow. They had a huge line and the team members behind the counter moved at a snails pace. So that was very annoying.

Popped in here on a Sunday morning and there was a huge line! It went by pretty quickly and I was able to place my order with the friendly barista! I ordered a full wintermoon which is a latte: a shot of espresso and the rest with their house made sweetened "moon milk." I also ordered an extra shot because I ordered the 20oz. It was really delicious and creamy. I would definitely come back but maybe go for the 3/4 or 1/2 moon to scale back on the sweetness. If you are in Austin and in need of a pick me up, this is the place to go!

When I lived in Korea for a few years I was absolutely ADDICTED to Red Mango and then moved back to NH where there weren't any. I was really excited to see one in the Natick Mall, but it seems like Red Mango USA isn't as good as the original. In Korea you pay for the yogurt and any five toppings (of which they have a bigger selection) and you stand in front of the topping bar while they're putting them on your yogurt. At this Red Mango you have to pay extra for each topping and it seems like people order the toppings at the cash register where you can't see what they have to offer. So it's more expensive and difficult to tell what you want. I wish this was a Tutti Fruiti instead!

The new year is upon us! Mr. Smidgens here! Did I eat all the things and drink all the drinks in 2014? Of course I did! I'm Mr. Smidgens you silly goose. 

Whether you are looking to start a juice cleanse to get back on track or just looking to get some oh so tasty nutrients in your carbon based self, Juiceland is the place to go! 

I mean come on, If a 275lb gorilla of a man like Mr. Smidgens can drink and eat everything on their menu, so can you. 

If you have food allergies, they can help. If you hate eating your veggies, they can help. If you hate tasting your veggies, they can help. If you hate being naked in public, they can help. No really they can. Juiceland sells gear to cover your beautiful bodies whilst you enjoy their juices and or smoothies. 

They have sooooo many choices for you. Tell them Mr. Smidgens sent you and order the WUNDERSHOWZEN!!! If you like a party in your mouth. 

They have 10 locations in Austin and they even have one in Park Slope, Brooklyn! Whaaaat?!!! Nuuuice.

I went here for the first time to have the waist hemmed on my jeans. 
It is close to my home so I thought I would give them a try.  What a mistake!  The woman who was working the front did not seem to know anything about alterations or what their prices were for alterations(which are not super cheap)  She kept going to the back to ask questions.  I told her 3 times I wanted the waist taken in 2 inches.  She told me it would be ready in a week(?)  After a week and no phone call, I stopped by after work to see if they were ready.  This same lady tells me that my pants are not ready because she forgot to write how many inches I wanted hemmed.  I told her just forget it and that I would go somewhere else. 
No apology or nothing.  I think cleaning is their main business here and not alterations.

Most people think "RMV - oh great.."  NOT AT WILMINGTON!!!!

I am giving an enthusiastic 5-stars to the Wilmington RMV location in general, and specifically to Caroline and Marc L.  I was in/out in like 20-mins, they were wicked friendly, and I am 100% happy with the service.  It sounds hilarious to say I can't wait to go back, but it's true.

My only advice to those of you still thinking "oh great" - if you can go online and use the forms and then print them, that helps.  They scanned my bar code and had everything right in front of them.  Incredibly efficient, and 100% accurate.

This place has fucken shitty service. Cheap shitty people.  The ramen was bland. The water taste like hot dog water. The chopsticks had stains on them. When we asked for extra lollipops they said 1 per person. Like they owned the lollipops or something. I have kids at home that couldn't make it to the restaurants and wanted to surprise them with lollipops BUT these people didn't wouldn't give me an extra lollipop. They forced me to give them a 20% tip. They said if I were to use a debit card they will charge extra. I will never return to this place EVER again. Thank u bye.

Based on the reviews here I contacted Dominique to see if the mysterious bites we were getting were from bed bugs. 

She responded fast and diligently and it was easy to schedule a time for her to come. 

While speaking with her on the phone, she heard how distressed my daughter was. I had told her that I had looked *everywhere* for bugs and I hadn't seen anything.  She said that it wasn't consistent with bedbugs. If my daughter had that many bites I would have seen something. 

She encouraged me to call my doctor and I did. It turns out my daughter has poison ivy. My bites are still unidentified but they are healing and I don't have any new ones. My daughter and I have two separate issues, but neither issue is bed bugs. 

Dominique is an honest professional and while I hope I never have to call her, I recommend her wholeheartedly.

After a long day in the parks, we had a craving for some authentic cuban food when we came across this restaurant.
Well when we arrived there was only one other table occupied.  We were seated and forgotten.  When the older gentleman came over he welcomed us and suggested the days special, which was "fichase de cerdo" when we declined he seemed upset and preceded to insist so we agreed to a small sample.  After sampling the dish we declined. From that moment on we were attended by a different server  
I ordered a steak with onions, rice and black beans and my wife ordered the same except she asked for the red beans.  After a few minutes the server returned to advice us that    They were out of red beans.  Anyway to make it short....  Even with an empty restaurant it took almost 40 minutes to receive our meals.  While we waited I told my wife at least we're going to get a hot fresh dish.   But I spoke too soon. The food arrived and to my dismay the food was at best a little warmer than room temperature.  And btw my steak literally had 4 tiny strands of onions. I preceded to get the attention of the server (remember the place was practically empty) after a few attempts and told him the dish was too cold for me and if he would microwave it for me.  He did and when it came back it was still Luke warm.  The only reason I'm giving it 2 stars is because I order a latte at the end, to which I give the 2 stars to.  It too was only warm.
In summary I wouldn't recommend this place.   I left disappointed with an unsatisfied taste for some authentic cuban cuisine.

I've been into this Warby Parker store multiple times. Every time the staff is very kind, welcoming, and friendly. Elizabeth was super helpful two times I visited. Ordering glasses and trying everything on was easy and there's even a photo-booth where you can see how you look. 

The reason I give it four stars instead of five is because when I received my glasses, something wasn't quite right and I couldn't focus/see out of them. I took them in and the Warby Parker employee told me my prescription must be wrong. I went back to the eye doctor who told me that the prescription was correct and that they had measured where the glasses should sit incorrectly.
