I then went back again, and this time the Warby Parker employee checked my glasses and said, yes they did have the wrong measurements, but that the original order was written correctly but not made correctly. 

Long story short, they manufactured my glasses incorrectly. The first employee should have caught this rather than sending me to the eye doctor (which the second employee even stated). So between screwing up the manufacturing of the glasses and having someone not do their job correctly, I knocked it down a star. I would've rated it three if their frames weren't so great and everyone wasn't so nice and helpful, besides the one guy. All that being said, you get what you pay for. 

There is a 30 day return policy, no questions asked, which is great. I would still order from Warby Parker, it was just inconvenient to have to go through such a back and forth when I just want my new glasses.

Sorry in advance for the long-winded review, but this has been the most painful process I have ever experienced!  Where do I begin?  On June 11, 2018 my wife and I go into the Katy, TX showroom looking for a replacement vent hood.  We selected the same brand as the one that was in the kitchen prior thinking that it should be a fairly easy process to get it installed.  Ferguson's process for this goes as follows: 1)you pick out what you want and then pay for it, 2)wait for the item to ship - and during this period the store sends someone to your house to measure where the item goes making sure what you purchased will fit and if any other prep work needs to be done prior to installation, 3)once the item arrives, they call you to setup a delivery time and an installation time (these are 2 different people).  Sounds easy right?  Not hardly.  It took a month for our vent hood to arrive at the store to be delivered.  During this time the guy came out and measured and everything was in order for the installation, or so we thought.  It was mid to late July when we finally took delivery of our vent hood (we were not at home the first time they came, then the truck broke down the next time, etc..).  When the installer came, it was discovered that the outlet needed to be moved and they don't do that kind of thing (This should have been noticed during the initial measuring phase, right?).  So we had to get an electrician to come move the outlet.  Another 2 weeks, and we get the installer back out.  It was then discovered that the cover for the pipe going up to the ceiling was not long enough and we needed to purchase an extension (Again, I thought this would have been discovered during the initial measuring phase).  While he is at the house the installer tells me that he has called Ferguson and placed the order for the extension and when it comes in the store will call me to set up a time for delivery.  After about 2 weeks I haven't heard anything, so I call the sales guy who sold us the vent hood.  He tells me that he sees that "Yes, we do need an extension".  Apparently the order was never placed for the extension.  Just to make sure we get the right one he has me measure the height of my ceiling (Again, I thought this would have been done during the initial measuring phase).  About a week goes by and the extension comes in and the installer comes over to finish up the install.  At this point I'm thinking this is finally over and I don't have to deal with the vent hood anymore.  The installer shows up and doesn't even have a ladder, so he has to borrow one of mine.  He gets up there and then discovers that in order to hang it correctly he will have to cut away a big chunk of crown molding on either side in order to attach it to the bracket.  Why was I not told about this at the beginning?  Just so I don't have to deal with this company and their incompetency, I am going to finish this up myself.  Do yourself a favor and DO NOT DO BUSINESS WITH THIS COMPANY!!

Not worth it. We were seated right away then everything went downhill. People that were seated after us got their food before us, we brought that to the attention of our server, she explained it was due to the prep of the lettuce and tomato on my sandwich. Then manager came by just checking out tables ... the obligatory sweep. I said it was really slow, he "yah, here's my card" 
Then I said " yah here's my bad Yelp review"
Way too loud,not good food, not good service

Explored the Conservatory today and found it to be an amazing place.  The entire conservatory is indoors and environmentally controlled.  There are lush tropics along with desert exhibits.  The place is very tranquil and relaxing not to mention beautiful.  General admission was $19.95 and I thought it was worth every penny.  There was an outdoor area set up for Halloween which featured hundreds of real and glass pumpkins.  The glass pumpkins light up at night and you know that's gotta be cool.

If you're visiting Columbus the conservatory is a must see.

ONLY GO HERE AS A LAST RESORT!!! Every time I go in here I am reminded of why I hate this store. I don't have a problem with Joann stores in general, although I do prefer Michael's, but this particular location is terrible. The people working here are so lazy and useless when it comes to providing any type of help, it is infuriating. In my experience it is nearly impossible to track someone down and I usually end up having to go back to the front of the store for help. Any time I have had a question like where a product is located in the store, whoever I've asked has just kind of waved their arm in the general direction they tell me the item "should be if they had it", sometimes sending me on a goose chase for something they don't even carry. When I asked if an item could be looked up to tell me if they had any in stock, the woman told me the only way would be if they had the code a for the item, and that I could go check the shelf for the code if I wanted. I absolutely hate going to this location, the employees are rude, lazy, and unhelpful; in my opinion there needs to be a major overhaul in the management or something!

I decided to try this place after having a craving for something different.   As others have reported it is easy to find and park.  I was greeted  warmly and went to the bar as I was dining alone.  The place is clean and decorated tastefully. 
The menu had several options to choose from, making a choice tough.  I also had several craft beers with a couple I had not tried before.   I was pleasantly surprised to find this at a restaurant.  Not being too hungry I ordered the Caesar salad and seafood gumbo.  Both were a good size and we'll seasoned.  The French bread was very nice as well.  The odd part of the experience was the music.  It was late 60's early 70' soul music.  I was not sure if I was in a soul food restaurant or a creole place. I would have preferred more of a New Orleans sound. Overall a good experience and would go back.

Waited 20 minutes past our reservation to get seated. No one seated us at the bar to wait and have a cocktail. The servers were all in outrageously low-cut tops. I have never been more hurried through a meal. Before my friends finished their app our pizzas arrived. Server was clearly rushing us out. Food was good but the service was so weirdly rushed and odd. We told our server we were ready to pay and sat waiting for our bill for another twenty.

Being Indian myself, I'm never pleased with any Indian restaurants. This one changed that. 

First off, their food actually is spicy. I like my food spicy, and we Indians can never get enough spice. Here, when you ask for spicy, they make it spicy. That's great.

Second, this actually tasted like Indian food should. I think it's better than my mom's Indian cooking, and what's funny is none of the people cooking the food are Indian. Amazing.

Also, they have free wifi, which is great because I don't have to use up my limited amount of 4G LTE.

All in all, the food here is probably some of the best you'll get in Austin.

Amazing. I fell in love with gelato after the first time I came here and haven't gone back to ice cream since. Me and 3 friends had a tradition of coming here after ever Monday meeting for an entire semester. I don't go back as often now -only about once every two weeks, but I can never stay away for too long. 

Every time I come I know I will be ordering half sugar free chocolate (not because it's healthier, but because I think it actually has a richer chocolate-ier taste) and half raspberry. It's the perfect flavor combination. But don't get me wrong, I still always ask for samples of any new creations - and they are always very friendly and don't ever get annoyed no matter how many samples I ask for. 


After trying gelato all over Italy, I can say that this place really knows what they're doing. Plus, who can compete with a cozy fireplace on the patio on a chilly Austin evening? Love this place.

Ghosts can be perceived by all of us in a number of ways: through sight, sound, smell, touch and sometimes they can just be sensed, this ride will force you to deal with your fear or maybe just your curiosity. People that fear often try to deny to themselves that they are being actually haunted by these mystic forces, this method of self-assurance will be tested as you ride through the darkness. They often look for reasons other than denial for not believing that paranormal forces exist, but remember your inability to focus or deal with reality doesn't change fact from fiction. Before you enter the haunted mansion you may want to ask yourself why am I doing this, why was this ride through the world of the supernatural created. In some cases it might not be a ghost it could be all in your mind created by your life experiences, but on the other hand it may be a place of balance. This park is full of joy, laughter and happiness and nothing bad is allowed to enter through its gates, can you be sure as you climb aboard the moving pods and travel into the darkness that Magic Kingdom is truly magical? Ask yourself how many places do you absolutely know for certain are true sanctuaries void of any negative influences or is it possible this small isolated section of the park is where all the darkness is captured and the mansion acts as the scale that balances the good with the bad. 

By now you may be beyond the point of no return and you'll be forced to face your inner fears or will you close your eyes and plug your ears so you are isolated within the isolation of the haunted mansion and your false sense of security will protect you from all that is evil. This ride has a history of breaking down mid way through the horror, is this by chance, can you convince yourself that this is only a ride. Some of what you see here is fantasy hopefully you'll be able to separate the two or will you take something with you by association, either way it will forever be part of your new life experience. Once the light appears no matter how faint it is you'll realize the ride is about to end and you'll need to focus on exiting the pod because others are waiting for their journey to begin and you need to prepare to make your next choice do you want to pretend you're one of the Seven Dwarfs, Cinderella or just plain old Goofy... This is one awesome trip.

I wish I could base this on the food...but due to the RUDENESS that I was presented by the two hostesses I didn't stick around to try...

I'm a frequent bruncher who was visiting a few friends from out of town for the weekend. About two weeks before my mini-vacation  I did a search for best brunches in orlando and found Santiago's as being fairly high in good ratings. The day of my reservation came, and unfortunately during my vacation I broke my arm causing me to only move slower than usual, but had me depending on others to drive me. 

As our reservation loomed, I noticed that we were going to be late so out of courtesy I called the establishment and let them know. Whoever I spoke to immediately sounded annoyed and reiterated (twice) that our table was booked for an hour after us so however late we were would cut into our brunch time. (Ummm...I thought this was all you can eat? Doesn't that mean at MY leisure?)

I let it slide. Since my friend was sooo ecstatic to try this place.

My friends babysitter cancelled last minute, and she had to bring her four year old son. She called the establishment who stated it was fine and that they wouldn't charge. When we arrived, we got a different story.

We received a phone call as we are looking for parking asking where we were in another rude manner by the hostess. When I told her that we were trying to find parking she informed us yet again about our time limit....

We walk in. Two hostess are bent over the podium looking bored AND annoyed as we walk in. After no greeting or acknowledgement I inform them that I had a reservation. I get a nasty look and was told "your reservation is for two not three". At this point I'm trying to keep it together and calmly inform them that we had called and explained the situation where we were told "you never told us the child needed a chair". 

I was more than shocked and annoyed by that comment but asked if they could just add a chair to the table where I was flat out told no. But, they would see what they could do. While they are "checking"  they kept whispering  amongst themselves and giving us dirty looks. Meanwhile we started looking up other options...

Eventually, as my friend was confirming a brunch spot with another establishment, the two hostesses look up and let us know that they found us a table. But, we would have to take no longer than 40 minutes to eat because they were booked...

Thanks, but NO thanks...

It took over a month to get the company to come out for a survey. Then had to wait another 2 weeks for a scheduled installation. Offered to pay more money and they still would not do it. That means they don't have a clue how to do business. I should have followed my instincts but instead decided to give them a chance. 

Internet connection was terrible, not much better than dial up. Paid for 2 Mb and didn't even get to 1. Asked for 4 and was told they could not provide it.

3 days after installation it failed completely and I have not yet been able to contact anyone regarding fixing it. I first reported the problem on 11-22 it is now 11-26 and still no communication from them.

They never answer the phone, have no names or contact info on website.

Paid $270 for installation and the check has already cleared. I would have cancelled it if it hadn't.

Installation grounding does not conform to National electrical code. Ground rod is not bonded to house grounding and incorrect ground wire size was used. I am an electrical engineer with a background in communications antenna installations, I know I am right and can show you the codes if you want me to. These codes apply to everyone in the USA for all antenna installations without exception. Proper grounding is necessary for protection of equipment, installation structure and safety of people. Very important.

Anyway, I told them today that I wanted the system functional by tomorrow or they can cancel my account and return my installation money. I don't expect them to answer me.

Don't waste your time or money on this company, they have no idea how to provide the level of service required to keep anyone happy.

Michael Frattaroli
mff at msn dot com

When I bought my new house and needed to get some electrical work done, I called around to several electricians to get an estimate.  Surprisingly, a lot of them didn't even return my calls, but Eugene called me back, gave me a thorough explanation of the electrical issues outlined in my home inspection report, and set up a time to fix my problems.  So far he's helped me out with replacing an outdated interior breaker box, and did a complete update of my outdoor electrical system.  He does great work, and he's a pleasure to work with.  Highly recommended.

Horrible dentist. I arrived for my appointment and after I had filled out my paperwork, it took them over an hour to get my exam started. 

While waiting, I heard the conversations between the receptionist and the customers over the phone. Over the course of that hour, she had received at least 6 phone calls of unhappy customers about their unexplained charges.

By this point, I should have left and saved myself my time. 

The x Ray process seemed dirty and the nurse didn't seem to care about how uncomfortable I was. She was shoving the x Ray thing into my mouth and I nearly lost my lunch.

Now the exam room also felt dirty and looked horribly ugly. I felt extremely nervous at this point.

I was told I had cavities and that was on the verge of gingivitis and if I didn't get this expensive clean soon then my teeth would fall out.
 
I'm 21 and I brush my teeth on a regular basis. How could I lose my teeth in a matter of weeks?

Anyways, the total time I spent at the dentist was almost 2.5 hours and They didn't even clean my teeth...

A couple weeks later, I went to a new dentist and found out I had NO cavities and there was no mention of my teeth falling out.

Aspen was trying to scam me out of money.
If I could give this place negative stars, I would.

I have been to going to Wilson farm ever since I moved to Massachusetts last year. I love the fresh produce, bakery items, dairy items, packaged lunches/dinners, and more. There usually are seasonal events that take place on the weekends but have been paused due to COVID. These events feature the produce in season such as corn, berries, apples. I love the family-like atmosphere of this farm. My weakness is the bakery. There are several freshly baked items to chose from such as cakes, breads, and pastries. I usually look forward to visit Wilson's! 
Only downside during COVID is the rush. They are very good about making sure that there are not many people shopping by allowing a certain number in at a time, however, I still feel it is a bit crowded due to the size of the store. I would recommend going at a non-peak grocery shopping time.

As a Southerner in Boston, I miss familiar flavors. Aside from BBQ or soul food, the pickings in New England are slim, especially with the closing of Hungry Mother in Cambridge. The Frogmore was good on our first try, and we will be back to taste more of the menu. Boiled peanuts were a clever welcome gift, with the smooth fattiness of the soft peanuts paired against the tart acidity of a cardamon infused grapefruit/lime drink called Sweater Weather. The greens may have been the tastiest thing we had - their secret sauce is peach syrup, which leaves a subtly sweet, rather than bitter, aftertaste. The catfish was cooked well but tasted bland (farm raised), which made me wish they had pushed the envelope more on that dish. Another disappointment was the po-boy - the fried oysters inside were divine, but nobody in New England supplies the right bread for a true po-boy taste (Leidenheimer's Bakery in New Orleans is too far away). The vibe was good on the Friday night we went, and Yankees will discover plenty of new things to try here, like Pimento cheese, fried green tomatoes, smoked turkey soup with okra and crispy pigs ears, Appalachian Paella, Anson Mills grits, and cornbread made the way it should be: savory and grainy, not sweet and soft like cake.

Came here with my bf on a Wednesday afternoon. Cafe was clean and modern. Very cute decor too. 

My bf had a mocha with almond milk (he wanted it with soy milk but they didn't had any) while I had an americano. His mocha didn't taste that good because we could barely taste any coffee and chocolate in it. I think the almond milk overpowered it. I would recommend just having it as is but since my bf is lactose intolerant, he had no choice. 

As for the dessert part, we shared a coconut mango cake which actually looked like a mini coconut (so cute!) and a macchiato cake. The coconut mango cake had a dark chocolate shell that held a coconut mousse, vanilla sponge cake and coconut water jelly inside, and on top was fresh chopped up mangoes. It was light and refreshing, and not too sweet. My bf really liked this one. I, however, really liked the macchiato cake because I love chocolate and coffee. The macchiato cake was a flourless chocolate cake with a coffee ganache, praline crunch, white chocolate mousse and caramel cream. It was rich and moist, and it wasn't too sweet because the coffee ganache was slightly bitter. 

Overall, staff was super friendly and place was inviting. The cakes were appetizing and delicious but they were quite pricey especially the coconut one because it was quite small. However, I will definitely come back to try the rest of their desserts (just occasionally). Also, I want to try their Afternoon High Tea because it looks so cute!

Best iced coffee; french bread rolls made from scratch; cakes with fruit flavor baked into them; pastelitos that are huge and filled with fresh ingredients and seasoning; giant muffins; homemade chocolate chip cookies; and best of all they offer everything at a low price-such a deal-with a smile and meeting your requests in any way possible. Love them. If you haven't been, it is truly a hidden gem and you need to try to get over there as soon as you can to taste and see the cozy, inviting Brazilian and bakery, healthy fare!

Davio's was hands down one of the best restaurants I have been to. It was my boyfriend & I six years anniversary and we wanted to go somewhere high end... and I'm so glad to came across this place. For appetizer, we had an order of Kobe Meatballs & Rockefeller Oysters which was the best I have ever had!! For entree, I had the bolognese pasta & my boyfriend had the lobster risotto which was both amazing. To finish off, we had Chocolate chip banana bread pudding with coconut ice cream. Needless to say, best dinner I have ever had at a restaurant. I really love the atmosphere and the customer service was great. I definitely would come back again and it was so worth every penny.

Maybe I don't know any better, but I really like the tangsuyuk that they have here. I always get the beef, but I keep getting told that the pork should definitely be tried. I'm also quite fond of their kimchi pancake and I like how when I ask for kimchi on the side to go, they give me a couple different kinds. I mostly get takeout so I can't comment on ambiance, but the hostess is always super nice to me and is patient and helpful when I ask for help or have questions about certain things on the menu. They also give a pretty decent amount of food that usually lasts me at least two meals if I'm stuffing myself to the brim.

I can't comment on authenticity because I honestly don't know if the food is supposed to taste the way it does, but it tastes good so I'll just continue ordering from here.

I really enjoyed dinner here. I ordered lamb with two sides. The lamb was tender, a little bit fatty, but overall had great flavor! I love the seasoning. I got the cabbage and split peas as my sides. Both were great. The cabbage was my favorite. I enjoyed the injera as well. The table next to me ordered collards and lentils as sides and they looked great, I think I'll have to go back and try them for sure. The service was quick. When the server made a mistake on our check, she was quick to fix it. The downstairs dining area was a bit tight, we sat at a small table nudged in a corner. But there are also an upstairs dining area and a patio.

I went fishing for springers with a Eastfork Outfitters and had a great time! Within ten minutes of putting our rods in the water we hooked up on a fish- I had never caught a salmon before and it was awesome! What a thrill! Before the day was through we wound up catching one more. What a day! Even if we hadn't caught any fish it still would have been a great day- Captain Matt is a great guide and made the day so much fun! He is a real professional and super personable. The boat was really nice too- very clean and comfortable! I highly recommend Eastfork Outfitters for a great time on the water! Thanks Captain Matt for the awesome experience!

I'm glad there is a vegetarian restaurant so close to my home and was encouraged by so many positive reviews. Sadly, my experience was not what I expected. Although the cook seems to know his/her craft, the menu failed to warn how spicy the chipotle sauce on the veggie fish tacos would be. Also, the menu said there was a, "slaw," on the tacos. All I got was lettuce and what seemed to be mayo w/chipotle powder. There was a tiny cup of tomatoes, cilantro & lemon juice, but I think that more a salsa than a slaw. 

It was 2 small soft tacos. No side. For $8+, I thought I'd have gotten a bit more. The bowl of chili, much lower priced, would have been a better choice, IMO. The unexpected spiciness upset my stomach for hours afterward. Also, the restroom sink barely trickled water and gave the impression of uncleanliness. I wanted to give a better rating but the menu needs to be more accurate. This is a serious issue. If people don't get what they expect as per the menu, they tend to suffer buyer's remorse.

"Every time I go to Trader Joe's (TJ's), I think it's going to be expensive. I expect to pay an arm and a leg for my kosher steak, or my veggie sticks, or my fruit shoeleather stuff, or whatnot (lots of whatnot).

But when I leave, the bill rarely ever comes to more than $50, which is a lot less than I pay at Shaw's, a grocery store that claims to *want* to save you money.

So TJ's is ... TJ's. It's a nicely-kept store, with semi-friendly staff (they do have their occasionally surly moments, like when "Shep" told me he wasn't feeling well but they wouldn't let him take the day off.... thanks, Shep, really inspiring confidence in me there), and a great selection of products you really won't find anywhere else. I love their trail mix, frozen foods, and corn salsa, which is the best salsa I've ever had (I'm a sucker for corn). You won't lose weight shopping here, and you won't be helping the environment like with Whole Foods, but you'll save money and enjoy your time there."

At first you might think, a spa for your dog? I don't even go to the spa for myself so the idea of a dog spa to me seems preposterous.

When we originally came here it was not for their spa service. They have a full holistic veterinary service that came recommended by my (and Casey's) favourite dog daycare Canine Corner. This is when we discovered their 20' x 9' pool.

Ok I admit, I'm interested now. You see Casey is the kind of dog that is not a natural swimmer, it would be really nice to play fetch with him in water. Right away I booked an appointment to go for a swim 

So for the first session we start by letting Casey run around the establishment, getting used to the place. A lot of sniffing, rolling and tail wagging.

We then move to the pool area and the instructor does her magic and slowly introduces Casey to the water as he is a little timid to go in. After 15 minutes of work Casey is now swimming all around the pool going after different toys. After lots of swimming Casey was towel dried then went to mad little sprints around the pool - that's one happy dog.

For our next session I will be jumping in the pool with Casey as you can have a private swim with your pet in a comfortable safe environment. I don't have to worry about him running way, and I don't have to freeze my a** off in a cold lake.

So if you are looking for something different to do with your dog I highly recommend this, especially if you are interested in introducing your dog in to water. The people there have a passion for dogs and it shows, you will be left with one very tired, happy hound when you come home.

Ken's Artisan Bakery was seriously one of my favorite food stops in Portland! In fact, so much so that I went back the next day. 

Unfortunately, the second time, I picked up a pastry that had a hair baked into it. I didn't notice until much later after we had already left. Since we were still in the city, I went back to return it, and they apologized and offered me another pastry and coffee on the house (they actually offered more, but I declined). 

Even with that incident, I'm still giving them 5 stars because the pastries were really tasty and the staff were sweet. So you know, it had to be pretty good.

Things I tried: apple tart, lemon meringue tart, Oregon croissant, apple croissant, and herb goat cheese with leeks croissant. 

The tarts were AMAZING. The apples in the apple tart tasted sweet, crisp, and fresh, and the tart and custard were absolutely scrumptious. The lemon meringue tart was tangy, creamy, and just the right amount of sweet. 

The croissants were great too. They were all flaky, buttery, and delicious. I loved the fresh mix of berries in the Oregon croissant, and the savory croissant was flavorful and good even the next day!

Definitely add Ken's bakery to your list if you are a fan of pastries/dessert!

The guys here are knowledgeable and polite to a vaping newbie like myself. Not pretentious/douchey.

They have a wide selection of juices and the staff knows all about the companies they carry. They will fix your vape if you bring it in and it's fixable. They will let you try whatever you want on the menu, so you know you'll like what you get.

One thing I dig is the rewards program - every time you purchase something, you swipe your rewards card. Once you get to a certain number of points you get either a house or premium juice for free.

I enjoy going in here, and I'll continue to support this business.

Very convenient location at the top of City Square mall a block from the City Broadway skytrain, and validated parking under the mall also (2 hours free). We came here on father's day weekend after Dynasty Seafood turned out to be booked full already. Staff were friendly and the restaurant is roomy and clean. The dim sum selection was a little small but what we had was mostly delicious. The deep fried squid (not listed on the dim sum menu, but available separately) was the best I've had in Vancouver so far, better than Dynasty's. The shrimp seafood rolls were a bit tasteless however, and the rib with squash was unfortunately pretty oily and not a lot of actual meat. Overall it was ok, but you'd have to learn over time which dishes are great and which to avoid.  I might come again if I'm in the area or if Dynasty is full again, but probably won't go out of my way to repeat.

One of the worst customer service experiences I've had in my life. 

The employees scowled at me as soon as I stepped in the door. (Yes, I know I don't look like your typical customer from the get-go.)

When I started asking questions about their nose rings, the girl helping me was insanely condescending. As though me looking typical, meant I was stupid, or not worth helping.

A small sample from our conversation went something like:

Me: So, those nose rings, where the thickness goes from smaller to bigger, will that gauge out my nose hole? 

Metro Staff (said with disgust, and like I was incompetent): Gauge!?!? You mean ... S-T-R-etch?

Me: Sure! Stretch. Sorry, I'm not sure about the lingo. 

Metro Staff: I don't know. It depends. 

Me: That makes sense. What's the smallest size of ring you have? I don't wear stuff often, and the hole is small. 

Metro: You mean what's the gauge? Are you asking what the GAUGE of the ring is?Because the size of the ring, is called a GAY-JUH. 

(Said with scowling, and condescension.)

I will never be going back.

Wow what a difference a good doctor makes!!! Make that two good doctors in one place!!! All I can say is don't be afraid if you have a skin issue of any kind dr Mamalak and dr Hansen will talk you through it and get it resolved!!  There aren't many doctors that can remove scars by subsicion and juvederm !!! In one week scars were filling in and I was feeling better about my face !!  thanks to these wonderful highly educated and caring doctors I can walk with head high !! Nothing is pushed on you. You decide what you want and when you want it. I'm going back to have more issues fixed now that l feel confident I have the best doctors.

This was so disappointing! I am only in Atlanta for a few days, so I doubt that I'll ever be able to get a chance to allow Noodle to redeem this experience, but nonetheless. I love Pho, it's amazing, it makes my rainy days sunny, and my tastebuds jump for joy. Pho is one of those foods that you go out with once, maybe it's a blind date, you're not sure where this will lead going in. By the end of the meal, you're planning to introduce the family, ring shopping, and planning out the rest of your life together. Pho is dependable, trustworthy, or so I thought. The Pho I had tonight? Not even worthy of finishing the date. The lack of flavor was sad, to say the least, and the unfortunate pile of shredded meat and meatball that masqueraded as meatballs, brisket, and flank hurt my feelings, quite frankly. Thankfully the seaweed salad was just enough to keep my tears at bay. So long, Noodle Midtown, I won't miss you when I go home.

So it has been relatively difficult for me to find good Israeli food and well, this place is really good, not just good. Being from LA generally have my pick of delicious food and beverage options including a few delicious Israeli restaurants. Still, this new place in Portland was good enough for me to come write a Yelp review about it.

I didn't get a chance to sample too many of their options but got their namesake dish (kind of a small combo plate of veggie options). The falafel was the centerpiece of the plate and boy was it good. Perfectly crisp outside with a wonderfully soft and well textured and flavorful center.  The labneh and hummus were delicious and went well when combined with the falafel and their pita. One really great thing in this case was the pita... soft and pillowy (homemade?) unlike what you're likely to normally find in a Mediterranean restaurant. Washed all of this down with a delicious steaming hot pot of Turkish coffee. Yum!

The service here is not to great but I think its partly because of the language barrier. But our server didn't check on us enough, we ran out of drinks and waited a
while before she came back to get us more. It would have been understandable if they where super busy but there was only two other people there. When we were done with a dish they didn't take it off our table! We had an appetizer first and I really liked it but my husband didn't, and he is of Asian decent. When we finished that they brought our main dish and didn't take the appetizer plate back with them! What the heck?! Who does that.... No restaurant I've ever been to. It was a nice quiet dinner though.

My husband didn't like it at all but I did like the pan fried dumplings and the pork fried rice. The soup was a little strange but still ok. I don't know if I would go back I don't think it was really worth it. I may order out with something different and see how that goes.

A very cozy and warm spot.  We got up late for breakfast and arrived just when the sign was turning closed.  The owner welcomed us in and served us with a smile.  I ordered a steak and cheese (the most amazing sandwich I have ever had!) the meat tasted like it was marinated for hours, velvety smooth cheese, and the bread tasted like it just came out of the oven.  My cousin ordered the chicken noodle soup and a slice of quiche lorraine.  Everything is made from scratch, just like the way grandma used to make.  It's hard to believe this place is in Watertown.  Buy a loaf of bread to take home, you won't be disappointed.  My only gripe, the coffee is barely drinkable; order some tea instead.

The food and service was more than expected. The wait staff was kind and knowledgeable. The food was served on time and was cooked as I wanted it. 

The scallops where amazing and the Gnocchi and Duck  equally as yummy. We had a bottle of great Cab, ( I believe) which was served by a very knowledgeable and welcoming waiter. My friends and I completely gorged ourselves.  The best part aside from the food is the wine list which offers 40 something bottles at $26 a pop. I love it and can't wait to go back.

Gregg,

Did you ever review a place and want to give it 4 or 5 stars, but have some seemingly minor hang-up completely kibosh the whole thing?  Well, for me, Johnson Drug is that review.

In May my wife and I had our first child.  K needed some prescriptions filled and we needed a few things to help take care of our baby who was in the NICU at the time.

At the time, I was in Pharmacy nirvana. They quickly filled my prescriptions and they had all the mother and baby gear we needed.  To make things easy, I even brought in insurance contact information and details on coverage for medical devices.  When I picked everything up I was a little disconcerted to have a $200 invoice, but as I had brought in REAMS of paperwork I figured it was just my deductible.

Fast forward...turns out they overcharged me.  This wouldn't be a big deal, but everything was paid for with Flex spending and getting the credit back was a nightmare. 

The mess all began with a careless mistake and hang-ups with the credit were compounded by additional mistakes.  All in all, we have spent a vast amount of time trying to clear all this up.

Johnson seemed like it might have been a great place for friendly staff, quick pharmacy services, and a enormous selection of alternative health care items, but their attention to detail, and I would have to deduce, their ability to listen to their customers is abysmal.  I'm not sure I'm willing to give them another shot.

I really enjoyed this place! My first time trying real Korean food and it was a pleasant experience. We got the pork rib soup, sweet and spicy fried chicken, and dubokke. The pork rib soup was rich, has the perfect amount of spice, the pork fell right off the bone and was very tender, and the potatoes complemented it perfectly. The dubokke was definitely an interesting taste for me but I liked it a lot. The melted mozzarella on the cheese tasted awesome with the rice cakes, it was a good dish but probably not one I would order again. The sweet and spicy fried chicken was really awesome! The breading on it was perfectly fried and the sauce was not too spicy. It was served with radish, which according to the server is how Korean fried chicken is traditionally eaten and it reset the pallet well. My only complaint is the menu is a little more pricy than most typical asian places, but it's worth it for the food and the experience. They also play k-pop in there quite loud, which may be annoying if you're looking for a quiet night out.

This is by far my favorite bakery in orlando. I have consistently been going to Mecatos since they opened. 

The quality of all the items are excellent, very consistent and a lot of traditional Colombian and Venezuelan items such as empanadas an tequeños.

Their coffee is absolutely amazing, it is made fresh from their espresso machine using freshly ground beans. 

Only downside of this place is that it has gained a lot of popularity and can be busy at times, however the food is definitely worth the wait.

Visiting Vancouver, saw this close by to our hotel, kids ordered kids chicken pho
husband had the #8 pho chicken, chicken ball and quail eggs (but it only cane with one egg), I had the Cambodian style pho.  Generous with their veggie garnish, also fresh.  Good lean slices of chicken in all the pho.  Quail egg was good.  Cambodian pho was flavorful, but very salty and had definite MSG in it.  My tongue is a bit swollen feeling from salt overload, but I would come back another day and try their vermicelli.  Overall grateful they are nearby!

It has been several years since we dined here so , on a whim, we decided to check them out for dinner.  Not sure if there has been a change in their food supplier / chef but our meal was highly disappointing and not worth the $$$$ we paid. 

We started with the kimchi and green onion pancake to share. It was paper thin and fell apart upon serving from the dish.  So I'm wondering if it needed more time to cook and they were just in a rush to get it out. It was just ok.  For my entrée, I ordered my usual Chicken Bulgogi which comes out on a hot, steaming dish along with white rice and the small side veggie sides that accompany. One look at my dish and I could tell that the chicken was of a poor, cheap quality. As my husband commented, "It looked like mall food court quality."   It was dark ,random choppy pieces of chicken, some stringy and gristly(?).  Some pieces tasted off...I can't really describe . And the spices added to it just made it seem like they were covering up the bad taste of the chicken. It was just way too salty and unappetizing.  I actually had plenty of leftovers and didn't even want to pack up to bring home since I knew it wouldn't be touched. It was that bad.   My husband had the Stone Pot Bibim Bap dish with red meat and he said it was bland and lacked flavor and spice. He had to add some of the sauce from the red bottle on our table to enhance the flavor.   So, as you can imagine, it was a pretty disappointing meal. 

Another thing that was a little annoying was that any loud noise in the restaurant essentially echoed. They either need some major insulation in that restaurant or more furniture to fill up the space . Any loud noise was magnified by 3.  There was a family with a young child screaming randomly which echoed throughout the restaurant. Not my idea of a pleasant dinner experience. No thank you. 

Service was good and my rating is based solely on the food quality. This was a lesson learned that I should sometimes follow my gut and go with the places I'm used to and love ....a total "meh" experience.

This is my favorite Jamaican spot!! The flavors & the portions are to die for. I normally get the brown stew chicken with rice & peas & cabbage which is my favorite. After many times of eating here, I tried oxtails for the first time (ever) & it was *chef's kiss* !! I even had my boyfriend try & he said he loved it & it was the best he's ever had . The cook & cashier(s) are amazing as well! 

It's not hard to find; just go up the stairs on the sides (the stairs aren't lit so I normally go during the day)

I tried this nail salon with a friend, & left extremely disappointed on my first visit. I got a pedicure & a full acrylic set; my pedicure was mediocre & my nails were horrible. I paid extra for a longer stiletto shaped length, but I left with short nails that were almond shaped, although I was still charged extra for the length that I did not receive. Also, my nails were not shaped uniformly, & the acrylic was layed too thick, resulting in an ugly looking set. My friend got her nails done by a man named Daniel, who seems to be the best technician working here, & hers were very pretty & better shaped, so I told him that I'd come back in 2 weeks to have him (specifically) fix my set. This is the ONLY reason that I came back. I did show him my nails before I left & explained why I did not like them, to which he responded "everyone does nails differently here" with a shrug. On my second visit to the shop Daniel was not working that day, so a woman (his wife I believe) did my nails & a young boy did my pedicure. Again, my pedicure was mediocre at best, & my nails came out better than last time, but I still left disappointed. There is old polish from my last set that she left around my cuticles, just being lazy in removing it; it's noticeable because my current polish color is a soft neutral taupe shade & my last polish was hot pink. So I have hot pink rings around my cuticles that you can see. She did thin out the acrylic from being so thick & reshaped them into the stiletto shape that I'd originally asked for. My mother got a basic manicure & pedicure, & had to ask them to remove the excess nail polish (caked up) from around her cuticle bed after the manicure, from a sloppy polish job, & they acted like they had an attitude about it. All in all, I'd say that the customer service is poor, the work is lazy, & I will definitely not be returning; there are a million nail salons in Atlanta, save your money & go somewhere else!

Horrible experience. I took the car for the end of lease pre inspection, they said every thing was fine. Less than One week later when I returned the car, the guy who did the final inspection told us that the front bumper was damaged and it cost 400$ to repair! I was surprised to hear that because they didn't tell me in pre inspection and during these 6 days the car was in the garage! I understand that the first person might have missed it, but instead of apologizing, they were very rude about it, and talked to me with no respect and manners and even acted as if I was lying!! I didn't expect this kind of customer service from BMW. The way they treated me was very unprofessional and disrespectful. He could have said they were sorry that the first inspector missed the scratches on the bumper, and I would have accepted that and I was ok to pay whatever I had to, but why they should be so rude and impolite and raise their voice and threaten me that they would send it to a third party inspector and charge me more. Unbelievable unpleasant experience.

They are horrible!  They over sprayed my foundation, deck, roof, plants and anything in the way.  They even spayed my patio furniture.  They never used one tarp to cover anything,  It was on my windows and all over the screens.  They powerwashed after they had taped my windows. They made a poor attempt to cover only the sides of my windows leaving the middle wide open for my screens to be painted.  It was such a big mess I had to let them go after 2 days.  Never again.  They kept saying they would fix everything but I couldn't risk more damage.   Now I am stuck with painted screens I cannot fix.  I contacted them about this but you guessed it they never returned my call.  I just called 1-800-327-2468 and they give me  the owner in my area.  O.k. the best part is when they stirred the 5 gallon paint bucket with a sick they found in my backyard.  "Pro"  I don't think so.

I must admit, I had never heard of Boston Beer Works before my coworker suggested we go there. It seems to be some sort of known establishment that even sells t-shirts and souveniers. Who knew!

As for the food...Yummm sweet potato fries. Yummm. The portions here are HUGE. The nachos are this mountain of goodness that make you feel tiny in comparison. My coworkers and I ordered a bunch of appetizers before then ordering dinner. I had a blueberry beer which really didn't taste much like blueberries. Although, they do put actual blueberries into the beer! They seem to be dried blueberries that then plump up from the liquid. Anyway. I was so full of fried and overprocessed food that I felt like I was going to explode. I recommend going here and trying one of their home-brewed beers. They even make their own soda which may or may not be something special? 

Much better than any other sort of chain restaurant. It really does seem to be a chain though so don't go here expecting wonderful food. Go here for some original beers and outrageous food portions. AKA, bring your appetite and your beer-ppetite!

Would definitely recommend.  We needed a bathtub-to-shower conversion.  Ultra Services gave us a better solution for a much lower price than what the bigger companies offered.  Communication on scope and price was clear and consistent.  They always let us know when they would be coming--and then showed up exactly  as scheduled.  The workers were very polite and accommodating, and they did an excellent job keeping the jobsite clean, and removed tools and floor coverings each evening before leaving. Overall a very good experience.

TLDR: Fun Sunday dimsum with traditional carts in an interesting setting.  

The Empire Garden Restaurant inhabits an old theater which you can tell with it's high vaulted ceilings and art style around the walls.  It's got that chinatown feel to it, so part of the interior looks little run down and tacky, but it certainly is a unique place to eat.  The sunday dim sum features lady's walking around with their dim sum wares. As a non Mandarin/Cantonese speaker I really appreciated that the cart lady's could tell me in English if it was pork/beef/shrimp.  I also got a mixed drink off of their drink menu which was fairly solid.  I've been to several of the other dim sum places in the area and food wise this seemed pretty comparable.  Bathroom was also decently maintained.

I went to Cuba Libre for dinner while in Orlando on business.  The restaurant was conveniently located across the street from my hotel on International Dr.  Inside the restaurant the decor is really cool. There was  a big dance floor in the middle, so the place must be a cool dance club on the weekends.  
Let's get to the food.  I ordered the Seafood Paella. It had fish, shrimp, clams, squid, mussels, and rice in this potted hot dish.  It was soooo good that I still dream about it!  
I recommended the Seafood Paella to a few people and they went the next night and said it was amazing.  Treat yourself and go to Cuba Libre.

There are over 450 reviews of this place. I'm not sure that my own comments here will have a statistically significant meaning.

Highlights:

1. Outdoor dining in the flavor of a German beer garden -- very cool atmosphere.
2. Good selection of beer if you like that kind of thing.
3. Wonderful sausages.
4. Ping-pong!!!
5. Delicious fresh deli meats.

On my most recent visit, the service was somewhat spotty. Our tab ended up having a beer on it from the party adjacent to us on the long table. You should be sure to scrutinize your own check for merged bills.

The afformentioned merging of bills would normally have sent me into a coniption fit of trying to click less than one star on this review. What had counterbalanced this misdeed was that earlier in our visit, I had mentioned to the server how it turned out that I didn't like horseradish on my sandwich. I politely said I knew there would be horseradish on there per the menu description, but I didn't know what it would taste like and I asked for a pair of replacement bread slices so I could eat the remainder of my sandwich without the horseradish. I really didn't want to make any fuss since it was my own mistake of trying out something I wasn't sure of. The server dismissed my request for the bread and instead got me a whole fresh sandwich! That was so unexpected and appreciated.

I've been a Lucky 13 client since 2007 and for a bunch of very good reasons!

The first time I came in was right before my freshman year of college. I was growing out a cut and a dye job I had given myself (yikes) and wanted a real haircut to start school with. I was nervous about bringing my hacked-up hair to a real salon but the stylist who did my cut just chuckled at my story and told me about her own experiences cutting her hair. 

Over the years, I'm pretty sure I've had all of their services that apply to my hair and I've loved all of them. Full highlights, partial highlights, all-over color, bang trim, 5 inches off etc etc. All of their stylists are extremely versatile and can take care of you no matter what you need.

I've seen nearly everyone that works there but Tejay has been my go-to stylist since he started. He is really good at taking my vague instructions and tiny pictures on my iPhone and turning them into the exact haircut I was looking for. He's also talked me out of a few things that I thought I wanted, like layers in the front, to give me the overall look I was going for. He's amazing!

Only negative bit: I have had a couple experiences over the years where some stylists have taken off more than I wanted so if you are particular about the length, make sure you give exact instructions and bring a photo. 

Overall I love Lucky 13 and I look forward to every cut or service I get there!

I am a fan! Studio C is a good energy salon and tribe full of talent. 
Nikki is my hair and makeup artist. She created my vibrant purple hair style with tape in hair extensions that match my hair perfectly. She's an award winning designer who we took to California with us to do hair and makeup for our red carpet experience at the Grammy's. 
Nikki nails my makeup the first time, every time and I always love the way it looks.

I was disappointed with the limo experience that we had last night for a bachelorette party. Our driver seemed nice at first, and our first stop upon pickup was to fire and ice. However he brought us to the one in Boston instead of in Cambridge like was discussed in the signed contract. Instead of getting there for a 5pm reservation we got there at 5:40pm and almost had our reservation for dinner cancelled twice because of the time. This gave us a little over an hour to eat so we could rush to our next location, and with 25 people it was chaotic. I called the driver 10 minutes to 7pm to let him know that we were ready to be picked up at 7 and he did not answer. I called him again five minutes later and then texted him and said we were all done eating. I let another five minutes pass and then I called the phone number that connected me with the  limo company directly. I told him that I could not get into contact with the driver and asked if he could try giving him a call. I let another five or ten minutes go by before I tried calling the driver again and this time he did answer and he said he would be right there. Once he got us I asked him what happened and why he didn't answer his phone because of the time crunch we were in and he rudely responded "I don't text" to which I said that we called him 2 times prior. Because of this we were also late to our next nightclub. After we spent some time there we headed to the Donkey Show, but he brought us to the wrong location. This yet again made us late for another stop. We were all very disappointed in the lack of communication that was there and the fact that we were late to every event that we had planned for that night. My suggestions would be to give the driver the addresses to every location you plan on going too and what time you want to be dropped off/picked up. Also the limos AC was not really cold and we asked the driver if we had the controls set right and he said the more the limo drives around the cooler it will get but that didn't seem to be the case and we kept the windows down the entire time.

Mediocre for ramen. I ordered a Paitan Chicken, came with (1) half soft boiled eggs, 4 slices of bamboo, and literally 2 small pieces of fried chicken! Chicken were salty but indeed does well with their broth since it was bland and buttery. Noodles were still too hard to chew (can't blame them since the line was hella long). They put boatloads of noodles so that you can feel full fast as well, a big plus on that . Hopefully they will evolve and improve overtime for my next visit! Oh yeah, y'all gotta try it since I already finished the bowl before I even realize to take a picture for reviews!

I came here to get my eyelash extensions taken off. I had never had extensions before, and a different salon completely botched them. They hurt, and the look was awful. I called the lash lounge and explained that I had just had them put on and they were so sweet to schedule me to remove them for the next morning. Camille was very gentle taking them off, and she also dyed my blonde eyelashes to brown and then permed them. They turned out fantastic  I absolutely love them, and will definitely be a returning customer!

Just not my scene.  A Live Oak Hefe on tap is $6.50, which is higher than average, and it just doesn't feel very Austiny.  Wait staff was pleasant and efficient even though they were pretty busy for a Tuesday.  I might have liked it more if there weren't multiple smokers on the patio near me, blech.  Probably a place I would have liked in college or if I was single, but not for me at this point in my life. I'm kind of shocked how much business they were doing on a random Tuesday, so clearly there is a market for what they are selling.

My personal experience here has always been positive. 
I went here looking for a particular item for my fuel band and I approached a young man that worked there and asked him about the item.

He told me he would be right back and came back with the item. The item I was looking for I don't think they sold but the guy had an extra one and gave it to me.

I was super happy about that, I felt like that was my blessing for that day...

Everytime I have visited this location I have had a good experience.I've never had any problems or issues here personally. Customer service here is great and all the employees are pretty friendly.

This Nike store is pretty spacious and has more than one floor so If you're looking for something sporty you should be able to find it here. Check them out, at least once..they are right across from Sprinkles the cupcake place so why not right?

The nightlife here is usually pretty fun--live band and dancing up top makes for a good time.  The brunch, however, left something to be desired.  The Bloody Mary bar left even more to be desired.  The food was fine, nothing special or horrible.  The Mary bar didn't have olives.  I'll repeat.  Did not have olives.  They also had some pretty crappy mixes, and it was just really disappointing (especially for the price).  They do have lots of different hot sauces, though, to end on a positive note ;)

I've been getting massages here for several months now and every time is amazing. From the friendly, courteous staff to the amazing atmosphere there isn't one thing to dislike about Massage Sway. 
They offer wine, hot tea or water while you wait in the relaxing waiting area full of comfortable furniture and gentle, low lighting. There are also snacks!
The one time there was a booking error, they worked with me to still get me in that same day. 
Do yourself a favor, become a member and visit as often as you need. They are wonderful.

Sad days at Fisherman's. This spot has been circling the drain for years but my visit today will be my last. They've got 3 dudes over 70 working in their gun department today and not one of them has any interest in selling a pistol. I was absolutely THERE TO BUY TODAY!! 2 of the 3 were showing some other relic a shotgun he had zero intention of buying and any of my questions were instantly dismissed and cut short.  Obviously I was a bother to their retirement job. Somebody needs to wake up over there or I give your store 1 year before there's plywood over the windows. 
1 motivated sales person could easily handle that department and actually get some work done.

4 Stars because they forgot to serve me the Clam Chowder and had to get up and remind them about the missing food item.

I have been searching for a few years in and out for the Best Lobster Rolls due to I never ate one but only seen pics on social media. Florida is known for seafood and fresh catch from the ocean and I lately started to research again after eating lobster rolls at Seaworld's Seven Seas Food Festival.

So this place is a hidden gem of the locals for fresh seafood especially lobster! So of course when you eat at a place you order what they are known or famous for.

This eatery is located on OBT across the street from goodwill and publix plaza on Premier Rd. Its really a hidden location!

Once you see a crowd on your left side eating outside on red tables and umbrellas - you found the spot! I got kind of excited when I saw the crowds because it shows this place is good!! 

I saw their parked delivery trucks heading out on their way to do local deliveries to your famous restaurants and markets and after I parked; A line was formed on both sides. Left side is fresh seafood purchases and right is hot Lunch purchases. I was here for the Lobster Roll $10.95 and after hearing raves on the Clam Chowder for $3.95 I say why not? Sweet Tea with FREE REFILLS is $1.99. 

The eating area is ONLY the outside area - Which is not bad if it does not rain or very hot. You order your food and pay .. They will give you a number stand and place it on the table you are seating at. 

Once you find your seating area - You wait while they freshly prepare your hot lunch. The wait was about 5-15 mins. This is a good time to do selfies, snapchat or ig stories! 

They delivered my lobster roll lunch and I opened the bag and noticed the clam chowder was not placed with my order. I quickly got up and had to go in between lunch line and remind them about the missing clam chowder. No apology from that. Since I was near the beverage area I also requested another refill of the sweet tea. The sweet tea is pretty good, Reminded me of WOODSBYS sweet tea. Nice brew and right amount of sweetness.

The food; The Lobster Roll is packed in a black heavy duty styrofoam take out box lined inside is parchment paper liner witha wedge of lemon; slightly crunchy fries seasoned with salt (you can see the salt speckles), and the lobster roll. The lobster roll is not big or tiny, depending how big your hand is - To me it was the size of the tip of my pinky to the end of my palm. The amount of lobster salad was ok not much not little but I did see bread spots on my roll meaning it wasn't fully packed in or was not enough lobster salad? Either way there were CHUNKS of LOBSTER in it! The bread is def a original lobster roll bread - golden toasted with some grease perhaps butter? The mayo and tiny bits of celery did not overpower the sweet chunks of lobster meat. It was perfect to me tasted more of the lobster than the mayo or celery. The splash of lemon juice on top of the lobster added umph to my lobster roll! 

The Clam Chowder was chunky and I mean CHUNKY! It was the right amount of thickness as far as soup base and perfect seasonings with lots of clams and I noticed 1-2 bits of potato which is a good thing; Not here to pay for potato chowder.. I want clams I got tons of it! This came with chowder oyster crackers and eating this kind of filled me up and I only end up eating 1/2 of my lobster roll! 

The Sweet Tea was delicious! The right about of brew and sweetness..

I will def come back again and try the Whole Steamed Lobsters, The lobster bisque, Fried Belly Clams - Along with the clam chowder and lobster roll! 

Mouth watering just thinking about my next visits to this place!

Definitely a local favorite and Now I know why!!

I don't know if I trust the direction this place is going.  They have a huge sign in front that says "support local businesses" as if they are family owned - from my understanding, they were bought out by a corporation a few years ago, which leads me to my next point. I noticed that they were marking the prices up on almost everything in the store that was not broken or actually usable in some way.  These things were donated and sometimes the prices of what the  item actually cost originally was still on the box (but the items were previously opened and used 'as expected') however, the price of the item at Goodwill was the same or even slightly higher in some cases.   This is what happens when large corporations get involved- this place is suppose to support families in need, but now it's just another target or wal mart.  :/ I attached an image of an example of this.   My advice: go to Salvation Army instead. Donate your belongings to them or other real local businesses and thrift stores.

I've been to Kula many times and loved it. Great concept and variety and reasonably priced. The conveyer belt is always stocked and loaded and you can just grab anything and everything that comes by. I've told all my friends about it. But today, on a Friday afternoon I came in with 4 friends who were there for the first time and excited to check it out. However, at 3:30 they didn't have anything coming thru on the conveyer and we were forced to order everything off the menu instead, which took much longer and defeated the purpose of impressing my friends with the revolving  sushi concept. VERY DISAPPOINTED.

I've been a regular patient of Dr. Cain's for 5 years now and I absolutely love him. He's extremely thorough, very knowledgeable, and overall just the best. A couple of years ago I was having daily headaches and I mentioned it to him during one of my visits. He ordered an MRI and we found some cysts in my sinus cavities, including my sphenoid cavity which was probably the cause of the headaches. He referred me to an ENT, that doctor tried some antibiotics but we ultimately had to do surgery. No more headaches thanks to Dr. Cain catching that! I highly recommend him!

Wow. I have never taken this many pictures inside of a restaurant before but I would have regretted it if I didn't document my time here. They have a few special seating in the restaurant but you probably have to reserve it a few days before, but what it entails is you and your party sit on the floor but on a bunch of beautifully tailored pillows without your shoes, makes it pretty authentic to say the least. I felt like I was eating in a museum, it was quite an experience.

It was distracting to make a decision with all the art surrounding but ultimately it was the Spicy Chicken Indonesian Peanut Noodle. The noodles were soft, the chicken was perfect, and the peanut sauce tasted sour and sweet at the same time, which perfectly complimented the rest of the meal. The service was pleasant. They were attentive to us even though the restaurant was packed.

 This compliment is mild compared to tea they offered. We ordered the blueberry tea and another flavored tea I forgot the name of but they were so refreshing. Taking a sip made me feel all good inside, like a quarantine kind of feeling. Even the leaves tasted good, yes I eat tea leaves occasionally.. but the point is my friend who goes to University of Colorado-Boulder picked this as his favorite place and I'm glad I trust his opinions.

wow, poor reviews spot on. great location, layout, swim facilities. just very, very, poorly managed. swim center jacuzzi down every 4 weeks or so. each time: know when it'll  be fixed?  "I dunno, i think they have to order a part". This has been going on for YEARS.  No hot water (never water pressure) from swim center showers today?  Once got berated by a towel laundry girl for not checking in at front desk.  Must be a nepitism issue with this place. Just so lacidaisical. Hope this place can stay afloat and IMPROVE to deliver value.... notwithstanding absentee ownership, leadership, management of facilities.

Know what you need and where to find it because no one here is going to help you. The store is large in scale, much needed in the area now that Sports Authority has closed it's doors. Located in the Crosslands shopping center next to a Party City. Ample parking, good amount of handicapped spots. The store carries just about everything you could think of. Lots of college shirts and etc. Nice UCF stuff. Prices are reasonable here. The big problem and I do mean BIG is employees. You can never find one when you need help. Or a register open. I found six employees altogether working in the front of the store(maybe there were more in back) 4 were in the gun section, one was on a register and the other was behind the customer service desk. No one was anywhere near the back of the store let alone in the sneaker section. After the line was 8 people deep, the customer service person called the people from the register over to help. I was next in line to go to the customer service desk but because I was in a wheelchair the person behind me run up to that desk. REALLY! Either way this store lacks the number of employees to properly run the way it should. After all, I will go back because the merchandise is good but I do plan on knowing what I what and exactly where ti find it. Store was very clean and appeared organized.

In the category of small, family-run, asian food markets, First Oriental is about as good as it gets. I love this place - I've been a customer for many years. 

Run by a Lao family, you'll always get a friendly greeting. I often just like to browse the aisles, they have so much interesting stuff. But sometimes I need something specific such as today's purchase of a new wok utensil (my old one is experiencing metal failure after years of service). While I was there, I picked up a new supply of Sichuan peppercorns and dried mushrooms.

As others have mentioned, it's a bit of a cluster inside. But one thing I can say is that once you figure out their organization, you're good for years. It has changed very little over the 10+ years I've been a customer.

Plenty of kitchen utensils, bowls, and the like, although you may have to search a bit because you'll have options. Not much in the way of fresh groceries, but they do have frozen goods. 

Easy parking in their private lot.

Great lunch spot and their BBQ sauce kicks butt!

-deviled eggs: very good but I personally did not like the fish roe. I think that's a personal choice though
-cheese dip: hard to steer wrong with something like this
-meats!!!: brisket sammy- sooooooo good. Brisket- fatty piece kicked butt and the non-fatty was just OK
-collard greens- meh...needed salt
-French fries- really good! Couldn't stop eating them
-fried green tomatoes with crab meat. I really enjoyed the flavor and the lightly fried tomatoes but the crab meat was very meager. I felt like I got the tiniest amount and wanted more. Probably the main reason I knocked off a star.

Good drinks and atmosphere! Would recommend and certainly return.

Four stars for food, service and ambiance.  Good wine list, patio seating, yellow walls (which seem to automatically make me love places, don't know why), yummy sangria, GREAT chocolate pudding desert which was really more like a mousse, really excellent queso and chorizo...

Which would earn it five stars except WOW, PRICES!  When I first looked at the menu I thought it would actually be really affordable, and having a friend who's never had tapas and who I was trying to impress, and both of us trying to stay on a budget, I brought him there and one other person.  We saw two groups of food: small dishes that started in the 4 or 5 $ range, and large dishes that went from $8 to more than $20.  I assumed that the first range was tapas and the second range was main courses...Only to learn when the food came that the HIGH range items were traditional tapas dishes and that the low range items were itty bitty portions that each fit on one slice of bread.  $5 for bread with a piece of sausage on it?  Yeah, maybe if it's a SANDWICH.  We ordered 4 items from the low-priced side and one item from the high priced side expecting it to be plenty for 3 people, but after seeing the portions I would question whether or not it's enough for 2.  Thank God for free bread.

And for the Dunkin Donuts across the street where we went for delicious personal pizzas at $2.99 a pop afterwards :D

Honestly, I'm used to being able to get large tapas plates for less than $10 and meal sized dishes for $20 at a tapas joint no problem.  This befuddled me.

Though kudos for having a squid ink rice thing.  Squid ink is delicious and unfortunately I did not get to try it here as my friend is a wimp, but it's cool nonetheless.

Very Great place run by a very nice man and his wife.

Been going there for over a year and have never been disappointed. I get them to wash and fold my laundry and it is always clean and folded with pride.

By evaluating the cleanliness of this place compared to other laundry mats in South Burnaby, you can really tell that these people take pride in their business. They are always friendly and happy to help you no matter how rushed you are or how much laundry you have for them. 

It's a pleasure to deal with these people.

I don't generally leave reviews but felt I should warn people about this place. Please DO NOT go here! I went over a month ago for a simple pedicure and I now have a horrific infection underneath my big toe nail. I had to go twice to urgent care. I went through one of the most painful procedures (which included a drill, four needles and a scalpel). Now I can't wear sandals all summer without grossing people out. After asking around I've heard this has happened to other people. Go somewhere else for your nails. Nail Talk Brookhaven is not worth the risk.

I refuse to shop at Walmart unless its my only option and I must say this is one of the worst ones. No matter when you go there is at least a 15 minute wait to check out. I opted to try the self check out and the lady working had to fix every register after every item scanned every time because something was wrong with the system. Very unorganized, although most walmarts are. This location has some of the rudest, well I won't say people both employee and customer.

Came in with a few friends for dinner on a Friday night hoping for a quick bite. We got in early, and were seated right away before the restaurant got busy. 
Our 'quick bite' turned into an hour and 45 minutes!
It was 15 minutes before any waitstaff approached our table to take a drink order after we had been seated, to the point where we thought they never told the waitress that we had come in. 
This is the way it went throughout the night. Even leaving was difficult as it took about 25 minutes to get the check, hand over our credit cards, get them back and sign the receipt. 
This is no exaggeration either. The slow service had become so laughable that we actually started using a stop watch on our phones.
I would avoid this place like the plague.

This is a second-hand review, so accept it for what it is.

My Director had a small dinner party at his house; the main food was barbeque from Salt Lick.  But, there was one vegetarian in the group.  Our administrator picked up "vegetarian barbeque" at Mr. Natural.  She said it didn't look that great, but the report from the party was that it tasted absolutely wonderful and everyone loved it (the meat-eaters  just piled it on their plates alongside the brisket and sausage)..

So, if you're in a similar situation, this is something to consider.

A must do when visiting historic Winter Garden. Plant street Market is a one stop shop for all of your eating and drinking and buying needs. Coffee, brewery, loose leaf tea, butcher, sushi, wood Fire pizza, specialty gifts items and more. Support local business and definitely make a trip to the market if you're in the area. Live music on the patio outside of the Crooked Can Brewery on the weekends with pet friendly outside seating. Just steps away from the local farmers market on Saturdays which is one of my favorite weekend stops.

From flashlights to waterproof bags, I am always amazed of how the product does exactly what they are designed to do.   
Protecting electronics from the elements associated with boating has been a huge challenge for years.   Just a small amount of moisture can ruin a cell, sat phone, hand held gps, etc.   I do not know how these people designed a waterproof, air tight zipper, but they did, and I am happy to protect my gear.   Their flashlights on the other hand are second to none.    Keep designing great stuff NiteIze.

This place is a wonderful small venue to listen to some great live musicians. We were so close that we almost felt like part of the band. We were able to see so much detail while they played. I was truly impressed with the sound quality of the room and it was at the perfect volume and not too loud. Beer and wine along with soft drinks and water can be purchased and they have complimentary popcorn. There's something going on just about every night
so I'm sure you can find a musical band that suits your taste or open up your mind and try something different.

Let me first say that I have been working for Starbucks for over two years now.  I can say I know a thing or two about how cafe's run.  When I have a craving to go and get an ice coffee and decide to try the closest cafe to my house, Refuge Cafe was the one.

So how hard is it exactly to get an ice coffee for a customer after they've just paid you and tipped you a dollar (which is generous if you've ever worked in a cafe) ?  Apparently very difficult for the three people just leaning against the register and talking.  

Really guys?  the ice coffee dispenser is right next the register and not one of you can pour me a large ice coffee.  

Apparently at Refuge it takes five minutes for the one person working on bar to pick up a ticket and notice that there is one person waiting on an ice coffee where they promptly go and pour it for you.  

I can say that I'm never going back there again and most definitely not recommending it to anyone.  If you want good service and good coffee go to In House Cafe right down the road on Harvard Ave.  

I was seriously considering sticking my hand back in the tip jar and taking my dollar back.

Super fun and funky local spot where the menu matches the eclectic set up. A great, relaxed spot for lunch and dinner with live music and outdoor seating. It's a little off the beaten path, but that's a good thing as it adds to the atmosphere.

The BBQ on its own isn't the best in town (hit 4Rivers for that) but it's a great base for all of their unique and creative combos. Think jalapeño jams, beer cheese soup, fried onions, bacon, and blue cheese crumbles as just a few additions to a pulled pork sandwich. Plus, they have tons of other sandwiches, salads, "scooby snacks" and desserts on the menu. With lots of microbrews on tap, you'll leave with a full and satisfied belly. Bring your wallet with your appetite because it is a little pricey. 

Bottom line: Great overall experience with a funky atmosphere and funkier food combos. A fantastic local spot and hidden gem.

I really hate to do this because the people who worked here were friendly enough, but I made a big mistake using this place. 

Until now, I've never published a bad review. 
I've started writing bad reviews for places then stopped because I don't wanna act like an entitled douche bag (yeah, you know who you are you fucking asshole yelpers) 

but...

My phone absolutely sucks now. 

Basically, typing is a god damned nightmare. I'll hit one letter and another random letter gets selected. And then, every once in awhile, for no reason at all, all my apps start shaking, like I'm going to delete one, then whatever I do somehow deletes my messenger app. 

It sucks, big time. I'd rather just go back to a flip phone or some bullshit. 

So let this be a lesson. No, let it be two lessons. 

#1: Don't break your smart phone
#2: Don't do business with anyone who has a "z" in their name instead of an "s" 

If someone corrects me and says "No that's just how it goes whenever you get a screen replaced" then I'll change my review, but for the life of me I had to do this because my fucked up iphone is a nightmare that follows me every minute of every day and I don't wish this tragedy on anyone else.

Terrible service, including manager who does not have any customer service skills to train others.  All employees in this store look so unhappy to be there and hate human beings, It is hard to understand why they are working in the customer service industry. RITEAID down the street is bad service too, but this Walgreen makes them look ten times better. I live in the area over 15 years and never walked out of this store satisfied and happy. Today was my last straw. I will not go back there again.
