First time visiting Mamak and I don't know why I waited so long to try them out! I really enjoy tapas style dining and I was even more excited to see that Mamak follows that same style. 

My favorite item was their Sweet Potato Fries with sweet thai chili!!! I have no idea what the 5 spices are on these fries but just know they were amazing and SO addicting. The chicken lo mein, wings, Kari mee and golden wontons were good as well. However, I wasn't really a fan of the Wontons with hot sauce. I felt like it lacked a little flavor compared to the golden wontons. For the most part I tasted more peanut in the wontons with hot sauce than the actual spices. Not sure if it's meant to be that way but it wasn't what I expected.

Overall, great place! Our server was so nice and accommodating. Definitely have plans to visit again.

This restaurant was quite delicious. It has very many exceptional qualities! 

The inside of the restaurant was very clean and organized. The menu has a wide variety of smoothies and sandwiches that looked very yummy. I heard about the restaurant through a friend who said it was really good. The moment I walked in, the first thing that I noticed was that there were many people in there enjoying the food and that it was clean. I was greeted by smiling and happy employees once I began to place my order. 

The smoothie that I got was called mango magic and it tasted very tropical. It was amazing! The sandwich that I got along with it complimented it perfectly as any of the ones on the menu would. The sandwich that I ordered was very filling. 

I would definitely recommend this restaurant to anyone who is in town and looking for a quick bite to eat

We checked out a Disney Vacation Club booth in Hollywood Studios and ended up booking a tour at the Saratoga Springs Resort. We took the DVC van there and back and the staff were very nice. The only reason for a 3-star review is the FastPass+ they give you for attending the tour is only good for a total of three rides over a four day timespan. We were under the impression that we would have unlimited use of the FastPass over four days. When we discovered the misunderstanding at Disney's Magic Kingdom, guest relations gave us three more FastPass uses, which was awesome. DVC might want to word their gimmick a little better!

Oh my, should have read the ol' reviews on this one! When coming out to look at the job and ENSURE proper measurements and specs the salesman had a discussion with my installer and figured out the best course of action. Well, of course they messed up the order, despite spending a fair amount of time with the installer figuring it out, and just blew it off upon delivery. My contractor was not happy at the increased difficulty of installation and didn't really want to do it. I called Grand Openings and  figured they'd take a LITTLE responsibility. Wrong. Their installers wanted $3,600 to install 3 windows and a door. Which is just saying F you, get lost, which is exactly what I'll say when the next job comes around.

I have only eaten at two other indian speciality restaurants in my life and those were in New York. 

Therefore, I can certainly confess that I am not adequately equipped with Indian food knowledge to perfectly review this place. 

With that said..

I liked it! The two people I was with had been there numerous times and they ordered for me, unlike most high-class yelpers I sadly cannot remember AT ALL what my dish was called.. we were debating about the whole giving money to africa thing. 

In the end, I would love to go back to this establishment. Other than the food, the building and people were very welcoming.

Went there to sell a car. We were attended to right away, they inspected the car, did a carfax check on my car, took a test drive, finished the paperwork in a short time and also gave us a ride to the T-stop. It was literally "Cash for your car". I think we got a little under the private party book price but was worth not having the hassle of dealing with random people calling and taking the car out for a joyride. Very friendly people!

Didn't eat here because the manager was a clown. I have my wife and three little kids with me. We are on a road trip back up to NJ. My wife was still fixing some issues in the car and I wanted to get my kids situated. There aren't many spots that can seat 5. Unfortunately he told us we couldn't sit because we hadn't ordered yet. He continues to reprimand me as I tried to explain the situation to him. We walked out

Terrible Practice.  You can never get through to them.  You call and are put on hold by the automated system and you hold for anywhere from 5 to 7 minutes and then are disconnected.  Sometimes you will get a recording asking you to leave a message and telling you that you will receive a call back within 24 hours - you don't.  They also tell you to e-mail them.  This is useless since they do not respond.  To get them via phone or e-mail is next to impossible.  Also not pleased with doctor.  Told him I would not be taking a certain medication any longer.  He did not take it off of my patient information and instead called in a refill for it instead of calling in the medication that I do take.  Also did not remember any of my history,  I sat and discussed my history with him and then went back 4 weeks later and he remembered nothing.  Needless to say I have changed my primary care physician.  Would not continue with this practice if it were for free.

Good luck getting any service after they take your money. Milk your visits and take your time making decisions. Because once you select a gown and pay them, you will not get anymore help and the scams begin. 

I went to get my wedding dress in August. I was showered with attention and the whole 9. Everyone was soooo nice. Then I picked my dress and the upselling and being overbearing began. I said I would only get the dress and undergarments because I wanted to shop around for accessories since I found theirs to be overpriced & the collection slim. The manager ordered my sales person to tell me that if I bought my accessories with my dress THAT DAY and only that day I would save 20%. Except that you save 20% on your accessories anyway because it's part of their "incentives" for you to do all your shopping there. But I guess they had sales goals to meet that day so they had no qualms about being dishonest. I decided to overlook it because it was a petty thing to cancel a transaction over. 

The next sign was when I came to pick up the dress they didn't have my sketch. They promise you a sketch of your dress when it comes. It's even advertised in their fitting rooms. The lady said maybe the sketch got mixed up in the back but I could call the next day and she would look for it. I called a couple of times that week and she either wasn't there or she hadn't "found it yet". Eventually it wasn't hard to figure out she didn't look at all. 

I decided to ignore these 2 very small signs and go there with my mom for her MOB dress. As we picked out my mom's dress, I asked if I could set up an appointment to steam my dress. The store's assistant manager told me it would be $50. I said: "why would you charge me $50 to steam a dress!" 

AM: Because it's not part of the dress cost
Me: but you gave me a wrinkled dress in a bag 9 months before my wedding. Were you expecting me to wear it like this? Did you think all wrinkles would magically go away?
AM: no but it's part of alterations. It's free if you do alterations.
Me: I don't need alterations. 
AM: most people (IMPORTANT*). If you don't you have to pay to steam. 
Me: never mind

When we began talking to the store manager about ordering my mom's dress their pressure tactics began:

1) "dresses are taking 6 months to come in and you won't get it before your wedding if you don't pay for a rush order." There were 3 pieces to the dress and they charged for each separately although the dress comes together as one Lol.  (more than $90) 

2) "if you gain weight we can't let the dress out. So we advise you order it bigger than you are." This is where my conversation with the manager comes in. 

My mom's dress came within a month (3 months before the wedding) and it was huge! We spent over $100 taking the dress in and shortening it. Buying the dress in her size would have been perfectly fine but it wouldn't have yielded them any alteration money. 

Ultimately after all this trouble they gave us a clear plastic bag. It was so ridiculous looking and sloppy I asked if they had a different bag. They told us they would sell us a garment bag for $10. Again never mind. 

So in summary:
1) they lie about giving you special discounts if you buy everything on the spot. In reality the discounts are available from the time you buy your dress until 60 days after the wedding date on record. 

2) they will give you a wrinkled dress and ask that you pay them to steam it. 

3) they will size you and ask that you order your dress larger so they can have an opportunity to charge you for alterations.

4) Their accessory selection is slim and overpriced. 

5) they will nickel and dime you. 

I could have gotten crap treatment like that from David's bridal. At least it would be a bigger selection of gowns.

I cannot speak to the climbing, but I took an acroyoga class here with some friends! It was really fun and the two instructors were great! The reason I can't give it five stars is because it's pricey ($20 if you're a student, or $25 if you're not), AND it was super crowded. It was so crowded to the point where we definitely couldn't do certain things because of the limited space. I get that they want to allow as many people has possible take the class, but they need to move the max from 33 to more like 25. It would give students the room to actually breathe and move! I also wish it was more affordable, but because of the price, there's no way I'll be able to go very often. Overall though it was a positive experience!

Troy Prouty*

This place was wonderful.   3 pools open with long hours from 8am-10pm I believe and then the main pool/water park with lazy river and splash was just fantastic, could have spent all day there if not for my fair skin! You can order drinks and food poolside and have delivered to you, pretty good food and price is average. 
There is small arcade/mini golf. I wish we had seen the pay $15 for unlimited hour play since our $15 in tickets lasted about 15 minutes. 
The rooms are very nice, spacious enough for our 5 night stay. Beds and pillows and blankets are actually comfortable as I have hard time sleeping often in hotels. 
A couple complaints-I thought the resort fee was a one time thing not every night until I read someone else's review on here. That is really frustrating as I really tried to research that beforehand. Also the elevators are confusing. We bypassed them over and over going from our room as they are kind of hidden. Accidents happen but the fire alarm went off at 4am so that was super fun to be awoken by loud flashing lights and having to take our kids downstairs to check if the place was burning down. Lastly the shuttle to Disney doesn't leave until 9am, which the lay said basically puts you in the park around 10:30.  I would have loved to save $25 on parking and use that but not worth it to get such a late start after paying so much for Disney tickets. 
Overall a great stay. Close to Disney, great environment and would stay again.

I love love love this place. It is always always crowded, but the line moves pretty fast. There are seats to sit but as I said, the shop is always crowded so you'll be lucky to get a seat(and parking!)

I always get my canolis from here whenever I am in Boston and they are FABULOUS! If you want amazing canolis, come here!!! They have all different fillings from espresso to chocolate to mocha to the regular canoli filling! They have other desserts as well but I just come here for the canolis! 

Enjoy!

Calumet is close to my house, and I've used them for five years.  I started for my photo classes in grad school, and later I've rented from them for my business and bought gear from them.  I've finally had it.  For the past month I started using EP Levine in Waltham.  The difference is customer service is amazing.  AMAZING.  There were times at Calumet where I waited and waited and waited for someone to help me even though the store was empty.  There were so many times I called to check a rental status and received no calls back.  The staff behind the counter is consistently rude and condescending.  I've done so much business in the past and I will NEVER go back.  I'd rather rent a zipcar and drive to Waltham and give a local company who treats me well my money.

1. Bought a modem to replace the rental modem and hooked it up. To register my equipment they asked me to bring the modem in to a local office. When I showed up they took it away and said it belonged to them and I should not buy used equipment with their name on it.

2. My basic cable became encrypted today (they did not provide an adapter in advance) and asked to pay for broadcast HD content with $10/mo adapter or get a free SD adapter for 2 years (to watch down-scaled local channels). They blamed it on FCC analog to digital transition and said that some broadcast channels have left basic cable for digital cable packages. 

3. Canceled basic cable so they raised my internet service by $9/mo.

This is my favorite hot pot place in Orlando. The food is always fresh when I come here. There are special snow pea tips, watercress and other yummy asian vegetables. The beef, chicken and shrimp come on a revolving plate line of food that keeps on coming. All you can eat is $25.99. You pick a soup base, tomato is my go to because i like sweet, but if you like spicy, they put alot of red chili oil and peppers. The shrimp comes with head on so make sure not to cook too long and watch out bc it will be boiling hot when you peel it. The best part is picking your sauces. I like the sweet spicy orange sauce and the house special sauce. Also if you mention the Facebook ad, you get 10 percent off until the middle of November. Make sure to come here with an empty stomach. If there is anything you don't see, you can ask the waiter to bring it to you.

Update: drove all the way to Snappy tonight for what we considered to be the best ramen around only to find out the changed their menu "a few days ago". They now only offer gyoza and 4 or 5 types of ramen- all chicken based or vegetable. They got rid of all of their pork products and broth. Really disappointed about the changes and choices... we ended up leaving.  Very disappointing!

We are huge ramen fans and like to try different places. Snappy Kitchen did not disappoint. Parking situation was not great, on street and it took us 20 minutes to find a spot but once we were inside, it was great. The spicy ramen and the tan tan ramen both had great flavor. I don't love add ons when the price of the ramen is on the higher side but my husband and son got the soft egg and loved it. Noodles were straight noodles but had a good consistency. Pork was tender and tasty!  Definitely recommend trying.

The family and I love Waffle House but never tried to eat it in the go. This Waffle House made that possible!! The breakfast was still just as yummy as if we were eating it at the restaurant. They gave us more then enough condiments to make sure we didn't miss out on any toppings. They even gave me sugar for my grits and I forgot to ask for it. All I can say is yummy yum yum!!  Thank you Waffle House, for the great on the road experience.  They family is happy and full !!

Damatas is a great place in a pinch. When I'm hungry to lazy to cook and not wanting to spend $$$, Damatas is there. I steer clear of the sandwiches, I don't like the bread they use. The Bacon pizza is great, get a small its perfect for one person. Steak tip dinner, or the chicken parm are my other two stand-bys. The seating is nice, I like the fist tanks. This really isn't a gourmet place, but if your going cheap, you have a lot of choices around. I recommend Damatas, cheap pizza that's way better then that stuff they call pizza at domino's or pizza hut

This is my kind of fast food. Super fresh, amazing selection, and really friendly staff. My lunch go to is the BLTA (bacon, lettuce, tomato, avocado) for sure, but their grill makes a mean biscuit and gravy at breakfast. Wow! So huge, so tasty, so soul satisfying, and its only $4.50!!!  
Everything I have ever had from Elephants has been delicious. There are so many sandwiches/salads/tasty goodness, I am sure I will never be able to try them all... but darn it if I'm not going to try! 

Oh, and I can't forget about the Cowboy cookie. Get it, eat it, love it, repeat.

The quality of the bagels at Einstein's is always unquestioned, but the really big plus of this location is the high quality of customer service I've received in the last couple of days!

I met with some friends yesterday afternoon and decided I wanted a bagel. Unfortunately, because I went so late in the afternoon, they had no more Potato Bagels, which are my absolute favorite!

Thankfully, Kris, the assistant manager, let me know that if I called an hour ahead next time, she would be able to make some more bagels and have them ready next time! I was SHOCKED. I had never heard of a corporate business place catering to customers so well before! In addition, she was personal and incredibly friendly during my time at Einstein's yesterday.

THIS MORNING, I went to grab breakfast with some friends, and Kris was there again! Before I got in line, I asked her if they had any Potato Bagels left, and she asked me how many I wanted. She grabbed some bagels and put them into a bag and told me that she would let me hold onto them while I was waiting in line so she wouldn't sell them!

I really like Einstein's bagels, and those will keep me coming back. However, it's really the good customer service that makes them GREAT. Thanks to people like Kris, this Einstein's location has my loyalty!

I've lived in PDX for 17 years and I can say Cha Lua is great in every possible way. Amazing food and all of the prices are friggin out of this world. The Sandwiches are fatty and so cheap you can walk out with 3 for less than $10 and that could feed you for a day easy. They also have endless fun little food items and side dishes that taste amazing in each of their own ways. The service is so sweet and the owners and workers are so nice as well - you feel right at home when you enter. Absolutely love this place.

This place was running a Groupon for iPod, iPhone, and iPad repairs, but said they would offer special pricing on HTC and other phones as well, and to call the store.  All of these answers were provided by someone working for the business named Kristi D.  I called the store and got a mumbling guy who said he was the business owner and that the best he could do was $60 to repair the cracked glass on my HTC EVO 4G or else he'd be "losing money".  

Here are the prices they offer for the Apple products:

***
Choose from Three Options

$25 for screen replacement for an iPhone 3G or 3GS--LCD not included (a $55 value)
$48 for screen replacement for an iPhone 4 or 4S--LCD included (a $99 value)
$109 for screen replacement for an iPad 1, 2, or 3--LCD not included (a $220 value)
***

I find it hard to believe that $60 is "the best price in town" and that he'd be "personally losing money" to repair just the glass on my EVO for $60 when they will replace the glass AND the LCD screen on an iPhone 4 or 4S for just $48.

The guy on the phone was SO sleazy and rude - I definitely will not be bringing any of my phones here.

Really disappointed by my experience here. I came here twice because of the awesome yelp reviews. Both times, she missed a ton of hair on my eyebrow. She also charges extra for using a credit card. I came in knowing this and brought cash but then she told me she would only except the exact amount because she didn't have change. I normally give places two chances since sometimes you just get unlucky. I'm not coming back here again. Really disappointed since there aren't a lot of good eyebrow threading places in Austin.

The staff is very friendly and there's usually not a wait. However, I got to the store at 735 am today and the door was locked. I called the front desk to see if someone was in the back and no one answered. I called again just now when I got home and still no answer. Frustrating because on the door it says weekday hours are from 7am-11pm so I'm not sure why no one was there. 

Update** 
Went in this morning 7/18 at 730am and the girl working locked herself out of the store! Two days within one week the store wasn't open when they were suppose to be.

Having just recently moved to Portland, I pushed off having to find a barber until recently. I've walked by Throne a couple of times, and finally got myself to take the leap towards giving them a try. Made an appointment through their website with Jake Kost, and he nailed the cut i wanted perfectly. Looked for an appointment on Saturday, and got one the same day. It having been my first time, didn't know what to expect. The ambiance of the shop was welcoming, came in a little early, they gave a complimentary drink while waiting. Jake is one of the best barbers I've ever been to. Fade was on point, knew exactly what I wanted, and taught me something new in how to do my hair when at home. Jake is highly recommended.

I have been going here since I moved to Austin (May 2008) based on the reviews of this salon and Tara's.  I used to get them threaded when I lived in Cali.  I liked the fact that the cost was inexpensive and the result was great!  I need to get my eyebrows threaded every three to four weeks, even though at two weeks they are almost mad scientist-ish.  I also am a big fan of getting my monthly pedicure by Jessica (she is by appointment only).  On my way home I usually stop off at Sorrento's  :)

A&A was dispatched to tow our RV by Good Sam Roadside Assistance, we were not a parking violation tow customer.

A&A dispatched a medium duty International 4700 that was able to tow us with ease. The driver (Angel) was polite, very professional and highly skilled. The shop we were at left the RV inoperable and had the RV parallel parked between a closed garage and car but this did not prevent the driver from getting the RV started from under the hood and pulling it around to get it on his tow truck. He was careful to disconnect the driveshaft and return all parts needed to us for reconnection by the new shop.

If you find yourself in Dripping Springs/Austin area and need a big truck or RV towed, I highly recommend this company.

Ryan is truly amazing - great old-school service!  He listens to you and what your goals are and then discusses what repairs and how they should be done based on that!  Want it done "right" with top level parts, Sure.  On a budget, he can work to that too and lets you know what might be an issue later, what can wait, and what should be really done now... And if you want to wrench on it yourself to learn, there's that option too. (Try that at a bigger shop!)

I have been dying to get to this store as soon as I heard of its opening! Luckily I live in Houston so the drive isn't too bad and I finally made it up there. Unfortunately, my experience was similar to previous reviewers and that just makes me sad. But I guess I was expecting a bit of disappointment as I had read the reviews before going, which also put me at high alert to be aware of what was going on around me.
As a seasoned EC customer I knew what was offered and was so stoked to get in there and buy all the things. 
I walked in, there were THREE employees standing at the table at the door chatting away and NONE of them greeted me or offered any assistance or guidance to the lay of the land or the process. 
The layout is great, and can most definitely be way overwhelming with stuff and excitement and wanting everything. I took a look around and after being at the store for 5 minutes, someone finally greeted me. But just a "hi" and that was it. 
I walked over to the wall of amazement where you can create your own planner right then and there. Again, two employees standing at the wall and I was offered no help or explanation, they were chatting amongst themselves about personal things (I could hear them). Finally, after getting half way down the wall a different girl walked up to me and asked if I wanted to make a planner. I said I was looking and she walked away - no explanation just "oh, okay" and moved on. I thought I had said it in a way that would've opened her up to discuss the process but nope, she joined the other two who were chatting. Two more times this happened. Then finally, another employee came up to me as I was looking at the different options of the layouts and we discussed layouts but by that time I was so discouraged with the experience I chose to not create my own like I had planned and anticipated. Instead I chose a small and large hardbound planner, some stickers and was able to select some items for my mom's birthday gift. Finally when I went to the check out counter the girl who checked me out was what I was looking for from the start - super bubbly, full of knowledge, excited to be there AND even informed me that if you spend over $75 you got the EC surprise box (just for that weekend I think) - and I was so stoked! The stuff inside was GREAT! I love EC and will always remain a fan and customer BUT the employees at the flagship store need to have a come to Jesus chat - or girls that truly love the EC life need to be employed. 
I will likely go back to the store, because I like being able to get the things instantly and see them in person but I will always have my guard up and come in prepared to possibly be ignored or not helped. Which again, is so sad because I know EC cherishes her customers. Just wish her employees did too.

I have been hanging out here off an on since they opened all most a year ago. Sorry it took me so long to review. 

Really nice growlery. Everything is new and very clean. The large windows in front provide nice amount of light inside. The owners are very friendly also the patrons. 

Beer and cider?  The have 32 taps that change frequently. All the red star are at the end of the keg and will be switched soon. If you like that one, get it while you can. 

Nice selection of 12 wines.  I guess they buy a few bottles and run through then buy different wine. 

Food?  Bring your own. They have a very small menu but there is a Thai restaurant, Beg Reds, and a coffee shop nearby.   

Events?  They do all kinds of events. Tap takeovers galore. Music meetups, bands, BBQs. No wonder the are number one in this area. 

Peace Out,
Fredrick!!!

Dog friendly, bike friendly, alien friendly too.

Sunday night Stripperoke at Devil's Point is some of the most fun you'll have in Portland. It's the ultimate dive bar stripper karaoke experience and you need to have it.

There's no cover, but they serve the most watered-down cocktails I've had to date. Win some, lose some. Hey, at least they take cards!

Go with a group of friends when you visit town and you're pretty much GUARANTEED to have a freaking blast. Some of the dancers are truly, insanely beautiful too.

Don't forget to tip the dancers!

Visited Sharetea after dinner to just chill and chat. We thought the TorDa thing was kind of interesting so we got one. It was a black tea pearl TorDa. I ordered the "handmade taro with fresh milk", not sure what handmade meant but it was made with actual taro. 

The taro drink was actually quite good, I enjoyed how there were still tiny pieces of taro in my drink, so you know they actually used real taro. The taro flavour was subtle but tasted good with the milk as a whole. It was a refreshing drink. 

The TorDa was a huge disappointment. It tasted so bad. First, it was very hard to cut with plastic forks, making it hard to eat, especially sharing between two people. The black tea custard tasted nothing like black tea, it was a tasteless custard base. I felt it was pretty much a solidified version of a regular milk tea drink with pearls. The pearls were chewy and often stuck together. The shell was too hard. We just didn't enjoy the TorDa, and we didn't finish it.

I'd follow Sarah Contey to the end of the earth and back for my hair, but fortunately she recently just moved down the street to Red Stella. That's a little bit more convenient.

I've been faithfully getting my hair dyed, bleached, cut and everything else by Sarah for 2 years. I'm pretty picky about who touches my hair, especially because I am constantly waivering between DARK burgandy red and a very ashy blonde. The fact that Sarah takes me between these in less than 6 months without a split end in sight should earn her a Nobel Peace Prize. 

Sarah also did my make up for my engagement photos. I'm having Sarah do my hair and make up for my wedding as well.

WORST AIRLINE EVER! I fly quite a bit and have never had such a horrible experience. My boyfriend and I booked a flight to Cancun 4 months ago, and just figured out our flights were cancelled (they never notified me!) And they couldn't offer us a replacement flight! On top of it they wanted to hold my $1,000 as a credit towards a future flight! After automated call loops and zero customer support I have to wait 7 business days to have my money refunded so I can find a new airline and spend hundreds more on last minute tickets! SO FURIOUS!!!

I've been here twice.  The first time was okay since we could do the walk along the river and it's pretty when you first arrive at the entrance.  But, both times our groups have ALL lost our budgeted amount within the first hour.  I've been to many casinos all over the United States and never experienced machines that suck up money so fast.  I don't expect to win at a Casino, but I would hope I could play more than 30 minutes with 100 dollars.  Oh and as far as I could both times there was no one serving drinks on the floor :(. 
The buffet was just "okay" and we had to wait over 45 minutes in a line with over 100 people waiting  (with someone who is unable to stand for long periods of time and no seating around the waiting area for them to sit :() and we went out of the Casino to eat the second time because you have no desire to put more money into the Casino when it's sucked you and all your friends dry in less than 30 minutes, so we stayed only an hour this last time.  Also this is not a casino for anyone who is elderly, has an injury, or disability where a chair or bench is needed for a break.  The casino provides no benches or seating areas for those who have issues walking or who need to sit down; we had one older adult with us and could find no where for them to sit down and wait for us.  I'd much, much rather go to Foxwoods; I've always been able to take a couple hundred dollars there and have fun for a couple of hours and they also provide more overall.  I won't be going back and won't be recommending others go; their machines are the worst I've ever, ever encountered. Is the Casino trying to go out of business?  Maybe they don't like it here?

I wanted to ask a question to see if they carried a product I needed. I tried calling twice and never could get anyone to answer the phone. I avoid going to the store because they carry scented soaps which are displayed near the cash register. The scent causes me to get an immediate headache. I cannot find the product anywhere near me so I was willing to walk in the store if they carried it. I called at times when I knew they would not be busy.

Apres Diem used to be an old stomping ground for me! It's nice to see it's just as busy as it was years ago. However, the service was another story. Our server showed up 15 minutes after we sat down. We were seated outside by the front door. She had no idea about any of the drinks on the menu or the desserts. Nor did she care to find out. When we finally ordered a few desserts she kept saying ... "well, if we have it... did you get up and look?" My 3 friends and I were stunned. We assured her the desserts were in the case and, yes we did get up and look. She dropped off dessert then disappeared. When we were finally ready to leave she was no where in sight. I finally tracked her down rolling silverware in the corner inside the restaurant. At this point it had easily been 30+ minutes since we had seen her. I handed her my credit card and asked for the check. It was 10:30 pm and the place was clearing out. She looked at me like a deer in headlights. She never once apologized to me. In fact she stared at me like she didn't know that we were her guests ( probably because she never spent any time waiting on us). I finally told her where we were sitting so she can pull the bill. I returned to the table to fill out the credit card slip. I always tip generously, especially around the holidays, but was so irritated that I left a minimal tip. I have a lot of previous experience in the restaurant industry and can't imagine ever giving such atrocious service. She never came back to apologize, thank us, say goodbye etc. I won't be returning.

I never thought walking into this place would get us thrown out in just under five-minutes but it did. The Alibi was one of my longtime favorite places to go... that was until last Saturday night.

My brother just flew in from the LA area and we decided to meet up with some friends at the Alibi.  We have celebrated a few birthday parties here and it has a great atmosphere.  Yeah, the service can be slow at times but it's usually hit or miss for this place.

As soon as we walked in my brother politely walked over to the DJ booth and told the guy that he just got off a plane and wanted to know if he could play a couple of songs. I am not sure what sparked his response but he replied, "without a tip it's not gonna happen." My brother said "common, I just got off a plane." He responded "yeah, right I hear that all the time."  A brief exchange occurred and my brother told him that he would have been willing to give him a 20-dollar tip had he been decent about it.  Mr. DJ, short of calling my brother a liar, ends up calling security and we were promptly shown the door.

So word to the wise when visiting this establishment... Until management ups their hiring requirements make sure you bring enough tip money and show it to whoever is running the music before making any requests otherwise you may end up suffering the same fate we did. As much as I hate giving one-star reviews to any establishment and think twice before doing so this place clearly deserves it.

I worked with Soraya at SYB Event Planning  and Catering for our department's annual three-shift holiday event and it went really well. People loved the food. We had thick ham slices, mashed potatoes, green beans, grilled chicken with sauce on the side, ziti pasta and rolls. The next day, people were still talking and complimenting the good food. The catering staff was very nice and did a good job serving the food at all three shifts. We also had strawberry shortcake for dessert and it was delish. Everyone loved it. Soraya is personable, friendly, provides suggestions, and helps to stay within your budget. I look forward to working with SYB in the near future.

I like coming here for happy hour which is between 3-6 and grabbing a booth in the dark bar. 

The happy hour menu has a wide variety. The best deals and tasting that I have found are the calamari - not too breaded or oily, the salad which has sunflower seeds and beets and is tossed in their house horseradish bleu cheese dressing, and the cheeseburger and fries. I think the burger is $6, the salad and calamari 4$ each or right around there it's a really good deal for the quality.

Beer/wine cocktails also a buck or so off during happy hour. 

A band is usually setting up and it's not crowded (when I have gone around 4pm). 

The service has been hit or miss I think due to timing of shift change but that's not really a good excuse...the servers are always friendly so that helps. 

I can't comment on the dining room area because I have always sat in bar during happy hour!

I had really long, heavy hair and came to Twig this morning wanting to get rid of the weight and leave with a light, above the shoulder, Spring look. I received exactly that. Laurel was a treat - nice, light conversation and she actually listened to what I wanted. She gave me exactly what I wished for and also offered styling advice - both at the salon and said that I could call her at any time with questions. It has been years since I've been a return customer to a salon, but I will definitely be returning to Twig and asking for Laurel.

I had a very complicated and stressful pregnancy and had to leave the birthing center at 32 weeks pregnant. Which made me scared and I felt hopeless of having the birth experience I was aiming for. I couldn't find an appointment  with anyone and finally came across gynics. I saw the reviews for Dr. Crumb and was happy to see he had so many good reviews. I asked around and everyone at the birthing center said he was "the best!". So I made my appointment and it was the best decision I could have made.  He is amazing. He immediately  calmed all of my fears, concerns and reassured me of my ability to reach my goals. He was very intelligent yet personable and funny. I definitely  needed some humor after everything I had been through. 
Birthing my daughter was complicated and we had to employ some techniques but he basically respected my birth plan and within reason followed it completely.  I was able to deliver my daughter without pain medication and minimal intervention. My daughter had shoulder dystocia and he was quick, skilled and delivered her safely in my arms. 
My family can't thank him enough. If you need an excellent doctor, he's the one.

Stop going to Panera Bread immediately. I mean it. Just try the Brown Bag Deli in German Village. Their fresh ingredients and inventive combinations make for some great salads, soups, desserts and sandwiches. Oh the sandwiches! You don't know what you're missing. I know I didn't.

I love gigantic sandwiches that can barely fit in your mouth. Naturally I am a sucker for a 'wich with roast beef, turkey, corned beef, scallion cream cheese, tomato, onion and mustard on an awesome roll. If there is a heaven for sandwiches, this one's going there. That's how saintly it is. 

Then there are some other sandwiches I should probably try sometime. They seem stellar too. Pastrami, smoked ham, smoked cheddar cheese, sauerkraut & thousand island dressing on rye? C'mon. I think I'm gonna go sleep on the Brown Bag's front step and wait for them to open.

Oh, and if you're a fan of that other German Village deli, consider visiting the Brown Bag. Your wallet will be thicker for it.

Matthew is a wonderful healer! I got in touch with him before having to travel and told him about my many health issues and recent injuries. He was extremely patient and helpful in answering all my questions, always available over the phone at anytime I had some concerns. I have had several sessions with him and have loved how relaxing they have been. 

The fact he stays and works on other body parts makes it such a more relaxing appointment than traditional acupuncture in which the therapist leaves you whilst attending other clients. He is always very gently in the way he applies the needles, I am very sensitive and have many sore areas but he managed to work through that. He has wonderful bedside manners and makes you feel at ease during your session, I highly recommend him and am excited to have him be a part of my healing team :-)

Sparkly a new facility. Friendly staff. Organized. Everyone that works there seems like they're really cool. Cool for school yo. 
I tried one free class to see how I liked it. Dim lights, bumpin hip hop & rnb beats (which I enjoy)...mirrored walls in the cycling room. Eek.
I felt weird looking at myself the whole class. It's definitely one of those cultures of exercise where the person will yell into their mic 'I said are we having a good time??! I can't hear youuuuu Woo hoo!'. If you like that kind of motivation, then this is for you. If you're LESS into that, you may want to wear earplugs (which I believe they do offer at reception! hehe) orrrr go somewhere else.
I definitely got my 'ass kicked', as the instructor said she would do. I pushed myself too hard though and ended up pulling a butt muscle. I'm not out of shape or anything but, I just pushed myself hard. That happens when the instructor is yelling at you to look in the mirror, pointing out that everyone is Not in sync with the beat. Because apparently, Ride is all about keeping rhythm (whichhhhh could lead to a pulled butt muscle). And for the record, I CAN keep the beat lol. I'm a dancer. But I physically was unable to keep up with the beats of the music selection becauseeee I am not a crazy-ass athlete. 

I may go back for a drop in on a day where I feel like I want to really push myself and burn carbs and be in dim lighting with loud music. But this isn't somewhere I'll be going regularly. I'm a dancer, I like a yoga class here n there...and I prefer YRide at yyoga to this place.

I really, really wish hair stylists would listen to their clients before going scissor crazy.  A month ago I decided to get my hair chopped off, and wanted to go to a more 'alternative' salon that would understand the 'funky' haircut I wanted.  Enter Bangtown. I noticed the salon (saloon?) while walking around Gastown, and booked an appointment with Melissa, one of the senior stylists I believe.  Going from mid length hair to a seriously short cut was dramatic, and Melissa did a fine job.  She took her time looking over the photos I provided of the cut I wanted, and determining how it would suit me.  I wasn't totally thrilled with the initial cut, but over the next few weeks I grew to love it.  

Then today, since short hair grows fast and needs plenty of upkeep, I decided to return to have it trimmed.  I guess my stylist (Melissa) wasn't on ball because I ended up with the most awkward cut ever... one side of my head is nearly shaved. I brought back the same photos as last time, but after a cursory glance, I guess my stylist didn't think to reference them again during the cut.  Which resulted in my hair being MUCH shorter than I wanted. In fact, you can even see my scalp, which is not good in my book.  I had to run home, shower again, and restyle my hair so it was somewhat decent.  I really wish stylists would be more conscious of how much they are taking off, especially when the client is apprehensive about going short in the first place.  I know, I know, it will grow out in the next few weeks, but I left unhappy.  Time to try out another salon I guess... why is it so hard to find a decent stylist?!

P.S. I was never offered beer in the two times I've been.

P.P.S. Cut was $55 plus HST and tip.

I went to iFly on 12/20 (my 30th birthday), and my experience there was so positive, that I even decided to create a yelp profile just so I can tell you how awesome my experience was. 

Before I go into the positives, the only minor issue I encountered was with the front desk girl. She seemed to be cold and not friendly. Other than that, iFly gets two thumbs and toes up.

My girlfriend and I went, and we were with the instructor named Travis. Travis alone probably made the experience just that much better for us, because his high level of energy and enthusiasm, combined with how extremely helpful he was in instructions and tips, are the reasons why I'm legitimately considering making this a hobby.

Travis had to leave our group for a bit so he could do the "high flies" for a different group, and he was kind enough to give us a free movie or picture of our flight for the inconvenience - talk about customer support! Then on my second flight, I was starting to get the hang of things pretty quickly, and he showed me how to control my solo flight and turn left or right, and go front or back. He's the type of "dude" that equally gets excited as you do when you do something kinda cool, and he's prone to giving you high fives in the middle of the wind tunnel. Also, at the end of it, he jumped in the wind tunnel and did a lot of really cool tricks.... blew my mind.

If you can get in a group of Travis, do so (I'm sure the other instructors are good too, but I'm biased). But at the end of the day, this was a blast, and made my 30th birthday that much better (and this is coming from a guy who has actually logged two tandem skydives in his life). Do yourself a favor and check this place out... if you like breathing air, then you'll love iFly.

We had the opportunity to celebrate the 50th birthday for one of my best friends over the weekend. Let me begin my review with a disclaimer: I've only been to one class here. It was the free trial. I've been searching for Crossfit gyms in Portland for a while, and I've been having trouble finding a box that I'm happy with. Still searching, as we speak. 

Crossfit Stumptown was one of the first gyms that I tried in Portland. While I was impressed with the gym's space, equipment, the coaching, and the community vibe in general, I wasn't too sure how I felt about this "dynamic workout" that Tony (the head coach) has you do before every WOD. First of all, each WOD is pretty different and requires different parts of your body to be warmed up and concentrated. While I understand the dynamic workout is comprehensive and does cover all the bases, I found it to be too long and fatiguing and almost ruined the actual WOD for me. Warming up is a very individualized thing -- for instance, that day, I had just biked 3 miles from work to the gym and then had to do a 15 minute warmup even though I was already warm -- and it should be acknowledged in coaching. 

At the end of the day, I thought it was also a cop out to be doing the same warmup for different WODs -- if I'm going to be paying $165 for a membership there, at least spend a little more time and tailor the warmups for each WOD, you know? But I do feel bad for saying this, because I do think that Tony is a good coach and a lot of the members there really seemed to love the gym. He was super nice too, and said I could come to as many classes for free as I need to be convinced before I signed up. But as somebody who's tried Crossfit at a bunch of different gyms, I wasn't convinced enough by that free trial to commit.

I have been here numerous times and have always had a most positive experience.  Even though I have moved to Austin, I will continue to go to this office.

I'd heard this place wasn't that great, but I wanted to check it out for myself. 

I can overlook that it's set up in a building that used to be a restaurant. Big deal. There was plenty of parking on a Wednesday morning (11am-ish); I'm sure it's full on the weekends, just like everywhere else (the zoo, OMSI, Children's Museum, etc). The girl at the check-in desk was nice when we first got there, so were the rest of the staff that we encountered. The first touch tank (set up in a boat) in the first room is cool. The tank for the Moray Eel seems really small and it states on a sign by it's tank that it's a nocturnal creature... so why is it in an aquarium that's open during the day? It was folded in half in a cave and looked like it was dying (I'm assuming it was asleep). 

The second room with the jelly fish and octopus were pretty cool, until I got closer and saw how small the tanks were. While we were there, we heard one of the employees say how much Roxy (the octopus) has grown since they've acquired her... I'm not sure what they plan on doing with her once she outgrows her tank. They had an octopus talk at 12pm, but my 2-year old wasn't interested enough for me to stay and listen or ask questions. 

The puffin exhibit is still being "prepped" by the snails, not sure when they'll get the birds in there. I did notice there are no windows in that room, though I'm not sure if the animals will notice that or not. 

The Lorikeet/Reptile/kid's climbing structure room is very loud. The birds, the kids... it seems like that area needs to be rethought. There's also a tortoise, but from what we could see, it was also in a tiny enclosure. My daughter was unable to use the play structure, it is definitely for kids at least 4 or 5 and up. I'm okay with that though, I feel like it's probably pretty gross and dirty up there, I'm not sure if the employees go up and sanitize/wipe everything down. 

The shark/ray tank is pretty awesome, but as we were petting/feeding the rays, I had to wonder about everyone's hands and bacteria getting into the tank (not to mention extra kid's food.... there was a birthday party being set up in there as we were leaving). I know they have a filtration system, but those aren't always foolproof. There are two hand washing stations (one by the Moray Eel and one by the Shark/Ray pool), but very few signs by the pool asking for people to wash their hands first. When my daughter and I went to wash our hands, there was a bottle of Johnson's baby soap/shampoo, extremely watered down. Also, when people buy food to feed to the fish/rays/sharks, the employees should remind people to wash their hands before feeding. 

There is a room at the end/outside the gift shop with fold up tables and chairs. Nice of them to put them there, so you can sit with your kids and have lunch or some snacks, but they could be nicer, for sure. As my daughter was sitting on one of the chairs, she almost fell through the back. I hope they have plans to re-do this area as well and get something that isn't so cheap. 

Unfortunately, we did buy a membership, luckily it was only the $67 dollar membership. We might go back once or twice, since our daughter enjoyed it, and after just a couple trips, we won't be out any money. The woman who entered our membership information was training, but I swear it was like she'd never seen a keyboard before and had no customer service skills. The girl who was training her stepped away for a few minutes and left the newbie to slowly struggle through entering information. She asked for my phone number about 6 times, I'm not kidding. I even repeated it slowly and she still couldn't get it right. For something that should have taken less than 5 minutes to do, it took her 15. 

It is interesting that it's called the Portland Aquarium, but isn't actually IN Portland... Also, on their website, they have an 'exhibits' link posted, but you don't get to see any of the exhibits, or pictures from this place.

Maitland is the home of Audubon in Florida. The first meeting was held on March 2, 1900. Illustrious early leaders of the society have included President Theodore Roosevelt, Florida's Governor, Rollins College's President, Stetson University's President, and the editors of the state's largest newspapers. Florida Audubon board member, Lisa von Borowsky, purchased this 3 acre property in 1959 that served as the Audubon's first permanent home. The historic 2 story wood frame house veranda bungalow was built in the 1920's by a builder named Patterson. The house was used for meetings, offices, and as a gift shop. 

In the 1970's gift shop manager Doris Mager began to care for injured birds brought to her by members from the community. To raise money for the center Doris Mager climbed into an inactive Bald Eagle nest and stayed there for six days and five nights. She wanted to bring awareness to the plight of the Bald Eagle. From this caring act and the donation of funds from Madelyn Baldwin and others, the Audubon Center for Birds of Prey was opened on October 19, 1979.  

The center is open year round 10 to 4, except for Mondays when they are closed. I was able to visit the center with my daughter on a recent trip to Winter Haven. The center takes in an average of 650 injured raptors a year. They rescue and rehabilitate the ones that can be released back into the wild and provide a permanent home for the ones that can't. Admission is $8 for adults and $5 for children but we purchased a Groupon. If I lived closer I would definitely purchase an annual family pass for $50. In addition to the birds they have a boardwalk at the back of the center that overlooks the wetlands. 

Some of the birds we got to see included eagles, owls, ospreys, kites, hawks, and vultures. Since they opened in 1979 they have released more than 40,000 birds back into the wild. They provide environmental programs to over 20,000 people annually and they are a nationally renowned research institute. It was a pleasure to see what they are doing here and to support their work. The Audubon center is leading the fight to save the endangered and threatened birds of prey.

I am very disappointed in this place.  I am a frequent user of Amazon but thought I would try to support our local Best Buy when I purchased my LG OLEDC7 and LG 4K blueray player. Moojo = Moments of joy

If heavens exists this must be it! I am not sure you can get much better than cookies and ice cream .. like really ... come on ... nothing better.  I literally went here twice in a week ... yup you heard me right ... 2 times in one week!  Good thing I don't live near by campus because I would be here every day probably.  

I realize now how they came up the name.  There is so much joy happening in this little spot on the drag. Everything from the decor, the employees to the product ... it is all joyful and providing happiness to it's patrons.

So here is the scoop ... ice cream and cookies.  Individually we all love them, but when you put them together something magical happens.

Moojo has about 6-10 different cookies options.  If you don't want a cookie they have these waffle things too.  They also have gluten free and vegan options for those people out there.  I was in a chocolate mood so I got the rocky road cookie.  Then for ice cream they have a bunch of flavors to choose from.  I ended up choosing the cookies and cream on my first visit.  When the ice cream sandwich artist handed me my creation I could tell the cookies were slightly warm.  My first bite I am telling you was magical .. if you are one of those people that thinks magic doesn't exist then you have not been to Moojo clearly.  The chocolate chunks in the rocky road cookie were so creamy good.  The cookies and cream ice cream was paired perfectly. 

If you are having trouble deciding what to choose they have some suggestions on the chalk board.  My girl, Kimberly K that was with me on my first visit did one of their suggestions - Bacon me crazy, which is a bacon chocolate chip cookie with vanilla bean ice cream.  My second visit I convinced Tiffany S that she needed some Moojo in her life too and she got the snickerdoodle cookie with salted caramel pretzel ice cream.  

So basically if you are looking for a little magic or joy in your life then look no further because it exists on the drag at this place called Moojo.

Just a quick update that a follow-up visit was just as good as the first.  The Chef's Choice option continues to offer a terrific variety of flavors, spread out nicely, and portioned for as many people as you have in your party - so there's no trying to split a tapas dish with 4 items among 6 people.  Of any place in Portland, this is the one I consider worth the wait for a table. My only quibble continues to be the sound system - loud enough to occasionally intrude on having a conversation, while being mostly just a dull, thumping noise that does not enhance the atmosphere.

I got my eyebrows done today and I'm very happy with the results. I am extremely impressed with Emily at Empress Brow. Emily is very professional and her consultation provided me with the confidence that I wanted to go ahead with microblading. I'm 52 and my eyebrows have thinned. I have never gotten any cosmetic tattoos done and I'm generally speaking skeptical about any type of beauty work. However, I'd grown tired of "painting" on eyebrows every morning. I'm also very active and outdoorsy and needed a better solution than daily eyebrow makeup. Emily took a lot of time to consult me and drew the outlines of my eyebrow shape. As I said, I'm new to this and I needed some time to try out different eyebrow shapes. Emily was extremely helpful and encouraged me to only settle for the eyebrow shape that I thought was right for me. Emily said this my face and it needs to be perfect. I really appreciated her patience with me. She also consulted me on the color to best match my hair and complexion. Once I felt comfortable with the shape Emily carefully started with the work. She made sure I was comfortable throughout the procedure and kept asking if I needed more numbing. I was pleasantly surprised about how it did not hurt at all and how easy and comfortable the procedure was. Emily's steady hand made me confident that this would turn out great. And it did. In fact I am much more pleased with the end result than I had expected. I understand that there is a healing process and that the color will change a little bit within a few days, however I'm already extremely pleased with the outcome, knowing that it will look even better once my skin has healed. I absolutely love my new eyebrows. I did a lot of research before I decided to do this and I'm glad I went to Empress Brow. I highly recommend Emily. I'm so happy with my brows, I'm going to make an appointment for lip blushing as well. Emily is a total Pro! She knows what she's doing. I will get more work done with Emily. So happy with my brows :))

So THRILLED to find this park!!! Althougth many parks exist in the Hunters Creek area, a lot of them are more ball parks--soccer, baseball, etc.  Although I really enjoy the scenery of Kissimmee Lakefront Park, currently a lot of construction is in progress, making it not walkable.

It's been very frustrating not finding a park dedicated to walkers and joggers, and so this park is an answer to my prayers.  It's actually in the same area as the Orland Magic recreation center.

Clear, walkable paths, with some scenic touches--a lake, park benches, and wildlife.  I spotted cranes, of course, along with a rabbit on my walk here.  In addition, signs warning people not to feed the alligators leads me to believe there is wildlife of a different kind here as well.

I also appreciate the water fountains and restrooms that were being cleaned on my visit.  Imagine, clean restrooms at a park.

I also love that this is also a dog park.  AND to have separate space for small and large dogs is a big plus.  I love watching the dogs go for it without any inhibitions.  It really is a great dog park because there are double fences so that the litter critters will have a harder time sneaking out of gates.  There are also covered tables inside the dog area.

Plus, playground areas are available for the little ones.  Such a great find.  I have a feeling I will be visiting this park a LOT.

I called All My Sons about two weeks prior to my move to set an appointment.  They were very friendly and the rates seemed reasonable.  It all went downhill from there.  

The day before my morning move was scheduled they called to verify that the movers would be there around noon.  Okay, sounds great.
12:00...
1:00...
2:00...

Time kept ticking by and no movers and no contact from the company.  I called them several times and they always said that "They're still on the first job.  Shouldn't be too much longer."  One time they told me they'd call the truck and call me back.  they never called me back.  I called again around 6:00 to tell me that we were being moved to the top of the queue the next day.  Okay, first thing in the morning the next day is doable.  Things happen.
7:00 the owner calls: we're moving to the next day, but the SECOND stop.  No estimated time.

The next day: no communication from them.  I start calling in late morning: no word on the job before me. "We'll call you back..."  No one called back.  Finally around 12:30 I called again for SOME kind of update or estimate and they told me that I should probably just call another mover.

So, by making an appointment two weeks in advance it took them until 28 hours AFTER the appointment was set to tell me to go somewhere else.

The company I called in desperation at 12:30 that second day, America's Best Movers, had a team at my place within thirty minutes of my call, were fast, courteous and professional.

I was recently in the market for my first bicycle & made a pit stop at David's World Cycle to check out their selection. As soon as I walked in the door their staff greeted my party, made sure we knew where we could find what we were looking for & pointed us in the right direction. David's has a huge selection of road, mountain & hybrid bikes. Pretty much any type of bike you can think of. 

I was in the market for a Cruiser (SO cute right?) & their staff walked me through all the intricacies of the various options they had in stock, as well as the accessories I could add like baskets, removable carry-ons, etc. I wasn't wearing the right shoes so I couldn't test drive one but I was told if I came back with sneakers they'd let me take several of the bikes around the block to check them out, I loved that option. The reason David's gets four stars instead of five is because the bikes are a little pricey. As I compared prices throughout several bike shops in town David's was on the higher end. Other than that, great selection, nice store, good staff!

I've actually never been to a Russian restaraunt. Look and behold, we were in the area and decided to give this place a try.

The menu is pretty simple, and a fantastic way to end the night, came here after a night out at the bars. We ordered the pelmini and vareniki dumplings,one had meats and the other cheese and green onions. Both were absolutely fantastic, they had a nice balance of acidity from the vinegar and savory from the meat and cheese. So good, we had two orders of the meat(pelmini)! 

The Vladimir poutine was a different style of poutine, the gravy wasn't as heavy as some other but it was delectable nontheless.

The drinks here are also superb, both volcano power and the Moscow mule slushie were great. They also have shot and beer combos that look pretty interesting.

If I'm in the area again, I will definitely stop in.

If you don't like the tourist crowd at this location they have a Hastings location now (see review). I used to come to this one, however, had issues browsing and asking question 'cause the place was treated more or less as a tourist destination/museum and less for the person wanting to look at hats. He was patient with me but I could tell that he was trying to juggle many customers at once with people who were just curious. He did display a great deal of customer service which was impressive considering the buying habits and the motives of the other customers.

I'm only writing up the Lake O outpost of Portland's favorite locally owned grocery store because this is where my online orders usually come from. Yeah, that's right, I said ONLINE ORDERS because I have discovered that there is nothing better in the world than just skipping the whole "people who think they're better/busier/more important than you" fiasco of grocery shopping. Oh, and I don't let my car go to grocery store parking lots if I can help it. I'm one of those people who take pains to return the shopping cart back to its shopping cart resting area, despite rain/snow/sleet/time crunches so when I see people maneuvering their cart onto the curb next to a parked car in the parking lot it drives me insane. I've actually yelled at people before, like, "really, how hard is it?!"

So back to the review. New Seasons has online shopping and delivery that costs $9.99. But they often will send you promotions in your email that give you even free delivery depending on how much you spend, such as save $10 off an order of $100 or $15 off an order of $150. They pick your order for you at the store, put everything in their chilled biodiesel van and bring it right into your kitchen. If something is out at the store, you can ask them to substitute a similar item for you. You can order as few as 4 hours in advance and have your groceries delivered that same day.

The whole thing is great, from the online shopping tool, to downloading all items of a recipe into your basket at once, to the delivery. The only suggestion I would make is for someone to develop a delivery service that would also go to Trader Joe's and Target for me ;)

I stumbled upon Grub Street while looking for a creative writing class, and I decided to sign up for a workshop in their narrative non-fiction genre offerings. Sadly, I am not impressed with the structure of the classes or passion of the instructor. Being that it is a workshop, I feel there is not enough of an opportunity to learn from the instructor. Instead of being taught how to, students are expected to figure it out on their own. Plus the meetings themselves are centerd around critiquing. Little writing happens while in class. 

I'm assuming other's who've raved about Grub must have expected this, but I, someone who was looking for a guided learning experience, feels a bit disappointed.

On the upside, GS is affordable, offers many classes, and has great facilities on the 4th floor of an obscure Theater district building overlooking the Boston Common. Pretty cushy if you ask me!

Even though the walk up was a little weird, I enjoyed sitting up on the second floor and watching everything down below. 

The soup I had was AMAZING. So good! My curry noodles were pretty good and the amount of vegetables was generous, but the eggplant I ordered with the dish was kind of mushy which I was not a fan of.

The service was decent, though I went in mid-afternoon so it wasn't too busy. I would definitely go back to try out some of the other dishes.

I have used Tree Tops for drop-in care several times for my 18-month-old and was very impressed with the facility and the care he received there. I like that there are outdoor play areas and nice indoor play areas as well where he can climb and be active. The people watching him have handled him well and he has seemed to have a good time when he goes, even though he is the kind of kid who gets upset when mommy and daddy leave him places. I plan to use Tree Tops on a regular basis for drop-in care.

I've been having coccyx pain for 6 months now and exhausted many forms of treatment so I decided to try acupuncture. Immediately upon talking to Sharon you know she has a lot of knowledge about not only acupuncture but also general well being. After talking to many doctors (I've seen 4 so far) who were unsympathetic and unwilling to do any extra research for me, it's so nice talking to Sharon. She's willing to listen to all your symptoms, give each one weight, and consider many treatment options. This was my first time going to this place and it's the cutest. Online reservations, but they don't tell you that your seating time is 60 minutes! *
Matcha Mochi soufflé pancake ($14) I really loved this! The red bean was spot on flavour wise and the matcha was not too strong!  9/10 - it was so delicious and I loved the texture! Super cute and fluffy. Wish there was more red bean in it! But overall amazing!

 8/10 - the portion was good and the photos turned out amazing! Good place to socialize with family and friends! Total bill before tip (matcha red bean pancake + earl grey latte = $21.28)

NOT A RELIABLE PLACE TO LEAVE YOUR CAR.

Pickup experience: When I went there to pick up the car I noticed there was damages. When I told the staff about this, a manager came to see me. 

Him: 'You have no proof that those damages were not there before'. 
Me: 'What if I took pictures of the car when I dropped off?'   
Him: 'In your parking slip it says that we are not responsible for any damages'

Drop off experience: They do not have self park, they just advertise it so online. After you arrive they offer everyone (in their words) a 'free upgrade to valet'. They want to keep your car keys so they can maximize the parking capacity. That's why when you'll pick up it takes longer to pull your car upfront, because they are moving other cars that are blocking your car.

Sum up: The management and business seemed very sketchy. Except a few staff. As I waited there I noticed maybe 1 or 2 guys and girls in the bunch who looked like good people and sincerely want to help the customers around, I'd rate those few people five stars and hope they'd find a better place to work.

If I have an older car I'd probably park here and take a chance and save some $$. But if you like your car or care about its value it can be unsafe and you may lose more $$$$.

My family and I have gone on fishing outfits across the world... So we read all the reviews, thought we picked the right boat and guide. Humm. Maybe Larry was having a bad day... 

It was the most unprofessional trip I've ever been on. First, we are out on the water for 15 mins, asks my nephew to toss off the anchor. He does it wrong and starts yelling at him. We found it funny at first that he was yelling, thinking he was just a grumpy sailor... Then it started to become abusive. This was supposed to be a guided fishing tour. All it was turned into was Larry yelling and talking trash. He spent half the trip on his cell phone with a girlfriend, complained about every boat on the water and he barely did anything but complain and harass my family. 

When his phone rang a few times he asked my nephew to get up and hand it to him?!? Wait a minute... You are our guide and we are doing everything? Including being your receptionist? 

Even when we got back to the dock, he needed lots of help. My husband even needed to drive his truck to pull out the boat. Wtf?

Trip cost $1000 by the time we were done. I should have just rented us a boat and gone ourselves for the amount of work. Lesson learned and hopefully we save someone else.

I went to Tajine on the second day of its existence, and I was very excited because I love both to eat and cook Moroccan food.  I don't mean to be too harsh and they might just have been disorganized since they had only opened the day before, but the restaurant was awful.  
For appetizers we had a carrot salad, hummus, and an eggplant dish.  These three were the only options then available, though the menu boasted many more.  Anyway, while the eggplant was at least edible and the carrots were okay if you added lots of salt, the hummus tasted like it had been bought in a can, as it had barely any flavor and it was way over-processed. 
For our main courses, we tried a kefta tajine (the highlight of the meal, although it wasn't that great and was way too salty), a tajne of lamb and prunes, and a beef tajine.  The lamb tajine was only sweet and had no other flavor (I realize that Moroccan cuisine frequently combines sweet and savory, but Moroccan food also contains plenty of spices, such as cinnamon, ginger, saffron, pepper, cardamom, nutmeg, turmeric, etc), and the beef was plain bland.  We also, unfortunately, ordered two couscous dishes- one with vegetables and the other with chicken.  The first consisted only of boiled root vegetables (way overcooked) and couscous-among the blandest dishes I've ever tried-while the other was the same except with chicken.  Again, no spices at all.
There were no Moroccan-style desserts and I made the mistake of ordering 'black forest' which was by far the worst dessert I've had in my entire life (my sisters did enjoy their desserts-tiramisu and 'imperial,' neither of which were Moroccan).  The mint tea which was served for free was actually delicious and the best part of my experience.  The service as well was fast and our waitress was very nice.

I'm in the middle of my second stay at this hotel. My first 1-night stay for a business trip was fine - the room seemed a little worn but the breakfast buffet that came with the State rate was good and there was nothing concerning about the stay.

 I'm here again for a 2-night stay because my Father has been inpatient at St. David's and they offer a discount for families/patients. No breakfast buffet included this time, which is fine given the discounted price. However, this time I'm encountering challenges with housekeeping. After my first night I leave very early in the AM to be at the hospital, so I ask the front desk what time housekeeping is finished with the rooms and they tell me they're done by 1:30. I return to my room at 2 pm to grab a nap before going back to the hospital -- the room hasn't been cleaned. Ok, fine, whatever. Day 2: I head out to the hospital very early in the morning and plan to come back in the afternoon. This time I call ahead at 12:30ish -- I let the front desk know I'll be heading back in an hour or so and ask that it be cleaned so I can rest when I arrive. I get back to my room -- not clean.

What the heck!?

I honestly wouldn't have worried much about missing one night of housekeeping, but given that this appears to be a pattern I'm not pleased. I might be back for a 1-night stay in the future, but if I ever have to stay multiple nights again I'll be rethinking my hotel choice. Getting a clean room shouldn't be so hard.

I got up this morning to find that my garage door would not budge at all so I took the bus to work and called Boulder Garage Door and told them about the problem. Highly recommended.

I went there for custom framing, knowing I wanted something good but not sure exactly what.  Jodi was very welcoming and patient. The Rijsttafel tasting menu ($14/person) comprises of:
Gado Gado - vegetables with peanut sauce
Rendang - simmered beef in coconut milk
Babi Kecap - pork in kecap with star anise and ketumbar
Sambal Tahu - tofu in spicy sauce
Sambal Kentang - salt & pepper potato
Acar - sweet & sour cucumber salad
Sayur Daun Kale - braised kale with chili sauce
Pisang Goreng- fried banana ball
Steamed Jasmine Rice

FOOD 5/5
Let me just say I love the Beef Rendang here and definitely the Rijsttafel tasting. With the Rijsttafel tasting, one gets to sample many of the dishes here in small portion. I would not hesitate to order the Rijsttafel tasting again simply cos every of the small dishes go so well with one another. The Pisang Goreng should definitely be eaten last since this is more of a dessert. I know the Rijsttafel is a little more elaborate with 15 items. For everyone with a bigger appetite or feeling super adventurous, I say go for it. I might even try that out one of these days.

AMBIANCE 5/5
This is a huge restaurant. It was freezing cold this morning, unfortunately the heat was not working at its optimal today here. The female staff, however, was so sweet and offered us hot tea to keep us warmth. The décor is definitely trendy/classy and the seating are comfortable. 

SERVICE 5/5
The female staff (Li Shan (sp?)) with adequate English was super sweet and very kind. The kitchen staffs (chefs probably?) each brought out our Rijsttafel tasting in a wooden tray with 9 dishes placed aesthetically on the tray.

Our complimentary hot tea was constantly filled. Staffs even brought out a piece of mini cupcake with candle when the female staff heard I was paying for lunch since someone had his birthday on Sunday. Service here is 100% attentive. 

This is definitely a solid 5 star I am happy to give to WIN Indonesian Grill & Gastrobar. I just hope more people would come to know of this place since it is located in a quite obscure location. There is ample parking at the back of the restaurant/building.

PS. Complimentary shrimp crackers with sambal chili was given before our meal!

Art and commerce.  Saints and sinners.  Order and chaos.

They make the world go round.  Especially the art world.  

I know it is much cooler to be artsy and independent, but art museums live and die by sponsorships.  Just look at the names on the gallery walls.  Then think about all the masters who had works commissioned by the church (they had some of the deepest pockets back in the day) juxtaposed with the current touring exhibit at PAM - art created for and collected by a mistress for her king and his court.  

You have the traditional main building connected to the renovated Mark Building (masonic temple) and Jubitz Center filled with the oddity that is the contemporary art collection.  So many little rooms and galleries, that I usually get a bit lost, which is not such a bad thing.

I've been coming here for over 10 years and just keep waiting to fall in love.  And there have been sparks, but most of those have nothing to do with the art.  You see, I must disclose, that I work for the man.  And when times were flush, I had the good fortune of attending several galas in the PAM ballrooms and it is a wow of a venue [1].

Whenever I go to a museum or gallery, I do a quick pass through the halls looking for something to stop me dead in my tracks.  Then I usually stand in slack-jawed gaze in front of 'the one' for about an hour.  It is becoming harder and harder for me to find something magical outside of the special exhibitions.  After having been to many museums in many countries, PAM strikes me as a great overview of different styles (Asian, Native American, European) for the local community, but it isn't spectacular in any of these areas.  

On my visits, I'm usually surrounded by a mix of school groups, seniors and families and I think it is a good place to visit for everyone who lives in Portland.  Just not a must see destination.  And I suggest you time your visit to see a touring exhibit that makes your heart go pitter-pat.

[1] The reason my overall rating is a 4 and not a 3.

My chive pancake/bun was dripping in oil, otherwise good.  Partner enjoyed the beef hamburger.  They were able to accommodate my request to add a cup of soup to my order.  No hot beverages here.  
Long wait for food as this place is popular.  The lady making XLB and the fellas cooking in the back entertained me the whole time.  Watching them work in the back gave me a greater appreciation for the place.  Hard workers who know their job well, multitasking and coordinating in concert with each other.  
Good authentic food freshly made.  Will continue to frequent this place and try different dishes on their menu.

I went to this clinic on a Friday evening to treat an ear infection. I didn't want to wait for an appt with my doctor and the standard "urgent care clinics" were closed. I give these guys two stars for being opened and for providing relatively efficient service. BUT I had to pay the Emergency Room copay which was much more expensive. I saw a doctor, received two shots,  and received a prescription. Today I get a bill from my insurance that this place is not in the United Healthcare plan, and that the bill submitted to them by Austin Emergency Center was $2500!! Yes, $2500 for a 5 minute doctor consultation and two shots. Unbelievable. It is more than my insurance will cover and they wanted me to know there may be an additional balance due. If you have urgent medical need my suggestion is to go to an actual hospital emergency room rather than deal with these guys.

Everyone in the store was exceptionally friendly and helpful! I came in hoping to fix a lamp, and when the associate realized there wasn't a replacement part available in the store, he offered to go check it using a multimeter.
