When the circuit tested out okay, he found a lightbulb to test with, and lo and behold, it lit up just fine! Turned out that although I'd put a new bulb into the lamp at home, it had been defective. I also needed a length of rubber tubing cut and after a different employee had called to request it for me, while I was waiting he entertained me with stories of some volunteer work he'd been doing. The cashier was equally friendly. I appreciated coming out of the store feeling so much better than when I went in, from what could easily have been a humiliating experience. Thanks to everyone there who made my day so much happier!

Came here to get some blinds made.

Parking is available in the back.  The entrance is a bit sketchy.

Pricing is quite reasonable - $100 for so for 1" aluminum Venetian blinds, and $150 for the newer-style (and more durable) vinyl panel Venetians.  The best part is that they make these on the spot - it takes about 30 minutes per set.

Only thing to keep in mind - they're cash only.

When the blinds I had made didn't fit, I was able to call the manager after hours, and he was able to talk me through modifying the blinds on the spot.  That was very helpful, and prevented me from having to make a trip back to the store.  Definitely appreciated.

Let me start by saying I began my search by looking for companies close to where I live.  After doing some Internet-based research, I chose Fair Winds over another company. Fair Winds were about $25 dollars more, and in the end  it was very well worth it.  

I'll start with the reservation process.  I like when a company offers reservations online, which is should be de riguer in this day and age, but sometimes isn't.  Fairwinds offers online reservations. Fair Winds had a good set up, although it was two-part, it was simple. There was also the option to reserve by phone, for the web-challenged. 

The Fair Winds website was well done and it was easy to find all the information I wanted. Follow-up was great.  Confirmation via a friendly phone call was done the day before the flight, to ensure that we were on, as there can be weather cancellations. The website includes information on location, equipment, what to wear, what to expect and the like.

On the day of the flight, the launch location was convenient and easy to get to, tucked into a business park in Gunbarrel (just north of Boulder). When we arrived, it was easy to spot the venue, as it was brightly and clearly signed. I noticed that van, trailers and other support equipment were current, clean and well-kept. Check-in was easy, there was a nice continental breakfast provided and everything ran on schedule. Jeff and his crew were professional, welcoming, and inclusive. 

We had about 11 people on our flight. Fellow passengers were encouraged to help with set up, which took about 15 minutes.  Then it was time to board. The baskets are very deep and passengers have to climb into them.  Accommodations for those with injuries or special needs can and were made; the crew provided extra time and assistance for those who needed it and the rest of the passengers were patient and understanding, too. Having flown before, I knew being in the basket would be close and we were but not sardined in nor was it uncomfortable. Of course, Colorado people have to be some of the friendliest, happiest people I have ever met, so that helped, as did the crew's cheer and enthusiasm.As we prepared for take-off, my friend Melissa got to help run the burners.

The flight itself was amazing! I just don't have words. It was amazing to see Boulder and environs from the air and the view of the mountains was breathtaking. It was intriguing to see airplanes from Boulder Municipal taking off BELOW us.  Our altitude ranged from 4,000 to 9,000 feet. The ride is smooth and quiet and there's really no sense of motion. It's lovely and peaceful. Jeff was ready and willing to answer questions and provide information but he wasn't overly chatty or tour-guide-y, he just let everyone experience the ride for themselves. I liked that and it's the mark of a true pro. He knows he doesn't need to sell it, the experience speaks for itself.

Our landing was smooth and uneventful.  The chase vehicles were already waiting for us, with bottles of cold water, which was welcome.  Again, passengers were encouraged to participate with the tear-down and packing of the equipment and it was fun to watch/do.

Once we returned to the launch site, we were given goodie bags. I won't disclose the contents, so I won't ruin the surprise for future balloonists, but I will say it was nicely done.  Check-out was quick and easy because everything was set up and ready to go for us. A few hours later, a thank-you email arrived from Jeff along with a couple of photographs of my group.

I cannot say enough good things about this company. Highly recommended. I'm glad I went with them. My family is visiting in mid-July and if there are reservations available, we will be planning to ride with Fair Winds again!

Can you believe that there is a Goodwill Outlet Store?
I love this place.  I don't go often but I always find some treasures.  I have been buying canvas grocery shopping bags there for a while.  The heavier ones are $1.50 and smaller ones are 50 cents.  I talked them down on the price one time and now that WFM sells cool bags for 99 cents, I think Blue Hanger should reconsider the $1.50  price.
The people watching is beyond compare.  Watch the crowd grow at the back of the building as the trucks back up to the loading dock to unload the piles of new stuff onto long tables.  The back tables are cordoned off by tape until the tables are full and then just watch the frenzy (that is really an accurate description) as the shoppers claw and paw through the stuff.  The experienced shoppers are identified by their gloves.  You never know what you will find - you get no treasures without some grimy work. I have gotten decorative iron work for the deck that is very cool.  I saw a man collecting legos and I helped him pick out pieces from the bin.  You'll find clothes, dishes, electronics, games, books, CDs , furniture holiday stuff- just about anything and everything.  I almost gave it 4 stars - but if it was any cleaner and nicer, it just wouldn't be the same.  It is perfect just the way it is.

I have been seeing Dr Thoreson for several years. I am entirely pleased with my care and the entire experience in his office. He identified and successfully treated a mystery condition where my knees were popping out of alignment when I turned over in bed. I always find him a cheerful good listener and he addresses several of my concerns in one encounter. I NEVER feel rushed. He even laughs at my jokes. When I raise a new issue, he typically describes the most recent research, which I find reassuring. 

Recently, I asked him to decide which of three practitioners I should see about doing prolotherapy, which he does, on my knee. To my amazement, he suggested I see the doc who had earlier successfully done prolo on the other knee. This was a further indicator that he has my interests at heart. 

I like and have a pleasant relationship with everyone at the office, and am never kept waiting. 

What more can I say?

I love the Canada Line. It's amazingly convenient and takes you (almost) right into departures at YVR.

This station in particular has lots of stairs. There are elevators but you have to switch between two (the first elevator is on the outside, the other is inside the Fare-Paid Zone). It's just as clean as any other Canada Line station, which is impressive for public transit.

Annoyingly, this station (along with many others on the Canada line) installed non-operational FareGates prematurely by ONE WHOLE YEAR. Seriously, what's the point of having a bunch of posts that do nothing except slow down foot traffic..? I understand a few weeks, maybe even a month or so...but a whole year? Come on.

The connections to surface routes is also not very good from this station - all there is in the immediate vicinity is the community shuttle to English Bay (C21). That being said, most things near the station are easily accessible on foot, the Granville buses are only a 5-7 minute walk away, and City Centre (the next station north, which is much closer to all the buses and shopping) is only an extra minute or so on the train anyway.

I've been using Ceci's maids a little over 6 months now for monthly cleaning, with the occasional extra. We recently bought a new house and had scheduled a move-out clean of our old place but ended up needing a move-in clean for our new home as well. Sylvia was able to accommodate me the very next morning and they did a great job. 

They have consistently been on time (which is huge considering some of the experiences I've had with past companies I tried) and always have a team of at least 2, if not 3 people. They are thorough and efficient and friendly. Bonus points for invoicing and online billing! Definitely recommend.

5 stars hands down! Our car was broken into and the thief attempted to hot wire our Honda. They were unsuccessful thank goodness but the car was not driveable. USAA hooked us up with Kadels in Woodstock who gave us great service from day one. Giving us daily updates on the status of repairs, detailed estimate from the beginning, courtesy tow/pick up, even fixed our broken AC for free. Not to mention the nice detail job at the end. Great experience and I would go back there in a heartbeat!

nope nope nope.....on the surface of it they appear great, caring, modern, but after the veneer wears off watch out. The lower level staff are genuinely kind, but the nurse supervisors and higher are a nightmare. They don't return calls or emails (after handing you their business cards) and have an aggressive attitude toward family members. I think it must be a difficult and stressful environment to work in, but for the money families are paying, you have the right to expect respectful treatment for both you and your family members. My grandma is there now but we are looking for a new place for her.

First off, Townshend's, in my opinion, makes the BEST kombucha out there.  I have been to two Townshend's tea houses (one in Eugene and the Alberta Street location reviewed here), and each has a distinctly different "vibe".  The Alberta street location is QUIET, quieter than a church quiet.  I went with my son, and we both left early because we felt uncomfortable talking to each other as our voices were the only sounds to be heard.  This location is pretty small compared to the Eugene location, but the teas are absolutely top-notch!  We opted for a peach tea with vanilla and a tarragon sprig, which was outstanding!!!  The flavors seemed to evolve over the course of consumption, which was a very enjoyable experience.

There are a huge variety of teas available: hot, cold, boba drinks, tea blends to help soothe ailments, etc.  Each is outstanding.  Also on tap is their kombucha.  They also sell growlers so you can take some home with you.  There are also pastries and baked goods available.

Definitely stop in for a great refreshing beverage, or a nice soothing tea.  It is a great place to do so!

I was very pleased with the cleaning job Michael did on our carpet! My house smelled wonderfully fresh and clean afterwards, and the carpet was dry within 2 hours! The only reason I didn't give 5  stars was there seemed to be a little confusion when Michael arrived bringing back a rug Kiwi had cleaned, he had not been informed that I wanted him to clean carpets when he delivered my rug back. He said "no problem", and he happily cleaned my carpet! I will definitely use Kiwi again!
Linda Schultz
Georgetown, TX

The decor and band were great, it's not just another restaurant trying to do cultural food, it's really Peruvian. 

I had the pisco-rita which was great and really tasted like both drinks mixed together. 

We started with the special ceviche which was made with fish, and no shellfish, which was my impression of what ceviche is normally. It was delicious and had a great orange colored sauce that still tasted like lime.

I then had the pasta with basil and spinach sauce which was delicious. My friend said she had it before at another place and it was creamy which I didn't miss. That makes the pasta healthy, right?

The owner/manager came over and talked to us to be sure that everything was perfect, which it was. He guessed everything that we were eating and drinking as well, so I know he is there often.

Only four stars because the Fantasyland reconstruction was taking place when we went, so a lot felt like it was missing. But all around, I am shocked at how good a time we have when we come. Another reason for one less star, is that a couple of the rides stopped in the middle, numerous times (Haunted House and Peter Pan).

Our family has a tradition that we always go to the Thunder Mountain train I finally got to go on the revamped Haunted House ride which was shut down for remodeling back in 2007 when I last came. It was a lot of fun!

I wish there were some nicer dining options for the price. For example, there are lots of great healthy snacks and other yummies, but when it comes to healthy meals it's not so easy. We ate lunch at the Tortuga Inn and the burritos where just this hard huge flour tortilla with a little rice and beans inside that tasted rather insipid. Try using whole grain tortillas, and flavor the rice and beans a little like Chipotle does.

The only things I felt were overpriced were the meals. The five-park pass and the merchandise seemed reasonable for the most part.

There's lots of photo opportunities with the spontaneous parades, character meet and greets, and other events going on all day.

For children of all ages. Always a good time.

Need a new Dental Office? This is the place to go. Modern and Professional but with the kindness and care you would expect from a much smaller office. You can tell they are a busy office but I was seen on time and Dr Buechele and his assistant Tina spent time with me and I never felt rushed. It took me over a year to find my new dental home because it had to be the right place. I worked in the dental field for 25 years so I was a bit picky. Can't say enough positive things about this Dental Office.

Really delicious beer, I mean really good (and I go to a lot of breweries) they have a nice outdoor area but the place was packed (for socially distancing standards) it was also a hot day and only the outside was open. Once everything opens up and we can go inside and more tables are set up this will be an awesome brewery!!!   Atlanta area has some really great breweries but based on taste alone, I would say this is one of the top breweries. We sampled 4 or 5 different samples and they were all really good! We stuck to the IPA and even got some to go.   Well done brewer!!! We will be back!

I had an absolutely delightful Experience at this picturesque old world style restaurant. We tried the escargot which I found to be a treat to the taste buds. We also tried the steak tatare- it was phenomenal. We tried this place this past Tuesday, therefore their special for the night was a grilled char which we both found to be cooked superbly. The staff was also super friend. Our server was very attentive. I also had a weekender bag with me which they were more than happy to store for me. Great date night spot!!

Host is extremely rude and unprofessional. I witnessed this with another gentleman last week  And I should have spoken up when I saw this, until I witnessed it myself. Seating is unprofessional, this manager is also condescending and pushy. You need someone who can control the situation at the restaurant better, not this sleazeball. Please change management! He is a middle aged man, short in stature. Must suffer from little man syndrome or something. I think his name is Kintaro or Kataru or something?

I had to write this.  I normally receive gifts like this and am so disappointed as they never seem to be very good.  But my sister sent us the Texas sampler popcorn big tin today and we just opened it and i can't stop eating it.  All 3 flavors included are wonderful. My husband, daughter and I all said this is definitely something to bookmark to send to others and to buy again for ourselves.  I am so impressed with the quality of the popcorn and the flavors.  Not to mention the tin with the 2020 Yelp review logo is a keepsake from this awful 2020 covid pandemic year. I'm not sure how she even heard about them as this is a Austin, Texas company and she lives in Orlando, Florida.  I'm going to find out.

I was lucky enough to be able to visit this museum during my trip to SXSW this year.  This museum is one of my favorites.

Most impressive is the European Art Collection that is anchored by many inspiring works of art from the Suida-Manning Collection.  I spent hours in the European Art section and still didn't give it enough time.

There were many other fine pieces of art, but it was the European Art that appealed the most to me.  I highly suggest you visit this museum if you are in Austin.

Will I return?  You bet, there are many other pieces from the Suida-Manning Collection I haven't seen yet!

Had not been around to the Spur until I stopped by with friends after a movie at the Paramount. The space is very large, and the patio features a sun screen, a shaded area with furniture, and misters for when it is hot outside, which it was today. While style of bar and the crowd is not exactly the most appropriate fit for my personality type, I have to say that the staff is decent, generally nice, and the overall time I had there was quite good. On this particular Sunday afternoon, the special was $1 drafts, which means I can stamp out my sorrows and otherwise uninteresting others get a WHOLE LOT more interesting for less that $5.00. That's a value!

I love waffles and always have waffle at college commons. Most of the time I can only have American style waffle, which is also very great, and I love eating plain waffle just with maple syrup on it. However, I fell in love with the Belgain style waffle at the first time I tasted it here and it was totally mind-blowing. I got the plain one with some sugar powder on the top of it, which is crisper and sweeter than the American waffle. It was a brand new experience and Taste of Belgium is the perfect place for waffle fans.

Rated a 5 because the food was amazing, but also the customer service was outstanding! Some in our party have food allergies and the kitchen manager came to table side to specifically review appropriate options and further researched nutritional information and provided a print out! The wine recommendation was excellent and the waiter offered to bring the bottle out so I could take a picture for future personal opportunity. We had a nice chat on wine so he showed me the top rated wine and again let me photo for personal purchase. The service excellence really gave us a wonderful dining experience!

Ah, possibly the best place to eat in Vancouver.  I'm biased as I'm just a big fan of public markets, but not only can you find some awesome native Canadian fare here (albeit a little tourist-y), but some slamming never before seen items. Did somone say: "Vancouver's Hottest Sea Salt"? and"Sea Asparagus"?  And "Goldenberries" (along with other fresh, fresh produce?)  

As an avid lover of Italian food, I almost peed in my pants when I saw the great Italian speciality shops with the world's tastiest fresh, handmade pasta. All shapes and sizes!  Rigatoni, cavatelli, ravioli.. you name it. It's there. Yum.  

You can come to get gourmet coffee, teas, spices, and even authentic Cowhan (cowhan?) cutting boards- made of the nicest wood ever. These are like $80 though so it's better just to admire then. These were sold about my favorite shop-- don't remember the name (sorry!) but since I'm a way out of towner from NYC, I really enjoy the native Canadian stuff. Birch syrup, and all kinds of different jams.  Ironically they also had some frozen take out Vij's here. Ha (see my commentary on that, elsewhere in this list). 

On the other end of the market (near the entrance) from presumbly where you parked, be sure not to miss the seafood shop. You can go crazy with salmon- all kind of smoked, sockeye salmon, wild, etc- they have salmon lasgna. Yum. Not always the biggest salmon fan but I like anything in pasta.   This shop also had by far, the biggest oysters I've ever seen- born and raised in Vancouver, BC. 

Anyway, after you shop till you drop, you can go to the back corner to get some lunch. And you should.  In this area, there is a place where you can get a flaxseed salmon roll- healthy AND tasty. I don't remember where this corner store was but it was right across the eating area by the exit out to the Aquabus.  The best spot to pick up lunch though is the little place called "A la Mode" which has Pacific Salmon Pie, but more importantly- NEW ENGLAND CLAM CHOWDER POT PIE.  Beef pot pie, chicken (blegh), and the corn chowder among the options but none compared to this.  Perfectly hot, flasky crust with a great gooey dough consistency that mixes well with the soup.  Thick, creamy and fattening is how this chowder tasted. Excellent. My only complaint is that there could have in fact been more clam- but perhaps the ingridients were so well mixed in that it was just super blended.  

It's true farmers' markets always cost a little more.  But, I would pay a premium for these locally grown, high quality ingredient if only there was the infrastruture in NYC!

I have had a mystery illness for a couple years now.  I found this place by what I would like to think is divine intervention.  I thought maybe a massage would at least ease the tension in my back.  I didn't know what Thai Massage was until I looked it up on my way to my appointment.  I knew it would not work for me with the amount of pain I was in.  So when I got there I had explained it to Nephyr.  She asked me many questions about my health.  She tried a different massage technique on me to see if that would help ease the pain.  It was amazing.  I kept going back to her as she was the only one who could relieve my symptoms.  I am very grateful that I have found her.  I would tell anyone that has an illness or pain that they can't figure out to go and try Thai Massage and see what happens.

Sorry, but this place stinks!  We arrived at 5:00PM, there was one other customer. We ordered at the same time as the other table and they had eaten and gone (after receiving their order wrong) before we even got our food!  It took 45 minutes to get our food, they screwed up the order, screwed up the bill and the portions were small.  Especially the kids portion fish were the size of two pinky fingers, just a couple bites for a 4-year-old!  Food was okay, nothing spectacular.  I thought the chips were far from crispy.  We had to go home and have a second meal to fill everyone up!  Maybe they were having a bad day, seems like the kitchen was really goofing up, but it's not worth $25.00 to take that risk again.

Cool place, with a lot of holistic remedies. Valerie was professional, knowledgeable, and welcoming. She was able to squeeze me in last minute for cryotherapy and a float. The entrance might be a little difficult to find (just a nondescript door), but once you enter, the atmosphere is completely changed. The spa was very clean and relaxing. It is located below street level and very spacious. I had only used a float pod before and had issues with getting too warm towards the end. The room-style float they offer was much better for me and I had no issues with any salt water getting on my face/eyes. They also offer a host of other services, like an infrared sauna and massage. If I was local, I would definitely be coming back in and trying more services. This place would be a great gift to give someone needs some relaxation (maybe a massage followed by a float?). I really enjoyed my experience and will back if given the opportunity.

My husband and I had a difficult time making a final choice to purchase a car for our graduating high school senior. When we arrived at Global Mini, we parked and anticipated the typical pouncing that happens when a customer pulls into a car dealership. However, as we exited our car, we were greeted after a few minutes of casual meandering on the lot. When we were approached, we were greeted with a friendly smile and were treated with respect. Peter, our salesman, was not pushy and asked us multiple questions to ensure he was able to show us exactly what we were looking for. Our entire experience was followed with a similar experience. We have purchased many cars over our 20 year marriage, but have never felt so at ease with the process. Peter was extremely attentive, but never pushy. He only showed us what we were looking for and offered a plethora of information about Mini's and made us feel he was very knowledgeable. If we have success in owning a Mini Countryman, then we will definitely purchase another one...but only from Global Mini.

Another yelp success story!  

Anne and Jess have a great practice in a lovely old building in Copley square.  Note:  It does not say acupuncture for everyone, but its housed in the "community church" building next to the World restaurant.  

They operate on a sliding scale, and are so accommodating to wonky schedules!  There are evening times and day times available, and the online registration is really awesome - just sign up for an open time and its yours!  They send email reminders for your appointments (but only if you want them :).  

If you are interested in acupuncture, go to them.  If you're a little skeptical of acupuncture, go to them.  They're very reassuring people, who are genuinely interested in treating whatever you need treated, without any judgement.  And thats so refreshing and rare.

My husband and I was visiting my old hood when suddenly he wanted something sweet.  It was chilly out so we just steppedin the first place we saw.  Got the Chocolate Chip and Flourless Chocolate cookies - AMAZINGLY GOOD.  

We first took a bite of the chocolate chip..... Crisp on the outside, chewy inside - just how we like it!  It had a hint of peanut butter with sugary butter and chunky choco chip goodness.  Here we thought that was good, then we had the flourless chocolate cookies, OMG.  Sooooo gooood.

I have to admit ,I kind of hate Natura.

It's an excellent idea, and the service is good, the employees are friendly, the beers are delicious and so are the hookahs.

My problem with it is the size. This place is just way too small for the number of people that frequent it. Many times I've gone there when you can hardly even walk from the back to the front. 

And the crowd is mostly stuck-up UCF kids.

So, I would say, if you're going out early with a big group of friends, Natura is a great place. But don't go there to meet people.

A complete rip-off. My check engine light came on, so I called here and they said they could run a diagnostic for me without an appointment. Great! I bring it in. They say I have to leave it for at least 2+ hours AND they charge $99 just for the diagnostic! 

I may not know how to fix cars, but I am the daughter of a mechanic, so I know when I'm being ripped off. I went to MacKenzie right down the street and had an answer in less than 5 minutes. See my review for them as well :)

They did a drainage project in the front yard to help with water runoff in my front yard, which they did, but it did not help at all. I called and the next summer they did a low point drain under the house, built a retaining wall and filled it and re did the yard. That looked nice but that should have been done last year and without the drainage in the front yard and water from rain in the winter and water from sprinklers drain into the street and create a slimy green creek bed in the street year around, so it actually made the problem worse and cost me many thousands of dollars.  A few years later I am selling my house so the buyer had it inspected and found that the low point drain they did in the foundation was done wrong. They built trenches right next to and up against the base of the foundation, which could case erosion under the foundation. The trenches should have bee away from the foundation and back fulled with dirt and gravel or should have drainage pipe and gravel per the inspection. So instead of fixing a problem they have created a problem!!!

We had our backyard done with Kerry and his crew, and they were an absolute pleasure to work with from beginning to end. He is extremely hard working and is a true professional.  He was constantly updating me on the progress of the work which my husband and I really appreciated. We have a large backyard and everything was done to perfection, from the irrigation, to the stonework, to the sod, finally to the follow-ups. We have recommended him to a number of our neighbors and wouldn't hesitate to recommend him to anyone on yelp! Thank you Kerry!

My husband and I decided to celebrate our 20th wedding anniversary at the Melting Pot. Since neither of us had ever been there, and since we both love fondue, it was obvious that's were we wanted to dine. The experience was great! Our table was set with rose petals, a candle, and a hand made card. We were sat in a very secluded corner that was set perfect for our occasion.  They even took our picture and bbn printed it for us as a keepsake. 
We tried the 4 course meal and it was so good. From the phone call confirming our reservation, to the very end of the evening, the service and hospitality was on point! Our server was outstanding. We will definitely be returning!

After I was quoted $575 for a front brake pad and rotor replacement, and $112 for a brake fluid flush, I was referred to Tony at Sun Auto. I called for a quote on a Monday, and on Tuesday, I was in the shop getting these items fixed. He was able to do both for $413, a $275 save for me. I stayed in the shop while they did the maintenance (free wifi and Dunkin' Donuts next door), expecting to be there for a good 2 hours. However, I was in and out in an hour and a half and on my merry way. Recommend to anyone looking for an honest quote and good fix! Thanks Tony!

We threw a 40th birthday party for my husband at the Cheshire Bridge location. It was AMAZING, and I cannot express how thankful I was for all of the hard work Alfredo ,and his entire team put into the party. The venue itself is a beautiful building with a lot of space, and a wrap around balcony on one side. We were able to bring in a ping pong table to the space, and there was still plenty of room for tables, chairs, open bar, photo booth, and DJ with large dance floor. Every single person that came to the party was blown away, and I'm so happy we chose Knock Music House. Thank you again Alfredo, Simone, and the entire team!

I really wish Yelp would allow me to rate 0 stars.  I do not usually give negative reviews unless there are extreme circumstances and I consider this to be exactly that.  I need to get a preventative maintenance rebuild of a supercharger done on my jet ski. I called Woods late last year and was quoted around approximately $500. I didn't end up getting the service done then so got a new quote three weeks ago while getting quotes from 5 local shops to see who was priced best while also taking into account their service record/reviews.  I spoke to Michael at Woods and he said he didn't know but would check and call me back. He called back and said it would be about $550-600 depending on parts.  I knew it was peak season so the increase was expected. I called back three weeks later and told him who I was and he said he remembered me and I mentioned his quote and made an apt for the following week. A day later I decided to call to see how long the service would take and during the conversation with Michael, I asked to confirm a price to see if it would be closer to $550 or $600. He said he needed to speak to his technician and get back to me. He emailed me a written estimate two days later (keep in-mind this interaction never would have happened before the repairs were performed if I hadn't called back to see how long the repairs would tak) for $1200. He said he quoted it wrong and made a mistake and I mentioned that I was given a similar quote twice and made an appointment based off that and that I wasn't happy with the change and needed to speak to the manager.  This was Monday and he said the manager was out sick and the foreman was out too but he would talk to him and get back to me.  I called again Tuesday (this was the day I was supposed to have my appointment if they didn't double the price) to see if he heard anything and he said he was still out. I told him to please keep me informed but he said I should hear back soon. I emailed the main service email address Wednesday asking for the manager and shop foreman's contact information as I had decided that this shady individual was going to continue jerking me around and I need to speak to someone higher up. Its Friday now and I haven't received an email or a phone call from them and all I can get when I call is an indefinite hold in their service dept and try to reach the manager. 

If you want to deal with dishonesty and poor service, I recommend you give these guys a call!

We HIGHLY recommend Verbena Floral. Initially, we decided to only have personal flowers done by a florist and emailed a couple while planning from Houston. Neither responded so our day-of coordinator set up a meeting with someone else, but she couldn't come in within our budget. We were strongly considering DIY at that point, but wanted to talk to one more florist first so went to Austin Flower Co. during a weekend visit to Austin three months before our wedding to investigate prices for DIY and asked them for a florist recommendation. Verbena was their recommendation and is around the corner so we walked over to say hello and pick up some info. That 5-minute drop-in was our only in-person meeting.

LuAnn was happy to do just the small amount we wanted (bridal bouquet, 3 small bridesmaid bouquets, 2 mom's corsages, and 7 boutonnieres) for our October 2013 wedding. Working with LuAnn was a breath of fresh air in the wedding planning process! She came in under our $500 budget for personal flowers and after just two phone calls and some email exchanges in which she patiently answered all of my questions, made great suggestions and was just generally fun to talk to, the flowers were beautiful and *exactly* what I had envisioned!

I've been to the East side location of Buenos Aires many times and have loved everything I've had. Ever. A friend and I stopped in for breakfast this morning and grabbed coffee & a dulce de leche croissant, which was incredible. 

The lunch menu is solid as well. Their hot and cold vegetarian sandwiches are just right - you feel satisfied but not too full that you'll go into a food coma for the afternoon. :) And, their spinach salad is perfect, with candied pecans and great dressing. Highly recommended.

Stop in for a lunch with friends or a romantic date - the atmosphere is great for both.

I did not expect to see any whale since they had that clause saying they were not responsible if none were seen.  However, I say plenty.  Of course, it was mostly backs and tails.  One actually jumped out.  I wish I got that shot.

Keep in mind, most of the trip is traveling there and that part is BORING.  The boat kept on shifting left and right, front and back.  My fiancee ended up getting sea sick.  So, don't bother if you cannot handle the sea.  Don't go without a sweater since the ride there is chilly regardless how warm the weather is.  Bring a fancy camera because the whales are very far.  Get a indoor seat until you arrive.  The ride there is more than 50% of the trip so getting the best view is not your first priority.  People starts crowding there anyway.  The best part is the front of the ship since the captain will shift the ship toward the whale so that their photographer can take close up shots.

I always feel like I'm catching a flight when I go to this practice.  Expect long lines, an expectation you will arrive long before your appt just to get thru check in (it seems they don't want to hire adequate support staff), impersonal treatment , treatment primarily by PA's, and a burned out dr or two.  The surgeons will only spent a nano second with you.

I have multiple issues going on.  After taking my ortho biz elsewhere years ago, I got referred back to them.  It's the same old airport I remember.  I was adequately treated for a foot issue.  By adequately I mean, not particularly well but not poorly either.

I saw my internist soon after getting out of a cast for my foot.  I was still limping due to pain in my hip.  He said I had bursitis in my hip and needed an injection.  I mentioned this to the physiatrist at my next appt. He told me to wait a month and see how I feel.  I decided to email my spine physiatrist at Spaulding for his thoughts.  He scheduled me for an injection under fluoroscope.

Then I developed a knee issue, no doubt, also from being in a cast and I decided to go elsewhere.  Strangely enough, the new ortho office (New England orthopedics) was serene, the front desk staff smiled and joked with me, the wait was minimal, the new doctor was super nice and didn't act like he'd just taken amphetamines, nor did he seem burned out.  Better still, he was not preceded by a PA.  I actually got to see the doctor AND he acted like he was listening to me, responding accordingly.  

I have traveled enough in my life that I don't care for the airport experience with my healthcare.  I'll finish up with the hand guy and likely ask my spine physiatrist if he knows someone good for feet if my foot issues continue.

In case anyone is keeping score, I just described 4 potential lost revenue streams:  foot, knee, hand and bak altho to be fair, they will likely retain hand.

(sigh) How did Elephant Walk get such high ratings?

A small group of us went with a restaurant cert because we'd read such fantastic reviews about the place.  "Cambodian cuisine" was a key reason why we came here, too.

We made reservations and were seated promptly enough.  The main entree menu consists of around 40 items: 5 each of  Original and Traditional Khmer and French recipes.  (The original recipes are those created by the chefs).  They also have soups, salads, and vegetarian entree options: http://www.elephantwalk.com/boston/menus/EWBOS_dinnermenu.html

I ordered the poulet a la citronelle and the beau had the poulet malika.  I won't say that the food wasn't good; it was decently made and a decent portion, too. It's just that I think the prices were kind of steep, considering what we were getting... it was pretty much regular food to me - chicken and rice.  

For some reason, after we'd presented our cert to our waiter, he did not wait on us as much any more.  I asked for some lime a few times before he actually got it (toward the end of my meal).  

When we were done eating and ready to pay, he brought us the bill - miscalculated, as he didn't take our cert into account.  We sent the bill back for him to correct.  I don't remember how long that took, but it seemed like a long time.  He brought back the bill, corrected.  We were ready with the credit card but he kept looking at us and walking right by, even though it was pretty obvious that we were ready  - the bill was at the edge of the table with a credit card sticking out.  

After he passed by about 4 times and then stood around his cashier station a few minutes, we decided to pay in cash rather than credit because who knows how long it would take him to bring back the receipts to be signed.  So we just left cash on the table, and went.  

When you don't like your customers, don't you just want to get rid of them?  I would.  i don't understand why there was such a change of heart, but after waiting forever to be "waited on", I give this dude a D for service because he was such a jackass.  

That alone is enough to make me not want to return, but the steep prices for regular food also contributes as a reason.

Came into this location to purchase stamps for my Christmas cards.  The speed of getting to the counter was decent; however, the gentleman that help me with my transaction was just horrible.  Never acknowledged me and stood there waiting for me to ask the question.  I asked for stamps and it looked liked it pained him to walk a few steps to get the binder they were in.  There was a gentleman behind me in line who clearly knew the postal man.  They exchanged conversations with each other (talking about retirement and how they were looking forward to it)!!  All this while I was the customer at the counter.  Plain rude!! I'll stick with my little post office in Kyle!

This is a fantastic family business.  At the last minute, I ordered 29 t-shirts for a family reunion, giving A Better T-Shirt only a week's time to complete the order.  They worked with me on the design and the shirt sizes and quality one Friday afternoon and a week later, on a Friday, I picked up the finished product.  All the shirts looked great and my family members were pleased.  The prices were better than online T-Shirt companies, by the way.  I wish I could post our pic of everyone wearing them!  Maybe this link will work.  http://lindsaywaite.shutterfly.com/pictures/242#%26emid%3dsite_tagginginvite%26cid%3dSHARE3SXXXX

On a rainy Sunday I trekked to Richmond Ikea from the Island, ready for a furniture-buying frenzy. I'd spent hours on the Ikea site, noting model numbers, colours, and taking measurements in my apartment. I even called Visa to alert them to a large purchase imminent. I was loaded for bear.
I expected to walk in, confirm my selections, make the purchase, and arrange for Saturday delivery.
Oh, how wrong I was. Here's what really happened. 
The sofa I wanted was out of stock, and I wasn't allowed to pay for it before it arrived. 
You can't pick your delivery date. Ikea picks it, depending on what day you bought your stuff. Their delivery window is 9am-9pm and no, they can't narrow that down. So be prepared to take a day off work and wait at home for twelve hours. (Ikea's website does not mention any of this)
Ikea's suggestion: call the store Tuesday when the sofa was scheduled to arrive, ask them to hold it, then make another three-hour trek to Richmond that night after work, and make the purchase in person. And of course, the sofa's arrival was not guaranteed, meaning I might have to go back the next Tuesday and try again. Assuming the sofa wasn't sold out again.
In the worlds of Dr. Evil, riiiiiight.
To be fair, the Ikea rep who helped me, Karen, was friendly, knowledgable, and apologetic for all the complications. But I still wasted a full day with almost nothing to show for it but some curtains. I couldn't find any of the smaller items I needed, and the store was so packed with people who apparently only just learned how to walk that morning, I gave up and left.
So, Ikea, Instead of spending thousands at your store I spent only fifty bucks. But I guess you're so big and successful, you don't need my money anyway.

Deco (Claudia, James, & Peggy) took customer service to a whole new level that the "other" large, well-known company I narrowed search to could not come close to accomplishing...& I tried...twice!

Choosing Deco was easy b/c I wanted to spend my $ where it was not simply competitive pricing, but where I was made to feel like a valued customer.  Claudia was knowledgeable, helpful, easy going, always a smile & nice laugh, and incredibly patient!

Peggy & James encompass the same qualities, but Claudia was my rock.  

A warm, inviting, positive experience w/ Deco topped off w/ James, Claudia's husband, coming on time & took care of the installation's subtle details.  James ensured I was very satisfied before leaving, n reminded me to please call if I needed anything. 

Product:  no triple cell blinds nor "timeless" shutters others push for resale b/c they limited what I wanted inside plus see outside via my 6 wall of windows & my choice, it's elegance & perks, & Hunter Douglas name make this a new timeless.

Vignette, Tiered Modern Roman Shades that give both up & down options for:     
      privacy, yet light in day even when all fully closed, more light based upon situation (bottom up or top down), or to fully see my lovely yard.  These have their own timeless elegance, Hunter Douglas name, & so much function that speak for themselves if I sell in next decade or more. 

Bonus was I no longer needed new windows b/c the heat gain coefficient in these particular shades improved my a/c bills n made my main living space more comfortable than my previous blind coverings I didn't like when buying my home.

Thank you Deco!!!

Terra Gallery is well-suited to the Olde Dublin downtown area. The gallery's owner, Jeff Hersey, is a real renaissance gent who has disciplines in metal sculpture, music and real people skills. There are many types and styles of art and design which Terra Gallery house.  One of the watercolor artists who regularly has he work there is Karen Groeniger. Small paintings and large paintings, both, can be viewed and purchased at Terra Gallery.

Popularity of Terra Gallery has allowed Jeff to expand the operation into the area which was once an olive oil distributor. The timing of the expansion couldn't have come at a better time with the new Bridge Street complex across the river coming along quickly.

Jeff/Terra Gallery continues to promote a Dublin gallery hop event with locals participating.  And there are some evening and weekend events such as a "Painting Night & Wine" that is sometimes offered.  Sounds like fun!   I would encourage everyone interested in art and design to pop-in to Terra Gallery and visit with Jeff.  The local artists will thank you and you'll thank yourself.

Do not let the spa like look & feel fool you. It looks nice here but they do not do quality work. I visited today & received a rush pedicure (my feet do not feel as if I got a pedicure today) & I had to instruct the man how to do my fill-in (shape all the nails the same, do not pretend he doesn't see the bubbles in the nail polish, there should be a top coat). I was 1 of a few people with an issue. After telling the man I did not want him to attempt to polish my nails again because it would have been his 4th time he said something to the manager & when she came over he threw my hand at her. She grabbed a nail file (not sure how filing helps the issue which was the entire nail was not polished) & I told her I didn't want her to try to fix it for the 2nd time. She walked off with an attitude, I assume pissed that the day was starting off so terribly (she had already called the cops on a customer who did not want to pay for a job they did not finish). I will never step foot in this shop again & I suggest you do not either.

It is now 724, I left the shop around 2, & the gel polish on my nails is coming off.

Returned Monday & they kindly fixed my nails but they (4) chipped Tuesday so I had to go back again. I almost want to give 2 stars because they were very nice both times & the manager kept asking if I was happy with the fix but I shouldn't have had to return 2 days in a row. Chipped again Wednesday, I don't know what the hell the problem is with the polish/top coat, but I refused to go back.

My Mother wanted to get her fence redone. She asked around to a few of the neighbors to inquire what company they had recently used and how much they charged. She was not satisfied with those companies. 

She found Luciano's Landscape on the BBB website. They checked off all of her boxes and even let her pay in installments. The workers that performed the jobs were very professional and very friendly. 

A few weeks later, she called the phone # on the business card the owner gave her and it was his direct line. Both services that the company provided left my mother extremely happy. She plans on using them for the future and recommending them to everyone.

Meh. First off - the concept of F45 is bad ass. I love that. However, this gym has no good vibes. I showed up to start my week trial and felt super awkward. I ask the coach to explain what was going to go on with the class (even showed up early to get the low down).  His response "you just do what the screens tell you to do". It was like pulling teeth to get more details (where do you start? How do you know when to start / stop? How do you know what's next?) 

Next class, same thing. Tried a different trainer - better but the coach from the previous class still didn't say anything to me even though he was there. 


Then, no follow up, no phone calls, no explanation of membership. I was very disappointed. 

Ended up going to a different F45 and joining there. So glad I tried a different gym. I didn't really feel welcomed at this one.

This is a good vet. Ask for Dr. Williams or Dr. Turner. I have had great experiences with both of these veterinarians. They really do take their time discussing anything that I have had questions on. I have taken my pup here since I first got her and have often come to the vet with a list of questions and each time, they have taken ample time to discuss the answers to my questions and my discussions.

While they are pricier than other vets around, I decided it was worth the money to go to them. Their normal operating hours are much longer than they are at other vets, so I can book vet appointments when they are convenient to me, 7a-9p M-F and they are even open on the weekends as well. 

I like that this is also the emergency vet. My pup was spayed there, and while it was more expensive than other vets that I researched, one night she was overly excited and popped a stitch in her belly and started to bleed. Had I taken her to a normal vet, I would have had to pay a very expensive emergency vet bill to have her seen that night. I called the vet and they told me to bring her right in, and there would be no fee. I also like how I can call them any time (day or night) and talk to a vet if I have a question about something my pup is doing.

The only reason that I did not give them that last 5th star is due to a negative experience I had with one veterinarian in particular, Dr. Phillips. My normal vet had gotten in an accident on the way to the clinic, and so they needed to have someone step into her place. Dr. Phillips was VERY short with me and didn't seem to listen to what I was asking/telling him. He took my dog back to get a shot (which normally only takes about 1 minute) and came back 30 minutes later saying that he was showing them something odd with her teeth... now I would have been fine with him using my pup as a teaching opportunity, but he did not bother to ask me if it was ok (which time time it was not as I was pressed for time). While he had my dog in the other room for show-and-tell, he also apparently ran some tests on her which I never authorized. He finally brought my dog back and told me he was going to get her paperwork he left in another room. He left for nearly another 30 minutes and when I finally popped my head out the door to ask where he went, another vet told me he was on the phone... rude. I was in such a rush and so angry when I left, I just signed the credit card receipt and left. It was a few hours later when I actually noticed the bill that I found the extra tests he had ordered (close to $100). I called the office, and they were extremely helpful. I told them about my frustrations, and they apologized, promptly gave me a credit on my account for the tests, and told me to call the main office the next day. I did and the office manager was also very helpful and sympathetic. 

Overall, I just know which veterinarian not to see, and will most definitely continue to go here. They offer services that no other vets around really seem to offer.

**** WARNING *** STAY AWAY
I was double billed and demanded refund. Instead my account was deleted and so was my $5,000 website. Customer service is India is a joke they do not understand nor comprehend the English language. There is no customer service and no help, you can not get through to anybody for help, circles and circles. I have been on 35 phone calls in the course of 10 days all to no avail.

Edit: In the end they finally heard my request and made things right.  Thank you !

Food: 2.5*
A Japanese joint run by Koreans.  I should've known better, but it's located conveniently close to my office.  Their selection of bento boxes & combos is small and the variety of rolls/nigiris is basic.  The food here is mediocre at best. The chicken donburi consists of chicken, rice, and teriyaki sauce. No egg, no onion, no vermicelli, nothing. The dynamite rolls are big but 3/4 of it is imitation crab meat. I can barely see the prawn tempura. Everything else is meh and uninspiring.

Ambiance: 3*
What the restaurant lacks in square footage it compensates by having high ceilings. Heh. It was recently renovated with new tables & chairs. The space is funky with orange accents everywhere, accompanied by some interesting art work on the wall.

Service: 2.5*
Self-serve. Order up front then they call out your number for pick up. The girls here are friendly and very accommodating with requests such as substituting different rolls in a bento box.

Value: 2*
For the amount of food, the price is decent, only because I am comparing to the many  overpriced Japanese restaurants in the downtown. But for the quality of food, and the fact that there is no table service.. not so much.

I had my first dress fitting session here. Dina was very attentive and helped me try on half a dozen different dresses. I let her pick out what she thought I might like, and she did a wonderful job keeping both my taste and my budget in mind. All the dresses I tried on were sold as store samples for around $900, but were in excellent condition and didn't need any corsets or petticoats. The price range is very reasonable compared to other boutiques in Boston. I ended up buying a dress elsewhere, but I still loved the ones I tried here.

I also met Ivy Ye, who gave me information on their wedding photography package. She also patiently explained to me what I should be aware of when choosing a venue, photographer and makeup artist, and I hadn't even booked her yet. They were also able to customize my photography package according to my needs, and the price is also good compared to other services I found online. I highly recommend them!

Shawndor, the handsome Hungarian Barista and host of the tiny coffee bar is quick, friendly and welcoming. He pulls one hell of an espresso and my stomach didn't react to it and I wasn't jittery either. They were playing great music too, taking the leap and trying this place was a good call. 

There is a good view of the street life walking past, but the best part of the tiny coffee bar is that it's size eliminates the people accumulation that happens downtown. Think about it, how many coffee shops in downtown Vancouver are cramped and crowded because of people sitting, spreading out their books, laptops, cables etc and staying until close. Tiny coffee bar solves this very Vancouver problem by structure. 

If you need to get out of the pool of people, rain and cars that is the Granville strip, you NEED to go to the tiny coffee bar. 

Fair prices and great snacks, but to the total opposite of what you might expect when it comes to space, mental physical or otherwise. If you want to relax at a coffee shop for a short amount of time and refocus, tiny coffee shop is literally overflowing with what you need.

On the one hand, you say to yourself, I'm sort of pathetic for being caught up in something as remote from the Real as high-end oil. On the other hand, I get crap at HEB or even Whole Foods that just isn't that good, and I wonder, why was the stuff I got everywhere when I traveled so good? It's because most olive oil is old, tainted, low quality, or both. The olive oil at Con' Olio is so good, I can't stop dunking my no-knead crusty bread in it. It's like being in Spain and sitting down at a small, great place and having everything be just perfect, you know?

Pool UPDATE:  Today, Dalton helped me out; and, my pool chemistry was in perfect condition. 
 I had a bunch of questions for Dalton, about variable speed pumps, installation, pool renovations and the like.  He was knowledgeable and very helpful.  I am so glad I stopped in, the scaling on the pool is completely gone, thanks to a nifty tool I picked up last week; and, the right pool chemistry working.  THANKS!
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
 Well, my pool chemistry is way out of whack, despite it looking clear and clean.  Had I not stopped in and had it tested, I'd be regretting the damage to my pool and equipment.  Not satisfied with the initial results, the tech brought in another person, to double and triple-check the results, before recommending an appropriate course of action, which I am beginning to implement today.  I plan to be back over the next couple of weeks, to make sure to get the pool chemicals right.  It's been on "auto pilot" for a few months, while I was recovering from an illness; but, I didn't know how bad it was.  I also picked up some equipment that had deteriorated over the winter; and, they had everything I needed - a small vacuum attachment, something to remove the calcium build-up; and, a replacement outlet. Service was very prompt, knowledgeable, and efficient, with a keen interest on my pool.  Glad I had some time to stop in!

Rolled in 8 people deep and wrapped ourselves around the wonderful stone bar. The drink/wine list was spot on and featured some favorite Hungarian wines and slivovitza (it turns you into a tiger). We had the salted cod dumplings that were soft but fluffy, with a hint of fish and the hangar steak medium - which was simple and perfect. Portions were modest and good for eating slowly, savoring and leaving room for desert. The bread pudding with creme freiche was out of this world. Servers were attentive as was the owner. Loved the light fixtures along the back banquette. Would be amazing if eventually they had brunch or breakfast as then it would probably become a local haunt (like my favorite Cafe Presse in Seattle). Lovely dining experience.

For one of my first outside of Vancouver trips, my partner and I went to Lynn Canyon to see the beauties of nature and to check out the Lynn Canyon Suspension Bridge. May not be as big as the Capilano Suspension Bridge, but it is free. I like free. The scenery is great and their are trails all over the area.  The best part of Lynn Canyon is the fact that you have the freedom to get off the trails and find places to just sit away from the crowds or get along the freezing water for a dip or in my case a toe to ankle step and get out immediately.  My favorite part was watching all the Asians in suits and shining black shoes / dresses and high heels and all the whites hiking in flip flops.  What the?!?!?. Okay, back to the bridge.  The views from the bridge are amazing.  The water is rushing below you, while the trees blow the trees.  I suggest you really hold on to your phone and cameras or else if you drop them, they are gone for good.

And as always, Have Fun!!!

(15/30)

Tasty lefse wraps. Did I know what they were prior to eating one, no. Did people rave about them on Yelp, yes. This is why I decided to give it a try. I'm very glad I did. I had read on some reviews they were on the small side so I decided to order two (there was a discount for this). I think people meant the sweet ones were small, because my two savory ones were very decent sizes and if I had realized I would have probably only ordered one. Oh well at least I got to try two different ones because of this. On this day there was a special chicken one that was very tasty but by far my favorite of the two was the meatball one. It was great. Definitely will have this next time. 

The people working the cart were very friendly and the wait was reasonable. In a pod with many great choices this is one of the top ones.

Don't sign a contract with company. My bill went up $80.00 per month. When I called to discuss I was told they are allowed to go up each year. What is the point of a contract. They did give me a $400.00 discount but that is only half the yearly increase. Contract is 3 years long and automatically renews if you don't cancel so if you do sign keep track of dates so you can opt out. Although they have bought out just about every other company out there, still a few small ones much cheaper for smaller companies to afford.

This was truly a sh*thole of place. Every surface was as grimy as possible, with the notable exception of the kitchen and the washrooms (thank god!). The shower was VERY slow. The rooms were dark, with very little sunshine. No well-accessible power outlets either. The bar downstairs would pump loud music late into the night. A party hostel... if you're into that. 

At 25 USD/night (35 CAD), that's what you get. On the plus side, you get a muffin and coffee for free at breakfast.

PS: I later moved to HI Vancouver Downtown, which was MUCH better in every possible way.

I didnt know I really liked dogs until recently (like the past year).  I have been entertaining the option of getting one over the past year or so, but I just havent found the perfect dog.

With that being said, the best place to get your "dog fix" is for sure Atlanta Humane Society.  This place typically has over 30 puppies waiting to be adopted.

I also like this place because all of the volunteers and staff are extremely knowledgeable and helpful which is a great value specifically when you dont know anything about animals/dogs.

Quiet as kept, sometimes i come here just to browse/hang out with the dogs....

Macao Restaurant is the new owner that takes over the Kam's Bakery & Restaurant at the same location on Main/ 8th. I was tempted to try it out because I heard the young chef was original from Macau & specializes in Portuguese cuisine. (FYI the distance between Hong Kong and Macau is 40 miles (64 km) over sea and the most common method of transportation is by ferry.)

I feel cozy and comfortable when l entered MR. Nothing really fancy but the ambience is accommodating, there are photos on the menu to help you make your choice. Price are reasonable and the portions are good. Most important of course is the rich taste of the food! I am pretty sure I shall be back for more :)*

One thing is you might need to be a bit patient as they are new and under staff, so the wait could be slightly longer...

LaRog is more than a Portland institution, it is friendly, knowledgeable staff who carefully listen to your needs.  We purchased my engagement ring 16 years ago and while looking at it on my finger several days later, I thought it looked like my great-grandmother's wedding band.  I took both in and Dave was so surprised that a vintage gold band matched so well to my new platinum ring.  He polished up my old ring and it became my wedding band.  Since then, each time I've taken my ring in to be cleaned and checked, whomever helps me is the epitome of professionalism and friendliness, something you don't often find in jewelry stores.  I would recommend LaRog Brothers to anyone.  Thanks!

Our family have been members twice at The Hills Country Club.  The staff is not responsive, horrible customer service.  We were given info about membership from Dana Barnett only worked there 11?years and Karen Deane is a nightmare, arrogant and completely by caring.  Both times we gave our 30 days notice after we sold our house to cancel membership and it took over 5 months the first time and this time 7 months.  The management structure protects their staff not members.  Do not move to where you are required to have their membership, the gym was shutdown for months our first time as members and then again the second membership the gym and bathroom inoperable.  It's a joke, all about their club benefits.

I called upon AIM when the buyer's inspection on our home in Buda indicated an issue with the AC.  I spoke with the young lady in the office and she scheduled  Jesse to go out and do the complete service for the following day.  Jesse found an issue, gave me a couple of options and effected the repairs on the spot.  I am almost sorry we have moved from the area.  AIM is my choice for heating and AC in the the Austin/Buda/Kyle area and I have passed the word to all of my friends who still live there.
Many thanks to all of the fine folks at AIM!

First time trying Russian food and I've to say I'm a fan!

The Herring "Under a Fur Coat" was very different from anything that I've had before. The acidic fermented beets and carrots complemented the saltiness of the fresh herring. The dish was made more substantial with boiled potato at the base of the tower and the boiled egg at the top. New and exciting!

We then had the Siberian Dumplings. Despite their small size, they were packed with flavors. Boiled, they were warm but the casing didn't lose its integrity and was fun to chew. The white sauce was buttery and creamy.

My favorite, and most surprising, dish of the meal was the Kachapuri which was essentially a grilled dough wrapped around kebab pieces and a generous amount of melty cheese. The dish looked simplistic but its flavors were out of this world! The complex sauce packed a lot of punch and had a nice blend of spices and heat; it paired very very wel with the cheesy Kachapuri. I loved loved this dish.

Kachka is a cool and contemporary spot for those who want to try Russian cuisine. You won't be disappointed!

This place is a little pricey compared to others around Boston, especially compared to the kiosks in malls. $12 for eyebrows and $10 for upper lips! BUT, Jana is amazing!! She understands the look I want for my eyebrows and cleans them up really nicely. She's also super fast but never careless. 

Multiple women work here and I made the mistake of going to a different one because Jana was out that day. Mistake!! I didn't catch her name but she threaded my eyebrows too thin and even created a bald spot under my left arch. Luckily my bangs covered it while it grew back out.

I'm giving 5-stars to Jana and would definitely recommend her to anyone.

TIP: They only accept credit cards for transactions over $20 so bring some cash.

I had been looking for a car for a while. Once I walked into this dealership I found myself blown away by the salesman Bernardo Vasquez who not only went above and beyond to find me the car that was perfect for me but also made sure I had the best deal that any other dealership wouldn't be able to offer me. The general manager Bart was more than kind and helpful and the finance process with Rusty Coffman and his red fish was smooth as possible. Great deal, great payments, great experience. 10/10 recommend this dealership!

Went zip lining with my mom and aunt today and we had such a great time! Our tour guides were Lizzie and Rebecca, they were awesome. Patient as we climbed up the long trail, explained everything, just really made it fun for everyone. 
Totally worth the money with really long zips and beautiful views of Lake Travis. I highly recommend! Reserve a spot online, it seems like it fills up, especially on the weekends. 
Make sure you weigh yourself before you go! The cut off is 250 and a guy that came in after us was over by 3 pounds and didn't get to go. He clearly was a weight lifter and said he weighs at home all the time and this scale was about 5 pounds higher, but they wouldn't let him go. Such a bummer if you've driven all the way out there!

the worst experience ever.
you have to hire better more knowable staff.
this guy Ryan H. so pushy and disrespectful. asking same questions over and over. apparently the poor kid got frustrated when he realized I knew I had other options. 
I have an excellent credit and was shopping around for better interest rate. keep the length of loan about the same and payment to be same or lower. how is this so difficult to understand? 
My 7 y/o has more skills than this guy.
I will never do business or recommend this rate genius company ever. 
thanks to your clever employee.

This place is great. It's in a beautiful old house on Everett street. There are saunas inside and outside on the secluded back porch are the hot tubs. It's a swimsuit-free kind of place and most nights of the week, it's open to both men and women. Tuesday nights, however,  are women only. You need to call ahead to reserve space. The best way to experience this place is to come with a group of friends and soak for the whole evening. Sometimes you'll have the place to yourselves, other times there will be a few other people there. It's a really comfortable and safe feeling environment though. If you really want to splurge, you can set up a massage before, after, or in the middle of your soaking session. I've always loved the idea of public bathhouses--like they have in China and Japan. I was so surprised to find a version of it here in Portland.

Well, up until a few months ago, I would have 1-2 starred TWC.

...but I gotta say...that changed recently.
Last month I decided that their recent price increase for substandard services and even worse customer service far from warranted the $100+ a month. So, I called customer service and was surprisingly met with a minimal wait time. I informed, cordially, that I would like to drop my cable service but retain my internet. When asked why, I was honest and told the CSR that I felt the price was way too high.

Surprisingly, he made me an "offer I could not refuse". He informed me that he was prepared to offer me regular (not digital) cable and maintain my current internet at a third of what I was paying. OK!!! Cable and internet for under $40. 

For once, TWC...you did me right!

This was our first stop at the Food Truck festival today. They had a huge pan of paella out front which was awesome! We had two beef empanadas and one chicken empanada with a side of fries. The empanadas were yummy! I tend to like my food a little crispy and one of the empanadas was a little darker and crunchier. It was my favorite . We liked the beef the best between the two. The fries were average but did have just the right amount of salt on them. The sauce was ok. I would definitely go back for the beef empanadas!!!

If you create any sort of event where you include baby animals... I'm signing up. Add in the fact that they climb all over you and you get to bottle feed them? What is this, heaven? Close enough, it's baby goat yoga at Wildflower Farm that they offer in the early spring. It's actually a legit yoga class but you can definitely just sit there and play with the goats if you want. 

The first thing you do is bottle feed the baby goats after they release them from their area, and boy do they really run into you with full force. Of course with the feeding you do have to watch out during class for some restroom usage... which did happen on someone's mat, but hey, who can get mad at baby goats? Plus they offer wipes for clean up and warned us beforehand. The goats will try to jump on you for pretty much the whole class, especially when you're in child's pose. They also like to chew on hair so watch out for that. I told my husband that this was one of the most fun things I've ever done. I will definitely be back next spring!

Went to Westside Market and saw the perfect little mirror. I was ready to make my purchase and BAM!!!  The cashier says we only take cards with a chip.  WTH!  Not only was I disappointed but I felt rejected and left out. My bank or credit card has not provided me with a card that contains a chip.  I was left standing there contemplating should I go get cash. But then I thought ... why inconvenience myself to spend money at Westside Market. I apologize to the owner of that booth who missed out on a sale.  But then again they probably didn't need my little money. Wouldn't it have been nice if they would have signs posted of this "policy". Did I mention I felt slighted.  Man I really wanted that mirror.  Oh well I'm sure there are other shops that offer a variety of ways to spend my money. Thank you Westside Market for being "exclusive"

Will not be returning. 

After 2 fun visits here previously, we had a bad experience with the floor staff and won't come back. Here are the reasons why: 1) My 9 year old daughter was scolded  in a pretty harsh voice for jumping near a coned area and made to cry by the woman on the floor. She was told that was for toddlers only and that this was her "one warning" and after that we'd be told to leave. There were no toddlers near the four tramps in the "coned area," they were running everywhere else. There was no signage about these rules even though the woman told my daughter and I to "go read the rules." 2) I talked to management about this woman's approach and that it was harsh and unnecessary and they said they'd speak to her about it, but that rules are at the discretion of the floor staff. I understand that, it makes sense, but the staff was pretty mean to my daughter without much reason. 3) I also asked if the toddlers are asked to stay within their boundaries and was told no, that toddlers/young children are guided at the discretion of their parents. However, the staff will give direction to older children and teens.We returned to the floor and the cones had been removed. (??)

This seems like a crazy policy or simply a lack of policy as the younger ones are bouncing off the walls without guidance and the older ones are trying to follow the rules. I think Altitude should have a universal policy to give guidance and/or warnings to trampoline users and their parents regardless of age or else they're going to see more accidents. 

Not more than 30 minutes later, a 3 year old boy ran directly into my daughter approaching her from behind, she had been was jumping up and down, alone, in a corner. The same floor monitor gave us a nasty look and carried the boy off the floor. The boy was fine and back out there on the floor a minute later, his father nodded to us that he was fine. My daughter was upset enough by the whole thing and asked me to take her home.  

This is unfortunate as she is conscientious and always looks around to see who may be in her way (or barreling toward her direction) but I don't want to pay for her to spend half her time not jumping  because of a number of kids on the floor at any given point that aren't well guided.

Needed a quick dinner option to go so I can head back to my hotel and finish up some work for the day. Honeygrow was in the neighborhood and had great reviews, so I stopped in. 
Upon walking in, their menu is nicely displayed on a chalkboard and there are several iPads set up to place your own ordered. The prompts are incredibly easy to follow. After you order, there is an old school number sign that will show your number as soon as your order is ready to be picked up at the window. 
I ordered the sesame garlic stir fry noodle bowl which was whole wheat noodles, braised beef, mushrooms, broccoli, scallions and sesame seeds. It carried very well to go. However it was very heavy on the sauce. I think it would have been better to go lighter on the sauce and get extra on the side if needed. They do have some available complimentary sauces I grabbed some sriracha and hoisin sauce as well. 
I also ordered a cup from their honeybar. This was obviously the star of the two items I ordered. The way this works is you select three fruits - I got pineapple, strawberries and blueberries. Then you select a honey or maple syrup - I ordered the wildflower honey. You then have the option to add two toppings - I went with dark chocolate chips and granola. This was a really fun after dinner treat. The fruit was incredibly fresh, the honey added a light sweetness, the granola brought crunch and the chocolate was a great surprise in every bite. Together this medley of flavors worked really well together. This also seems to be a honeybar staple as many of the yogis from the studio next door we're stopping in to grab their cup. 
When I'm back in town I'll definitely stop by to get another honeybar cup!

Overall a great coworking space. WeWork and the staff at Fort Point often hold events that allow you to interact with the other businesses in the building giving everyone a great chance to network. The WeWork app allows the staff to be responsive and extremely helpful. They are always a joy to talk to and work with if something goes wrong and needs some fixing. The community manager and staff at Fort Point are top notch and willing to do whatever it takes to meet your needs. As mentioned before, they frequently hold events that offer free food and drinks and are always trying to get everyone involved in the community. It is a great space with lots of energy, perks, and wonderful people. Highly recommend the space to anyone looking for a space for the startup or small business.

There are not enough words to express how blessed I was by Meg and Leo (as well as their assistant and student, Brittany and Anya).

I hired them during a critical time. Not just because of COVID, but at 36 weeks pregnant, I found myself needing to be transferred to a new provider. My doulas worked with Meg & Leo and suggested I would click well with them. I'll never forget that Sunday afternoon, my heart was pounding and my mind was racing as I shakily wrote an email asking if they could take me on.

Within hours, I got an email back and we met over Zoom the next day. (From the get go, I was impressed with how communicative and efficient they were!) My husband and I had a consult with them and I immediately felt at ease. They listened to my concerns from my previous provider, responded respectfully, asked great questions and by the end of the call, the four of us felt like we were a good fit.

These women are a dynamic duo! Even though we only had a few prenatal appointments together, I never felt disregarded or my questions weren't valid. But if I needed some grounding and reality checks, they didn't shy away from telling me. They made sure to get caught up to speed as quickly as possible. 

I ended up going 12 days past my EDD so they really came in clutch when I'd frantically text them or feel like I was losing my mind. They always responded promptly, gave great tips and never let me feel like a nag.

The birth itself was calm. I actually don't remember Meg and Brittany interfering for majority of the birth (which I believe is ideal LOL). They trusted my body do its thing but I always knew they were close by if I needed anything.

When it came to the final pushes, I had a moment of feeling like I wouldn't make it. Meg immediately refuted my doubt and said the most convincing, "YES YOU CAN." like only Meg can. Two seconds later, my baby girl was in my arms.

I've attributed my beautiful birth to Home Birth Honey so many times, a friend of mine ended up transferring to them, too!

You cannot go wrong with these powerhouse midwives. No doubt we will be meeting again for Baby #2!

This place is truly an unexpected gem. Food court food doesn't get any better than this. The flavors, and there are many, are at once unique and comforting. The family that runs the operation appears completely proud of their work, and as well they should be.
