Much of the food is made fresh after you order so the wait maybe a little longer than most food court stands but it's worth it. On my last visit I tried the lamb Kittu Roti and the Biryani and both were exceptional with perfectly balanced flavors. Also, their Dosas are crispy and delicious and come with wonderful sides. Highly recommended even if you have no other reason to be at the very strange International Village. For the the quality I'm not sure if there's anything else like it in the city.

A full 5-stars, despite the lack of ambience, because of the food and the crazy value.

I used to love Uber. Preferred it over Yellow Cab, not anymore.

Without going into a long story about issues from the past, I will tell you about these past two days.

First, you cannot open the Uber app on a Galaxy S5. It closes every time saying it has stopped. Pretty sad since it's 2015. Nevertheless, I downloaded it and ran it on my old phone yesterday for a return trip from Wal-mart. I and my mother called the driver no less than 10 times and each time there was no answer or it went to voicemail. I texted repeatedly and no response. Finally, he said he couldn't find us and cancelled the trip. The next driver had not one problem locating us.

I was charged for the cancelled trip and immediately contacted Uber who claimed they refunded me although I've yet to get it.

Today, I order Uber to go to work in. I wait and wait and no response from the driver. No call to ask me where I am. No text. Nothing Her number was disconnected when I tried calling. I have learned my trip was cancelled and I again was charged 5 dollars.

I will NEVER use Uber again and I urge others not to as well. I asked to have my account cancelled and both trips refunded to me. I would rather suffer with the thieves of yellow cab then the dishonesty that is Uber.

I came in with friends for lunch yesterday; there was five of us. We said outside as the day was nice. The waitress came up and took our order fairly promptly. I got the Philly cheese steak sandwich with sweet potato fries, my friend got the firecracker shrimp and ribs, and my other friend got the surf and turf sushi roll. My philly was terrible and expensive. How you can get ribeye beef so dry while covered in cheese is a mystery. My friends ribs we're tough. The sushi roll was pretty good. All in all the service was absolutely terrible. She never asked how her food was, she never asked if two the two of us that were drinking beer would like another one, and we literally had to get up after sitting completely done for 30 minutes to go find her and get our tab. When you get that service combined with bad food and then add the fact that the food is overpriced you get one star. I will not be back and neither will my friends. I suggest walking across the street there are four very good restaurants within a 2-minute walk of this place that are cheaper and better.

As a Russian I enjoy the food here quite a bit.  It is typical comfort food for Russia but is nothing that I would consider high end.  These are typical home cooked style meals and they are adorned and served as such.  My favorite appetizer is the pickled vegetables and for salad you have to go with the Russian standard, the Olivier.  For the main course I would recommend the Golubtsy.  Truly an authentic Russian experience.
My problem being I can't seem to control myself around the shot selection at this place.  This is truly where the restaurant shines.  The selection of infused vodkas is unparalleled and has something to suit even the most eclectic taste.  My personal favorites are the dill, pickle and the cranberry vodkas.

I'm not a coffee shop connoisseur, but I like what I 'see see' here at See See Motor Coffee Co. We were directed here from VooDoo Donuts Too, when seeking caffeine and wifi to work. It's a funky coffee shop in what looks to be an old mechanic garage, and then it's all about the motorcycle vibe, clothing and gear. It's like combining chicken and waffles...who knew how good they'd be together!? A for originality, for sure. Service was quick and friendly and I quite liked my iced green tea with some various other flavors.

There is ample seating at the bar or in one of two rooms with two and four tops, as well as a several outdoor seating options. The wifi was speedy with the wifi codes placed on each table. I loved the music, ranging from Prince to Tina Turner, and a little bit of everything in between. The apparel looked fun if you want a nice See See motorcycle shirt to rock. 

Cool place, I hope to visit again on a future Portland trip!

AWFUL experience with Vacasa. Rented a house in Homewood, Lake Tahoe for 4th of July weekend. Got a call from Vacasa less than 2 weeks before my stay telling me that I could not have the house anymore. The only option they gave me was to stay in a house at Squaw or Northstar (miles away from the lake, not comparable properties whatsoever). I ended up having to look on my own to find another place. Kimberly,one of the head supervisors, would not even call me back, only would respond by email. Everyone I dealt with was unprofessional and not willing to admit that the situation they put me in was unacceptable. Seems like cancelling reservations is a regular practice based on reviews below.

OHHHHH SNAP! 
I love me a good photo booth, and I've had the pleasure of getting my pic snapped inside the SNAP! photobooths on various occasions throughout the year. A few years ago I even got a video done for Yelp Spring Break from Trung (owner of SNAP!)

Trung loves photography - and he's a damn nice fella. As a photographer he has some of the coolest shots I've ever seen...I follow along on his travels via social media. His booths always create a fun and festive atmosphere. They bring out various props - and all of the shots are uploaded almost instantly so folks can snag a digital copy of their pics.

He's always been super professional, on time (often early!) and stays till the very end. All of the other employees I've come in contact with have been SUPER nice as well. They walk you through how the program works, and keep the line moving at a steady pace.

When we first walked in, I felt the overwhelming urge to ask my husband if "I could go play now?". Unfortunately for me, I had to let my baby play instead. My son is only 10 months old so a lot of things there he is not yet able to do. However, if you go upstairs,tucked away behind the "farmers market" and sea of strollers, you will find there is an infant play area. They have a mountain of bean bags for them to crawl up to the top part and up there they will find hidden holes that have squirrels and other slightly creepy things. They have a wall of mirrors which my already narcissistic son happens to love. All in all, this is a place I will be taking him for years to come, and it doesn't hurt that it's in Mueller and Momma can get some shopping done!

Incredibly educated friendly staff and a good, easy, clearly marked, safe set up for Covid testing. They deal directly with insurance companies. 

We got results within a couple hours and the dr making the results calls didn't rush me through any questions I had. I felt valued and cared for.  I didn't panic. 

They absolutely deeply care and even made calls to follow up on how I was feeling (I tested positive, my family tested negative, twice!) then followed up with calls to let us know they were working with insurance and to let us know about what was going on l, how to deal with any bills received and how they ensured we were covered.

I cannot sing their praises highly enough.   When I find myself in need again I will not hesitate to go there for treatment and have sent everyone I know there for their testing and emergency services. 

Thank you so much for taking care of me and making me feel safe.

I decided on a whim to check the Yelp reviews on the church I've been attending, with my husband, for four years. I especially want to address the LGBT issue raised by a reviewer last Spring. My husband and I had our marriage blessed at the Advent in October 2013. Good friends of ours, gay, had their marriage blessed there last month. I don't know the person who wrote the review from April 2014, or any circumstances surrounding that decision, but I want to rebut the notion that clergy at the Advent are fundamentally opposed to blessing same-sex marriages. That's just simply not true, on the whole. 

Yes, it is high, high church (with lots of music). Quite a diverse congregation. Mostly families at 9am (with a strong contingent of older folks). The 11:15am has plenty of every stripe. Conservatives, liberals, singles, couples, young, old, gay, straight - a real hodgepodge - everyone gathered for the quiet, peaceful, serene, moving, powerful, mysterious, ancient, and holy liturgy.

Definitely visit! And definitely stay for "coffee hour!"

If you are walking too fast, you may miss the restaurant sign as it's not very eye catching. It is across from Tinseltown and a bit past Abbott St. on W. Hastings. The server was very attentive and explained in detail the source of the food and informed my friends and I about what was in each plate. That was a unique experience that I appreciated. The Lamb Sausage Tagine that I ordered was very flavourful but the couscous and veggies were too sweet and salty for my liking. My mouth was very thirsty afterward and I needed to drink warm water throughout the day to quench my thirst. The decor is quite unique and nice. I recommend going during the day time (such as a Sunday afternoon, which was when we went) if you prefer a quieter people with not as many people. We were the only table there that day.

As we walked down Granville Ave, looking for laid-back pubs to pop into, we passed Two Parrots. I had a hazy memory of being there on my first trip to Vancouver and from what I could recollect had had a good time. Even so, it didn't seem to be quite the establishment we'd had in mind, so we continued on by. 

After about an hour, three pubs, and some slightly lowered standards later, we were heading inside after all. 

I mean, let's be honest: It's kitschy. Garish Hawaiian decorations, themed drinks, etc. But the fruity island-inspired drinks were cheap and yummy, and it wasn't all techno-and-stilettos like many of the places we'd wandered past. 

Turns out this is my go-to joint in Vancouver. *shrugs*

We used to go to this location when it was Yuki Hana so we decided to try it out. Our server recognized us from when we used to come in when it was Yuki Hana, so that was nice we had her as a server. I ordered the delicious sashimi sampler, beef yakisoba and beef teriyaki sushi. It was all super delicious and the service was wonderful! I highly recommend it to anyone who really loves sushi or just Japanese food. We will definitely  be regulars for sure.

I went here today to get a new needle for my vintage Dual record player that has been in storage for 20+ years. Over the phone, I was told that they would install parts and balance the player for free if brought in. I was so glad that I had brought the turntable instead of just bringing the cartridge itself. Nicholas, the owner, not only told me the needle was perfectly fine, but took the time to test my turntable to make sure the cartridge and all the mechanisms still worked. We discovered that sound only came out one side. Nicholas then troubleshooted the issue, trying to see if he could just fix the cartridge instead of me having to spend the money buying a new one. Unfortunately, the cartridge couldn't be fixed so he installed a new one for me. He also balanced the player and checked both speeds and the arm. The arm had issues dropping down but he told me it wasn't a necessity to spend the money to fix it since the arm would return on its own. I needed speakers and he happened to have some in the back that he showed me how to wire and wired for me so I would know how to connect them to my amp at home. He also gave me his card and said I could phone the shop for help if I ran into any issues with the turntable at home. I would highly recommend this store for turntable repair because the prices are very reasonable and the owner really goes above and beyond helping people out. It is clear that the owner really loves records, record players, and all things related and he is super knowledgeable! In the end, I was only charged for the parts and not for any of the labour even though the owner spent at least 45 minutes fixing my turntable and making sure everything worked properly. It seems to be a popular place -- I went after lunch on a weekday and at least 6 other people were in the store while I was there either looking at records or picking up/dropping off turntables.

(Note 8/4/14: Now operating under the name Gyro House.)

There are tons of food cart choices to choose from in the two blocks of Alder St in downtown Portland. Just about every type of cuisine you can think of is represented. 

The location is quite competitive as a result. Some carts from my visits last year to Portland had been replaced by different ones in my two visits to the city last month. Separating yourself from your competition is very important.

As I was looking for a meal before my bus ride back up to Seattle, I headed over to the Alder food carts for a bite. I had passed Egyptian Food numerous times in my visit. It seemed like this cart always managed to draw a crowd which piqued my interest so I decided to give this cart a try.

Not sure why this cart does not have any reviews yet. There is another cart by the same name several blocks away from here. Perhaps they were written in that Yelp listing? Anyways, Egyptian/Mediterranean halal food is what is offered here. Think items like gyros and meat/rice platters. Though they do have some American items like burgers and hot dogs as well if you prefer something less exotic.

The items on the menu here are reasonably priced. Typically in the $5-7 range. I decided to go with the lamb over rice ($7). What I got was a large heaping of fragrant rice covered with thinly sliced pieces of lamb and a salad with tzatziki and hummus. Definitely more food than I expected to receive given the price.

I did have some concern that my stomach would not deal well with such a large meal when I was ordering, but I didn't feel any ill effects on my bus ride. The meal was actually so filling that I skipped dinner.

The lamb is quite tasty. It did not have any gamey taste to it. It really does not taste that much different to beef or pork if you have not tried it before. The rice went well with lamb though just a tad on the oily side. Not a problem though since the salad served as a good palate cleanser for this.

Lastly, there is one additional plus to this cart as they have a few covered tables and seats on the side of it if you are concerned about where to eat. If you are looking for a good Mediterranean cart, I would give this one a try as their menu is quite varied.

Nothing says drunken good time like gambling drinks against strangers on free games of skeeball.  I love this bar and I think after a weekend spent here (Friday night and all Sunday), it may have become my favorite bar in Austin.  The bar gets busy which is understandable but they make great drinks.  I would defintly say visit on a sunday.  Not only did I witness the most intense game of Jenga (as did everyone else outside on the patio), free games on Sundays is super legit.  Get drunk off cheap drinks and play Cruisin World.  My 1 disappointment, Buck Hunter was broken and Golden Tee wasn't free.  Other than that, it may be the coolest hidden hangout.  Its also worth noting since its on West 6th the patrons are a little classier and older than on East 6th.

IF I COULD GIVE NEGITIVE STARS -5STARS This place is an absoulte rip off payed hundreds of dollars for audio work in my car and after going back and forth 5 times it's still not done right and now its my problem because I kept getting the run around  ill never recommend anyone here they r awful unintelligible buisnessmen and thry scratched my mirror on there tight garage door opening but they won't admit it....STAY AWAY FROM THESE HACKS DO U AND UR CAR A FAVOR

I have been a MARTA rider since the 80s...Well a MARTA train rider as I try to avoid the busses at all costs.

I have given MARTA 3 of 5 stars. I give MARTA 5 stars for going into town and for going to the airport. I find no better way to get to either .


Coming back home (Sandy Springs station) after 9 pm I give MARTA 0-1 stars. Coming home is awful they cut the number of trains and it is a 17 minute wait between trains and you have to transfer again at Lindburgh after 9. So coming home from Hawks game the train at Phillips station waited for people to fill at least 2 minutes but that was enough time to miss the train from 5 points to Lindburgh so we had to wait 17 minutes. That train was late causing us to miss the North Springs train so we had to wait another 15 minutes.

Coming back from Turner Field you can forget a decent ride. Delays in busses that go way out of the way to go to the West Point train station. It is best to take MARTA into town but take UBER home.


In the stations the monitors are usually wrong and if they ever announce anything it is nearly impossible to understand what they are trying to say. Think Charlie Browns teacher.

They have a program "see something say something" but if anything were to ever happen on the train 9 times out of 10 phone service is not working and nothing could be reported. Marta has a twitter account but they NEVER respond to anyones posts so even if there was wireless on the trains I would have little faith that anyone would even respond.

Overall we had a good experience here. We had been looking for a 5th wheel for quite some time with little luck. We had visited B Young a few times but did not find anything we liked. We were never pressured and had our names taken down each time and assured we would be called if anything came in that matched our criteria and none followed through except one sales person that was very accommodating. He would call every week or so with a few that we may like which was very nice because their inventory did change constantly. 

We went to view on trailer that he called us about but another that had just been traded caught our eye. The whole process was pretty simple and they even fixed and looked over a few things that we had concerns about. The delivery and walk through the trailer was amazing and they even had it arranged to be delivered to our house since the hitch on the truck hadn't been installed yet. 

With any camp trailer there have been a few problems and minor leaks. One in particular I could not figure out and they were reluctant to help with the diagnosis which is why I have given 4 stars instead of 5. I would expect them to be very helpful in at least trying to figure out why and how the leak started and the methods to fix it. 

Overall good experience, great delivery, but just lacking in the followup department. Will eventually trade in our current unit and upgrade and it will more than likely be at B Young.

This is a nice museum, but it wasn't clear to me - even after I received the guided tour - why such a museum with George Washington Carver's name existed in the Austin area. There appeared to be no real link between Washington Carver and the Austin area. The tour guide said they just picked someone at random!?! There were some lovely exhibits devoted to local African American families but why George Washington Carver's name was on the building is still a mystery to me. How about changing the name to reflect the rich African American diversity contained within Austin and the building? (A name that reflects the great scientist and the wonderful locals.)

This is one of the nicer Seminole County offices.  My husband made his appointment and mine online and we were both taken right on time.  The staff were friendly and we were in and out of the office in the time expected.

Parking can be a challenge as the lot is small and you will be towed if you park next door.  Be sure to give yourself a few minutes to drive around the lot in order to grab a parking spot in the right place.

I am glad Rita's is in Columbus. I just moved from Rochester, where there is only one Rita's. There are a few in Columbus, albeit in suburban locations.

Like I wrote in my Rochester Rita's review:  

"Italian Ice individually = yum

Frozen custard individually = yum

Italian ice + Frozen custard (gelati) together = Mind-blowingly yum"

This Gahanna Rita's is somewhat of a hole-in-the-wall. It's attached to a pizza store and there is no real inside seating area. They have a few bench tables outside, but that's about it. The portions seem larger than the Rochester's Rita's. 

They are not in "downtown" Gahanna, but they aren't too far. It's pretty much isolated amongst random retail stores, so there's no place to walk around. A group of us visited Rita's after glow-in-the-dark mini-golf. They are right across the street, which makes it a convenient post-putting activity.

My biggest hang up with leaving my corporate job to work for myself was losing my healthcare coverage.  After years of navigating through the unstable train wreck that is Kaiser Permanente, I had finally found a wonderful doctor, we were happy and life was good.  

Having to leave him after getting to this sweet spot was like having to abruptly dump the love of my life. No one would get me like he did, I thought.  He knew very intimate things about me, including what I look like naked.

The new insurance listed the Portland Clinic as an eligible provider. I made an appointment with Dr. Cooper, half expecting to meet a pre-occupied nitpicker who had more important things to do.  Dr. Cooper confirmed my theory before I even met him.  The day of my appointment,  his assistant called to say he didn't want to see me.  Huh?  Apparently, he chooses who he wants to see and who he doesn't,  and my chart was on the reject list. It was really thoughtful of him to make that determination the very day of my appointment, after I had adjusted my work schedule to be there. Perhaps if I were a rich old white man he might consider gracing me with his royal presence.

As it turns out, Dr. Cooper's douche bag maneuver, proved to be the best gift I could ever ask for.  I got a same day spot with Dr. Trafficante who is equal to or greater than my old Dr., but taller and with a cooler last name.  Dr. Trafficante listened to my concerns and suggested new medication that has made a world of difference for me.  He is knowledgeable, professional but laid back, which is something that I really appreciate.  Additionally, I have never called his nurse for something without her not answering the phone or responding the same day. 

I personally have never thanked anybody for being a douche bag, but I guess there is a first time for everything.  Thank you, Dr. Cooper, for leading me to one of the best Drs. The Portland Clinic has to offer.  In the end, saying the name "Trafficante" instead of pedestrian "Cooper" makes for a lot more fun.

At the risk of anthropomorphizing animals, this show has some of the cutest and most engaging animals available at Sea World.  They even just look like they're smiling at you.  They can't seem more playful and happy than they do, and that helps you want to watch them.

The stunts and tricks that they engage in, the banter of the group and everything makes it a pretty good experience.  In fact, the only negative I can say is how loud the sound and music are.  My wife had to completely sit and plug her ears during the show because of the unbelievable volume.  That old saying, "If it's too loud, you're too old."  Well, I guess I'm too old, but at least I still have my hearing.

We are first time customers that hired HomeJoy to come in and thoroughly clean for an appt we booked earlier this month.

This is what happened.

- We contacted HomeJoy's services (around 8am) to check on our appt for this morning. Due to all the weather and restrictions put on by local government, we thought for sure this would be rescheduled. To our surprise, found they were still sending someone out for our 10am appt.
- By 10:20, the maid had not arrived, and no one had called. I was okay with the maid being late (due to weather), but would have hoped someone would at least call to let us know. I received a #415 from my husband and called. The phone rang once and disconnected me.
- Somewhere between 10:30-10:50am, the maid began repeatedly texting my husband about parking. (something that is not complicated in this area)
- I again tried to call the maid at the 415 # I was provided and again, it rang once and I was disconnected.
- At 10:50am, I called the #617-762-5141 and went through a phone tree for several minutes. I finally was connected to someone who found my account. 
- The maid knocked on the door and came in around 11am. He was talking about was how he only makes $15 an hour and that he had just paid $20 for parking. He attempted to reach HomeJoy. He also made sure to tell me he was not familiar with the area (we live in Boston, where HomeJoy is based).
- I had to asked the maid if he would like booties, he opted to remove his shoes and placed the wet shoes on top of a bench we use by the entryway
- I gave him some direction when he came in, and told him floors were very important. He started in the kitchen.
- He was coughing all over the kitchen, I mean at least try to put that in a shoulder or something
- About 45-50 min in, I happened to notice he was slumped over and not moving.. so I asked him if everything was okay. He said he was texting HomeJoy again to see about being reimbursed for parking.
- Disappointed with the whole experience, I just wanted it over. I asked the maid to just make the appt one hour and please just finish up at 12pm (I felt like he at least deserved an hour for being here and wanted to be fair). My request was NOT received w respect. He smirked and I was told to "just relax" and let him finish the job. I replied with that I would really feel best if we just wrapped things by up 12pm. He then got defensive and immediately asked if I was going to pay for his parking. I gave him a few more minutes (11:55pm) From here, I was extremely uncomfortable (and kept telling him so).. and just wanted him to go (expecting he would be packing up at this point because 12pm was the time to go), instead he was still scrubbing and not putting things back. At 11:57am, I asked him to please just finish up and leave. He left the kitchen with everything out (and took pictures of it, I imagine as evidence). He kept saying "I didn't do anything wrong", then said something about how he's cleaned hundreds of houses and continued to mumble under his breath as he left.
- My husband just confirmed that he received a charge from HomeJoy for $20 from around 11am. 
- I called HomeJoy's # again just after the maid left to provide details of this incident and was cycled through a lot of ringing phones, until I was disconnected.
- I cannot find a HomeJoy email address to reach out to with this feedback.

Completely unacceptable and unprofessional.

Update: I went in and picked up after the maid. He had used our dish sponge on the stovetop (hopefully not with the sprays, tossed it to be on the safe side)... and there were wet paper towels everywhere (on the floor, caked in the sink, around the stove)... he left one of his dirty rags and our pot in the sink and it's filled with some combo of dirty water (shouldn't you remove that before you start putting cleaners everywhere?). Yuck, yuck, yuck!

Bought tickets for the ghost tour and the witch tour (3 pm) through Living Social - am really glad I didn't pay full price for tickets. The ghost tour was pretty cool (which is why this is a 2-star rating, and not less) - the guide was pretty knowledgeable, and very nice. And we actually, you know, walked. The earlier tour was PAINFUL. We stood at one site (an alley, next to a plaque) for at LEAST half the tour (so about 30 mins). And I think that's underestimating. The guide (who I'm sure is a very nice person) was a horrible public speaker...kept losing track of what she was saying / repeating things / jumping around from topic to topic so following her train of thought was impossible. And there was very little info re: the witch trials on the WITCH TRIAL TOUR. Ended up being more of a history lesson on religion.

I cannot believe it's been 6 years since we ate here -- and so realizing that, my wife and I (now with a 3 year old in tow!) popped over for a late anniversary dinner last week. My wife got the Polish plate and I got the potato dumplings, and both were as divine as we remembered. Our three year old happily ate the pierogi, stuffing from the stuffed cabbage, and potato dumplings, and I had to fight my wife for a bite of anything from her plate. The gravy/sauce on the potato dumplings is divine. Staff and service were awesome, too -- I asked if it was possible to get a glass of milk for my toddler, and they brought a full sized glass along -- and didn't charge us for it. Here's hoping we can get in another visit before six years goes by again!

We used Commonwealth Masonry for a driveway project recently. We were expanding a single-width driveway, which required significant excavation and rebuilding, all while working around an existing gas line and a beast of a tree stump.

They were fantastic!

Communication. The foreman we worked with, Luke, picked up the phone every time we called. It was great. They also provided a detailed proposal at our first meeting.

Price. Their estimate came in a good 30% cheaper than our next-cheapest one (and it included more work, to boot).

Can-do attitude. They did a great job working with our needs, and every question was met with, "Yeah, we can make that happen!" They built a new retaining wall using the stones left over after demolition, and matched it perfectly to the original 60-year-old wall on the other side.

Speed. They excavated a monstrous tree stump, pressure-washed, repointed, and capped our old wall, demo'd and rebuilt/capped a completely new wall plus a new set of steps, and tore up and repaved our entire driveway in just a week.

We are so happy with the work they did, and would recommend Commonwealth to anyone who needs paving/masonry work.

Auto Hero contacted me about a car I have for sale on cars.com & Craigslist. They said they liked the car & price & would like to buy it. I was skeptical so I asked if they would give me my asking price. They said if it matched the pictures & description they WOULD. I told the wife not to get too excited & took them the car. They appraised it & it was every bit as nice as described. The appraiser said there was nothing wrong with it. Their offer however was thousands less. I guess it has to be since they buy from you & sell to the dealers. It was a waste of my time.

I ordered a gun from them and was told it would arrive in 2-3 weeks.  After 4 weeks and no call, I called them.  They told me it would be another week.  I waited a week, and called...they said the same thing, promising that it would be in the next Friday, and that they would call.  They never called.  So after a month I called on a Monday.  They said it was in Austin, but not at the store yet, that it would be in the next day guaranteed.  I called every day that week, and they promised every day it was there and would be available the next day.  After a month an a half I got the owner, and he guaranteed it would be in the next Tuesday, and offered free ammo as an apology.  Next Tuesday came, and no call.  I called, and they said it still hadn't arrived yet...but that it would be in at the end of the week for sure.  Needless to say after almost 2 months, and being lied to for 3 weeks over a dozen times, I never got the gun.  When I asked for a refund, they said they couldn't process it and someone would have to call me back later that day.  They never called.  I called back again, and the owner Mike said that he'd process it when he got back.  He never did.  I finally called a third time about my refund, and after being told that they couldn't process it again and would have to call me back, I  informed them that I was not going to call again, and if I didn't get my refund this time I was reporting it as fraud. They told me to hold, and Mike got on the line and submitted my refund.  The refund still took almost a week to go through after that.  So 2 months later I still have no gun, and wasted hours dealing with CTGW.  Worst gun shop I've ever dealt with, and I've been a hobbyist for most of my life.  Worst customer service ever, bordering on fraud.  I work in Digital Marketing with Businesses all the time, and I've never seen anything short of a scam that was this bad. I went to another local gun store and ordered the same gun, and got it the same day for $50 less than what CTGW had charged me.  Completely ridiculous.  Steer far away from this place if you value your time, money, and honesty.

When my son had an accident and totaled the truck, it was a very stressful time.  I contacted a few different salvage companies and took the best price offered over the phone.  Waiting at the facility, a tow driver arrived and said he would need to contact head office.  He came back to me and said sorry, but we can only offer you half the price you were quoted.  I quickly realized this was an unscrupulous and deceitful business as I had told them everything about the damages over the phone including the vehicle VIN.  I then phoned Special Truck and Auto Salvage, quickly sent them photos along with my description and they promised me a cashiers check in an amount that while not as high, it was still far better than other quotes I had received.  The driver arrived exactly on time and I was presented a check made out to the exact amount quoted.  No games, no stress, just a prompt fair and honest transaction.

It was a U-Haul and I can't see much difference in that door and any other, and as far as being Saturday, I just don't see lockout service as a 9-5, M-F job, they just picked my pocket because they could.

Do NOT hire this company. If you have a problem with property damage, the office will be condescending and dismissive instead of apologetic and helpful when they DO reply, and then they'll never get back to you or reimburse you. 

The only reason I'm leaving two stars is that one of the three guys in the moving crew was awesome. He was fast, efficient, didn't stop working until the job was done, and kept the other two going. Everything else about the experience, including the office staff, was terrible. One of the other three movers was a complete disaster. He was incredibly slow, had to be told by the guy in charge to keep working over and over, damaged my floor (think big chips, not small scratches) and constantly put things in the wrong place. For example, when I said, "please put that in my bedroom" he'd say , "right...the kitchen?" I thought the third guy was fine until they left and I realized almost everything he'd put in the house was backwards. One of my couches, my serving bar, and a few other random items were backwards, and the glass in my china cabinet was installed upside down AND backwards. He also started unpacking my tv, even though I hadn't asked, and said he couldn't find the screws. I told him they were taped to the back, which they were, but he said they weren't there. I asked him to put it back in the box, but he left it balancing on the small plastic neck that attaches to the base. I'm just glad it didn't snap from the weight of my tv or topple over before I found it. 

I later contacted the office about the floor damage, and got a snippy, condescending reply that said the claims department would get back to me. I emailed twice, and it's been three weeks since my move, and they still haven't bothered to respond. I've found a few other damaged items since then... Glass shattered on an art piece, chips and scratches on furniture, but nothing as major as the floor. Apparently I'm on my own for the cost of repairs. 

If all their movers were like the guy in charge, I would hire them again, despite the terrible customer service from the office, but sadly, two incompetent movers and a refusal to respond to property damage seems to be what I'll remember this company for.

Lovely team at Float On and Cruise On. I booked a boat & shuttle for my sister's bachelorette party and everyone I encountered from booking to the day of was so courteous. The day of our rental was cloudy and rainy (very disappointing as you can imagine!) but as I was talking with our driver & captain, they were open to do anything that would work best for us. Our Cruise On driver was happy to take us anywhere and pick us up anywhere within the 4 hours we were meant to be on the boat. When we decided to go out on the water anyway (in hopes it would clear up -- which it did!) our captain was game to take us to one of the bars on the water we could dock up to, or turn back around anytime. I believe their rain day policy was that we'd be refunded for the time we didn't spend out on the water, but you'd need to double check. Either way, it was clear to me they'd do what they could to give us the best possible experience given the unfortunate circumstances. I'm so happy we ended up staying out on the water & will definitely use Float On again. Thanks!

Our office started with The Scheduling Institute last year, and it has been the single most team busting, demoralizing decision that could have been made.  Just mark me as a "DITTO" for every one star rating listed for this company, and I too would give them a ZERO if Yelp had the option. 
 We all sat through 10 or 12 hours of poorly produced audio and video training, and all the while we received "Mystery Calls" and had the results emailed directly to our Doctor.  Imagine the stress on our team, there was no opportunity for questions, feedback.  Oh, we could have "practiced" with them over the phone one day a week, but we did not shut down the office while we did this, it was all between patients and was time consuming enough.  It was all very demoralizing, with many on our staff receiving a grade of "0"  at first.  Can you imagine a legitimate adult education program giving untrained or partially trained students that type of grade?  Imagine your boss, who is paying you to perform a service, hearing that you have received a "0".  We were all sick about it, and tried so hard to improve, but the concepts that were described in the training could not be applied to our phone calls, no matter how hard we tried.  And we did try.  Hard.  Because we love your jobs, we love our team, and we loved working for our Doctor and wanted to do our best for him and get all this trauma (I mean, training) behind us so we could be happy at work again.  Please don't underestimate how destructive this was to our workplace.  We were literally frustrated to tears.  And then we figured it out - the metric that the Scheduling Institute was using to "rate" us.  They were not interested in concepts, tone, or even connecting with our new patients.  They were simply rating us according to an exact script - words.  We had specific words they wanted us to say, and if we strayed from the script even a little we did not get the passing score.  So we created a script, and it worked.  We said the words in the most dispassionate manner possible, and it worked.  10 to 12 hours of PAID staff time PER PERSON and it all boiled down to a short script.  There was no reason to learn any concepts as there was no room for personalizing the script.  Unbelievable.  But it gets worse.  The Scheduling Institute set the stage by saying that if we followed EXACTLY the guidelines given we would be successful.  If staff don't buy in to the program 100% it will not work, and that is not Jay's fault, it is the fault of the staff.  That effectively squelched communication with the Doc about this program that he had already invested in.  Smart move, Jay. We turned this training from the office nightmare to the office joke, and we made it through.  We did not get a SINGLE (please re-read that) new patient because of this program.  We were already scheduling consults TWO weeks out, so there was no gaps in our schedule that were not being filled.  We knew the Scheduling Institute calls when they came in because of 1) they were usually an unlisted number, and 2) they asked the questions listed on our script in a way that NO patient would ever ask.  When patients call us, they are calling to make appointments and rarely need to be "sold".  And that's what we felt like the training videos were more suited for, used car salesmen.  The Scheduling Institute sends snail mail and email to our office EVERY SINGLE DAY.  He must have an enormous marketing budget, as it clearly does not go into training or materials.  A recent opportunity to attend a Scheduling Institute seminar in Atlanta presented itself.  Every attempt to get an agenda or syllabus was responded to with "It is so motivational!  There will be a concert!"  No answer to the question "But what will we learn?"  Our Doctor was all ready to sign us up, but as one voice we said "no".  Leif L., you said in your review something negative about me, a person leaving a one star review.  I'm not going to reciprocate and get personal with you but I will say that I still love my job, my team, and our patients.  It is a privilege to serve in this profession.  If you feel the same way, please save your money, don't damage the team you have worked so hard to build, and find another company to provide REAL training.

Fox Creek Golf Club has a par-62 executive course, a large driving range with 50 grass hitting stations, and a practice putting green. It's located next to Legacy Golf Links which has a sister par-58 executive course and an extensive practice facility. These two courses have the same owner and are managed by the same company. These are great places to get acquainted with and learn the game of golf because both Fox Creek and Legacy offer short, reasonably priced courses to go along with solid practice facilities.

I've always preferred Legacy over Fox Creek because the course layout and scenery at Legacy is more interesting. Also, Legacy has short game (chipping) practice areas whereas Fox Creek does not. In my experience, one advantage Fox Creek has over Legacy is it's less crowded and busy. If you just want to go to the driving range, either will do, though it should be noted Fox Creek's range has more of a drop-off if you're picky about yardages and stuff like that.

Fox Creek's clubhouse is small and simple, but stocked with all the essentials including golf apparel, snacks, and refreshments. There are places to sit and lounge and there are TVs (including over the urinals in the men's restroom). The covered patio is nice and fairly spacious. It still looks relatively new with outdoor sofas, grills, and more. The patio is located adjacent to the practice putting green and overlooks the range.

Range balls cost $6 for a small bucket, $9.50 for a medium, and $12 for a large. The range balls are average quality and are dispensed from a big machine. The quality of the grass has been fine the times I've used the range. The last time I used the practice putting green, it was in very good condition.

Fox Creek uses electric-powered Yamaha golf carts which I am a fan of. They are much better than loud and smelly fuel-injected carts in my opinion. The last time I visited, our cart provided a quiet, smooth, and comfortable ride with quick acceleration and good braking. The carts were in good condition. As soon as we pulled into the parking lot and got out of our cars, a cart attendant drove up and dropped a cart off for us.

The golf course is fairly basic and straightforward. There are three sets of tees. From the tips, the course measures 3,892 yards. The last time I played, there was no rating/slope. I was told this was because the course was undergoing (or had recently undergone) some renovations. One of the guys at the starter's box told me the course slope was 106, but he didn't specify from which tees. Perhaps the course will have a rating/slope by the time you read this.

The front nine is par 32 with the course's only par-5 hole to go along with three par-4 holes and five par-3 holes. The back nine is par 30 with three par-4 holes and the rest (six holes) par 3s. There are no hole layouts on the scorecard nor at the hole markers, but you don't really need them since most of the holes are short. The par-5 6th hole is the longest hole and it's only 402 yards from the black tees (356 from the white). There is a pin sheet with 6 areas per green. A sign at the first tee will tell you the day's hole location and cart rule (e.g. 90 degree, cart path only, etc.).

The course really doesn't have very memorable holes except for Nos. 8 and 9 where your tee shots play over water (the only lake on the course). The par-3 17th hole parallels Windy Hill Road. There are bunkers, but not a whole lot. They're filled with soft white sand (the good kind). The greens are big so they're relatively easy to hit, making this course suitable for beginners and casual golfers. The greens are made with Champion Bermudagrass and are generally good to very good quality. The greens have a decent bit of undulation to them, which makes putting both challenging and fun. The course design is compact and forgiving. There are minor to moderate elevation changes, typical of a Georgia course.

As for course conditions, in my visits to this course over the years (my first recorded score from this course for handicap purposes was June 24, 2003 - a long time ago), they have been average at best. The last time I played here, the course was in OK shape overall. However, there were definitely some problem areas such as huge patches of dirt greenside on the 9th hole, stretches of dirt in the middle of 11 fairway, a tee box with barely any grass (13), and a significantly damaged green (14). And all this was after a good two weeks of rain. I noticed one of the fairway sprinkler heads on the back nine was broken. There were golf ball washers stationed throughout the course, but some were out of soap.

Service was satisfactory. There was a beverage cart.

I paid $34.98 (tax included) for my last round which was on a Saturday morning. We were able to book our tee time weeks in advance. At the time of writing this review, the Saturday-Sunday rate for 18 holes with cart is $37. I'm not sure why I was charged less. I'd say the prices are fair for what you get.

What a wonderful experience!  I found a beautiful dress for my upcoming baby shower and Izzy Maternity had much better options, service, and modern styles compared to Destination Maternity (which is a major rip off...they charge $70 for tee shirts).  I was helped every step of the way. 

I am a bargain shopper and so far all my maternity clothes have come from Old Navy Maternity or Target for casual wear, but I wanted something special to wear for my baby shower and the oversized dresses at TJMaxx or maternity dresses from Target just didn't cut it.  Izzy has gorgeous dresses in the $80 range and many cool clothes that you would look forward to wearing for work or nice evenings out.  

 I highly recommend Izzy for the price, value, quality, and excellent service.

Jimmy Hodges talked to me at Earth Day about getting solar, and I asked a few other companies to come out and give me quotes as well.  After reviewing my site, not only did Jimmy respond first, but he let me know that I have too much shade over my roof and it wouldn't be worth it to install the panels.  

So, if they didn't actually do any work for me, why am I writing an excellent review?  
1) When we talked, he completely explained the process, normal costs, type of evaluation they would do, types of panels, limitations set by the city, etc.  I didn't think I needed that much information, but it turns out that all of that was relevant.
2) They set up a very prompt evaluation and I didn't even need to be at home.  They responded days before anyone else, and he remembered me and my questions at Earth Day.  That shows that he really cares about each person. 
3) He gave me a totally honest evaluation (ie- it would take too many panels and be too expensive to make up my losses due to shade).  Even though that means that he didn't make a profit, he saved ME a ton of time and money in the long run.  

TL;DR - Jimmy is a good dude.  10/10, would recommend.

I'm shocked that there are so few reviews of Nu Aeon, I feel like it's been there forever...though it might be understandable, considering many people I've talked to only know it as "Gypsy's Shop". I wasn't even sure of the name until I needed to look up the phone number one day. 

Nu Aeon has a little bit from every corner, from Greek and Roman, to Egyptian, to Norse, and Thelemic and ceremonial supplies. Their book selection is pretty good and they have a great selection of jewelry and pagan wall hangings. They have good suppliers and can get you what you need if you ask for it. 

The people there are actual practitioners--as such they can answer questions and give advice depending on what you'd like to do. 

They do not generally cater to the "touristy" set...you won't find bumper stickers or Salem, MA coffee mugs. You won't even find those cheap DYI crafts that the owners of some other shops do and then try to sell for stupid amounts of money (pendulum mats and love spells in a bag, anyone?) Nu Aeon is a classy ritual supply store. I try to support them when I can because there are so few of them around.

I am one of those rare individuals that loves to write....on anything I can get my hands on. So when there's a store filled with pretty and original journals and paper items, I'm in heaven!

Whenever I go to a new city, I always look up stationary and paper stores. Yelp highly recommended this one and I have say kudos! It has so many different options, I picked up a few pens, spiral notebooks, a couple journals, and a couple composition books. All a great deal and all original. Back in the states I'm asked where I got the journals I'm writing in.

A great little find and will make this a stop whenever I'm in Vancouver. I didn't get any photos as I was too busy salivating over everything in the store.

when are we getting 1/2 stars?  actual review is 3.5

great food, awesome proportions.

the special birthday dinner (compleanos?) is superb. A very nice cut of steak with chimichurri sauce, fried plaintains, rice and beans (I wish it were more traditional rice and beans, but ok), and 2 different sausages. They could call this dish the meat lovers delight.

I apologize ahead of time for the lengthiness of this review.  I also want to express that I am a big supporter of small local businesses and authentic good food.

I went to this place for the first time to attend a party for a friend. If the saying that "you don't get a second chance to make a first impression holds true", I would say that there's no chance I would ever be going back to this place. First of all, one of the people at our party ordered an appetizer which took an hour to come. The reason it took an hour to come out was because it was being made fresh; however, it was supposed to be a warm dish, but it was cold when it came out.

Secondly, our table was a party of 10. We all ordered our meals at the same time, but some of us ended up getting our meals at least 20 minutes (if not more) before others. Meals were brought to the table incomplete. For example, the Oxtail was brought 10-15 minutes before the salad and the plantains came out for one person. Mind you, the salad and the plantains were part of her entree; which means the person was eating oxtail by itself.  Other people also got fractions of their meals at a time.  My honest opinion is that the staff at Kalalou Caribbean Restaurant definitely need some Hospitality 101 training, urgently, if they want to continue to be in business.

The flavor of the food was decent, but not exhilarating to justify the delay and service.  The manager came out a couple of times to check on our party and apologized by explaining that there were three parties that night, and that the food was being prepared fresh; however, those parties (including ours) were scheduled prior to the event, so in reality they should have been prepared for the volume of people they were expecting. Not to mention that most of the items came out cold when they finally came to our table; so that is simply not an excuse for the poor service.  In my opinion, management did not do a very good job that night.

Needless to say, I would not be going back to this restaurant any time soon.

To begin, what could be better than a club located in DKR (Darrell K. Royal Memorial Stadium).  Then once inside, the beautifully and recently redecorated interior is full of Longhorn motifs and memorabilia.  Any Longhorn-lover will feel so much at home in this environment.  The chef is personable and does a great job.  The club offers a variety of events and specials for members--we've enjoyed the chef's cooking demonstrations, the hill country wine tours, etc.  As others have mentioned, they offer complimentary appetizers at Happy Hour that are nice for some--options like Frito Pie for example and complimentary continental breakfast in the mornings.  For a club structure, they don't gauge you on additional fees and charges. Their lunch buffet is a really nice, fresh and tasty buffet spread with food to satisfy everyone from your vegan self to your Paleo self to your carnivore self to your fall off-the-wagon self and everyone in between.  Parking is abundant (except for game days!) in the structure across the street.  They will validate your parking as a convenience for you and your guests (it is added to your bill).They have a super helpful club member coordinator who makes many things very smooth--Jetta.  If you do eat there on a weekday lunch, they offer menu ordering but they aren't really staffed to accommodate that.  I would suggest just doing the buffet unless you have a couple of hours to spend there.

This year was my 2nd PeachTree and definitely will not be my last. The course is not for the weak that is for sure. If you plan on running in the Peachtree road race I would highly recommend signing up as an Atlanta Track Club member, so you are guaranteed entry into the race, otherwise to get in the race it goes by a lottery and you may or may not get to register for the race. Also, It would also be wise to run another race before this one that is a Peachtree qualifier, meaning that you can use your time to be seeded for the PeachTree Roadrace so you can be further up in the wave. If you run at least 8-10 minute miles, you do not want to be in the back, as the majority of those who take part in the race towards the end are walkers. 

Whatever you do, DO NOT cheat. Just like the rest of us, you start at the starting line and you end at the finishing line. As of 2017 they now have added timing chip areas because there were several people who were starting towards the middle and finishing, but never ran the entire course, because they just wanted their t-shirt. Just like everyone else, I know people are having to pay to run this race, but in order to get a shirt, it is only fair that you complete the entire course. It is my understanding that those who cheat will be banned from future races, so do not cheat. I run in the D wave and saw quite a few people wearing G's and below who were cheering for people on the sidewalks, so I can only assume they will just start wherever and finish, yet never completing the entire course.

Keep in mind this is the largest 10K in the world. If you plan on racing, definitely take MARTA or have someone drop you off. The race starts at Lenox mall and finishes at Piedmont Park. If you park at the Mall, your car will not be anywhere near you. Give yourself plenty of time to get to the starting line prior to the race and make sure you get plenty of sleep the day before the race....

The race is on the 4th of July, so make sure the week before the race you stay hydrated... The biggest health related issue I see is due to hydration. July is extremely hot, so make sure you have plenty of liquids the days before the race and make sure you stop at the water stations that are on the course. They are about every mile.

As for clothing, do not wear cotton. Make sure you wear clothing that wicks away moisture, this would be clothing made from polyester blends. They are made from synthetic materials that do not retain sweat like all the natural fabrics do.

If you have not done the Peachree Roadrace, I'd highly recommend it at least once, so you can at least say you did it.

This is the area's best secret cheap gym.  I mean, what stair master could ever be as effective as the epic walk up the Porter steps?  It's an intense climb that can be both daunting and challenging, as well as crazy.   And going down is an adventure in and of itself, with the descent down into the wonder that is the Red Line.

The bronzed gloves are a nice and interesting touch as well, as I would assume that they are a representation of the work that went into the station, or someone's love of bronzing stuff.  And the train paintings are cool too.

Furthermore, this is a combination Red Line/Commuter Rail station, so it does have one of those convenience store-type places all the kids like.

(I should point out that I almost accidentally posted this review on the Watch Shop at Porter Square page... I was trying to figure out why an article on the T station would talk about watches, and then was like, wait a minute?! I've got the wrong page... I just thought I'd mention that).

I started classes here after I purchased a groupon, but I plan to keep with it! It's clear Grace has a passion for her work. I've only taken the barre mixed levels class and the barre cardio. I really love the barre cardio. It gives me a great overall workout. Colleen is a great instructor as well. The class sizes are smaller and more intimate than other group exercises I've attended. Colleen and Grace do a great job of correcting your form while keeping you motivated through the workout.

Headed down to Portland to eat as much as we could. White Elephant food truck was recommended by several friends so as part of the Mississippi food truck pod, we went to try their wings. They have numerous flavours of wings to choose from and they were 6 for $8. The owner was super friendly and helpful in helping me make my decision - went for the recommended Uncle OG's Sticky Icky Wings. Everything is make to order (which is a  from a good truck), so the wait was about 10minutes.

When my name was called I was so excited to dig in! The wings were freshly fried and the owner said they'd also just made a fresh batch of sauce  I could smell the delicious sauce and waft of fish sauce and garlic as I hurried back to our table. The wings were big and juicy (not those tiny wings you sometimes get at bars), fried to perfection, and that sauce was the bomb! It was sweet, salty, tangy and spicy. One of the best wings I've ever had, and I'll definitely be back to have more wings and try other items on the menu.

He has really perfected his craft and knows how to bring your paint back to life or how to get out the toughest stain. I recently had my Mustang Cobra detailed inside and out and it looks brand new! The paint shines and the interior is immaculate. They were able to take out the scratches that the car wash left as well as shampoo the rug and get into every tight spot of the interior. The inside looks so good! I just made an appointment to get my girlfriends BMX X5 windows tinted. Alex always goes above and beyond to fit me in when I need an exterior hand wash or an express detail. I highly recommend these guys over all the rest!

I visited today with my 3 yr. old granddaughter, when it was time to go she didn't quite grasp the fact that everyone had to leave.  As I was working with her that we had to go, the manager came over to her and said "you have 4 seconds to get out" since she didn't understand (she is only 3) he than said "okay, you can never come back!) she cried and was so heartbroken... I told the receptionist up front and all she said was "I'll tell the manager"
Well not to worry, we will not be back...you don't treat a 3 yr. old in this manner...shame on you!

Overall poor experience.  Difficulties ordering due to payment processing problem.  Placed order on 10/21/16 with quoted delivery time of 5-7 business days and did not receive wood until 11/7/2016.  Understandable given the time of year I ordered but I had hoped for better communication.  Could have overlooked those things if the wood was as advertised.  Unfortunately that was not the case as the wood is very green and will not be useable until next year.  If you want to know if wood is green it's easy to tell as it sounds like meat searing on a hot pan when it is burning.  I will now have to purchase expensive kiln dried wood to have fires this winter.  Very disappointed.

My two boys, age 6 and 7, attended My First French Bakery camp.  They had so much fun and asked to sign up for more camps there.  Unfortunately, the summer is nearly over, and we have travel plans for the rest of the summer.

The camp had two instructors and maybe two older kids as helpers.  There were about 15 kids at the camp.  The camp started at 9 and ended at noon, Monday to Thursday.  The price is higher than other camps, especially only for three hours, but it is well-justified because the kids get to prepare and taste so many different recipes each day.

I registered the kids online a few weeks prior to the start of the camp.  The online registration was staightforward.  Not much info regarding what to bring or what to expect.  They don't really need anything.  Everything is provided.  At pickup on the first day, both kids asked to bring a water bottle instead of getting cups of water from the dispenser.

Each morning, kids get dropped off, and parents sign them in.  But then at pick up, there is really no formal sign out procedure.  I made sure I arrived well before noon so that they would not wander off while others are being picked up and are not left unattended.  

They made and sampled quite a few dishes each day.  Quiche, bechamel sauce, crepe, croque monsieur, ratatouilli, salad with dressing, beignet with chocolate sauce, baguette, macaron, apple tart are the ones I recall.  At this age range, I don't expect intense kitchen instructions.  My older son went to Central Market cooking camp before, and that was more demonstrations than hands on.  At Foodie Kids, the instructors were friendly and patient.  The kids were engaged and given enough hands on participation, which they enjoyed tremendously.

On the last two days, they held a "bake sale" out front for charity.  The kids had a lot of fun prepping and selling the food they help make and lemonades.  I can see how parents may feel they they have to pay extra for the food the kids should be bringing home.  But then, the proceeds go to a charity and the kids have fun while learning.  It's all good.

This place is great! Food is delicious. The service is fantastic. We go every week. Today we met the owner. What a great person. Spoke to us about the menu and how much he loves to share with his customers meals from his country. You can tell he loves what he does and enjoys having people enjoy his food. 

My husband and I are originally from NYC and we are foodies. Travel lots and tried many different restaurants. You can't go wrong here. When the owner tells you is not about the money but making sure we try the food from his country -- and that we enjoy it-- you know the food is made with lots of heart. 

Great portions. Great Taste. Great Service. Great Prices.

When I saw the pic of the lovely couple for Sandy Springs Locksmith, I knew they would handle me with care. I had a small issue that (I thought) could easily be resolved over the phone. I called, asked my question and was given a brief yet clear response. I got off the phone and tried what was suggested with relative ease. Voila! Problem solved.

In a time when it's hard to trust service providers (especially as a woman), Sandy Springs Locksmith showed me in less than five minutes that they are a reputable and integrity filled company. THANK YOU, SSL for having small-town values in the big city.

I highly recommend and would pay for their services over and over again. 

10 for customer service!

I saw Gary at the beginning of august for stuttering. Somewhat of a creepy guy, he let me into his house and had me get comfortable on his couch. He asked me some basic questions about my experience and then we got started. His dogs barked occasionally throughout the session from a back room. After the session I left quickly. I found no change in my behavior or the nature of my problem. Gary wrote me an email starting with the phrase: "Got a bit over loaded yesterday and today." Not my idea of professional discourse. As of now, less than one month later, my speech problems are worse than ever and i see absolutely no advantage from my session. Charlatan.

There were about 18 of us and we rented out a private track to celebrate my friend's bachelorette party.  I think if you go with a large group, that is definitely the way to do it.  We all raced against each other which was fun, we didn't have any "strangers" racing against us.    Our briefing was straightforward, with a bit of humor, and easy to understand. We suited up, and hit the track in different heats.  We were able to do 4 different races of 10 laps each race and they took all the top times and had us do a 15 lap race against each other.  Since we were all girls in our 20's and 30's, we had a blast doing it together.  I'm not sure if I'd just go with a few friends and race, but since it was a competition among friends, that made it fun. We also got print outs of our race times before we left.  Overall, it was a great experience.

Sunvena Solar was not my least expensive quote, but I chose them for the reputation and recommendations - not to mention how easy they were to work with when she came to do the home assessment which was more educational than the others. Everyone at Sunvena that I communicated with were knowledgeable and courteous, I felt like we were family.
I'm highly satisfied with everything, from Sunvena coordinating installation of my new roof before my solar installation to the consultation with Nathan after the install to show me how everything works and what to expect. I'll definitely recommend Sunvena to friends and family who are interested in switching to solar.

This is just one of those shops that you just have to go to! The employees are over the top friendly. The bikes are well polished and ready to test ride. And riding one of these beauties will.ake you want to take one home, well I was ready to sign the line until the wife reminded me I will be out of commission for a year and it will only sit in the garage. Well I made plans to come back and buy the fastest one they had on the lot! Great show room guys! Thanks for the VIP treatment!

If I had known that renting from Columbia Residential properties would be such a nightmare, I have would have steered clear of these places. Complaints of mold and mildew were completely ignored, even after forwarding corporate photos of furniture and clothing that was destroyed by living in their poisonous apartment units. The property manager was too busy hanging out with her boyfriend during office hours to actually do her job. Not to mention how rude, and unprofessional she was. Seeing as the apartment complex goes through several property managers over a course of a few years, this should be an indication that something is amidst. 

Did I mention that they will find every way not to let you out of your lease and will refuse to return your security deposit? If you can, steer clear of this company. Seek out the services of more professionally run apartment complexes that will give you your money's worth.

We LOVED working with Nicolette as our doula, and we had a very positive birth experience for our first child. Nicolette was with us every step of the way - from prenatal care to labor and delivery to postpartum. I especially appreciated how Nicolette involved my husband - half the time I didn't know who was massaging my back, I just knew that I was supported the whole time. I would HIGHLY recommend a doula to any parents-to-be. Added bonus are the classes / support circles / etc that Brave Birth offers!

After deciding upon a Yamaha G2 Baby Grand as the piano that my wife wanted to play upon, I searched the local stores in the San Francisco Bay Area and all they had were well used ones or the classic ebony black.  I was looking on Craig's List and I saw a beautiful satin mahogany yamaha g2 that would be perfect.  The only problem was that it was in Portland.  I called Portland Piano Company that was advertising it and talked to Ron and he said that the piano was in great condition and played wonderfully.  The price was right but how to evaluate whether the piano was right was the question.  I phoned a local piano tuner and he recommended a fellow piano tuner in Portland.  I called him and he called Ron and asked the right questions.  They had known each other and respected each others opinions. Between the two of them I got the reassurance that I needed.  Now how to get the piano to the Bay Area.  I was in luck the store's moving truck company was going down to California that very week and I got a special moving price.  I started the process on Monday and by Saturday we had the piano in our front room.  It was just as Ron said it would be.  They gave a 5 year labor and parts guarantee and agreed to let my local tuner tune the piano in a few weeks, all within the agreed to price.  We couldn't have been happier.

They put us brown people in a corner room and put the other customers outside with everyone else. There were two of us who came first, and they worked on only one of us at a time while working on the other customers who came after us. Clearly a very racist place for those who are brown. We were asked if we're from Mexico...seriously??!! I was sitting there waiting in my chair with my feet soaking while my friend was being given the pedicure. My water got cold, but no one came to check on me. The person who had started working on me left to work on the other customers who came after us. We weren't even shown or told about the massage chairs and how to work them. The remote was tied to the chair. And, as always, they talk amongst each other in their Asian language, leaving us wondering if they're talking smack about us. I would not recommend this place for anyone.

I started coming here after my employer switched insurance providers to Aetna. Once the kinks in filling prescriptions were ironed out (whether to fill at AbsoluteCare's pharmacy or through my insurance's mail order), everything is good. Terry Hackworth is knowledgeable and I feel comfortable seeing him as my primary physician. Yesterday I called to see if I could be seen the same day, without an appointment,  for an issue with my leg swelling with pain and redness. I was given an appointment with Dr Ann Hoos who is extremely knowledgeable. She was able to treat the issue immediately and I'm feeling better already.

Nice Marina located in walking distance to downtown. Over priced.  You should use launch service  as the mooring field is quite far out.   My experience was that they are not organized.    I made a reservation for 2 nights  through the online form and never received a confirmation.  When I called to check on it, they thought I was coming for 1 night.  It all got squared away on the phone- then I sent an email reconfirming for 2 nights (it's not their practice to give written confirmation)  I receive a note  back that all was OK.  Upon arrival we were escorted to our mooring.  (no problem)  the following morning while we were enjoying breakfast we felt a thud... it was the launch.  She wanted to know if we were planning to stay another night (hello......)  When we replied yes, she told us we needed to move (right away) as we were not on a transient mooring the customer whose mooring we were on was at the dock.    I told her that we were placed on this mooring - she graciously apologized and said "mistakes happen" as I made my way up the damp deck in my pajamas and sock.  That wasn't super impressive, but not  unusual for the industry, so they still get a 3 star...  sadly.

Originally was happy about the car care center--thinking I'd finally have access to honest mechanics. To start with, I only did oil changes and minor stuff at this service center but then decided to trust them to replace a headlight in my car.

When I picked up the car it was daylight. Upon my first nighttime use of the car I noticed the headlight was on--but very obviously pointing at the ground. It was frustrating to me that I had to make a second trip for something they should have checked. When I took it back in, they said that it shouldn't need aiming. Replacing a bulb doesn't disturb the aim--but they had also replaced the socket  (at a pretty significant expense to me.) Regardless of what "should" happen, they should not argue with me and checked it. The aim of the headlight was so obviously wrong they could have seen it in broad daylight shining up against a wall--and should fix it.

When they took it in the second time and had it for about an hour--they said they tried but could not adjust the aim because it would need to go to the dealer as a screw was stripped/it was impossible for them to adjust. Lots of BS talk because my trip to a factory authorized mechanic for my car said someone had broken the headlight frame that is under the hood. The only way it could have been broken is from an impact like a fender bender (which there wasnt) or a mechanic putting pressure on it.

I'm now looking for the regional manager for AAA service center to file a complaint and to pay the $600 for a new headlight bracket and labor, to replace what they broke! Beware of AAA Car Care Plus--not only are they not knowledgeable but even worse, they are not telling customers the truth--and I thought that was the point of having AAA service centers!

One of - okay THE - nicest playground I've been to so far. 

It is always clean. There are plenty of benches for weary caregivers to rest while the kids run around and burn off that endless supply of energy. 

There are two play structures, both with slides and an array of climbing structures separated by a fence. One side for tots and one for older kids. There's a substantial set of swings (6 total - one for all ages). 

The playground is adjacent to a set of large baseball fields, tennis and basketball courts. 

There is no parking lot but I've never had trouble finding an on street space on beautiful LaGrange street. 

Its proximity to the plenty of shops and restaurants along Centre Street lend to making the visit to the playground a multi-purpose outing. I know how much effort it took to get the kids loaded up and out the door - so let's make the most of it! 

While it can get busy, it's never been so overwhelmingly crowded that my introverted personality couldn't handle it. I've always been very comfortable with the amount of kids and guardians. 

This is our favorite playground in the city so far, it has become our regular spot.

We got there around 6:45 on a Thursday night, and wanted to sit at the bar and watch the cook a do their thang, as we heard that was the best part. There were two open spots at the bar, and we asked the hostess of we could sit there. She said no, they were reserved for some of their 'regulars'. For a place that doesn't take reservations, this was quite dissapointing. We could have started becoming regulars, but probably won't due to this pretentious attitude. Sorry, nuestra. Going somewhere that wants us next time!

Visited Angela's Pizza while my Mom was in town. My mom had a salad and a few slices of pizza. I ate the rest of the pizza. My mom said her salad was pretty bad. Have to knock down my overall rating a bit for that. 

The pizza was pretty good, though. I'd rate it 8 / 10. It was better than chain pizza like Papa John's or Domino's, but not quite at the level of some of the best pizza restaurants I've been to. Crust was a slight bit burnt on our pizza, but not too bad. The crust was also a bit too light and thin for my liking, but it tasted alright.

Service was OK, but not great. Don't think I ever got a refill on my water and I didn't see the servers around much. I'll give service 6 / 10.  

Overall, I'm a bit torn between giving this 3- and 4- stars. I'd go with 3.5 stars if they'd let me, but since I can't, I'll give it 3 for the bad salad (2 / 10), good pizza (8 / 10), OK service (6 / 10), and moderate value (6 / 10).

I might give this one another go at a future date. Would like to push it up to 4 stars and feel like it was pretty close to that level if not for some minor issues.

I am so torn with this place! We have ordered 4 or 5 pizzas from here and have had the same problem with all of them. The dough is a total flop- literally! You try to pick the pizza up out of the box and if it doesn't completely tear apart and you are able to keep the piece together, then all the toppings fall of. Even with two hands you can't keep the pizza and all the toppings together. Try cutting the slices with a knife and it's like trying to cut through rubber. The flavor is great and the ingredients are quality, I really wish they could get the crust crispy!

I spent an entire day with Kristal in three locations, doing a full website re-branding shoot for my Body Wisdom Nutrition website. It was a lot, but Kristal is a gifted pro and helped me feel totally comfortable and confident all day. Everyone should smell some calming essential oils at their photo shoot! She was completely encouraging and great at styling the background and helping me choose outfits and accessories. 

I ended up with so many great photos that it was extremely difficult to pare them down to 30! I have never liked so many photos of myself. 
Overall Kristal was so professional, quick getting me the photos, and excellent about communication. I recommend her to everyone and I can't imagine going to anyone else for photos in the future.

After reading a recent Thrillist article on traditional and unique ramen eats in Atlanta, I found out about Pijiu Belly.  

We decided to check it out and were pleasantly surprised by the decor and ambiance.  The bar was fairly packed, so we grabbed a table.  The menu while at first looks to be simple, became evident that their offerings were not and choices had to be made.  We opted for the mini corn dogs to start which was great with the sweet mustard.  For entrees, I had the bulgogi cheesesteak and my better half the raymun soup.  The portions are bigger than we expected, which is not a bad thing.  The flavor of each dish were very satisfying and enjoyed to the last bite.  


I would recommend this place if you are looking for a    fun and casual dinner that packs in bold flavor in a great setting.  Can't wait to try the to rotisserie chicken and kickin' it on the patio!
