While I didn't end up getting my wedding dress from Alfred Angelo, I DID get the best service there, so I felt it only fair to write a nice review.

First off, I hated dress-shopping. It's not that I mind shopping so much (hey, I'm female!), but the whole process of getting an entourage of girlfriends together and then getting trussed up like a frosted cupcake for them to ooh and ahh over is sort of nightmarish to me. I did that on my first dress-hunting outing (at David's Bridal, incidentally) and it was miserable. 

I think Alfred Angelo was our next stop, and it was less miserable, but still disheartening. All the dresses just seemed so... well, /dressy/. Full of lace and frills and beads and bows... I wanted something simple and understated (and not too pricey, cuz hey, I'm only gonna wear it once), but that seemed to be a tall order, cuz I wasn't having much luck.

I went back a week or so later, by myself, and got the same good service that I had the first time (no complaint at all, there). This time, I happened upon the idea of getting a bridesmaid's dress, but ordering it in white or ivory. I tried on a number of different styles, but unfortunately, none of 'em were /quite/ what I had in mind. Still, each sales person that I dealt with was polite and friendly and helpful, and overall made the experience much more pleasant than I thought it'd be.

I found my "dream dress" elsewhere, but Alfred Angelo was still my favorite spot in my dress-hunting expedition. Perhaps other brides will have better luck there than I did -- I'd certainly recommend giving them a try!

Philosophers say that perfection is an elusive goal unreachable by imperfect human beings.  And when our woodworker placed an errant fastener in his otherwise perfect workmanship, it was time to call in Matt Burstein of Burma Design to mitigate the error and repair a small fragment of the world.

The basic project had seemed simple enough: fabricate and install three fluted oak columns to match an existing column made over a hundred years ago.  And while it seemed simple, it required the precise milling of quarter-sawn oak stock and the careful matching of stain and varnish of the 1890s.  The woodworker's results were spectacular, marred only by the calamity of a screw just breaking through the surface at the edge of one of the columns.  

After a hundred hours work, this seemed a cruel twist of fate -- the stuff of ancient Greek tragedies about the hubris of mortals aspiring to perfection reserved to the gods.  But like a Euripidian' deus ex machina, Matt Burstein of Burma Design Antique Restoration descended upon the problem and set things right.  

Matt carefully filled and smoothed the area, matching the color, and painstakingly restoring the look of the grain using an artist's brush and custom mixed pigments.   Truly a remarkable process to watch.

And, of course, both woodworker and client have nothing but praise for Matt's work.

Door #8: Milltown Arms Tavern
Door #9: King of Pops Walkup Window

Her racing experience added to her professional service and also helped me learn some important things about the protective gear. Jessica was also very helpful in assisting me with the first time use of my Honda Credit card. The girls made it a most enjoyable experience. And of course the always friendly and super knowledgeable Jason lent his expertise to make it a perfect buying experience. Highly recommend these friendly and very professional folks! Mac Lanagan.

We are nerdy tourists that appreciate local history and museums. I absolutely loved all the local Portland history here. We arrived just before they closed the doors for the day, but the staff were kind and patient and allowed us to peruse the rooms at our leisure. We didn't mind the price of admission because we knew it was an investment in keeping up a local historical landmark. In each room there was great descriptions of the room, it's inhabitants and period pieces. The decorations were era specific, which I really appreciated. Down stairs there was a great deal of history of how the Pittock family helped develop Portland. Outside there is an amazing view of the city. We were amazed at how many landmarks we could identify as we looked around. It's a really great place to visit!

Unbelievable!! I thought I was working with a used car salesman! Initial meeting with Abigail about options and $1000 had to be immediately given to her ... yikes, what??! it didn't end there..then, she showed us a 2018 home and said she'd give us 30% off to total around 80K..as she was making copies of our I.d's we just chanced to look at a brochure of new 2020 homes conveniently on her desk and found the same exact model and it was 65k..!! We should've walked out then but we had hopes that we also would be given that same home, New and with the 65k price.  Well, curious as I was on past sales, I started looking at their reviews and since this was not a $20 item, I was a bit concerned on the horrible experiences other customers had from them, so...I asked Abigail if all their concerns had eventually been resolved.. her response, Oh come on, anyone can put negative reviews , no one reads that anyways..Didn't even ask which one specifically or that they took care of them.. she was very defensive and didn't want to discuss it further!

Okay, well with COVID creating havoc on our job routine and not all positive about the near future on our jobs we decided to hold off so we asked for our $1000 back and it's been 2 weeks and several emails and still nothing.. her response, just wait we don't hold money, the bank does !!

We will give her a few more days then hopefully take time off to meet with the General Manager, Nikki Todd on this issue.

Wish us luck folks, we really need our money right now..

My 3 sons are all customers so this is my third time around with wisdom teeth surgery.
The staff is professional and caring.  The doctor went above and beyond more than any other medical professional I've ever encountered to explain the risks of surgery and the FL laws related to addictive pain medicine that he is able to prescribe post-op.
My son this past month didn't want the oxy that the doctor could prescribe because he is an athlete and will work thru his pain.  The doc explained how is own son didn't need potentially addictive pain meds, either. 
In summary, I like FOS for their position on educating patients, pain management and a faith based practice that said a prayer for my son prior to surgery.
They worked with me on scheduling and payments as well.  The location is convenient to I4 and 417.

We had so much fun this past weekend for my son's birthday. We booked this place with enough time ( a month before). I had never heard of this place before but a couple of mamas recommended it. 
I can't thank enough to Eddie, who I was emailing since the beginning. He assured me that everything was taken care of and let me tell IT WAS. The only thing I brought was the birthday cake. 

We ordered some starters for the adults from the bar, and the birthday package included the pizza and drinks. 

The coaches DID an AMAZING JOB!!! handling all the kids, they start a warming, training section and then the kids can have a real play against parents. WE ALL HAD A GREAT TIME!! THAnKS

We went there for my birthday dinner and while making the reservation this was mentioned.  When we reached the restaurant (on time), it was partly full with quite a few empty tables but the hostess guided us to the end of the restaurant to a table right next to the restrooms ! When we refused to seat there, we were moved to a table in the middle of the restaurant even though a couple of tables by the window were empty.  Long story short we were totally disappointed with their service!
The food was average and pretty forgettable.  We ordered two appetizers, two entrees and some bread (you have to pay for this) and even then we were not full.  They made absolutely no effort to make my birthday a memorable one. I don't think i will return !

I want to start by saying that I absolutely LOVE cryotherapy, but after my experience today at Restore Cryotherapy, I probably will go elsewhere. When I walked in, the place was empty and the employee behind the front desk was on the phone. I did not initially see her until she moved the sign on the desk to try and hide herself. She did not greet me or acknowledge me until I walked right up to the front desk. I am not sure the importance of the phone call, but would have appreciated at least a "hello."  After hearing some of her phone conversation, she finally acknowledged me by mouthing, "just a minute." I not only felt like this was unprofessional, but after waiting for a minute, it did not sound like she was getting off the phone any time soon, so I left. I did not receive any services and was frustrated that I wasted my lunch break on this. 

The two stars I gave were for my first experience at Restore Therapy, as the gentlemen who helped me was very friendly and helpful. The store itself is clean and organized as a whole. Unfortunately this negative experience has forced me to look for other places to receive my cryotherapy treatments.

Tonight was my second class here, and it was even better than the first one. This is a top notch club, and I could not recommend them enough. I had never fenced previously, so I was unsure how the experience would go. The coaches made me feel comfortable and give great individual attention. I am so happy that I made the decision to try fencing out, and so happy that I chose to do it here. Daniel Hondor is a great coach, and you can tell he truly cares about your experience at Olympia Fencing Center. Whether you're an adult who is curious or never had a chance as a kid, or you're looking for somewhere to send your children, I think this is the place you should be going to.

Finding a doctor, mechanic, or dentist is often like playing a lottery ticket.

But I think I have a winning one with Dr. Glasgow and the Linworth Family Dental team. 

I had moved from CLE a few years ago but stuck with my old dentist for years, then my girlfriend recommended me to Linworth Family Dental. I had a cleaning done with my old dentist, but knew that I might need a root canal in the future. 

I was able to get my records transferred to Linworth Family Dental within 24 hours, and a few days after that I met Dr. Glasgow and her team. The dentist office itself is on a nice street just west of Linworth, a village just west of Worthington. 

I waited only 15 minutes for my appointment, as I had scheduled it later in the afternoon. The waiting room was clean and airy, and it felt upscale and modern. The hygienist, Rebecca, was super-nice and helpful, as was the front-desk team. The front-desk team was a lifesaver--they rescheduled me from 6:10 to 4:50 on very short notice!

After being evaluated and having my X-rays scanned, I met with Dr. Glasgow and she explained that I would need a root canal, but also explained why and how it would take place. She also helped me with a few other things about the procedure, as I'd never had a root canal done before. 

She then referred me to a good endodontist, and I had my root canal taken care of the next day. I will have to make a follow-up visit for my temporary and permanent crowns in a few weeks, but I'm excited to discover Linworth Family Dental. Short of an actual winning lottery ticket, this is a pretty good consolation prize! :)

As a transfer student, I needed to find housing quickly that was close to UT and affordable. The co-ops have exceeded my expectations and I believe everyone should experience this community first hand. 
I'm typically a shy, introverted individual but found it easy to make friends here and am loving the co-op lifestyle. Some people say this is a "hippy" or "alternative" lifestyle but that should deter anyone. The people here are open, kind and genuinely care for your well being. On top of that, the people working in the office are great individuals who put a lot of effort into making sure you're comfortable.
I have personally lived in Nueces in the Super Co-op for the past year and it's the best deal on West Campus. Plus I'm two blocks from campus! I have my own bedroom, bathroom and share a kitchen in my suite. You have to do 2 hours of labor a week but the rent is worth the trouble. 

All in all, be here or be square.

I have had a loved one here for 4 months.  This is a new facility so some brief chaos is to be expected as they staff and learn routine. However, the turnover of staff in this place is incredible!  The chaos is ongoing. The nurses are loving caring people overworked and being taken advantage of by an administration not willing to provide enough help. There are simply not enough care givers.  Corners are being cut constantly.  Everyone who is working there is disgruntled and looking to jump ship.  All of the families I've spoken to are worried.We are paying over 6 grand a month to be worried!!  There are very few engagements for residents. Most they do have are volunteers. The salon is not regularly staffed to keep residents looking and feeling good. The food has gone from excellent to mediocre, smaller portions.  My mom has lost 15 pounds in 4 months!!  Maybe at some point this place will be run as beautifully as it is decorated.  But for now RUN! Run fast as you can in another direction. Autumn Leaves is sadly not ready for the task ahead.

If I ask my daughter (now 1 month shy of 4) on any given day what she'd like to do, her reply would be, "the cupcake place," which is of course because her favorite activity at Foodie Kids is to decorate cupcakes. We have been many times alone, and have had really easy playdates here. I have yet to attend a birthday party here, but I can imagine it's fabulous! The store itself is very fun with lots to look at, get inspired by, and play with- like tea sets on the kid-size table. The owner and staff are so personable and a real pleasure to visit! Excellent place to stop and grab a birthday gift too!

Still the best. My last review of Mr. Trevena was more than a decade old so I wanted to write a quick update:

Since then I have worked with him to obtain the following:

2014 Obtained my Citizenship (big Hurrah there!)
2018-2019 Green Card application for my mother who may come and live with me due to health issues.

I won't write a long review this time as I was more than detailed last time.  Mr. Trevena has delivered his side of the deal every time, every step of the way. He is professional, trustworthy, compassionate, knowledgeable, friendly always one step ahead of the game. 

For Central Texas I still would recommend him as the go-to-representation for dealing with matters related to immigration law.

Thanks Mr. Trevena and team!

Heard great reviews and was excited. 
Will NEVER be back.
Our waitress never checked on us after our food was served.
They wagyu beef was over cooked. 
The pasta was a bit pricey, but we were ready to try it since our appetizer was so good. It was ok, and way over priced. Really.
The "no smoking" back patio had one person out there, and it was a waitress, on break, smoking. Really?
The proscuitto was wonderful as our appetizer, but the rest just ruined it for me.

Have you ever taken a bite into something and instantly heard...the dulcet song of Angels something?!  Love at first Bite! Seriously.  This place is incredible.  I can't say I have ever had Czech food but apparently I am a fan! The Schnitzelwich is a large pounded pork loin deep fried and served up on a ciabatta roll with a red pepper papricka schmear.  Dear lordy!  Life changing.   I also tried the spinach soup which is a cream based pureed concoction which was also pretty grand.  There are a number of other awesome things to try on this menu.  I believe they are only open on the weekdays (like many food carts in P-town) so come on a nice weekday.

My dad was recently at Beverly Hospital & a woman, from Care Dimensions, came bursting into the room 10 minutes after the doctor told us my dad was going to die.   
She was a salesperson, rude, unprofessional & started by saying, "so, what is going on, how did we get here.
She jumped right into the menu of services that Care Dimensions offers & then abruptly said, I will be in the building until 2:00 pm if you want to sign up for hospice.  My 84 year old mom asked if hospice was covered by insurance & she said she did not know.
There were 9 of us in the room, all well educated & all felt that the Care Dimensions woman was cold, unprepared & should have taken the 5 minutes to read my dad's chart before bursting in & burdening us.

I've worked at indoor soccer facilities for a combined 4 years or so, played indoor and outdoor my whole life. Rose City Futsal is, hands-down, the best environment for futsal I've ever seen.

Great schedules, competent refs, the right atmosphere (nobody two-footing you on a work night kinda thing), bar with local beer on tap and surprisingly good food, friendly staff, hour-long game blocks that afford an actual warm-up, everything in good shape (scoreboards, turf, game balls, etc), awesome viewing areas throughout, reasonable temperature (a little stuffy in the summer, but still better than most), and a pro-shop. They don't even gauge you for player cards, just $5 one-time and that's it, for life!

Personal preferences: no walls, good set of house rules, and tightly-called games. Even the ownership group plays here, so they have an ear to the ground as to what's happening.

I can't say enough good things about this place. I've been in the Portland soccer scene for about 5 years now, and this place is simply the best.

I have known the owner of this business for 7 years or so. I met him through aviation and we have trained together, traveled together, invested together, spent family time together, etc.  Al is a top notch person who I consider as a brother. Another reviewer left a review about "chronic tardiness." ... A lot of times, when people are training or have signed up for a tour, they don't understand the dynamics behind aviation.  Especially with helicopters.  Planning a flight has multiple facets; weather, airworthiness of the helicopter, the attitude and mental state of instructor and student / pilot and occupants and more.  This reviewer seems like he thinks the world should revolve around his time, when in fact, you can't trade time for safety. It looks like Al was trying to plan a safe flight, not rush, and make sure this guy was safe when flying. Al is a great instructor and business owner and nobody should rely on this guys review as accurate.

After nearly three years, my disability case has wrapped up with a judgement in my favor. Greg Reed was excellent, as was Craig, his paralegal. Between the two of them, they were always on top of my case, were there to answer any questions, and were extremely informative throughout the whole procedure. Not once did I feel like they put me on the back burner. Every phone call was returned promptly, and every email was replied to within 24 business hours. As opposed to the enormous disability law firms you see in ads, going with Bemis, Roach & Reed allowed me to deal only with the lawyer's paralegal, and the lawyer who would be physically present throughout the process. So, when the time came to sit in front of a judge, I was joined by someone I actually knew, had shaken hands with, and had joked with and conversed with in person, more than once. On top of all that, Mr Reed is a likable guy, someone that you'll be glad has your back in the fight that is applying for disability.

Mr. Reed was an absolute rock of stability in the courtroom when it came time for my hearing, which greatly allayed my own nervousness. I initially chose this law firm to handle my disability case because their office is only a few miles away from my home, but that was merely an incredibly happy coincidence as I couldn't have possibly made a better choice.

My mother was in this facility, and I visited my mom every weekend. She had Alzheimer's. One day, Pam, the social worker, called me at work at 4pm. Apparently, my mom had been raging all morning and afternoon.  Rather than call me when the raging started, she had her sent to Saint Elizabeth's psych ward and started using the term FTD to describe her condition. She said she had never seen such violent behavior. (My mom was 5'2" tall and about 105 pounds, mind you.) Since I worked for the Alzheimer's Association at the time (which is probably the real reason my mom was sent out, as I was fully aware that this facility did not have the required activities programming to market itself as having an Alzheimer's unit but did so anyway), I called contacts at McLean and had her transferred there. Her doctor there said my mom had no business being in a psych ward. She had Alzheimer's type dementia, and her behaviors were relatively common. I had her transferred to Newton Wellesley Alzheimer's Center, and the staff there cared for her lovingly and with tremendous empathy and kindness until she passed away yesterday. 

I'm writing this review now because I don't want any family to have to suffer through what we went through. If you are absent and don't really care about your loved one with dementia, then choose Golden Living Center in Dedham. However, if you love your mom or dad and plan on visiting regularly, then place your parent somewhere else. You will sleep better, trust me.

So I struggled with how many stars to give the Epicurean tour ... I settled on only two because it failed in the food category.  It was educational and entertaining because Alyssa was able to answer all questions and offered many insights into local culture.
As for the "food" I was disappointed.  Everyone agrees that the bakery and Cacao were positive experiences.  But this tour does not offer a true representation of the host of wonderful and fresh dining choices in the city.  In Good Taste was a waste - 3 crackers + mustard and ketchup?!?!? With Pinot Noir?!?!  
Definitely NOT worth the price.  This was billed as a foodie tour, not a city tour!

On Mother's Day, I was zipping my way up I-75 on my way to surprise my mom, singing along to my jams at the top of my lungs. I was feeling great! The road was nearly empty due to COVID-19 and I commented "Wow, I've shaved 20 minutes off of our ETA!" I kid you not, no sooner did the words leave my mouth did I see the flashing red and blue lights in my rearview. Oops! 

Next thing I know, I'm driving away with a summons for court after a stern talking to by the officer. Not to sound dramatic, but I was pretty devastated. There was certainly no more singing. Although the trooper said he "clocked" me at 94, he put 100 on the ticket. 30 miles over the limit in Florida is an automatic court hearing. It was my first time ever being pulled over. 

I reached out to a traffic lawyer that told me I was likely lose my license and wanted to charge me a $750 retainer in addition to whatever court fees and fines were assessed. Say what!?!

So I did some more research. The Ticket Clinic (TTC) came up in every search. I found it the low prices too good to be true, but being furloughed I didn't have much of a choice. I figured TTC might be the Walmart of law firms, but I gave it a shot and I'm so glad I did. My main concern was receiving points on my record and my insurance shooting up. For a mere $150 ($600 less than the first lawyer quoted me), TTC took care of the hearing for me an I received a "withheld adjudication." No points, and no conviction on my record. Awwww yissssss. Sweet, sweet victory, yeah. Sure, I'm still responsible for the court fees, but I expected it and that is a small consequence to endure for my illegal high speed karaoke session. All said and done, I still paid less than half of what the first lawyer wanted as a retainer. Boo-yah! 

I can't recommend TTC more! Hopefully, I won't need to use them again anytime soon... but should the situation arise, I have no doubt they'd be my go-to.

This review is for the office of the Parking Clerk.  Normally, just the mere mention of the Parking Clerk brings my blood pressure levels to a dangerous high.  However, I want to give credit where credit is due:  I went in to renew my parking permit, and the clerk I ended up working with was quick, efficient, and helpful.  The potential argument I had anticipated never even materialized.  She even tried to help me out with a parking ticket appeal, which was greatly appreciated.  I was in and out of City Hall in 10 minutes, permit renewed, parking tickets paid and all.  Your experience with the parking clerk will really all depend on who you get at the window, and what time of day/week you go.  If you go during a weekday around 2pm, you may be pleasantly surprised.  Low expectations are also key to your satisfaction here.  So, since the Parking Clerk's office never gets any love, I just have to point out the rare gem hidden in this pile of crap that is the MA Government offices.  Let's be honest... who LIKES working in a building that resembles a dungeon anyway....

I just returned home from a trip to Dover Saddlery and I was so pleased.  I am just beginning to ride again after a five or so year hiatus after college.  I was a little nervous and I had lots of questions about the items that I needed to purchase to fill in with what I already had. The staff were so helpful and gave me real advice on the products I knew I was interested in from online searches and past ownership.  The girl that helped us was very knowledgeable and helped us make the right choices.  On the outside, the store looks like it will be very small and based on the other reviews I thought it would be tiny!  I did not really think that this was the case at all.  They have a large selection and really utilize all of their space as most stores do in the area.  I will definitely return when I need items in the future!

Just got back from a 3 hour glassblowing class. It was great. We had two girls instruct us. One had been doing it for 9 years who was awesome, the other just 3.5 and who had just started working there, but she was good as well, althouhg needs some practice doing classes (as to be expected since she's new). We ended up with two pieces each and there were only 4 of us in the class which meant it wasn't rushed and we got very personalized attention. I like that we had choices of what we could make, and even though we didn't get to do EVERYTHING start-to-finish, I felt that I did enough to get a good experience of what it's like to work with glass. 

Some colors and objects were added money but it was definitely worth it to do what you wanted. I made an round blown ornament and a scalloped bowl. You have to let everything cool overnight and come back to get them so if you live far away it might not be the most convenient. 

This was a Living Social deal that I got but my mom and I are totally planning on coming back for another class. AND they do private parties so I'm thinking ahead for all sorts of cool things!

I don't know that there's anything overly positive that can be said about waiting for the ferry in Schwartz Bay. 

But here are some dos and donts. 
1. Don't speed on your way in. Every Islander I know has either had a ticket or a warning on that last stretch in. Just don't do it. 
2. Bring a snack. There's something incredibly awful about the food in the waiting area at Schwartz Bay.  If you really miss a ferry, by like 2 hours, you can walk and have a beer at the pub that's around the point. But don't risk that if you don't have time. 
3. Walk your dog. The only really redeeming feature of the Schwartz Bay terminal is the cute little dog park by the small ferry docks. 
Other than that, I don't know what to say. As someone who has travelled through that ferry terminal more than 200 times, I have a love hate relationship with it. I love that it's there, because I'd hate to have to go to Nanaimo to take a ferry, but it does nothing to make my trip better. Especially after they got rid of the café in the walk on waiting area.

I had a great first experience at Asmara. My parents, two friends, and I were all new to Ethiopian food, and the waitress patiently helped each of us figure out what we'd like best.  When she brought out the food not long after, she poured our individual entrees onto one huge central injera platter, explaining that it is a communal eating experience as we could easily pick at our neighbors' dishes as well.  We had informed the waitress that my dad has Celiac disease, and he was served on a separate plate with gluten-free injera.

The food was delicious.  I was very pleased with the spice and tenderness of my Begeeh Mloukhiya, lamb mixed with high fiber jute plant (which I did not really notice) and curried with a thick red pepper sauce.  I'd describe injera's flavor as a whole-grain sourdough, and the consistency is chewy and moist but still firm enough to tear up and use to scoop up the rest of the meal. The salad was simple--greens, tomatoes, and feta dressed with olive oil--and paired well with all the strong flavors of the entrees.   We also tried their honey wine, which was quite tasty and refreshing.  

I was quite satisfied with my portion, although my mom, who ordered the meat combination, actually felt she could have enjoyed a bit more.  There was plenty of salad and injera for the four of us.

I will definitely visit Asmara again!

This is an Asian/Japanese-style cafe located in Kits, on 4th Avenue. In addition to serving up various drinks, both hot and cold, they have various sandwiches and baked goods. I had a Matcha Latte, Japanese Cheesecake, and Matcha Pound Cake. While I wasn't a huge fan of their cheesecake, I enjoyed the pound cake and was impressed by their latte, which had a pretty good matcha flavour. The staff was friendly and the prices were fair. This is definitely worth checking out.

Matcha Latte ($4.75):
4/5
The latte was actually not sweet at all, but was slightly bitter with a creamy texture. It had a pretty good matcha flavour, which was quite impressive seeing that most matcha-flavoured drinks tend to be a little weak.

Japanese Cheesecake ($4):
3/5
The cake was more light and yogurt like compared to NY cheescake. The filling was creamy and tangy, but a bit lacking in flavour and gummy in some areas. Unfortunately, I wasn't a big fan of the crust beneath, which was a bit grainy.

Matcha Pound Cake (around $4-5):
3.5/5
The cake was a bit hard, but still tasty and had a mildly sweet flavour. The matcha flavour was a bit weak, but that is kind of expected from most matcha-flavoured desserts.

Summary:
Food: 3.5/5
Price: 4/5
Service: N/A
Overall: 3.5/5
Recommendations: Matcha Latte, Matcha Pound Cake

So, despite second thoughts, I went to a show here.  No, no, not the usual show.  Apparently sometimes they give the girls the night off, and open up as a music venue.

As my friend and I walked in, a stream of guys were walking out- having been told at the door that there were no dancers tonight.  Ha- thought that was kind of funny.  On that note, because the clientele here is so largely male- the women's' washroom was very clean (perhaps never used before?).

The show was good, and the space provided lots of areas to stand and sit.  The worst part was promptly at 2- the lights came on with shouts of "Get Out!"  Seriously?

That "Get Out' really rubbed me the wrong way.  I paid to get in, I paid for drinks, and then at 2am you have zero customer service.  Nice.  If an amazing band came to play here- I'd go see them, but I'd rather go somewhere else.

Meghan Alexander is truly a class act. We had some questions regarding the probate process with one of our projects, and she took the time to speak with us without charging a fee. An attorney's time is very valuable and most attorneys will charge for a consultation. But that's just the beginning. Meghan even recommended an option that would help us to avoid the probate process and possibly save us thousands of dollars. This speaks volumes about her character and integrity because this alternative option would not involve using her services. Meghan truly has the client's best interest at heart and, though we have not used her services yet, we most definitely will in the near future. Thanks, Meghan!

I purchased a Vita Spa from them and I have been very unhappy with the spa. To the credit of the company they did come out once and paid for spa specialist to come out once as well. This small four person spa has never been right. The water is never clean, and if you try to filter it enough to be clean then the water is so hot you can't get in it. Both the manufacturer and the folks at Unique Pools have told me, "that's the way it is". Well for $5000 you should not have to sit in a dirty spa or not be able to use it.

This experience has definitely been the opposite of relaxing.

After getting a deal online, I easily booked a tour through their website. The day before the tour, the captain had to cancel and he immediately gave us the option of rescheduling for the next day. This actually ended up being so much better, given the weather. 

Our captain (oy, cannot remember his name!) was welcoming, funny, and very relaxed, which helped all of us newbies to sailing. At 7pm, we disembarked from the Willamette boat ramp and headed down the river. We cruised by the Portland Yacht club, where all the cool floating homes are, around the island, and under a few bridges, finally heading back right right before reaching the Hawthorne Bridge. Sitting near the front of the boat, another guest and I helped with the sails and learned some new nautical terms (jib!) while the captain regaled us with tales of his travels and facts about the river and Portland. 

All in all, the deal we got was very well worth it and I recommend any of the tours through Scovare to friends. It is a very unique and fun way to see Portland!

Chris is AWESOME!  

Had relatives in from out of town.  Chris was very patient & helpful with our senior citizens!

Not the high drama stuff you see on TV, but very nice.  Chris knows his stuff about Austin history, haunted & creepy or not.  We've lived in Austin for fours and still learned a lot.  My aunt from Oklahoma just loved it and constantly asked Chris questions; which he always had the answer to.

This tour will be on the list every time we get out-of-towners and I recommend it to people of all ages.  Some of the stairs can be daunting, but my 71 year old aunt, while slower, didn't have any problems!

Thank You Chris.  My aunt will definately remember her trip AND everyone that cancelled on her (she ended up traveling alone) is so jealous of the pictures!

STAY FAR AWAY FROM THIS NIGHTMARISH PLACE !!! 

Aides are rude and untrained. They treat the patients like they are not human

Food is vile. Absolutely a disgrace that they think it's ok to feed this horrid slop to someone. They call the water in which broccoli was boiled, soup. It's is truly one of the worst places I have ever experienced. 


The place should not be allowed to still be operating. They are short staffed and they all get away with cruel and abhorrent behavior. 

No one cares. Even the doctor, who was obviously a reject from inferior schools and low rated hospitals shrugged off the bad behavior. The doctor could care less. Only there to collect her contracted $$$

Directors did nothing to improve things. They can't keep a director job filled for obvious reasons. They have NO CONTROL!!!

Handing out wrong drugs, not knowing what drugs they were giving out, leaving patients sitting in filth for hours even after being buzzed.

The state should close them down!!! NOW!!

I have tickets for Bottleneck purchased for Napa and paid for overnight shipping.. I have plans with 8 other woman who got the tickets from other venders and they have the tickets they purchased and they did not pay for over night but they have the tickets in hand. I have been waiting for my tickets for 3 weeks now nothing and OMG be aware that overnight does not mean overnight. My day for leaving on our trip is 5/19 the concert is 5/25 also another problem is they do not give you anytime for travel so if your concert is to far for don't buy from this company infact I would think twice about using them.. They are trying to tell me that the tickets might be here but no guarantee. Thats not what I expect from any companies that cares about customer service which tells me they do not care. I will not do business with them again and believe me when I say maybe is unacceptable when 3000.00 dollars is on the line. If they screw this up I will be out RV rental RV sight Tickets etc.  Not to mention the other 8 woman traveling with us..... Very happy to have found this place.  Gary was very helpful and knowledgeable (which I am not).  He helped suggest the proper plants and fish for our tank. I'm new to the Muay Thai program at Easton, and so far there's an immense amount to love about it, and also one thing that is crazy-making, directly related to the fact that I have experience prior to training at this gym. 

The things I love:
*GREAT teaching
There hasn't been a single coach that doesn't have great fundamental skills. All are dedicated. And the coaching team is unified in their teaching message. There's also a clear system for developing skill sets - there's always a "Focus of the Week" so you'll go one week working on round kick offense, the next on round kick defense, the following on clench, and so on. This is AWESOME, and my fundamentals knowledge has grown immensely just in the 1.5 months I've been here. Kick ass.

*Many of their teachers are fighters themselves - Danny Wilson, Wes Argrow, Matt Bloss, Terrence Moore. Inspiring!

*The community is friendly and supportive.

*The gym is clean, with thoughtful amenities like hair ties in the women's locker room in case you've forgotten yours, and two very nice showers to use after class if you need. 

*It's very family oriented, and they have a great children's program.

*Free parking which is easy to come by, even on busy days.

Awesome!

The one thing that's a bit crazy-making for me:

I've had 5.5 years of striking experience prior to starting at Easton 1.5 months ago - I trained 4 years in American Kenpo, and specifically in Muay Thai for over a year and a half, much of that time at Muay Thai America in Los Angeles - a well-respected Muay Thai training center that also trains professional and amateur fighters, many of whom fight in K1. Also, by-the-by, where you spar every single class no matter how novice you are. 

Easton's approach to people who have trained before is a bit haphazard. They have developed their own colored shirt system (akin to a belt system) for Muay Thai - Muay Thai typically doesn't have belts or ranks. They have thus created four levels of classes -
1. Kickboxing - all welcome
2. Muay Thai Fundamentals - Yellow Shirt and above - no sparring
3. Muay Thai Intermediate - Orange Shirt and above - limited sparring
4. Fight Team - Green shirt and above - sparring allowed

Which is kinda cool, and likely avoids some injuries. However, there doesn't appear to be any clear system to evaluate and properly place people. So there's no way to come into this gym at a certain rank, because their ranks are solely their own, so it doesn't appear to matter one bit if you've trained 10 years in Muay Thai, or not at all, everyone starts in the Kickboxing class - a fun, high intensity bag workout.  Presumably someone is keeping an eye out for skilled folks, and advancing them, but the advancement is just into the Fundamentals class - the most basic of the Muay Thai classes. There you languish for an unspecified, unclear period of time. 

The Fundamentals class is AWESOME, so it could be ok, except that the way it actually shakes out, I feel super limited. Wearing a yellow shirt, I appear to be only seen as an extension of my shirt. The teachers will encourage us to pair with someone of "like size and ability". Which appears to mean the same shirt color. But most yellow shirts are just learning pad work, many get confused by the drills, and so I spend most of my time working at an immensely slow pace, smiling and encouraging my partner while they stumble through it. I don't mind this at all, except if it's the only training I'm getting. And I would say 80% of the time, this is my experience. I long for the days of being challenged, and wish I could sometimes pair with someone who is more experienced than me so I can grow as a fighter in other ways.

Unfortunately, I haven't had a good experience so far in expressing this to the coaches. The response so far has been a shut-down look and encouragement to just focus on getting comfortable slowing down my strikes and let the instructors teach the fundamental pad work my partner needs. So it goes. 

I also miss sparring :(

Experienced students, be forewarned. It's great training, but may come with some frustrations.

YESSSSSS. Absolutely stellar vendor fit for the North Market! I had been hearing so many good things about their original location but never made it out there to try it, so when I saw they were moving to the North Market I knew this would be my chance. Their set up is a bit like Chipotle; you pick a base (salad, rice bowl, or injera bowl) and then pick your meats and veggies to go on top. I wanted to try a bit of everything, so I had the rice bowl with the chicken suqaar, spinach, chickpeas, and injera on the side. The woman at the counter suggested doing a half and half of the regular rice and the spicy rice, so I jumped at the opportunity to try both.  The combination of the spicy rice + spices in the chicken suqaar where almost too spicy for me... but I am a wuss. I'd say they are slightly spicier than a medium salsa. Next time I'll get some of that tasty-looking yogurt sauce to drizzle on top and cool it off a bit. I loved the spinach/potato dish, and the chickpeas were so incredibly creamy in texture. The regular rice still had a piece of cinnamon stick in it - so you know it's legit. It was incredibly aromatic and paired well with the other dishes. I love that they offer goat, and I'll have to get that next time. 

If you get a meat dish, you also get two veggie sides, so it ends up being a very generous portion of food! I thought the injera was a little too crumbly to use for dipping/wrapping, but it still tasted fantastic so I just ate bites of it with my entree. I had to make myself save half to take home so I wasn't painfully stuffed, but I could have kept eating forever. Hoyo's is  a fantastic deal; tons of flavorful, expertly prepared food, and plenty of options for veg/vegan eaters.

Well, this review is going to be all about my vagina so there's your heads up.

There are articles going around telling every woman to go get an IUD as soon as possible before Trump gets into office, but please do your research about IUDs. This is your body you are talking about so don't let some random article or a trending hashtag scare you into doing something that might not be beneficial to your health. Be smart. 

Planned Parenthood is great for an STD test or a pap smear. You know, things they probably can't mess up because they send the specimens out to labs and have nothing to do with the mechanics. 

I wanted an IUD, a copper IUD because I don't trust hormonal birth control. There is no way pumping your body up with estrogen and progesterone does not affect your breast cancer risk. Do some research.

Anyway, June 2016 I went and got the IUD inserted. I was told that even though I have never had children, that would not be a problem. IUDs work for everyone. Great! The insertion went smoothly (just some cramping) and for the past five months I have been hormone and stress free! 

Well, I went and got an ultrasound yesterday with my gynecologist (NOT Planned Parenthood) and guess what? My IUD had descended and was almost completely dislodged. I was told that IUDs are designed for women whose cervixes are at least 24mm-28mm, in other words women who have had children. Guess what I am. 20mm! So IUDs won't be effective for me because I am too small.

In Europe, every woman who wants an IUD is sent for an ultrasound to measure her. Then, an IUD is selected that will fit her. Do we do that in the United States? No. Because insurance companies don't want to pay for every woman to get an ultrasound. So they designed a "one-size-will-hopefully-fit-you" IUD and pray it works. It might work for some, but not work for others. Wouldn't it be nice if the Planned Parenthood "doctors" actually discussed these things with you? 

Oh, and my gynecologist also told me that MY IUD HADN'T BEEN WORKING FOR THE PAST 5 MONTHS. Because I was too small for it, it wasn't able to do its job properly. She said I am ridiculously lucky that I didn't get pregnant.

It is sad because, for some women, Planned Parenthood is their only option to receive reproductive services. Don't just take a doctor's word as fact like I did. Just like how you'll contact more than one plumber or repairman or appraiser for second opinions, do the same with doctors, ESPECIALLY the idiots at Planned Parenthood. Actually, just avoid them altogether.

So thanks, Planned Parenthood. I was almost an unplanned pregnancy statistic because of you.

The pontoons are nice for a slow time ride up the St. John's for 4-6 people (comfortably), you can make it to the springs and back easily. The staff is very friendly, check in and check out are completed quickly. Reservations are taken over the phone and held with a credit card, it's wise to call a week or two in advance. A nice way to spend a FL day!

After rearranging some furniture in my house, some "imperfections" in the previous paint job were now exposed.  The owner had left some old paint cans in the garage, the most recent had a label from the Drive In Paint Mart.  I grabbed a couple cans and a couple wallplates and headed to the store.  The guy behind the counter was very helpful.  First he tried to salvage the paint in the cans i brought in, but it was just too old.  Next he helped me match the colors i was working with and get me some new cans mixed up.  I told me the area I was painting and he sold me just enough paint to get the job done. I've been receiving colonics at All's Well That End Well for almost 3 years. It has been an enormous part of my treatment of long term Lyme Disease, and I know I wouldn't have gotten through it without this place. From the front desk staff to the colon hydrotherapists, these folks are the folks you want in your life. Their kindness, support, gentleness, reliability are second to none. Your therapist will walk you through every step, making sure that you understand exactly what's happening. Colonics are a vulnerable experience, can be uncomfortable, and sometimes are straight up painful, but the therapists are always happy to adjust settings, encourage breaks, and do whatever else they can to make your experience as pleasant as can be (especially considering the nature of what's going down!)  

Not only are they excellent colon hydrotherapists, they're just some of the best people to talk to! Sometimes during the week, I'll think..."I'll have to tell Jill all about this." They literally deal with your crap, and they do it with ease and accommodation. Just stellar people. If you're interested in colonics, call them, ask questions, and don't hesitate to make an appointment. You won't regret it.

This is my second visit to Spoleto.  I love the concept and since I'm a pasta fanatic this is perfect.  They have a great menu of pre-selected items.  But the best option is you choose a pasta, focaccia or salad and pick up up 6 ingredients and you can add premium toppings as well. 

I chose cavatappi with cheese, mushrooms, tomatoes, broccoli and artichokes with Meat sauce.  I added an Italian sausage as a premium topping. They warm the premium topping up in a stone oven.  You can choose some toasted ciabatta bread as well complimentary. 

The pasta was warm, flavorful and just the right portion size.  I would recommend this for a great little Italian meal.  And for two people with drinks it was under $30.

I was organizing a bus to a concert at Gillette Stadium and found Eco Ride on yelp. I was nervous about it because there were so few reviews and I would have had to put down a lot of money and hope the company would be legitimate. I spoke with Joel on the phone 4 or 5 times asking questions before the day of the event. He was okay with making some last minute adjustments (changing time and location of pick up and drop off) without no trouble. He was responsive by email and sent me adjustments to the contract as needed. Our driver Kevin came and was super friendly and accommodating (which is really a treat for a huge group of 23 year olds with many coolers and eager to have a good time) throughout the ride. 

While we tailgated, Kevin just asked for a burger and was happy to stick around and allow us on and off the bus to get our stuff. We left right on time from the stadium and he was open to taking back roads to alleviate some traffic which was a big plus. Someone left a phone on the bus and the driver called immediately to tell us, and Joel was there the next day to help us pick it up. That really impressed me. 

All in all the day was a big success. A few small things caused 4 rather than 5 star review:

1. The 50% deposit included ALL of the 20% tip. Ultimately I explained to the bus driver that we would be tipping at the end (and tipped over the 20%), but I wanted the option to make that decision after the service was provided. I asked for the contract to be changed to make sure our balance did not include the tip, but the driver's copy indicated that he must collect all of it at the time of pick up. Our driver was good about this, but I was disappointed that it was not corrected. 

2. Joel called the day of the trip and said we would be getting upgraded to bus with AC and when the bus arrived, we asked about the AC and he said there was no AC. Not a huge deal, but we were a bit confused about that. 

Mostly, this is a great company, so don't let the limited reviews dissuade you from using them!

My electric lawnmower would not start, so I let it sit in the storage room until the warranty ran out and then, after paying people to mow my lawn for months, read Carl's yelp review of this service place.  I love Carl F.

I love mowing the lawn, too.  The smell of the freshly cut grass, being outside, hearing the birds ... all reminds me of mowing our lawn as a kid and I really like it.  I was just a bit slow on knowing where to take it to get repaired.  

What prompted my search for a Black and Decker repair place, though, was when I was given my third  B & D tool.  A neighbor GAVE me his year old Hawgbuster blower sucker at his garage sale.  That's right... free.  He was getting rid of it because the bag would no longer fit on the Hawg.  

BTW, with a touch of a button, this Hawg both blows and sucks, so I feel like I was gifted a pretty amazing lawn toy.  Blowing and sucking should always be free, right?

So, I load my car up with the lawnmower and the Hawg, and I follow Carl's yelp review advice... 

They give me an estimate for $189 for my lawnmower to be fixed (as it is out of warranty) and then give me a brand new bag for the Hawg, saying it is still under warranty and the bag is free.  Total score.  Free Bag.  Free Blow.  Free Suck.

I did not meet a "Helmut" nor did i get a detailed explanation of what they were going to do to my lawnmower... I just wanted them to fix it, they said they would, and they did.

When I arrived to pick it up, the lawnmower looked brand new.  BSN... Brand Spanking New. Actually, I  had to ask if they had made a mistake... where was my dirty lawnmower? They also gave me a new battery, a new starter, and they sharpened my blades.  Seriously seemed like a $189 new lawn mower and totally worth it because now I can stop paying others to do what I like to do... mow my own lawn.*

Blowing, sucking... free.  Bag, Battery, energy, sharpness... free.  Yelp advice from my good friend, Carl... free.  Dewalt/Black and Decker Factory service... great discovery. (of course, you were expecting "priceless", right?  well, i just couldn't do it... and then again, i couldn't resist, because deep down, i knew what you were thinking...)

*this is a nice review, in theory, but this past summer I also took Hoa's advice and "killed my lawn"... which is to say, with the drought and all, I did not water it, at all. There is now a LOT less lawn to mow. 

Thanks to Carl my lawnmower is alive and thanks to Hoa my lawn is dead.  What is the christmas story about a woman who sold her hair to buy a watch fob and the man who sold his watch to buy a brush...?

My children have been experiencing a lice pandemic at their school. I was lucky enough to get away with them not getting it, but sent them to their grandparent's house over Christmas break, where they were exposed to another relative whose head was crawling in them. My MIL treated them without letting me know until after the fact and told me she had checked them, and they were "just fine" and I didn't need to come get them. Despite their objections, I got up really early and drove 8 hours round trip to get them, and took them straight to LKY on the recommendation of my hair dresser. Sure enough, my son had several very alive lice and some nits, despite it being 40 hours since my MIL treating them with Rid and using the lice comb that came with the kit. 

They were slamming busy, because it was New Year's Eve, but still got us in there and managed to check the whole family and get my husband in and out quickly since he couldn't take much time off from work.. My son is 10 and was mortified that he had it. I am so grateful we took him there, because the problem was over and done with after we took him there, and he was spared the humiliation (in his mind) of being sent home from school, or having to tell anyone. Plus, we just left all the stuff that came from Grandma and Grandpa's house in the car, and didn't touch it or the car for the next 2 weeks, so it was so much less work than dealing with lice normally would have been. He was declared lice free on 12/31, and we haven't seen a thing since then. I would never have used pesticide-based treatments on him, especially since they didn't do a thing to even slow the lice down, much less kill them, and am happy that those kinds of products aren't used here. Plus, the entire cost of treatment (which actually wasn't as much as I thought it would be, because they were so fast) and the lice comb will be reimbursed to me through my HRA VEBA account.

If you can't do anything else, at least get their lice comb. It is miles better than anything you can get at the local drugstore. It does pull the hair a little, but it so good that it picks up dust-sized particles of colored fuzz from their heads. My daughter has super-long, thick hair, and it does a great job of checking hers, which I was doing like crazy to make sure that even though she didn't have it, nothing got missed.

Great find!! 
We looked all over for a nice place to get chicks this year. 
We were really impressed with the setup. 

Chicks were healthy & organized in clean, ventilated pens. Large selection of breeds & some age ranges. 

Staff were really helpful & friendly, & helped us get everything we needed to start. Also answered a TON of questions we had as new chicken farmers. 

The book written by the owners was the perfect intro / guide on what to expect. We referred to it constantly as our chickies changed from week to week. 

Believe me, there are a lot of stores where chicks are in open tubs where they're very cute but you have no idea how many hands have reached in there to pick them up all week. 
Or breeders where the chicks are crowded in dank basements with heat lamps out, chicks sneezing or with infected eyes

Urban Farm Store is legit!

Came in to get my bike checked out after another bike shop had really let me down in terms of communication and knowledge. I had heard JRA had a good reputation with high-end mountain bikes, so I went there seeking some real professionals. I roll the bike in the shop, explain what my concerns are, and what I'd like done. First thing I hear is that I will need a new front outer chainring - I am totally on-board and give the go ahead immediately. We discuss flushing the brake lines, adding new fluid, checking out the shifting (which was sub-par) -  I am all for this, I just want the bike in great shape for summer. The employee notices that I have only one grip on the bike, I say I have new grips and I'll install them myself - he says no worries, bring 'em in - I'll put' 'em on. The bike already has a new cassette, new chain, new rear derailleur cable, and new tires - AND had just been given a tune-up literally 2 days before at another bike shop (told them this). These guys seem to know their bikes though - I walk out confident that 7 days from now I will be happy with their work....

I call a day before the expected finish date  just confirm we are all on track. They confirm we are. JRA calls back 10 minutes after this and says - man, we're looking at the front chainring and you're going to need a new one....I tell them I know this from the initial visit (?) - he says OK and goes and checks to see if they have the part in stock - no, need to order it. So now I have to wait for the order to arrive,  pay whatever mark-up it they give it and wait again for them to install it - after waiting 7 days for my bike in the first place. Not happening - I am very capable of putting a chainring on - they had their chance for that business.  JRA employee continues to go on about how the shifting is off because of said FRONT chainring. I'm feeling a little insulted at this point. A like new XTR derailleur, new cassette, new chain, new cable -  and we're talking about rear shifting here - I would understand if the chainring was severely warped or missing several teeth, but as long as there is continuous, non-variable linear pull on the chain - the rear shifting is completely dictated by the rear components (chain doesn't skip under heavy pedaling, only while being shifted through the cassette, in both front rings) - I am not waiting any longer for my bike and I reiterate that if this needs to be done I will do it  myself.  He obliges.

Walk in to pick up the bike - give them my name, one guy finds my bike the other give me the invoice - $195  WHAT?
The estimate I got for the work to be done on the bike was $200 after the discussion of me approving the new chainring and installation. That seemed reasonable because I know a new ring can be $60-$70.

The breakdown was as follows:
$60 for the brake flush
$20 for the brake fluid
$30 for suspension linkage re-tightening
$10 for grips install (???)
$75 for tune up (?????)

I am kind of in shock and start asking questions about my suspension - like the fact when I touched the bike seat I felt the rear shock compress and "hey, never had a lefty front shock before, whats the deal with this rebound...."

Now the employee is back-pedaling with the "good point we should check that, and let me get someone over here, I am not sure" - this, after he just told me he is the one who worked on my bike, and charged the $195. 

Next I notice that my tubeless tires have at least 60 psi in them - I say hey I heard that these should be at about 30-40 psi - he says 'yeah, these feel really hard, but you can put them where ever you want when you get home - this is a good starting point...." The MAX psi for these tires is 60 psi - I just let this go. 

Notice I was charged $75 dollars for a tune-up, no one told me what that was, no print out of services done, the guy who "worked" on my bike indicates nothing in the way of tune-up procedures that were done - in fact, tells me the bike is in GREAT shape and ready to be ridden, NO mention of the chainring issue that was of catastrophic importance a day earlier. 

You also may notice that I was charged $10 for grip installation - AWESOME - after I was told to "bring'em in"  
So I leave after paying because I was in no mood for an argument and I'm not going to trust these guys with my bike ever again, so no point in trying to get them to "redo" anything. 
I get home and hop on the bike for a spin around the block - immediately notice that the shifting is not dialed-in, exactly like it was when I brought it in to them. Then I notice they put the grips on wrong. ESI grips have a thicker side that goes toward your palm, this was facing down on one grip and forward on the other - AMAZING. These grips come in a package, this package has instructions. 

Overall, I think these guys know their bikes but are using their rep to overcharge and under-deliver. Do Not Recommend.

THIS IS THE ULTIMATE "KNOW BEFORE YOU GO" EXPERIENCE!

No Honey, I did not shank anyone and end up in county jail!   Let's just say I went on a field trip today and there are some things that you need to know before you go. 

 If you are going to the Fulton County Jail on Rice Street from the burbs, you will want to drive.  We took Marta down because we were handling business at the courthouse and somehow it was assumed that the jail was connected. 

No Ma'am, that is not the case as the jail is miles away.  We hailed a taxi to get to the jail and were met with a little surprise when we arrived.  Here is what you need to know:

It is located in an isolated area away from any businesses so you can't just walk down the street for refreshments or anything.  

You are not allowed to enter the building if you are wearing sandals or carrying a bag, (not even a purse).
You are not allowed to take in a cell phone under any circumstances.
You cannot wear a short skirt or mini-dress.  

Since my daughter and I were wearing sandals, we were not going to be able to go inside of the building.  However, my daughter really needed to go inside because she was the interpreter.  So in order to go inside, she had to trade shoes with her father.  Yes, she gave my husband her black sandals with the cute little flowers while he gave her his size 12 boats.  After adjusting her dress, (ideally it should reach her knees but it didn't) she was permitted to enter.  

Daddy and I waited outside bewildered!  We obviously did not handle this morning's plans, but simply tagged along for moral support so this is why we ended up in this dilemma.   Anyway, the officers who were handling the security checks were very helpful with answering our questions and providing information.

As you are facing the building, there is a small sitting area off to the left.  However, it is for smoking, so not an option.  We wander over to the general area because it is shaded and we find a concrete structure (away from the smoking), to sit on as we wait for our daughter to return.  

Just remember that if you must visit this area, you want to know all of the rules and policies in advance and you will definitely want to drive instead of taking a taxi.  Parking is not an issue here so it is highly recommended that you drive.  

***As we are walking away from the facility just trying to find a commercial area so that we can summon a ride back to the station.   A guardian Angel  (Tasha),suddenly  pulls over and offers us a ride to the train station, which we gladly accept because it a hot day and we really have no idea where we are.  We accept her kind gesture and arrive at the station with only minutes (3) to spare.    Thanks Ms. Tasha!

***Several years ago as I was driving around Alpharetta, an unfamiliar woman (sweating profusely), approached me and asked for a ride to the bus station.  Although I had lived in the area for years, I did not know that there was a bus station here.  It was an extremely hot day so I gave her a ride as she directed me to the location.  She was very appreciative and thanked me repeatedly. 

 Today as I received an act of kindness, I remembered her.   You get back what you put out in the universe so make sure that what you put out is positive and kind!

In my opinion this law firm practices unfair billing & uprofessional practices. I hired Amaral & Associates for a simple divorce: no kids, no large assets. 

A) Billing Practices:  They represented me for 4 months & charged me close to $30K. Few examples: Billing included charges for scanning docs ( very expensive). In addition, the law firm  was inattentive with  documents I had sent them via USPS with tracker. I would receive emails about  sending documents I had already sent, which would then make me reply to them with proof & explanations .I would then get billed for additional correspondence for no fault of mine. Emails correspondence would then be billed as hours of correspondence.

B) Lack of Financial & Accounting Knowhow:  One of the most important aspect of a divorce, in my opinion, is not a lawyer who knows how to work the system ( submitting motions, counter-motions etc). In a probate court, I believe procedural  lawyers don't matter. Everything , in my opinion, boils down to negotiating divorce settlement  for which, in mu opinion, the lawyer should have at least a basic knowledge of Math, Finance & Accounting.  The law firm I believe is not good at it. For example, if you are going to ask your client to take the retirement account instead of the house, the lawyer should at the least know different types of retirement account, pros&cons of  401(K) vs 403(B). That was not the case here. 

C) Misrepresenting Final Cost of Case: When I was billed over $10k in a month, I emailed them stating very clearly, that I was not going to afford this type of payments. I also stated that since the assets were not large spending this type of money made no sense to me. ( Email sent to them is on file with me.) They asked me to call them up  made what I believe to a verbal contract with me stating that the case was almost done & at the most there was 20 hours left. When I pushed them to give me an amount, they stated falsely, that it would be around $7,000. The total bill should have been $17k.  But the final total bill was close to $30,000.

D) Reporting me to credit agency  -  After my divorce settlement, I had three months to remortgage from date of settlement or else I had to sell the house.   During this time I was sent $9,000 bill. By this time I had already paid close to $20,,000 to this law firm. I sent them a mail ( USPS as I had been advised) disputing their amount. In it I stated, that I was told the entire case would be complete amounting to additional $7,000 , which I had  paid& I needed time to look at the bill carefully & get back to them. However they  started to harass me to pay the money by emailing me threatening to report me to credit rating agency, if I didn't pay. This before the 3 months given to me by he courts to refinance the house. The bill sent to be after settlement agreement ,was not even 90 days overdue when they reported me to credit agency. I have evidence of the exact date because I use credit karma to check my scores regularly.  My mortgage had been approved by then. Amaral & Associates name in on the credit agency derogatory remark section. I believe they violated their professional standards by reporting me to credit agency which in turn led to steep decline in my credit score, which in turn would have affected my right to refinance.  ABA claims such measures to be punitive. If I was not able to take out a mortgage I would have to sell the house. My credit score has been affected so badly my student loan refinance attempt has been rejected due to derogatory comment & getting credit cards with good interest rates has been difficult.  

E) Sending Collection Agency Lawyers Against Me: After that incident, they got their debt collection lawyer pals to start harassing me with threatening letters of lawsuit , phone calls & brought a  lawsuit.   At this point, I borrowed money & settled the case. After settling I sent an email to their debt lawyer to remove the derogatory remark on my credit report. It's no action has been taken or response provided until today.

Jennifer was referred to us by an Elder Care attorney and we feel very fortunate to have made the connection. We had a very challenging time with skilled nursing and their referral for out placement started our conversation by setting up a time to look at facilities located between work and home. Jennifer took an entirely different approach. We started with an 1.5 hour interview followed by an independent visit to the SNF where she performed an independent evaluation of the patient and consulted with the SNF staff. Based on her findings, she provided 3 options for us to consider and offered to provide more if these did not meet with our approval. We thought that all 3 were good options and two in particular seemed outstanding.

If that wasn't enough, we had a last minute issue on discharge that left us uncertain as to how to proceed. Jennifer came to our immediate aid and helped us through the remaining hurdles.

We can't say enough good about her. She is kind, considerate, and experienced. She has a thorough knowledge of the facilities in the Portland area and was willing to answer all of our questions without a trace of impatience. We feel extremely fortunate to have found her and cannot recommend her highly enough. Given all of the stress that accompanies the challenges of elder care, having a resource such as Jennifer is an invaluable asset.

Let me first say that the concept of this place is excellent.  But I don't think it's healthy or legal for places to sell expired food to food stamp recipients. Sometimes it smells so bad in there that we walk in and walk right back out. The prices are really good on some products but then again they are expired and considered trash to the stores that donated their waste.  The thrift store nextdoor was AWESOME when Jason was there... now the prices are ridiculously high for people who qualify to shop there....key word is that you have to have a low income to even shop there.  I don't know what happened or why they had to change employees but I used to love going in there... now it just makes me sad to see discards being sold for so much money.

When you visit a local hardware store you never know what you'll get. I'm always curious if it's one of those places with the hidden rooms and endless nooks. 

It wasn't until the 3rd time there that I discovered hillside is one of those places. I had to use the bathroom and finding it took me through a wonderful journey of how hardware stores did things in 1965 (and still do here).  I for one love it. 

I am starting with 3 stars only due to limited experience. Unless I am blown away I'm not going to give 4 or 5 stars until multiple visits. 

I enjoyed my visits so far here. I received helpful paint advice and in searching for a product they had a decent variety. Certainly saved a trip to HD. And since they have so many nooks in the store chances are they have as much inventory as HD. It reminds me a bit of how Hillside Hardware in Medford operates. They always had everything and I had no idea where they stored it all. 

Where Medford hillside carried Benjamin Moore paints as their primary line (an excellent paint for those who don't already know) hillside in Belmont carries Pittsburgh. Pittsburg isn't bad. I have them a shot after foolishly trying  Behr. It worked well and price was cheaper than top HD paint and BM. 

Note to those who don't know - you get the semi gruff hardware store service here. If you're looking for soft kisses or such no way. So just use your best people skills (Daniel Goleman) and get what you need. 

I plan to go back as I have more work to do and they are walking distance. I'll update.

This review is for their PT/OT services, not the doctors and nurses. Having only been there one time for hand therapy, I don't know how well I will like the end results, but here are my first impressions:

The place is very clean, modern, and there is hardly any wait. The staff seems to genuinely want to help. They have some really cool gadgets like the fluidotherapy machine. It's a dry heat machine, feels like hot sand blowing around in it though I believe it's actually corn, and amazingly I was able to do some movements in it without pain. As soon as I got out of there I had to look it up and unfortunately the smallest one starts at something like 5k. I wish I could rent one! Another thing the therapist had on her desk for me to rest my hand on looked like a just a simple thing to elevate a hand on, but having tried pillows and all sorts of other ways to elevate at work all I can say is I want one of these! The most comfortable position I have been in in 6 weeks, whoever invented this thing is a genius. Of course there were all sorts of torture exercises involved but so far so good, hope these people can get me on my way to holding a cup of coffee again. Not that the fist thing isn't useful I just won't need that as often.

A really hidden gem! When we think of Chinese and Indian food, we think of Hong Kong style food, Szechuan food, Shanghainese food, etc! We have Korean-Chinese food, Japanese-Chinese food, but I recently came here with my best friend who's Indian, and she introduced me to Chinese-Indian fusion! (Indo-Chinese food) My parents, being very traditional Chinese folks in terms of food, aren't really used to the extensive spices used in curries, pakoras, and other Indian foods, so whenever I get chili paneer, or butter chicken, my family only has a little bit and I'm left with finishing the lot. But since getting Green Lettuce, my parents are able to enjoy the taste of traditional Chinese, and I'm able to enjoy the spices from traditional Indian food! I often order the veggie fried rice, which has a rich and bolder spicier flavour than traditional Chinese fried rice. I also get the gobi manchurian, which is a deep fried cauliflower dish served with a spiced, slightly sweet sauce! I usually hate cauliflower, but I found this dish to be right up my alley! Their honey garlic chicken is also very good! The meat is very fresh, and you can tell that it was just made to order and not batch cooked! Yes these dishes are "Chinese" but they have the flavours and boldness you would find in Indian cuisine! Definitely worth a try! The owners of both Green Lettuce's are all super nice! (I believe that's who answers the phone anyway) Check it out! I haven't taken many pictures because my phone camera cracked when I dropped it, but I'll make sure to do that with my later reviews!

This was one of the first places I went when I first moved to town and it helped me decide that I had chosen the right city for me.  Vince, the creator was very sweet and let us climb all over this incredible THING that he has built in his back yard.  I think it had two, maybe three stories and all of the old toys that you lost as a kid were stuck in amongst the rest of the "junk".  Vince created a beautiful, weird, magical place that I love to take visitors to.  
If you are looking for other things like this, the Museum of the Weird (on 6th St) is fun and the Museum of Ephemerata is really cool.  Next time you have guests, show them what Austin is really about.

Wow, what a difference driving a few miles make. Please read my reviews regarding Golf Cart Zone. 

Kenfield was the 2nd golf cart business we visited. Didn't hold much hope since the first place was a dud (Golf Cart Zone). Immediately, Kaleb enthusiastically greeted us, acted like he was glad we were there. Like a breath of fresh air! We explained what we were looking for and we weren't golf cart savvy. He respected that we were hesitant to go inside because of Covid, to see another one he thought we would like to see, offered to just open the door so we could see it. This is hands-down my favorite store in Portland. I have never left empty handed, and the only warning I would give is that this place hooks you in. You will want everything in there if you are into all things strange and beautiful. Unique items that you won't find anywhere else. Books, jewelry, art, rocks, plants (I picked up a carnivorous plant last time I was in), bones, oddities, curiosities, gorgeous taxidermy. They make an effort to only use animals that died naturally (when it comes to the babies) or vintage pieces, so an animal lover like myself can shop there with a clear conscience.

The folks here deal with a wide range of patients and a lot of the folks who come through the door are living with chronic pain issues. Some of the reviews complain about the appearance of this clinic. It's not a boutique, no, but it's clean, people are efficient and polite enough, and the technicians doing the job are as informative as they can be given that they're meant to report findings to your doctor and not to you. It's a good all 'round service and I'm hugely pleased to have this service in our neighbourhood. I'm off in a few minutes for another test I don't like having, the results of which I dread getting, but I'm confident that these folks won't screw up and they won't treat me like meat. Beyond that, what would you want?

I recently did a whole home remodel with National Tile and Stone at the helm for many aspects of the work. The parking garage is free and it beats driving into Boston - paying tolls and paying for parking any day.

I happened to go to Polcari's the other night for a couple drinks.  I love this place. It reminds me of my younger days hanging out in the North End when it was located at the corner. The place has that old school Italian flare about it. There are old photos etc scattered around the place as if it were still 1980. The restaurant is quite large and can easily accommodate large parties without reservations. They also have a bar area that has live bands. And don't forget that Regina Pizza is located inside Polcari's...Any way you look at it, you will have an enjoyable time here. As for the food, I did not order any this time around but having been there dozens of times in the past and frequented this place for many many moons. 20-30 years I can give a pretty good summery of the cuisine. Like I mentioned they are old school so you are served complimentary bread, served hot with oil so everyone has a great start... The entrees are huge and over sized and range from 3-4 stars on an average, Your not going to go home and brag about the food, but you will certainly leave full and very satisfied. I have never had a bad meal, nor heard of any bad meals being served there. The service is usually good and very attentive. I would suggest going there for a date or family functions or just hitting the bar for some nice drinks...
