The animals were also over priced because "they breed them themselves". 
If you need a reptile, or reptile food I would avoid this location.

I haven't made any new toy purchases for a few years, decided to contact them since they are one of the 2 vendors that I can remember the names of. 

I called, asked one question he rudely just said : "No idea".
And when I asked if he could direct to the right direction so I can find what I'm looking for, he abruptly hung up on me. 

This is one of the rudest nonsense I had to deal with in customer service.
Totally unacceptable. 

PS: It was the store front supervisor that I spoke to whose name is Tom apparently. Bravo on losing an old customer.

I am a Cambridge resident, St. Paul Parish member, who finds the congregation is very multicultural (as is the residency of this fair town). The  church has a welcoming atmosphere with the priests greeting us with handshakes and smiles after church. My understanding of the church's Harvard affiliation is to provide fellowship and support for the students. After all the church is located with student residences, and Harvard university, offices and Harvard yard within a few short blocks. The music is especially beautiful when the  Catholic Boys choir sings mass, but there are many exceptional cantors with music degrees and professional training. Many vacationers attend the shortened summer masses that leave us with a message of goodwill with love to all.

Employee theft, machine hogs, & broken equipment

When you walk in it looks great. Nice new facility and they have everything. Unfortunately...

I went to purchase a 10 visit pass. I paid cash (don't do that!) and was given a number. The next 4 times gave the number and went in. But the 5th time they verified my name - it wasn't me. The person who sold me the pass pretty clearly pocketed the money and gave me someone else's number. And the two people I talked to there about it insisted that no one working there would ever do this.

They also allow people to park on a machine as long as they want. You'll see pairs of people going back and forth on a machine for 10+ minutes and others that do reps themselves for as long. There's also lots of people who take breaks on the machine, check their email, etc., and again allowed. You're left having to work around the ones parked.

Finally a lot of the bikes are broken. And when they do work, most are impossible to figure out. The other equipment all seems to be good, but the bikes are a mess.

With that said, most of the people working out there are fine. And most are good about taking turns on the equipment. So if you purchase with a credit card, don't care about the bikes, and are good with not getting 1 or 2 machines each time you're there - then it's fine.

We worked with Aaron because our wedding venue recommended him. During the planning process, he sent us a link where we can prepare our song lists of must play, optional etc. I told him from the beginning that most important thing for us is to go around tables with our photographer, say hi to everyone and have a photo with them since we have many guests that are from out of town. I said you can play slow songs while people are eating and we are going through the tables. And since this was a Turkish-American wedding, I added notes to Turkish songs to give him directions like play towards the end of the party etc. We picked our first dance and last dance songs as well. Then we haven't heard from him until 2 days before the wedding. he left a voice message apologizing he wasn't being very responsive, had family issues, which I can understand and would like to talk to us about the details of the event. I said please call us whenever it works for you but he didn't. In the meanwhile our day of coordinator sent him the detailed timeline showing what time we enter, first dance song, walk through tables, toasts, dance, last dance song etc. So the wedding day Aaron did not stop by neither groom's suite or bridal suite before the event. We thought he has the song lists and timeline so we should be all set. Well we were wrong because he completely disregarded the timeline and I ended up dancing to songs I have never even heard of, at my own wedding because instead of playing our song list, he ended up playing what guests kept requesting from him. He didn't play any romantic songs except the first dance song. While we were having dinner, he was dancing by himself behind the DJ table to the point guests asked me if our DJ is drunk. I said he is probably just trying to set a fun mood. But that was awkward because you'd expect a DJ to play slower songs while bride and groom are still eating. As we were getting ready to go around the tables, He totally disregarded the timeline and started the dancing, with the song I put on the list saying "play towards the end of the party". Luckily our videographer had to cut off the dancing so we were at least able to have the toasts. We were thinking maybe we can go around the tables after the toasts but here Aaron again kicked off the dancing so now I'm trying to go around the tables but everyone is on the dance floor. He only played some songs from our must play list and our guests started requesting songs from him so he kept playing those one. Well what's super frustrating about this is we already asked people's song recommendations in our RSVP and prepared our song lists according to this. But when he kept playing the songs some people asked for, other guests thought we totally disregarded their recommendations. If that was Aaron's plan, why did he asked us to prepare song lists as if we didn't have enough on our plates. And it is not polite for people to requests songs at a wedding but after couple of drinks, people do whatever they want. That's why the DJ should talk to the couple before hand or at least stick to the play list the couple prepared since they prepared it for a reason! We were getting frustrated but I also didn't want to be the bridezilla arguing with the DJ at her own wedding. Oh well he changed our grand exit song too and played a completely different song than what we picked!!!!! Did we had fun? Yes we sure did, I danced all night but mostly because our guests were there to have fun and we didn't want one vendor to ruin our night. When I realized things are already out of my control, I just went with the flow. After we got home I sent a long email to Aaron explaining all our frustration. He said he will get back to us and I haven't heard from him (it's been a month)The venue said he had never done something like this before. I'm sure he is a good DJ but lack of communication, not respecting the requests of your client, not understanding what's important to the client is simply bad client service...If only he followed the timeline, I wouldn't be so frustrated about songs but a wedding is a big team event and Aaron was the only one who didn't follow the plans.

I took my son (20 yrs old) and daughter (16yo) here while on vacation. My son had to be talked into it. They had the time of their lives! Both of them spent hours afterwards watching the videos and reliving the experience. My daughter said it was the best vacation adventure of her life! My husband and I watched to two hour class and our faces hurt from smiling. I could not believe how quickly the instructors taught them and how much they progressed in one night. Incredible. Thank you Andre and Pasha and Justin! We will return every time we come back to Orlando and send all our friends. Thank you!!

I gave Altec another shot at a small job and worked with Dan again.  I found him to be responsive and helpful.  Altec ultimately didn't get the job because I got a better price somewhere else, but I wouldn't hesitate to let them bid on another job.  I wish that I lived close enough to actually see samples of various options and that may have helped to justify the price difference, but I live far away so it's really about price, speed, and quality (I want them all and it usually works out that way.)  Three stars is defined by Yelp as "A-OK" and I guess that's about right since I'd be glad to let them bid on future jobs.

I have never been made to feel more horrible about myself than I did when I went here. I get it, I'm not perfect, I wouldn't even come to your office if I was. The least anyone in the office could have attempted to do was to make me feel even a little good about myself our even give a hopeful outlook. I was basically told I was too fat for most of the procedures to help me and the ones that might help would probably result in terrible looking skin. Please, by all means, sign me up for more negativity and mental torment. While you're at it, I'll go ahead and pay $8000 to possibly look less fat, but of course you can't promise a thing. I will gladly take my money elsewhere to a more professional and positive environment.

Shrimp Pasta in pesto sauce, (side of 2 garlic bread) was a really huge serving (3 persons can eat it) for $14.95 & it was good.  $5.00 for a glass of wine.  Chicken Caesar salad was perfect.  Fish sandwich w/fresh lettuce & tomatoes w/a side of coleslaw & (crispy) curly fries--good :)).  Different burgers including bison burger (didn't try it though).  Garlic cheeseburger--Really Tasty-fresh lettuce, tomatoes, red onions, garlic flavored condiment, curly fries & large pickles!  New York steak is also available.  They also have flatbread sandwiches in their menu.  Kids cheeseburger was ok for the price--$5.00 w/lots of curly fries.  They also have a couple of desserts.  Few draft beers--Miller, Bud, some beers.  2 pool tables that I saw.  Accessible to kids game room (just behind it).  Hershey's Ice cream shop (beside it).  They also have breakfast buffet.  To sum it up the place was convenient for people visiting the villas bec. it's within the vicinity & it's not that bad ;)

Do yourself a favor and FIND SOMEWHERE ELSE. Seriously, this place is a freaking scam. THREE TIMES, I have called to have a prescription refilled only to learn that my "doctor is no longer with the practice" and I'll have to "schedule an appointment with the new doctor" to get my prescription refilled. AKA - I have to PAY FOR AN APPOINTMENT to walk into an office for someone that I will likely never see again say, "So you need a refill? (Yes) I see on your chart that you've been taking it now for 2 years. (Yep) Has anything changed? (Nope) Okay great, I'll get that in for you. Anything else you're concerned about? (Literally no). Have a great day - that'll be $150." 

ABSOLUTELY NOT. 

I was never informed or alerted that ANY of my doctors were leaving the practice and rather than assign me to a doctor with some tenure in the practice, they assign me to the newb. 

This place is a joke. With turnover clearly an issue, you're better off going elsewhere.

This company doesn't take responsibility for damage they do when hauling their dumpsters. Spoke to Paul about damage in front of my house when they were moving a dumpster from my neighbor's house and he said they get complaints all the time but it isn't their problem and I need to get in touch with the contractor that hired them.  But then he wouldn't give me the number for the contractor.  The driver was also rude when we tried to talk to him about it.
Thanks for nothing.  
My advice to customers is call Trojan.  We have used them many times with No issues, No damage and cheap prices.

I think this is a pretty cool park. They built it just a few years ago so it's pretty new, or at least parts of it are new. There's history about an old train station that used to be there. There's a bunch of picnic tables under an awning and also some picnic tables out in the sunshine. There's a park with a climbing wall type structure that looks pretty cool. I'm almost 30 so there's no way I've gotten the courage to climb it yet. Maybe one day. Lol There's a few different jungle gym pieces and quite a few swings. Also a handicap swing which is so neat and inclusive. There's a little water park for the kids in the summertime and large swing benches along the water park which are fun to sit on in any weather. It's very relaxing there and we sometimes take books or snacks and sit in the grassy patch to enjoy watching life go by on nice sunny days. There's a Dairy Queen right down the road from here so sometimes we walk there first and bring treats back to enjoy in the park. Our pup likes the kids size peanut butter sundae best.  There really is a lot jampacked in a small area here but this is a pretty neat park to have close to home. If I had kids I could definitely see myself spending a day here. Kids seem to love the water park that shoots water out of the ground. I mean, how could they not love that?! Lol I love it and I'm an adult!

Absolutely fantastic service. 

I needed to get my DJI Phantom 4 fixed and found out that EZDrone is the only DJI authorized service provider in the entire PNW. I went to their location in the Pearl District and unfortunately, no one was there, even though they were supposed to have opened an hour earlier. I was a little perturbed to have made the trip down there, and left a voice mail letting them know I'd been by.

About an hour later, Ben called me apologizing for his absence, and asked me if it would be OK for him to stop by my house later that day. He finally came by, and was the nicest guy, answering any questions I had, and taking my drone back with him to get serviced. 

They got my drone all sorted out, and even went the extra mile by making a house call. Great job, guys. I'll definitely be giving you my future drone business from here on out :)

Thanks so much!

I started coming here to refill my kegerator's CO2 tank (~$16 for 20 lbs). Unlike Airgas, which only does swaps, they'll fill your tank while you wait (under 20 lbs) or usually same day (for 20 lbs). If you need to buy a (used) tank, their prices are also much better than Airgas, especially for a 20 lbs tank ($130 filled vs. $240 empty!). Everyone I dealt with seemed friendly and cool. They weren't so great about calling me when my refill was delayed or when it was ready, but I've come to expect that from most places, and it's not hard to call and check.

Aubrey Ducker was exactly what I needed during my divorce.  He was blunt, didn't sugar coat the realities of divorce, and even offered some fatherly advice when the emotional side of the divorce began to get overwhelming.  Tacey, his paralegal, was eager to help and is very knowledgable.  Working through her helped reduce cost and she made herself available when my schedule had many conflicts.  Every penny I spent was worth the closure I gained when the divorce was final...ultimately, in my favor.  Thank you Aubrey!

My body has been in desperate cry for help, my shoulders and entire back were so exhausted that I felt like one big stone.  It was truly affecting the quality of my life and it was making me feel truly demotivated to do anything (even going for walks around which I usually enjoy doing) 

I knew that my pain was caused due to super poor posture, and using my laptop and phone excessively.  To add insult to the injury, I was using those devices in bed everyday.  From all that you can imagine I was a big tired and stiff wreck.

This is the second time we have used Bounce Around Austin for a kid's birthday party and both times have been extremely pleased and highly recommend this company.  The process to reserve and pay for the rental was easy, the price is reasonable, and when I had to change the date of our party Jason accommodated our updated plans.  The weather on the day of our party was questionable, when Jason called to confirm a set up time the day before the party we discussed the forecast and safety; since it was just a chance of rain and no wind (key) we decided to move forward, but I got the impression that if the forecast had called for any wind they would have declined to set up the bounce house putting safety first which means a lot to me.  The bounce house was delivered/set up on time on the day of our party; the Justice League house was clean and in great condition and has a roof so even with the light rain the kiddos stayed dry and were able to bounce without any issue.  The employees are professional and courteous.  Bonus - we rented the bounce house for a four hour block, but ended up keeping it for 24 hours+ at no additional charge which was awesome.  The kids has a great time at the party, but with a house full of relatives for the entire weekend it was really neat to have this attraction for kids and adults alike for more than the planned time.  We live outside of town so that may have factored into the late pickup/bonus time, which the driver cleared with us in advance upon delivery, some might want to clear their yard right away as the bounce house does take up a lot of space, but we were thrilled and appreciated the extra time. Highly recommend!  :-)

Absolutely beautiful book selection -  smart, funny, hip and cover a wide range of topics from artsy to scientific.

 In the past month or so they have redone the space and it now has an amazing little play area in the middle for kids to tinker. I would no longer hesitate to come in with my kids fearing they will grab all the products because they have a dedicated, central play area. 

The space also hosts regular Saturday events and birthday parties for age 5+. We'll be back!

His prices are very reasonable for the work he does and how quickly he does it. If you're thinking about it, book him...you won't regret it!

I feel like I hit the jackpot finding Natasha. Ive been very ill over the last 5-6 months and have not been able to move or exercise the way I need to in order to feel like myself. My body has lost so much mobility and twisted me up in chronic pain. Natasha took her time to recognize the biggest sources causing imbalance. I was looking for lunch in the area and "Italian Street Food" piqued my interest.  There are a lot of different possibilities with that, and they're all good.  Piada only reinforces that.

I decided to order the pasta carbonara with some grilled chicken.  It's very rich and there's a lot of pasta.  I would've liked a little more chicken to balance it out, but it was delicious nonetheless.

Everything is made in an assembly line, so you get your food very quickly and effectively.  Everything is portioned very particularly.  For the price, it's well worth it.

Great service. After another location refused to even diagnose out iPhone 5, we took it here based on the 2 good reviews it had. The screen was completely cracked and slightly raised from a piece of the case that had gotten wedged under the screen. In about an hour the screen was repaired and fully functioning. They also fixed the power button which had been broken for months (that Apple wouldn't fix for us). And you can't beat the price. 10/10 would repair again.

This is pretty much the only place I like on Mississippi where I live. The service is so bloody good and like no where else in Portland, especially for a coffee shop. However their food is great too. Simple and delicious and they are so nice and they care so hard about what they are putting in front of you. I have become a super scroodgy fussy pants in response to the abysmal service pervading Portland and I just LOVE Local. Go there...or don't and let me keep it to myself.

Powdery, then icy.

I left my car at work to take Trimet. It worked, mostly. I didn't have to deal with terrible Portland drivers, and I saved some money not paying for gas. Unfortunately, I did have to pay more for heating my place. Probably a toss up.

Cross country skis or snowshoes may have been the best ways to get around. I appreciated that it made people stay inside, allowing my antisocial self to go out in public without having to deal with crowds. The epic storm also gave me an opportunity to sit at home without feeling lazy, and getting stuff I needed to get done around the house done.

Player's is great. They specialize in racquets, shoes, gear, strings etc. for racquet sports and it can be hard to find specific stuff in other general purpose sports stores. They have a racquet trial program which is nice and a frequent stringer card which is rather nice. They are also really friendly and easy to work with and reasonable. The one downer, which isn't really their fault, is that they're across town for me and getting there on a weekday in their working hours involves moving my schedule around a lot. But I highly recommend them.

When I told him I stopped a medication because of side-effects, he told me there was nothing he could do for me & his tone went from 'so-charming' to 'not-so-charming.' Surprised by Heather S.'s review, because out of the 3 GI doctors I saw, Dr. Trey was definitely the least condescending. But maybe it's all relative (the other two doctors were abysmal). Still, Dr. Trey was very responsive, a very creative problem-solver, and very accommodating.

A little too honest - he told me that cases like mine depress him, because I'm so young. I didn't really need to hear that, or comfort him that I was depressing him. But really, that mostly just amused me. As long as the doctor gets the job done, I'll put up with the rest.

Been here a handful of times after moving up from Miami and it is EXTREMELY OVERPRICED for the quality. It's in the 'hood, but an improving part of the 'hood (across from the hospital).
I think the reason why they rate 3 stars instead of 2 is because of the neato factor of being a place that production companies go to in order to rent stuff.  With that perspective in mind, you don't look at the collection of items as "Who the hell would buy this worthless piece of shit" and think instead "Did I see that on that movie I saw recently?".

There are better places, but if you are looking for stuff from the late 60's and 70's (i.e., harvest gold and avocado are primo on your color wheel) then this may be the place for you.

We had an enjoyable time here celebrating my daughter's 4th birthday with all her little friends! The museum folks were good to work with - they were able to confirm our booking quickly, recommended a good place to order pizza and subs (Al's Pizza and Grill in South Boston), suggested the agenda of events, and acted as host. The kids were also able to interact with the exhibits downstairs on the 1st floor, where they reenacted a fire scene and let the kids carry the hose to "extinguish" it. I got a classic-looking gold frame for a oil on canvas painting. The store person helped select something that matched well and aimed at the style I was looking for. The place was a bit pricy, but I was looking for convenience so I went with it. I had a claim ticket to come back in about 2 weeks. 

Two weeks and two days went buy and, while walking by, I checked in on its status. I was told by the owner that all ready dates given are approximate. Puzzled how their estimates were rather off, I accepted the owner's assurances of being called the moment it was ready. 

A week later, I called and asked for an update. They informed me it was ready (no call given) and I could pick it up any time. 

I arrive to pick it up and the owner says it was ready the day after I was in last. While it was not urgent, I was miffed the order took so long. Additionally, the owner was flippant about it's readiness and service. 

The framing turned out well and I was pleased with the result. However, for the handling and customer service, next time I'll be going elsewhere.

If you're on the fence about it-- I just wanted to give you that extra push to JUST DO IT. If you're nervous just wear your clothes and meet up with the group. Odds are you're going to want to strip down, but if you decide you don't you can always cheer people on or just be a spectator. 

The Good:
I've heard a lot of good things about the ride and all of them are true. Being naked amongst ~10K people is really liberating. It reminds you how beautiful the human body is and how many different body types there are.

It's pretty organized for the most part. The cops are very helpful. Everyone's looking out for each other including spectators who are cheering you on and warning you about train tracks, potholes, etc.

The Bad:
A LOT of people take pictures and record video. 

You might run into people you don't want to. The odds are actually quite high that you'll run into people you know. I personally ran into a bunch of coworkers but you're on level playing ground.

Tips:
Do whatever makes you feel comfortable. If you want to wear a mask-- do it. If you want to wear paint, underwear, fairy wings, etc. go for it!

Think about what you're packing and don't over pack. You'll want water and perhaps a snack. Especially if your first ride-- you might be flustered so be careful and don't lose your stuff.

I emailed them about getting some work done on my poorly running scooter.  I had an idea of what the problem was and asked for an estimate on that particular service.  I got a response that said $60 + install time, but they wanted to diagnose it to be sure.  Sounded reasonable so I took it in.  The guy working that day (I later found out his name is Bill), told me it sounded like a clogged carb, but if it was the fuel pump, as I asked about, it should "only take his guy about a half an hour.  He's done those a hundred times."  At this point, I didn't even know what they charged for labor, but even if it was $100/hr, I was ok.

I called three days later to find out if it was ready.  He said that they had to order the fuel pump, so give it about a week.  It seemed like a long time, but oh well.  I called a week later to check in and was told that they had gotten the part a couple days ago but it arrived broken, so they ordered a new one.  At this point I was pretty mad.  I understand the part broken wasn't their fault, but not calling me when it happened was bad.  This meant scrambling to figure out my commute for another week.  

Got a call 4 days later that the part was in and ready to go.  I had them email me the invoice.  It was twice what I was told it would cost.  Bill wasn't there, and the girl who said she's "just the counter girl" told me to take it up with the mechanic.  My problem, again, was bad communication.  If anyone had called me and said there were some recommended parts (filter & valve) to change while they had it apart, and that the labor was going to be triple the estimated time I was told, I would have told them no because I wasn't okay paying $250 for the service, but they just went ahead and did it.  The mechanic said it's common practice for a scooter that's dropped off to them to just do their thing without okaying the work.  After a civil but not friendly discussion with the mechanic, I had him remove the part and put the old pump back in.  To his credit, the mechanic kept his cool and neither of us raised his voice, though neither was happy, and he had it switched back in under a half an hour.  

Based on this service debacle I have a hard time recommending them to anyone.

The standout is the salsa, hot and packed with flavor (both verde and roja). I give the al pastor high marks for being juicy and the cachete was the best. Talking to Rabbi Levy over the phone my Partner and I knew he was the guy for the job.  

Rabbi Levy came to perform the procedure in our home, which to me was very special as it was a comforting setting for our son. Rabbi Levy was very through about letting us know how the procedure would take place as well as after care for our son. He made sure everything felt in the room felt positive and that everything was calm and said a really beautiful prayer. He was extremely professional, trustworthy and came with sterile equipment.  The procedure was done quickly within 2 minutes and we were able to assist him in aiding our son. It was not done in a traumatizing Hospital setting where my friends told me stories of how their sons are wheeled to away from them and strapped down to a table, instead of being held by parents. If we had another son we'd definitely have Rabbi Levy assist us again. The care he has for the families, the professionalism of his work, the fact he was willing to help us and travel to us, we definitely made the right decision enlisting in his care

I engaged the Repacke Law Group to correct fraudulent assignments against two of my patents.  It was a complex case and they told me I might have to sue to get the patent ownership corrected, but we could try an Affidavit of Declaration first.  I agreed, they drafted the document, I approved it, signed it, and they told me they sent it to the USPTO Assignment Division for recording.  This was in April.  I kept checking back with the lawyers and they told me it took a long time and they could not speed up the patent office.  The document they said they filed never showed up in the patent files, so after five months, I called the assignment Division and they told me they never received the document.  For several weeks, I asked Repacke for shipping confirmation, but got no answer.  They just told me they sent it and there was nothing else they could do.  When I pushed, they sent me USPS tracking information showing they never sent the document, after stalling me for five months.  Repacke agreed to resent the document and sent me tracking information showing that some document was received at the USPTO.  After a few more weeks of seeing nothing in the patent file wrapper, I called the Patent Office and they told me they had nothing showing in my patent files from my lawyers.  I paid them $2500 to draft and file the document, but now they tell me I have to pay more if I want them to make sure it gets recorded.  I decided to call the USPTO and found out how to file the Correction by Declaration form online, submitted the Affidavit and supporting documents online, and had it show up in the image file wrapper within a few days.  It seems like legal professionals would also be able to do this.  I am not sure if they really sent my Affidavit, but it took a long time and my patents assignments are still not completely corrected.  Hopefully I can find someone who can get the job done or do it myself.  I would probably not use Repacke Law Group again.

Beware the man that professes to know and deliver it all! We hired Berman Adjusters following the disappointing settlement offered by our insurance company for the catastrophic fire to our three-family property. When we initially met Larry, he gave a virtuoso performance going on in detail about his impressive resume, strong insurance and political contacts, and ability to right a wrong quickly and efficiently. Upon examining the insurance company's proposed settlement to us, Larry offered up a condemnation of the adjustor's methodology and without doubt, said that he would have this settlement properly "re-settled" within 60 days. Larry exuded, with great confidence, that a little dialogue between him and the insurance adjustor would right a very grave wrong. After being wooed and wowed, we confidently signed a contract with Berman Adjusters which allowed for 5 % of the total settlement as a fee for their services. That turned out to be a mistake.

During the 60 days that Larry promised for a revised settlement, we had to contact his office repeatedly for a status of his efforts and communication back from him was always delayed. After many weeks of waiting, the calculations arrived with a higher bottom line and Larry passed those on to the insurance company. After reviewing, the insurance company sent back an e-mail indicating disagreement with the calculations and reaffirmed their position on the initial set of their calculations. At that point Larry told us there is nothing more he can do and referred us to a law firm that specializes in legal resolution of such matters (which of course charges their own fee). 

Skip ahead, a year later, the law firm sets up a final hearing with the insurance company's adjuster and legal team, expert witnesses, the referee panel, and us. Berman Adjusters is not represented. At the hearing, the insurance adjustor under oath indicates that he never spoke with anyone from Berman Adjusters and that his communications boiled down to a couple emails back and forth. In fact, the insurance adjustor said he was surprised to hear that the case had moved onto the legal phase since he had not felt that Berman Adjusters had completed or sustained the dialogue of the case with the insurance company.

At the end of the process, Berman Adjusters received a substantial fee (5% on the entire settlement). I reached out to Larry Berman to address my concerns of his apparent non-performance of his contractual responsibilities to represent us (again, all he did is outsource the calculations, send those to insurance, and then refer us to a different law firm). Larry chose not to address my concerns. He arrogantly stated that since we knew nothing of the insurance litigation process we would have failed in appealing the insurance company's initial settlement. Also given we had received extra money from the settlement, we should have no problem paying his fee. A lot of money for a lot of nothing!
